notes.notes: From Spanish 'como esta'. 'Kumusta ka?' Also 'Kumusta ang trabaho?' = How's work? Casual 'Musta?'

examples.tl: Kumusta ka na?
examples.en: How have you been?
examples.taglish: Musta na, pre?

examples.tl: Kumusta ang interview mo?
examples.en: How was your interview?

examples.tl: Kumusta ang trabaho?
examples.en: How's work?
examples.taglish: Kumusta ang work? Okay pa ba?

notes.taglish: Kumusta? Busy ka ba ngayon?
Musta? Tagal na nating di nag-usap.
notes.notes: Clipped 'kumusta'. Very casual, friends and texts only. Also a conversation opener on chat with no real question intended.

examples.tl: Musta na? Buhay pa?
examples.en: How you been? Still alive?
examples.taglish: Musta na, bro? Buhay pa?

notes.taglish: Uy, kumusta ka na? Tagal na nating di nagkita.
notes.notes: 'na' adds 'by now', so it fits someone you have not seen in a while. Neutral.

examples.tl: Kumusta ka na? Nasa Makati pa ba kayo?
examples.en: How have you been? Are you still in Makati?
examples.taglish: Kumusta ka na? Makati pa ba kayo?

notes.taglish: Okay lang ako, medyo busy lang sa work.
notes.notes: Default reply to 'kumusta'. Also 'Okay lang' = 'no worries' after an apology. 'lang' = just, so it can hint 'just okay, nothing special'.

examples.tl: Okay lang. Ikaw, kumusta?
examples.en: I'm fine. And you, how are you?

examples.tl: Okay lang yun, wag mo na isipin.
examples.en: It's fine, don't worry about it.
examples.taglish: Okay lang yun, chill ka lang.

examples.tl: Okay lang, hindi ko na kailangan.
examples.en: It's fine, I don't need it anymore.

notes.taglish: Ayos lang, nag-rest lang ako sa condo buong weekend.
notes.notes: Slightly more upbeat than 'okay lang'. Neutral-casual. 'Ayos!' alone = 'nice'.

examples.tl: Ayos lang kami dito, wala namang baha.
examples.en: We're fine here, no flooding anyway.
examples.taglish: Ayos lang kami dito, walang baha sa BGC.

notes.taglish: Eto, buhay pa. Puro work lang.
notes.notes: Humorous reply to 'kumusta'. 'Eto' = 'here (I am)'. Casual, very common among adults joking about being tired.

examples.tl: Kumusta? -- Eto, buhay pa, nakakaraos.
examples.en: How are you? -- Here, still alive, getting by.

notes.taglish: Uy, long time no see! Kumusta na?
notes.notes: Said in English even mid-Tagalog. The Tagalog version 'Ang tagal nating 'di nagkita' is also natural. Neutral.

examples.tl: Long time no see! Tumaba ka, ah.
examples.en: Long time no see! You got heavier, huh.
examples.taglish: Long time no see! Ang laki ng pinagbago mo.

notes.taglish: Oy! Nasaan ka na? Andito na kami.
notes.notes: Casual attention-getter among friends. Fine with peers; do not 'oy' strangers, elders, or staff.

examples.tl: Oy, ikaw pala yan!
examples.en: Hey, it's you!

examples.tl: Oy, tara, kain tayo.
examples.en: Hey, come on, let's eat.

notes.taglish: Uy, may bago kang phone!
notes.notes: Softer than 'oy'. Opens a text ('Uy, musta?'), shows mild surprise, or teases ('Uy, kinikilig!'). Very common.

examples.tl: Uy, salamat ha!
examples.en: Oh hey, thanks!

examples.tl: Uy, sino yun? May date ka?
examples.en: Ooh, who's that? You have a date?
examples.taglish: Uy, sino yun? May date ka, ah?

notes.taglish: Hoy! Bakit di ka nag-reply kanina?
notes.notes: Brash, louder than 'oy'. Fine for scolding a close friend or calling someone far away; rude to strangers, elders, or service staff.

examples.tl: Hoy, tumigil ka nga!
examples.en: Hey, stop it!

examples.tl: Hoy, gising! Late na tayo.
examples.en: Hey, wake up! We're late.
examples.taglish: Hoy, gising! Late na tayo sa meeting.

notes.taglish: Pssst! Kuya, pa-order.
notes.notes: Hissed to call a waiter, vendor, or someone nearby. Extremely common but considered a bit rude in nicer places; pair with 'Kuya/Ate' or 'excuse me' to soften.

examples.tl: Pssst, ate, bill out po.
examples.en: Psst, miss, the bill please.

notes.taglish: Tara, coffee tayo sa Salcedo.
notes.notes: Short for 'tayo na'. The everyday way to propose doing something. Casual, friendly. 'Tara' + verb: 'Tara kain', 'Tara gala'.

examples.tl: Tara, kain tayo sa labas.
examples.en: Come on, let's eat out.

examples.tl: Tara, mall tayo.
examples.en: Let's go, let's hit the mall.

notes.taglish: Tara na, nag-book na ako ng Grab.
notes.notes: 'na' = now/already; use when it's actually time to leave. 'Tayo na' is the fuller form, same meaning.

examples.tl: Tara na, baka ma-traffic pa tayo.
examples.en: Let's go now, we might hit traffic.
examples.taglish: Tara na, baka ma-traffic tayo sa EDSA.

examples.tl: Tara na, baka ma-late tayo sa flight.
examples.en: Let's go, we might be late for the flight.
examples.taglish: Tara na, baka ma-late tayo, traffic pa sa airport road.

examples.tl: Tara, sabay na tayo sa Grab, BGC din ako.
examples.en: Come on, let's share a Grab, I'm going to BGC too.

notes.taglish: Inom mamaya sa Poblacion, G?
notes.notes: Short for 'game'. Slang, mostly in texts and chats among friends. Answer with 'G!' or 'G ako'.

examples.tl: Lakad bukas, G?
examples.en: Going out tomorrow, you in?
examples.taglish: Lakad bukas sa BGC, G?

notes.taglish: G ako, anong oras?
notes.notes: Slang reply to 'G?'. 'Hindi ako G' or 'pass muna ako' to decline. Casual.

examples.tl: G ako, basta libre mo ako.
examples.en: I'm in, as long as you treat me.

notes.taglish: Sige, see you sa lobby.
notes.notes: The all-purpose yes. Also closes a chat ('Sige, ingat'). Tone can be enthusiastic or resigned, so watch the delivery.

examples.tl: Sige, bukas na lang tayo magkita.
examples.en: Okay, let's just meet tomorrow.

examples.tl: Sige, salamat ha.
examples.en: Alright, thanks.

examples.tl: Sige, kita tayo mamaya.
examples.en: Okay, see you later.

notes.en: Come on, please / fine, go ahead
notes.taglish: Sige na, sama ka na. Isang inom lang.
notes.notes: Two uses: begging ('Sige na, please') or giving in ('Sige na, go'). Also 'Sige na nga' = fine, whatever. Casual.

examples.tl: Sige na, isang kain lang tapos uwi na tayo.
examples.en: Come on, just one meal then we go home.

examples.tl: Sige na nga, ikaw na ang bahala.
examples.en: Fine then, you handle it.

notes.taglish: O siya, sige, mag-rest ka na.
notes.notes: Signals the conversation is ending. Slightly older-sounding but still common, especially from parents and titas. Often 'O siya, sige.'

examples.tl: O siya, ingat ka pauwi.
examples.en: Alright then, take care going home.

notes.taglish: Sige, ingat! Text mo ako pag nakauwi ka.
notes.notes: The standard goodbye, more common than 'paalam'. Root ingat = care. 'Ingat po' to elders.

examples.tl: Bye, ingat!
examples.en: Bye, take care!

examples.tl: Ingat kayo sa daan.
examples.en: You all be careful on the road.

examples.tl: Ingat sa biyahe, text ka pag nakarating.
examples.en: Safe travels, text when you arrive.
examples.taglish: Ingat sa biyahe, text mo ako pag nakarating ka na.

notes.taglish: Ingat ka, ha. Mag-text ka pag nasa bahay ka na.
notes.notes: Warmer than plain 'ingat'. Add 'ha' to make it tender. 'Ingat kayo' to several people or an elder.

examples.tl: Ingat ka, malakas ang ulan.
examples.en: Take care, the rain is heavy.
examples.taglish: Ingat ka, grabe ang ulan sa labas.

examples.tl: Ingat ka pauwi, madilim na.
examples.en: Take care going home, it's dark already.
examples.taglish: Ingat ka pauwi, madilim na, share mo location mo.

examples.tl: Ingat kayo sa daan, baha daw sa Taft.
examples.en: Take care on the road, Taft is flooded they say.

notes.taglish: Bye na! Kita-kits sa Sabado.
notes.notes: What people actually say instead of 'paalam'. 'na' = now. Common full sign-off: 'Sige, bye na, ingat.'

examples.tl: Bye na, late na ako!
examples.en: Bye now, I'm running late!

notes.taglish: Una na ako, may 8 AM meeting ako bukas.
notes.notes: Polite way to leave a group. Full form 'Mauna na ako'. In chat, 'Una na ako, ingat kayo'.

examples.tl: Una na ako, kuya, may pasok pa ako bukas.
examples.en: I'll go ahead, bro, I still have work tomorrow.

notes.taglish: Nobody texts 'paalam'; they text 'Sige, bye na, ingat.'
notes.notes: Textbook goodbye. In real life it sounds dramatic or literary (songs, speeches, leaving for good). Say 'bye', 'sige', 'ingat', 'una na ako' instead.

examples.tl: Paalam, at salamat sa lahat.
examples.en: Goodbye, and thank you for everything.

notes.taglish: Kita-kits bukas sa Greenbelt!
notes.notes: Playful slang from 'kita' (see each other). Casual texts among friends. 'See you' in English is equally common.

examples.tl: Sige, kita-kits mamaya!
examples.en: Okay, see you later!

notes.taglish: Ano, pupunta ka ba sa party ni Mark?
notes.notes: Question word 'what', but also the #1 filler ('ano...') and a placeholder noun ('yung ano'). 'Ano?' alone = 'What?' (blunt).

examples.tl: Ano, kain na tayo?
examples.en: So, shall we eat now?

examples.tl: Nasaan yung ano... yung charger?
examples.en: Where's the um... the charger?

examples.tl: Ano ang gusto mong kainin?
examples.en: What do you want to eat?

notes.taglish: Si kuwan, yung officemate mo, nag-resign na daw.
notes.notes: Placeholder when a word escapes you: a thing, a person, even a verb ('nag-kuwan'). Very natural, neutral.

examples.tl: Pakiabot yung kuwan... yung remote.
examples.en: Hand me the thingy... the remote.

examples.tl: Si kuwan, yung kapitbahay niyo, nag-move out na.
examples.en: Whatshername, your neighbor, moved out already.

notes.taglish: Parang na-late na tayo sa reservation.
notes.notes: Softens any statement, the way Americans use 'like' or 'kinda'. Also 'it seems'. Neutral, extremely common.

examples.tl: Parang uulan.
examples.en: Looks like it's going to rain.

examples.tl: Parang ayaw ko na.
examples.en: I kind of don't want to anymore.

examples.tl: Parang uulan mamaya.
examples.en: Looks like it'll rain later.

notes.taglish: Na-late ako kasi traffic sa EDSA.
notes.notes: 'Because', but also a filler starting an excuse ('Kasi...'). Comes after the first word or at the start. 'Dahil' is the formal version.

examples.tl: Hindi ako nakapunta kasi may lagnat ako.
examples.en: I couldn't go because I had a fever.

examples.tl: Kasi naman, ang tagal mong mag-reply.
examples.en: It's just that you take forever to reply.

examples.tl: Na-late ako kasi traffic.
examples.en: I was late because of traffic.

notes.taglish: Eh kasi, wala akong budget ngayong week eh.
notes.notes: Starts a hesitant reply ('Eh...') or ends a sentence as an excuse marker ('wala akong pera eh'). 'Eh kasi' = well, it's because.

examples.tl: Eh, hindi ko alam eh.
examples.en: Well, I don't really know.

examples.tl: Gusto ko sana, pero busy ako eh.
examples.en: I'd like to, but I'm busy, you see.

notes.taglish: Ikaw naman, chill ka lang.
notes.notes: Hard to translate; adds contrast, softening or mild complaint. 'Ako naman' = me, for my part. 'Hindi naman' = not really. Neutral.

examples.tl: Ang ganda naman nito!
examples.en: This is so pretty!

examples.tl: Ikaw naman, lagi kang late.
examples.en: Oh come on, you're always late.

examples.tl: Ikaw naman, kumusta?
examples.en: And you, how are you?

notes.taglish: Ha? Anong sabi mo? Maingay dito eh.
notes.notes: Rising 'Ha?' = huh? Sentence-final 'ha' = 'okay?' tag that softens ('Sorry ha', 'Ingat ka ha'). Both very common.

examples.tl: Ha? Di kita narinig.
examples.en: Huh? I didn't hear you.

examples.tl: Dito lang ako, ha?
examples.en: I'll just be here, okay?

notes.taglish: Ah okay, so bukas na yung delivery.
notes.notes: Acknowledgment that you understood. Neutral. In chat, a lone 'Ah okay' can read as cold, so add an emoji or 'sige'.

examples.tl: Ah okay, kaya pala wala ka kanina.
examples.en: Oh okay, so that's why you weren't around earlier.

notes.en: Oh, I see / that's how it is.
notes.taglish: Ah ganun, kaya pala nag-cancel siya.
notes.notes: 'Ganun' = like that. Shows you now understand. Spelled 'ganon' in texts; 'ganoon' is formal.

examples.tl: Ah ganun ba? Hindi ko alam yun.
examples.en: Oh is that so? I didn't know that.

notes.taglish: Talaga? Nag-resign siya? Grabe.
notes.notes: Also 'talaga' as 'really/truly' inside a sentence ('Ikaw talaga' = oh, you). Neutral, safe with anyone.

examples.tl: Talaga? Kailan?
examples.en: Really? When?

examples.tl: Masarap talaga dito.
examples.en: The food here is really good.

examples.tl: Talaga? Hindi ko alam yun.
examples.en: Really? I didn't know that.

notes.taglish: Seryoso? Nag-propose na siya?
notes.notes: From Spanish 'serio'. Neutral-casual. 'Seryoso ka?' = are you serious? 'Seryosohin' = take seriously.

examples.tl: Seryoso? Sold out na yung tickets?
examples.en: Seriously? The tickets are sold out already?

notes.taglish: Weh? Di nga? Ikaw, nag-gym?
notes.notes: Playful disbelief, like 'oh really?' with a raised eyebrow. Often 'Weh, di nga?' Slang, friends only.

examples.tl: Weh? Nag-aral ka ng Tagalog? Patunayan mo.
examples.en: Oh really? You studied Tagalog? Prove it.

notes.taglish: Legit ba yung seller na yan sa Shopee?
notes.notes: English slang fully adopted. 'Legit ba?' = is it real / are you serious? 'Legit!' = confirmed, for real. Casual.

examples.tl: Legit masarap yung sisig dun.
examples.en: The sisig there is legit good.

examples.tl: Legit? Libre talaga?
examples.en: For real? It's really free?

notes.taglish: Grabe yung traffic kanina, 2 hours ako sa Grab.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'grave'. Reacts to anything extreme, good or bad. Neutral-casual, used constantly.

examples.tl: Grabe ang init ngayon!
examples.en: It's crazy hot today!

examples.tl: Grabe, ang ganda ng view dito.
examples.en: Wow, the view here is gorgeous.

examples.tl: Tatlong oras ako sa EDSA kanina. — Grabe! Bakit di ka nag-MRT?
examples.en: I was on EDSA for three hours earlier. — Wow! Why didn't you take the MRT?

notes.taglish: Grabe naman, 500 pesos yung parking?
notes.notes: 'naman' turns 'grabe' into a mild protest or sympathy. 'Grabe ka naman' = you're too much (teasing or complaining).

examples.tl: Grabe naman, hindi ka man lang nag-text.
examples.en: Come on, you didn't even text.

notes.taglish: Sus, sabi mo di ka na iinom.
notes.notes: Short for 'Hesus'. Dismissive disbelief or 'oh please'. Casual, friends and family. Also 'Susmaryosep' for bigger shock.

examples.tl: Sus, alam ko na yun.
examples.en: Pfft, I already knew that.

notes.taglish: Ikaw na ang pinakagwapo dito. Charot!
notes.notes: From gay lingo, now universal. Tacked after a joke, exaggeration or awkward truth. Slang, casual, fine for all ages in friendly chat.

examples.tl: Bibilhan kita ng kotse. Charot!
examples.en: I'll buy you a car. Just kidding!

notes.taglish: Miss na kita. Char.
notes.notes: Clipped 'charot'. Standard in texts, often lowercase at the end: 'char'. Also 'charing' (older variant). Slang.

examples.tl: Libre mo ako ng dinner. Char, KKB tayo.
examples.en: Treat me to dinner. Jk, we'll split.

notes.taglish: Ako na ang bahala sa bill. Chariz.
notes.notes: Variant of 'char/charot' with extra sass; gay-lingo flavor. Still heard but 'char' is the default in 2026. Slang.

examples.tl: Ang gwapo mo today. Chariz.
examples.en: You look handsome today. Jk.

notes.taglish: Joke lang! Wag kang ma-offend.
notes.notes: Plain, neutral version of 'charot'. 'Biro lang' is the pure Tagalog form, less common in Manila chat.

examples.tl: Joke lang, hindi talaga ako galit.
examples.en: Just kidding, I'm not really mad.

notes.taglish: HAHAHAHA grabe ka, tumahimik ka nga.
notes.notes: Filipinos laugh in text with long 'HAHAHA', caps = funnier. A bare 'haha' reads lukewarm or passive-aggressive; 'hahaha' is the polite minimum.

examples.tl: HAHAHAHA sira ulo ka talaga.
examples.en: Hahaha you're seriously nuts.

notes.taglish: Nakalimutan ko yung wallet ko lol.
notes.notes: Used, but less than 'HAHAHA'. Often marks mild self-deprecation rather than real laughter. Dropping it for 'haha' sounds more local.

examples.tl: Late na naman ako lol.
examples.en: I'm late again lol.

notes.taglish: Basta, sama ka na lang. Wag ka nang magtanong.
notes.notes: Ends an argument or dodges a 'why'. Also 'basta' = 'as long as' ('Basta ikaw' = as long as it's you). Casual, can sound stubborn.

examples.tl: Bakit? -- Basta.
examples.en: Why? -- Just because.

examples.tl: Okay lang kahit saan, basta may aircon.
examples.en: Anywhere is fine, as long as there's AC.

notes.taglish: Ewan, di pa siya nag-reply.
notes.notes: Short for 'ewan ko'. Casual; with a shrug it can mean 'who cares'. 'Hindi ko alam' is the neutral full sentence.

examples.tl: Anong oras siya darating? -- Ewan.
examples.en: What time is he arriving? -- Dunno.

examples.tl: Ewan ko kung open pa sila.
examples.en: I don't know if they're still open.

examples.tl: Saan si Marco? Ewan.
examples.en: Where's Marco? Dunno.

notes.taglish: Ewan ko kung open pa yung store.
notes.notes: Everyday 'I don't know'. 'Ewan ko ba' = beats me. 'Hindi ko alam' is slightly more careful or polite.

examples.tl: Ewan ko kung sino yun.
examples.en: I don't know who that is.

notes.en: I don't know what to do with you.
notes.taglish: Ewan ko sa'yo, late ka na naman.
notes.notes: Exasperated 'whatever, you'. Teasing between friends or scolding from a parent. Casual.

examples.tl: Ewan ko sa'yo, bahala ka na.
examples.en: I give up on you, do what you want.

notes.taglish: Bakit ka tumawag? -- Wala lang, na-miss lang kita.
notes.notes: Answer to 'why?' or 'what?'. Can hide a real reason; 'Wala lang, na-miss lang kita' is a classic.

examples.tl: Anong ginagawa mo? -- Wala lang, nakahiga.
examples.en: What are you doing? -- Nothing, just lying down.

examples.tl: Bakit ka nag-Tagalog bigla? — Wala lang, nagpa-practice.
examples.en: Why did you suddenly speak Tagalog? — Nothing, just practicing.

notes.en: like that / that's how it is
notes.taglish: Ganun talaga sa Manila, traffic lagi.
notes.notes: 'Ganoon' spelled as spoken. 'Ganun talaga' = that's just how it is. 'Ganun ba?' = is that so? 'Ganun?!' = seriously, like that?

examples.tl: Ganun talaga ang buhay.
examples.en: That's just life.

examples.tl: Ganun? Hindi man lang nag-sorry?
examples.en: Like that? Didn't even say sorry?

notes.taglish: Ganyan din yung phone ko, same model.
notes.notes: Refers to something near the listener. 'Ganito' = like this (near me). In practice 'ganyan' and 'ganun' overlap in casual speech.

examples.tl: Wag kang ganyan.
examples.en: Don't be like that.

examples.tl: Ganyan ba talaga siya?
examples.en: Is he really like that?

examples.tl: Huwag kang ganyan.
examples.en: Don't be like that.

notes.en: There it is / so yeah / exactly
notes.taglish: Ayun, nakita ko na yung keys ko sa kotse.
notes.notes: Literally 'that over there'. In speech it wraps up a story ('Ayun, nag-break sila') or means 'exactly'. Very common filler.

examples.tl: Ayun, umuwi na lang ako.
examples.en: So yeah, I just went home.

examples.tl: Ayun oh, nandun si Jeff.
examples.en: There, look, Jeff is over there.

examples.tl: Ayun, o! Yung jeep natin.
examples.en: There! That's our jeep.

notes.taglish: Ayun na! Finally nag-load na yung GCash.
notes.notes: Said when something finally happens or someone gets it right. Casual, encouraging.

examples.tl: Ayun na! Tama ang pronunciation mo.
examples.en: There you go! Your pronunciation is right.

notes.taglish: Ayan, sabi ko sa'yo mag-dala ka ng payong.
notes.notes: Points at something near you or at a result ('Ayan, sabi ko' = see, I told you). Also 'Ayan na!' = here it comes / here it is.

examples.tl: Ayan na yung Grab natin.
examples.en: There's our Grab.

examples.tl: Ayan, nasira na.
examples.en: See, now it's broken.

examples.tl: Ayan, dumating na ang order mo.
examples.en: There, your order has arrived.

notes.taglish: Oo nga, ang mahal na ng kape dito.
notes.notes: Agreement with emphasis. 'Oo nga eh' adds resignation; 'Oo nga no?' = yeah, right? (realizing). Neutral.

examples.tl: Oo nga, kaya di na ako bumili.
examples.en: Yeah true, that's why I didn't buy anymore.

notes.en: Oh right, I forgot / by the way.
notes.taglish: Oo nga pala, may birthday si Ate sa Sabado.
notes.notes: 'Pala' = realization. Use when you suddenly remember something or shift topic. Neutral, very common.

examples.tl: Oo nga pala, nabayaran mo na ba yung kuryente?
examples.en: Oh right, did you pay the electric bill yet?
examples.taglish: Oo nga pala, bayad na ba yung Meralco?

notes.taglish: Ano nga pala yung pangalan ng resto?
notes.notes: Slots after the first word: 'Ano nga pala...', 'Sino nga pala...'. Marks a side note or something you forgot to ask. Neutral.

examples.tl: Saan nga pala tayo magkikita?
examples.en: By the way, where are we meeting?

notes.taglish: Sabi ko nga, mag-Grab na lang tayo.
notes.notes: Emphasizes ('Sabi ko nga' = like I said) or softens a request ('Pakuha nga' = get it for me, would you). 'Di nga?' = no way, really?

examples.tl: Patingin nga.
examples.en: Let me see.

examples.tl: Di nga? Totoo?
examples.en: No way? Really?

examples.tl: Oo nga, ang init talaga.
examples.en: Yeah, right, it really is hot.

notes.taglish: Kaya nga di ako sumama, alam kong mauulanan.
notes.notes: Strong agreement, 'that's exactly my point'. 'Kaya nga eh' adds 'ugh, I know'. Neutral.

examples.tl: Ang mahal! -- Kaya nga.
examples.en: So expensive! -- Exactly.

notes.taglish: Ang sarap dito, di ba?
notes.notes: Tag question seeking agreement; also 'Di ba...' to start a reminder ('Di ba sabi mo...'). Spelled 'diba' in texts. Neutral.

examples.tl: Kaibigan mo siya, di ba?
examples.en: He's your friend, right?

examples.tl: Di ba sabi mo libre mo ako?
examples.en: Didn't you say you'd treat me?

examples.tl: Masarap, di ba?
examples.en: It's delicious, right?

notes.taglish: Ano ba! Bakit mo ni-leave on read?
notes.notes: Annoyed exclamation. 'Ano ba?' with a question tone = what is it / what do you want? Casual; harsh with strangers.

examples.tl: Ano ba, ang ingay niyo!
examples.en: Come on, you're so loud!

notes.en: What is that / ugh, what now
notes.taglish: Ano ba yan, nag-brownout na naman.
notes.notes: Frustration at a situation rather than a person. Casual, safe to mutter anywhere.

examples.tl: Ano ba yan, wala na namang tubig.
examples.en: Ugh, what now, no water again.

notes.taglish: Hay naku, traffic na naman sa Ayala.
notes.notes: Sigh of exasperation or sympathy. 'Hay' = sigh, 'naku' from 'Ina ko' (my mother). Neutral, all ages.

examples.tl: Hay naku, ikaw talaga.
examples.en: Oh my, you really are something.

notes.taglish: Naku, nakalimutan ko yung umbrella ko.
notes.notes: Alarm or sympathy. 'Naku po!' is stronger. Spelled 'nako' in texts. Neutral.

examples.tl: Naku, nahulog yung phone ko.
examples.en: Oh no, I dropped my phone.

notes.taglish: Sayang, sold out na yung size ko.
notes.notes: For missed chances, wasted food or money. 'Nakakasayang' = such a waste. 'Sayang ka' = you're wasted (on this). Neutral.

examples.tl: Sayang, hindi kita nakita sa event.
examples.en: Too bad, I didn't see you at the event.

examples.tl: Sold out na yung tickets. — Sayang! Next time na lang.
examples.en: The tickets are sold out. — Too bad! Maybe next time.

notes.taglish: Buti na lang nag-dala ako ng powerbank.
notes.notes: Relief. 'Buti na lang' + what went right. 'Buti nga' = serves you right (sarcastic). Neutral.

examples.tl: Buti na lang hindi umulan.
examples.en: Good thing it didn't rain.

notes.taglish: Mabuti naman, salamat sa pagtanong.
notes.notes: Textbook reply to 'kumusta'. Real-life Manileños say 'okay lang' or 'ayos lang'; 'mabuti naman' sounds polite or older. Neutral-formal.

examples.tl: Kumusta po kayo? -- Mabuti naman, salamat.
examples.en: How are you, sir? -- I'm well, thanks.

examples.tl: Kumusta ka? Mabuti naman.
examples.en: How are you? I'm good.

examples.tl: Buti na lang may dala akong payong.
examples.en: Good thing I brought an umbrella.

notes.taglish: Syempre, hindi ko ma-miss yung reunion.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'siempre'. Spelled 'syempre' in texts. 'Syempre naman' = well obviously. Neutral.

examples.tl: Sasama ka ba? -- Siyempre!
examples.en: Are you coming along? -- Of course!

examples.tl: Siyempre, sama ako sa kainan.
examples.en: Of course, I'm joining the meal.

examples.tl: Syempre mahal, BGC yun.
examples.en: Of course it's expensive, that's BGC.

notes.taglish: Oo naman, G ako sa Baguio trip.
notes.notes: Warm, emphatic yes. Can carry 'duh' if said flatly. Neutral.

examples.tl: Masarap ba? -- Oo naman!
examples.en: Is it good? -- Of course!

notes.taglish: Hindi naman mahal, 200 lang.
notes.notes: Softened no; 'naman' keeps it polite. 'Hindi naman masyado' = not that much. Neutral.

examples.tl: Galit ka ba? -- Hindi naman.
examples.en: Are you mad? -- Not really.

notes.taglish: Medyo late ako, 10 mins.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'medio'. Softens adjectives: 'medyo busy', 'medyo malayo'. Neutral, very frequent.

examples.tl: Medyo mahal pero masarap.
examples.en: A bit pricey but delicious.

examples.tl: Medyo nahihilo ako.
examples.en: I'm feeling a little dizzy.

examples.tl: Medyo late ako, sorry.
examples.en: I'm a bit late, sorry.

notes.taglish: Sobrang init sa labas, grabe.
notes.notes: 'Sobrang' + adjective = extremely. 'Sobra ka' = you're too much. 'Sobra na' = that's enough. Neutral.

examples.tl: Sobrang sarap!
examples.en: So delicious!

examples.tl: Sobra na yan, tama na.
examples.en: That's too much, that's enough.

examples.tl: Sobrang init ngayon.
examples.en: It's extremely hot today.

notes.taglish: Nakaka-stress yung internet dito sa condo.
notes.notes: Attach to Tagalog or English roots: nakakainis (annoying), nakakatawa (funny), nakaka-stress, nakaka-proud. Neutral, hugely productive.

examples.tl: Nakakainis yung traffic.
examples.en: The traffic is annoying.

examples.tl: Nakakatuwa yung aso mo.
examples.en: Your dog is adorable.

notes.taglish: Ang init! Nasaan yung aircon?
notes.notes: 'Ang' + adjective is the everyday exclamation: 'Ang ganda!', 'Ang sarap!', 'Ang mahal!'. 'Ang cute!' works with English too.

examples.tl: Ang tagal ng Grab!
examples.en: The Grab is taking forever!

examples.tl: Ang ganda ng sunset.
examples.en: The sunset is so beautiful.

notes.taglish: Umulan kaya na-late ako.
notes.notes: 'Kaya' = so/that's why. Also 'kaya ko' = I can handle it, and 'Pupunta kaya siya?' = I wonder if he'll go. Neutral.

examples.tl: Puno yung MRT, kaya nag-Grab ako.
examples.en: The MRT was full, so I took a Grab.

examples.tl: Kaya mo yan!
examples.en: You can do it!

examples.tl: Traffic, kaya na-late ako.
examples.en: There was traffic, so I was late.

notes.en: Can I? / is it okay? / seriously?!
notes.taglish: Pwede ba, isang message lang, ang hirap i-reply?
notes.notes: Literal: may I? Said sharply, it's 'seriously?!' or 'can you not?'. Tone decides. Casual.

examples.tl: Pwede ba akong umupo dito?
examples.en: Can I sit here?

examples.tl: Pwede ba! Tumahimik ka nga.
examples.en: Seriously! Be quiet.

notes.taglish: Pwede, free ako after 6.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'puede'. The 'yes, that's possible' answer. 'Pwede ba?' asks permission. 'Pwede pa' = still possible. Neutral.

examples.tl: Bukas ng gabi? -- Pwede.
examples.en: Tomorrow night? -- That works.

examples.tl: Pwede bang GCash?
examples.en: Can I pay with GCash?

examples.tl: Pwede ka bang mamaya?
examples.en: Are you free later?

notes.taglish: Pwede na yung Tagalog mo, gets ko naman.
notes.notes: 'That'll do' with a shrug; not high praise. Often said of food, work, or someone's attempt. Casual.

examples.tl: Pwede na yung kwarto, malinis naman.
examples.en: The room is good enough, it's clean anyway.

notes.taglish: Okay na yung wifi, nag-restart lang ako ng router.
notes.notes: 'na' = now/already: a problem is resolved or you're ready. 'Okay na ako' = I'm good now. Neutral.

examples.tl: Okay na ba kayo?
examples.en: Are you two okay now?

examples.tl: Okay na, nabayaran ko na.
examples.en: All set, I already paid.

notes.taglish: Tapos na yung meeting, otw na ako.
notes.notes: 'Tapos' = finished; also 'then/after that' as a story connector ('Tapos, umuwi ako'). Neutral.

examples.tl: Tapos na ba kayo kumain?
examples.en: Are you done eating?

examples.tl: Tapos na ang sale.
examples.en: The sale is over.

notes.en: Go ahead / keep going / it's fine
notes.taglish: Sige lang, kaya ko na dito.
notes.notes: Lets someone proceed or reassures them ('sige lang, okay lang'). Also to a driver: 'Sige lang, diretso'. Neutral.

examples.tl: Sige lang, mauna ka na.
examples.en: Go ahead, you go first.

notes.taglish: Go lang, i-apply mo yung job.
notes.notes: English 'go' + 'lang'. Encouragement or 'proceed without me'. Casual slang.

examples.tl: Go lang kayo, susunod ako.
examples.en: You guys go ahead, I'll follow.

notes.taglish: Wala akong review. Bahala na.
notes.notes: Famous Filipino fatalism, from 'Bathala' (God). Joke version: 'Bahala na si Batman'. Casual.

examples.tl: Baka umulan, pero bahala na, tara.
examples.en: It might rain, but whatever, let's go.

notes.taglish: Bahala ka, ikaw naman magbabayad.
notes.notes: Can be neutral ('your choice') or dismissive ('fine, do what you want'). 'Ikaw bahala' is the friendlier version. Casual.

examples.tl: Ayaw mong sumama? Bahala ka.
examples.en: You don't want to come? Suit yourself.

examples.tl: Saan tayo kakain? — Ikaw ang bahala, okay lang sa akin.
examples.en: Where should we eat? — You decide, I'm fine with anything.

notes.taglish: Ikaw bahala kung saan tayo kakain.
notes.notes: Hands the decision over politely. Word order matters: 'Ikaw bahala' is kind, 'Bahala ka' can sound like a brush-off.

examples.tl: Anong oras? -- Ikaw bahala, free ako buong araw.
examples.en: What time? -- Your call, I'm free all day.

notes.taglish: Ikaw na! Ikaw na ang may bagong iPhone.
notes.notes: Mock-conceding: 'you're the one, you win'. Playful envy among friends. 'Ikaw na ang ___' = you're the one with ___. Slang-ish.

examples.tl: Promoted ka? Ikaw na!
examples.en: You got promoted? Look at you!

notes.en: Oh come on, you / your turn
notes.taglish: Ikaw naman, ang sensitive mo.
notes.notes: Mild scolding or teasing ('oh, you'), or literally 'your turn' ('Ikaw naman, kumanta ka'). Casual.

examples.tl: Ikaw naman, joke lang yun.
examples.en: Oh come on, that was just a joke.

examples.tl: Ako na nagbayad kanina, ikaw naman ngayon.
examples.en: I paid earlier, your turn now.

notes.en: You handle it / you take over.
notes.taglish: 'Kaw na bahala sa order, kahit ano basta spicy.
notes.notes: Clipped 'ikaw na ang bahala'. Delegates a task or decision, friendly tone. Casual texting form.

examples.tl: Kaw na bahala sa reservation, ha.
examples.en: You take care of the reservation, okay.

notes.taglish: Na-late ako kasi traffic.
notes.notes: Taglish verb everyone uses; 'nahuli' sounds formal or means 'got caught'. 'Ma-late' = might be late.

examples.tl: Na-late ako sa trabaho kasi may aberya ang MRT.
examples.en: I was late for work because the MRT broke down.
examples.taglish: Na-late ako sa work kasi may aberya ulit ang MRT.

examples.tl: Baka ma-late ako, mauna na kayo.
examples.en: I might be late, go ahead without me.

examples.tl: Na-late ako sa flight ko.
examples.en: I was late for my flight.

notes.taglish: Nag-grocery ako sa Landmark kanina, ang dami ng tao.
notes.notes: Pattern: nag- + English noun/verb = did it (completed); mag- for future. nag-gym, nag-shopping, nag-laundry, nag-work. Neutral Taglish.

examples.tl: Nag-grocery na ako, may ulam na tayo.
examples.en: I already did the groceries, we have food now.

examples.tl: Mag-gro-grocery pa ako mamaya.
examples.en: I still have to do groceries later.

notes.taglish: Mag-meet tayo sa Glorietta, 7 PM.
notes.notes: mag- + English = infinitive/future. 'Nag-meet kami' = we met up. Pure Tagalog 'magkita' is equally common.

examples.tl: Kailan tayo pwedeng mag-meet?
examples.en: When can we meet up?

examples.tl: Nag-meet na kami ng landlord.
examples.en: We already met with the landlord.

notes.taglish: Na-miss kita! Tagal na nating di nagkita.
notes.notes: ma- + English feeling verb. 'Na-miss kita' = I missed you; 'Mami-miss kita' = I'll miss you. Also 'na-miss ko yung flight' = I missed the flight.

examples.tl: Na-miss ko yung sinigang ni Mama.
examples.en: I missed my mom's sinigang.

examples.tl: Mami-miss ka namin dito.
examples.en: We'll miss you here.

notes.taglish: I-send mo sa akin yung pic mamaya.
notes.notes: i- + English verb = object-focus command/infinitive. i-check, i-download, i-book. 'Sinend' or 'na-send' = sent. Neutral Taglish.

examples.tl: I-send mo yung location sa Viber.
examples.en: Send the location on Viber.

examples.tl: Na-send ko na yung GCash.
examples.en: I already sent the GCash.

notes.taglish: I-text mo ako pag andun ka na.
notes.notes: The default 'keep in touch' line. 'Text' covers SMS, Messenger, Viber. 'Pag' = when. Neutral.

examples.tl: I-text mo ako pag nakauwi ka na.
examples.en: Text me when you get home.

examples.tl: I-text mo ako ng address. — Sige, i-send ko yung pin sa Viber.
examples.en: Text me the address. — Okay, I'll send the pin on Viber.

notes.taglish: Paki-send yung address ng resto.
notes.notes: paki- + verb = polite request. Works with English: paki-check, paki-forward, paki-open. Add 'po' for elders or staff. Neutral-polite.

examples.tl: Paki-send po ng screenshot ng payment.
examples.en: Please send a screenshot of the payment.

notes.taglish: Pa-send ng pics kanina, ha.
notes.notes: pa- + verb = 'let me have you do it'. More casual than paki-. pa-check, pa-order, pa-pic (take my photo). Friends and peers.

examples.tl: Pa-send ng link ng Lazada.
examples.en: Send me the Lazada link.

examples.tl: Pa-pic naman.
examples.en: Take a picture of me, would you.

notes.taglish: Otw na ako, 15 mins.
notes.notes: Universal text shorthand. Running joke: 'otw' often means still in the shower. Casual.

examples.tl: Otw na, wait lang.
examples.en: On the way, hold on.

notes.en: Wish we all had that / lucky you
notes.taglish: Nasa Japan ka ulit? Sana all.
notes.notes: 'Sana' (hopefully) + 'all'. Envious but friendly reaction to good news. Spelled 'sanaol' in memes. Slang from 2018, still standard in 2026.

examples.tl: May bonus ka? Sana all.
examples.en: You got a bonus? Must be nice.

notes.taglish: Awit, na-reject yung application ko.
notes.notes: From 'aw, sakit' (ouch, pain); 'awit' also means song. Gen Z slang for anything painful or disappointing. Casual, young crowd.

examples.tl: Awit, wala nang stock.
examples.en: Oof, it's out of stock.

notes.taglish: Lodi! Ikaw na ang nag-top sa exam.
notes.notes: 'Idol' with syllables reversed. Peaked around 2017; dated now, used ironically or by older millennials. Slang.

examples.tl: Lodi ka talaga, salamat sa tulong.
examples.en: You're my idol, thanks for the help.

notes.taglish: Petmalu yung game kagabi!
notes.notes: 'Malupit' (fierce) reversed. Same 2017 wave as 'lodi' and 'werpa'; dated, now jokey. Slang. Say 'grabe' or 'lupet' instead.

examples.tl: Petmalu yung bagong kotse mo.
examples.en: Your new car is sick.

notes.taglish: Werpa sa inyo, mga lodi!
notes.notes: 'Power' reversed, as in 'more power to you'. Dated (2017); mainly ironic now. Slang.

examples.tl: Werpa, idol!
examples.en: More power, idol!

notes.taglish: Shookt ako sa presyo ng kape dito.
notes.notes: From English 'shook'. Big in 2017-2018; dated, used tongue-in-cheek now. Slang. 'Na-shock ako' is the normal phrasing.

examples.tl: Shookt ako nung nag-resign siya.
examples.en: I was shook when he resigned.

notes.taglish: May bagong Macbook ka? Edi wow.
notes.notes: 'Edi' (so then) + 'wow'. Sarcastic shrug at a brag. Peaked mid-2010s but still used casually among friends; a bit dated.

examples.tl: Nag-gym ka araw-araw? Edi wow.
examples.en: You go to the gym every day? Well, good for you.

notes.taglish: Keri pa ba o uwi na tayo?
notes.notes: From English 'carry'. Gay lingo turned mainstream. 'Keri ba?' = can you manage? 'Di keri' = can't handle it. Slang, casual.

examples.tl: Keri mo pa mag-overtime?
examples.en: Can you still manage overtime?

notes.en: It's manageable / I can handle it.
notes.taglish: Keri lang, konting stress lang sa work.
notes.notes: Reply to 'kumusta' or 'kaya mo pa?'. Understated 'I'm coping'. Slang, casual.

examples.tl: Mahirap ba yung Tagalog? -- Keri lang.
examples.en: Is Tagalog hard? -- It's manageable.

notes.taglish: Anong chika? May bago ba?
notes.notes: 'Anong chika?' = what's new/the tea? 'Mag-chika' = to chat/catch up. 'Chika lang' = just talk, no big deal. Casual, very common.

examples.tl: Chika mo naman, anong nangyari?
examples.en: Spill it, what happened?

examples.tl: Wala akong chika, boring ang week ko.
examples.en: I have no news, my week was boring.

notes.taglish: Chikahan tayo mamaya over coffee.
notes.notes: -han makes it a shared activity: a gossip or catch-up session. 'Kwentuhan' is the neutral synonym. Casual.

examples.tl: Ang tagal ng chikahan niyo kagabi.
examples.en: You two chatted forever last night.

notes.taglish: May tsismis ako about sa boss natin.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'chisme'. 'Tsismosa/tsismoso' = gossipy person; 'Marites' is the slang version. Neutral-casual.

examples.tl: Totoo ba yun o tsismis lang?
examples.en: Is that true or just gossip?

notes.taglish: Marites ka talaga, lahat alam mo.
notes.notes: Meme name for a nosy gossip, from 'Mare, anong latest?'. Pandemic-era slang still common in 2026. 'Mag-Marites' = to gossip. Casual, playful.

examples.tl: Anong balita, Marites?
examples.en: What's the news, gossip queen?

notes.taglish: Na-ghost ako after 3 dates. Awit.
notes.notes: English 'ghost' with na-. Dating slang, also for friends or job recruiters who vanish. 'Nang-ghost' = did the ghosting. Casual.

examples.tl: Na-ghost ako ng recruiter, walang update.
examples.en: The recruiter ghosted me, no update.

notes.taglish: Puro ka landi, wala kang jowa.
notes.notes: 'Malandi' = flirty (insulting if serious, teasing among friends). 'Nakikipaglandian' = flirting around. Casual, loaded word.

examples.tl: Tama na ang landi, mag-aral ka.
examples.en: Enough flirting, go study.

notes.taglish: Kinikilig ako sa text niya, grabe.
notes.notes: Romantic giddiness; no English equal. 'Kinikilig ako' = I'm getting butterflies. 'Nakakakilig' = swoon-worthy. Casual, all ages.

examples.tl: Kilig much? Ngiting-ngiti ka.
examples.en: Feeling giddy? You're grinning so much.

notes.taglish: May hugot ka na naman? Sino nanakit sa'yo?
notes.notes: Literally 'to pull out'. A quotable line drawn from personal pain, often a pun. 'Hugot lines'. Casual, 2010s but still alive.

examples.tl: Hugot na naman, ikaw ha.
examples.en: Another feels line, look at you.

notes.taglish: Pak na pak yung outfit mo!
notes.notes: Gay-lingo/showbiz exclamation of approval. 'Pak ganern' is 2016-era and dated; 'pak na pak' survives in drag and queer spaces. Slang.

examples.tl: Pak! Tama yung sagot mo.
examples.en: Boom! Your answer is right.

notes.taglish: Nag-break sila after 8 years. Walang forever talaga.
notes.notes: Mid-2010s heartbreak meme that became a stock joke. Used ironically about anything ending (promos, relationships). Casual.

examples.tl: Tapos na yung sale? Walang forever.
examples.en: The sale is over? Nothing lasts forever.

notes.taglish: Push natin yung Baguio trip sa long weekend.
notes.notes: English 'push' meaning 'go through with it'. 'Push ba?' = are we still on? 'Hindi na push' = cancelled. Casual slang.

examples.tl: Push ba yung dinner bukas?
examples.en: Is dinner tomorrow still on?

notes.taglish: Approved yung leave ko. Lezgo, Palawan!
notes.notes: Playful spelling of 'let's go', hype or excitement. Text slang, young crowd. 'Tara' is the Tagalog equal.

examples.tl: Payday na. Lezgo, kain tayo sa labas!
examples.en: It's payday. Let's go, let's eat out!

notes.taglish: Hala, nakalimutan ko i-send yung report!
notes.notes: Surprise or alarm. 'Hala ka' = uh oh, you're in trouble. Neutral, all ages, said constantly.

examples.tl: Hala, umuulan na.
examples.en: Oh no, it's raining already.

notes.taglish: Yun oh! Nakuha mo na yung license!
notes.notes: Cheer for a win or a correct answer; 'oh' here is a pointing word, not surprise. Casual slang.

examples.tl: Yun oh! Tama ang Tagalog mo.
examples.en: There you go! Your Tagalog is right.

notes.taglish: Bet ko yung Korean place sa Poblacion.
notes.notes: English 'bet' meaning 'I like / I'm into'. 'Bet ko siya' = I like him. 'Bet!' = deal, I'm down. Slang, Gen Z and millennials.

examples.tl: Bet mo ba yung plano?
examples.en: Are you into the plan?

notes.taglish: Kita tayo sa Sabado, coffee lang.
notes.notes: Clipped 'magkita tayo'. 'Kita tayo soon' is a common sign-off that may or may not happen. Neutral.

examples.tl: Kita tayo bukas sa office.
examples.en: Let's meet tomorrow at the office.

notes.en: Where to? / where are we meeting?
notes.taglish: Saan tayo? BGC o Makati?
notes.notes: Standard planning question. 'San' in texts. 'Saan tayo kakain?' = where will we eat? Neutral.

examples.tl: Saan tayo magkikita?
examples.en: Where are we meeting?

notes.taglish: Anong plano mamaya? Inom o movie?
notes.notes: 'Ano ang plano' contracted. 'Anong plano mo sa weekend?' = weekend plans? Neutral.

examples.tl: Anong plano niyo sa Sunday?
examples.en: What's your plan for Sunday?

notes.taglish: Gala tayo sa BGC after work.
notes.notes: Aimless going out: malls, food, drives. 'Gala tayo' = let's go out. 'Lakwatsa' is the older synonym. Casual.

examples.tl: Tara gala, boring sa bahay.
examples.en: Let's go out, it's boring at home.

examples.tl: Saan ka naggala kahapon?
examples.en: Where'd you wander off to yesterday?

notes.taglish: May lakad ako bukas, pass muna ako.
notes.notes: Literally 'walk', but 'may lakad ako' = I have plans/something to do. The polite way to decline. Neutral.

examples.tl: May lakad ka ba sa Sabado?
examples.en: Do you have plans on Saturday?

notes.taglish: Libre kita ng kape, birthday ko eh.
notes.notes: 'Libre' = free/treat. 'Sagot ko' (my responsibility) also means 'on me'. Birthday celebrant treats others, not the reverse.

examples.tl: Libre kita ng lunch bukas.
examples.en: I'll treat you to lunch tomorrow.

examples.tl: Magkano hati natin? — Wala, libre kita. Birthday ko kahapon.
examples.en: How much is my share? — Nothing, my treat. It was my birthday yesterday.

notes.taglish: Promoted ka? Libre mo ako!
notes.notes: Playful demand after someone's good news ('blowout'). Casual; only with friends.

examples.tl: Libre mo ako, ikaw naman ang may pera.
examples.en: Treat me, you're the one with money.

accept: split the bill; everyone pays their own
notes.taglish: KKB tayo ha, wala akong budget for libre.
notes.notes: 'Kanya-kanyang bayad' = each pays their own. Say it upfront to avoid awkwardness. Neutral, standard.

examples.tl: KKB ba o may nagli-libre?
examples.en: Are we splitting or is someone treating?

examples.tl: KKB tayo ha, walang libre.
examples.en: We each pay our own, okay? Nobody's treating.

examples.tl: Hati tayo sa bill, 350 each.
examples.en: Let's split the bill, 350 each.
examples.taglish: Hati tayo sa bill, 350 each, GCash mo sa akin.

notes.taglish: Mag-ambag tayo ng 200 each for the gift.
notes.notes: Group money for food, gifts, or drinks. 'Walang ambag' = freeloader (also a meme insult for useless people). Neutral.

examples.tl: Magkano ang ambag para sa inuman?
examples.en: How much is the chip-in for the drinks?

examples.tl: Ambag tayo para sa gift ni boss, 200 each.
examples.en: Let's chip in for the boss's gift, 200 each.

notes.taglish: Chip-in tayo sa Grab, 50 each.
notes.notes: English with mag-. Same as 'mag-ambag'. 'Nag-chip-in kami' = we pooled money. Casual Taglish.

examples.tl: Mag-chip-in tayo para sa cake ni Tita.
examples.en: Let's chip in for Tita's cake.

notes.taglish: Wait lang, kinukuha ko yung wallet ko.
notes.notes: English 'wait' + 'lang'. Most common form in Manila. 'Teka' (from 'hintay ka') and 'sandali' are the Tagalog versions. Neutral.

examples.tl: Wait lang, ha, tatawagan ko siya.
examples.en: Hold on, I'll call him.

notes.taglish: Sandali lang, nag-lo-load pa yung GCash.
notes.notes: Slightly more polite than 'wait lang'; 'sandali lang po' to staff or elders. 'Saglit' = a sec. 'Teka' = casual hold up.

examples.tl: Sandali lang po, kukunin ko yung sukli.
examples.en: Just a moment, I'll get the change.

examples.tl: Sandali, hindi ko pa nakikita ang message mo.
examples.en: Hold on, I haven't seen your message yet.

notes.taglish: Andito na ako sa lobby, saan ka?
notes.notes: 'Nandito' is the full form; 'andito' is how it's said. 'Nandito na kami' = we're here. Neutral.

examples.tl: Andito na ako sa labas ng building.
examples.en: I'm here outside the building.

notes.taglish: Malapit na ako, nasa Ayala na yung Grab.
notes.notes: 'Malapit' = near. Sincerity varies as much as with 'otw'. Neutral.

examples.tl: Malapit na ako, 5 minutes.
examples.en: I'm almost there, 5 minutes.

notes.taglish: Papunta na ako, nag-book na ng Grab.
notes.notes: From 'punta' (to go to). 'Papunta na ako dun' = heading there now. Same job as 'otw'. Neutral.

examples.tl: Papunta na kami, umorder na kayo.
examples.en: We're on our way, go ahead and order.

notes.taglish: 5 mins! Promise, nasa Grab na ako.
notes.notes: The universal text ETA, understood to mean 15-30. Filipino time humor. Casual.

examples.tl: 5 mins na lang, wait lang.
examples.en: Just 5 more minutes, hold on.

notes.taglish: Nasaan ka? Andito na kami sa resto.
notes.notes: Full form. 'Nasan ka' or 'san ka' in texts. 'Nasaan ka na?' adds impatience. Neutral.

examples.tl: Nasaan ka ngayon?
examples.en: Where are you right now?

notes.taglish: San ka? Order na ba kami?
notes.notes: Clipped 'nasaan ka'. Pure texting form among friends. Can also mean 'where are you going' depending on context.

examples.tl: San ka? Tagal mo.
examples.en: Where are you? You're taking forever.

notes.taglish: San ka na? Start na yung movie.
notes.notes: 'na' = already/now, so it implies you're waiting. Casual text.

examples.tl: San ka na? Nag-order na kami.
examples.en: Where are you now? We've already ordered.

notes.taglish: Ang tagal mo! 30 mins na kaming nag-aantay.
notes.notes: 'Tagal' = length of time. Greeting for a late friend. 'Tagal mo mag-reply' = you take forever to reply. Casual.

examples.tl: Ang tagal mo, nasaan ka ba?
examples.en: You took forever, where were you?

notes.taglish: Sorry, traffic eh. Grabe sa EDSA.
notes.notes: The default Metro Manila excuse for lateness, always accepted. 'Na-traffic ako' = I got stuck in traffic. Casual.

examples.tl: Late ako, traffic eh.
examples.en: I'm late, there was traffic.

notes.taglish: Gutom na ako, saan tayo kakain?
notes.notes: 'Gutom' used as 'hungry' directly in speech; 'nagugutom' is the fuller verb. 'na' = now. Neutral.

examples.tl: Gutom na ako, kain na tayo.
examples.en: I'm hungry, let's eat now.

examples.tl: Gutom na ako. — Ako rin, kain tayo sa labas.
examples.en: I'm hungry. — Me too, let's eat out.

notes.taglish: Kain tayo sa Jollibee, tapos gala.
notes.notes: Everyday invitation using the bare root 'kain'. 'Kain tayo!' is also a polite thing to say when you have food in front of others.

examples.tl: Kain tayo mamaya after work.
examples.en: Let's eat later after work.

notes.taglish: Inom tayo Friday, Poblacion. G?
notes.notes: Bare root 'inom' = drink (alcohol implied). 'Tara inom' = let's go drink. 'Inuman' = a drinking session. Casual.

examples.tl: Inom tayo mamaya, payday ko.
examples.en: Let's drink later, it's my payday.

notes.taglish: Pahinga muna, ang tagal nating naglakad sa Ayala.
notes.notes: 'Muna' = first/for now. Suggestion or self-care sign-off ('Pahinga muna ako'). Neutral.

examples.tl: Pahinga ka muna, pagod ka na.
examples.en: Rest first, you're tired.

notes.taglish: Antok na ako, tulog na ako. Goodnight!
notes.notes: 'Antok' = sleepiness, used directly like an adjective. 'Inaantok' is the full verb. Common chat sign-off. Neutral.

examples.tl: Antok na ako, bukas na lang ulit.
examples.en: I'm sleepy, let's continue tomorrow.

notes.taglish: Uwi na ako, may 7 AM call pa ako.
notes.notes: Root 'uwi' = go home. 'Pauwi na ako' = on my way home. 'Umuwi ka na' = go home now. Neutral.

examples.tl: Uwi na ako, ingat kayo.
examples.en: I'm heading home, take care everyone.

examples.tl: Uwi na ako, late na. — Sige, text mo ako pag nakauwi ka.
examples.en: I'm heading home, it's late. — Okay, text me when you get home.

notes.taglish: Tulog na ako, gn! Chat tayo bukas.
notes.notes: Bare root form, standard chat sign-off. 'Matulog ka na' = go to sleep. Neutral.

examples.tl: Tulog na ako, goodnight.
examples.en: Going to sleep now, goodnight.

notes.taglish: Goodnight! Ingat sa biyahe bukas.
notes.notes: Said in English. 'Magandang gabi' means 'good evening' (a greeting), not 'goodnight'. Texts: 'gn', 'gnyt'. Neutral.

examples.tl: Goodnight, tulog ka na.
examples.en: Goodnight, go to sleep.

notes.taglish: Ingat sa biyahe! Text mo ako pag naka-land ka.
notes.notes: For any trip: a Grab home, a flight, a drive to the province. 'Byahe' in texts. Neutral.

examples.tl: Ingat sa biyahe, malakas ang ulan.
examples.en: Travel safe, the rain is heavy.

notes.taglish: Balitaan mo ako kung push yung trip.
notes.notes: 'Balita' = news. Friendly way to end a plan-in-progress. 'I-update mo ako' is the Taglish version. Neutral.

examples.tl: Balitaan mo ako pag may update sa visa.
examples.en: Keep me posted when there's an update on the visa.

notes.taglish: Anong balita sa'yo? Nag-move na ba kayo?
notes.notes: Opener after a while apart. 'Anong balita sa'yo' = what's new with you. Neutral.

examples.tl: Anong balita? Kumusta ang bagong work?
examples.en: What's new? How's the new job?

notes.taglish: Pasensya na, na-late ako. Traffic eh.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'paciencia': literally 'have patience'. The everyday Tagalog sorry for small faults. Add 'po' for elders, 'ha' for warmth.

examples.tl: Pasensya na, hindi ko nakita yung message mo.
examples.en: Sorry, I didn't see your message.

examples.tl: Pasensya na, na-late ako. — Okay lang, kakadating ko lang din.
examples.en: Sorry about that, I was late. — It's fine, I just got here too.

notes.taglish: Sorry ha, di kita natext kagabi, nakatulog ako.
notes.notes: English 'sorry' plus the 'ha' tag that makes it gentle and sincere. 'Sorry na' = come on, I said sorry. Casual.

examples.tl: Sorry ha, na-miss ko yung call mo.
examples.en: Sorry, I missed your call.

notes.taglish: Pasensya na po, late po ako nag-reply.
notes.notes: 'Po' adds respect; use with elders, staff, guards, officials, strangers. 'Sorry po' is also very common. Polite-neutral.

examples.tl: Pasensya na po, hindi ko po alam.
examples.en: I'm sorry, I didn't know.

notes.taglish: Excuse me po, pwede makiraan?
notes.notes: Used as-is in English; 'excuse me po' is the polite form. Also 'excuse' alone to squeeze past someone. Neutral.

examples.tl: Excuse me po, saan po yung CR?
examples.en: Excuse me, where's the restroom?

notes.taglish: Makikiraan po, lalabas lang ako.
notes.notes: From 'daan' (path) with maki- (may I join in). Said on jeeps, crowded sidewalks, elevators. 'Padaan po' is the shorter version. Polite.

examples.tl: Makikiraan po, bababa na ako.
examples.en: Excuse me, I'm getting off.

notes.taglish: Nobody texts 'paumanhin'; it's 'sorry ha' or 'pasensya na'.
notes.notes: Formal, written Tagalog: announcements, news, speeches ('Paumanhin sa abala'). In conversation it sounds stiff. Learn to recognize, not to say.

examples.tl: Paumanhin po sa abala.
examples.en: We apologize for the inconvenience.

notes.taglish: Salamat sa kape! Libre ko next time.
notes.notes: 'Salamat po' to anyone older or serving you. 'Maraming salamat' = thanks a lot. 'Thank you' in English is equally normal.

examples.tl: Salamat sa tulong, ha.
examples.en: Thanks for the help.

examples.tl: Salamat po, kuya.
examples.en: Thank you, sir (driver/staff).

notes.taglish: Thank you ha, ang bait mo talaga.
notes.notes: English thanks plus 'ha' for sincerity. The most common thanks among friends in Manila. Casual-warm.

examples.tl: Thank you ha, nakakahiya.
examples.en: Thanks a lot, I feel bad making you do that.

notes.taglish: Salamat ulit sa kanina! Kita-kits.
notes.notes: 'Ulit' = again. Good closing line after someone did you a favor. Neutral.

examples.tl: Salamat ulit sa pagsundo.
examples.en: Thanks again for picking me up.

notes.taglish: Walang anuman! Anytime.
notes.notes: Textbook 'you're welcome'. Slightly formal; Manileños usually say 'wala yun', 'okay lang', or 'no problem'. Neutral-formal.

examples.tl: Salamat po. -- Walang anuman.
examples.en: Thank you. -- You're welcome.

examples.tl: Salamat sa tulong! — Walang anuman, kahit kailan.
examples.en: Thanks for the help! — You're welcome, anytime.

notes.taglish: Wala yun, bro. Anytime.
notes.notes: Everyday 'you're welcome' or 'no big deal' after an apology. Casual, warm.

examples.tl: Salamat sa pag-abot. -- Wala yun.
examples.en: Thanks for handing it over. -- It's nothing.

notes.taglish: Salamat po, kuya. Dito na lang po.
notes.notes: Add to any sentence for respect: elders, staff, guards, officials, strangers. 'Opo' = polite yes. 'Ho' is a softer regional variant. Skip with close friends.

examples.tl: Magkano po ito?
examples.en: How much is this, please?

examples.tl: Opo, nandito na po ako.
examples.en: Yes sir, I'm here now.

examples.tl: Salamat po.
examples.en: Thank you (polite).

notes.taglish: Pasok ka, upo ka, kuha ka ng tubig.
notes.notes: Hospitality line at the door. 'Tuloy po kayo' is the classic polite version for guests. Neutral.

examples.tl: Pasok ka, wag kang mahiya.
examples.en: Come in, don't be shy.

notes.taglish: Upo ka muna, pakuha lang ako ng tubig.
notes.notes: Bare-root command, friendly. 'Maupo po kayo' to guests or elders. Neutral.

examples.tl: Upo ka dito, may space pa.
examples.en: Sit here, there's still space.

notes.taglish: Kain ka, may leftover pizza sa ref.
notes.notes: Offered whenever food is around; often polite ritual, not a demand. Polite decline: 'Salamat, busog pa ako.' Accepting is also fine.

examples.tl: Kain ka, marami pa.
examples.en: Have some, there's plenty.

notes.taglish: Kain na! Nandito na yung delivery.
notes.notes: Called out when food is served. 'Kain na tayo' = let's eat now. Neutral, family and friends.

examples.tl: Kain na, lumalamig yung ulam.
examples.en: Eat now, the food is getting cold.

notes.notes: Drinking water is delivered in 5-gallon 'galon' refills.

examples.tl: Walang tubig sa buong building ngayon.
examples.en: There's no water in the whole building right now.

examples.tl: Pabili ng tubig, isang galon.
examples.en: Please buy water, one gallon.

examples.tl: Tubig? Malamig ito.
examples.en: Water? This one's cold.

notes.taglish: Tubig? O gusto mo ng Coke?
Sorry, hindi ko maintindihan. Pakiulit?
notes.notes: From Spanish 'entender'. Neutral and polite. 'Di ko gets' is the casual version.

examples.tl: Hindi ko maintindihan, ang bilis mo magsalita.
examples.en: I don't understand, you talk too fast.

examples.tl: Hindi ko maintindihan, pakiulit. — Ah, sorry. In English: turn left.
examples.en: I don't understand, please repeat. — Oh, sorry. In English: turn left.

notes.taglish: Ulit? Di ko narinig, maingay yung jeep.
notes.notes: One word asks for a repeat. 'Ano ulit?' = what was that again? 'Ulit' also = 'again' in general ('Salamat ulit'). Casual.

examples.tl: Ano ulit yung pangalan niya?
examples.en: What was his name again?

examples.tl: Pakisabi ulit?
examples.en: Could you say that again?

examples.tl: Balik tayo dito ulit.
examples.en: Let's come back here again.

notes.taglish: Pakiulit po, ang bilis niyo magsalita.
notes.notes: paki- + ulit. Polite and useful for learners. Add 'po' for strangers. Neutral-polite.

examples.tl: Pakiulit po, hindi ko nakuha.
examples.en: Please repeat that, I didn't catch it.

notes.taglish: Ano yun? Bagong slang ba?
notes.notes: 'Yun' = that (far). Asks about a thing, a word, or a noise. 'Ano yan?' = what's that (near you)? Neutral.

examples.tl: Ano yun? Di ko alam yung word na yun.
examples.en: What's that? I don't know that word.

notes.taglish: Ibig sabihin, cancelled na yung meeting?
notes.notes: Literally 'wants to say'. Starts a clarification: 'Ibig sabihin, ...' = so that means... People also just say 'meaning'. Neutral.

examples.tl: Ibig sabihin, hindi ka sasama?
examples.en: So that means you're not coming?

notes.taglish: Ano ibig sabihin ng 'sana all'?
notes.notes: Your core learner question. 'Anong meaning ng ___?' is the Taglish version everyone uses. Neutral.

examples.tl: Ano ibig sabihin ng 'charot'?
examples.en: What does 'charot' mean?

notes.en: How do you say ___ in Tagalog?
accept: How do you say in Tagalog
notes.taglish: Paano sabihin sa Tagalog ang 'receipt'?
notes.notes: Shorter everyday form: 'Anong Tagalog ng ___?' Neutral. Expect the answer to often be the English word itself.

examples.tl: Ano sa Tagalog ang 'elevator'?
examples.en: What's 'elevator' in Tagalog?

notes.taglish: Marunong ka mag-Tagalog? Konti lang? Okay lang yun.
notes.notes: 'Marunong' = knows how. The question you'll be asked constantly. Answer: 'Konti lang' or 'Nag-aaral pa ako'. Neutral.

examples.tl: Marunong ka pala mag-Tagalog!
examples.en: Oh, you know Tagalog!

notes.taglish: Konti lang, pero nag-aaral ako. Bagal-bagalan mo lang.
notes.notes: 'Kaunti' is the standard spelling; 'konti' is how it's said. Also for portions: 'Konti lang, busog pa ako.' Neutral.

examples.tl: Marunong ka mag-Tagalog? -- Konti lang.
examples.en: Do you know Tagalog? -- Just a little.

notes.taglish: Nag-aaral ako ng Tagalog, so pasensya na sa grammar ko.
notes.notes: Add 'pa' (still) for 'I'm still learning'. People will respond warmly and switch to slow Tagalog or English. Neutral.

examples.tl: Nag-aaral pa ako ng Tagalog, pakicorrect ako.
examples.en: I'm still learning Tagalog, please correct me.

examples.tl: Marunong ka mag-Tagalog? — Nag-aaral pa ako ng Tagalog. Konti lang.
examples.en: Can you speak Tagalog? — I'm still learning Tagalog. Just a little.

notes.taglish: Bagal-bagalan mo, nag-aaral pa ako.
notes.notes: Reduplication of 'bagal' (slow) softens the request: 'slow-ish'. 'Bagalan mo' alone is a bit blunt. Casual-polite.

examples.tl: Bagal-bagalan mo lang magsalita, please.
examples.en: Just speak a little slower, please.

notes.taglish: Dahan-dahan lang, kuya, may bata.
notes.notes: Works for speech ('speak slowly'), driving ('go slow, driver'), or handling things gently. Neutral, very common.

examples.tl: Dahan-dahan lang po, kuya, madulas.
examples.en: Slowly please, driver, it's slippery.

examples.tl: Dahan-dahan, di kita masundan.
examples.en: Slowly, I can't follow you.

notes.taglish: 'Kumain na ako,' tama ba?
notes.notes: Check your own sentence or someone's claim. 'Tama?' alone is fine. 'Tama!' as a reply = correct. Neutral.

examples.tl: Sa Monday yung meeting, tama ba?
examples.en: The meeting is on Monday, is that right?

notes.taglish: Mali yung sinend mo, ibang address yun.
notes.notes: 'Mali ako' = I was wrong. 'Nagkamali ako' = I made a mistake. 'Mali-mali' = all wrong. Neutral, direct.

examples.tl: Mali yung spelling, pero gets ko.
examples.en: The spelling is wrong, but I get it.

examples.tl: Mali yung address na binigay ko sa Grab.
examples.en: The address I gave to Grab was wrong.

examples.tl: Mali ka, Linggo ang flight, hindi Sabado.
examples.en: You're wrong, the flight is Sunday, not Saturday.

notes.taglish: Ayos! Approved na yung leave ko.
notes.notes: Approval or 'all set'. 'Ayos ba?' = is it okay/does it work? 'Ayos na' = fixed/done. Casual-neutral.

examples.tl: Ayos yung pronunciation mo.
examples.en: Your pronunciation is good.

examples.tl: Ayos ba yung kwarto?
examples.en: Is the room okay?

examples.tl: Ayos lang, walang problema.
examples.en: It's fine, no problem.

notes.taglish: Mag-left ka sa Jupiter tapos diretso. Gets?
notes.notes: From English 'get'. Standard casual check for understanding. 'Gets ko' = I get it. Slang but universal, even in offices.

examples.tl: Ganun yung rule. Gets mo?
examples.en: That's the rule. You get it?

notes.taglish: Ah, gets ko. So 'po' for elders lang.
notes.notes: 'Gets ko na' = now I get it. 'Na-gets ko' = I got it (completed). Casual, friendly.

examples.tl: Gets ko na, salamat sa paliwanag.
examples.en: I get it now, thanks for explaining.

notes.taglish: Di ko gets yung joke, explain mo.
notes.notes: Casual version of 'hindi ko maintindihan'. Works for words, jokes, directions, people's behavior. Casual.

examples.tl: Di ko gets, bakit cancelled?
examples.en: I don't get it, why is it cancelled?

notes.taglish: Dalawang kanto tapos kanan. Kuha mo?
notes.notes: 'Kuha' = get/catch. Slightly more Tagalog than 'gets?' but same job. Also literal: 'Kuha mo na?' = did you get (fetch) it? Casual.

examples.tl: Kuha mo yung sinabi niya?
examples.en: Did you catch what he said?

notes.taglish: Nakuha ko. So mag-'po' ako sa guard.
notes.notes: 'Nakuha ko na' = I've got it now. 'Hindi ko nakuha' = I didn't catch that. Neutral.

examples.tl: Nakuha ko, salamat. Ulit na lang pag nalito ako.
examples.en: Got it, thanks. I'll just ask again if I get confused.

notes.taglish: Sorry, pwede English? Di ko pa gets yung Tagalog.
notes.notes: Polite bailout when you're lost; nearly everyone in Makati will switch. Add 'po' with strangers. Neutral.

examples.tl: Pwede po English? Nag-aaral pa ako ng Tagalog.
examples.en: Can we use English? I'm still learning Tagalog.

notes.en: Like I said / told you so.
notes.taglish: Sabi ko nga, mag-Grab tayo. Ayan, late tayo.
notes.notes: 'Sabi ko na nga ba' = I knew it / I told you so (smug). 'Sabi ko sa'yo' = I told you. Casual.

examples.tl: Sabi ko nga, masarap dito.
examples.en: Like I said, the food here is good.

notes.taglish: Teka, sino yung nag-text sa'yo?
notes.notes: From 'hintay ka' (you wait). Also 'wait, what?' when something surprises you ('Teka, seryoso?'). Casual, very common.

examples.tl: Teka, nasaan yung susi ko?
examples.en: Wait, where are my keys?

examples.tl: Teka lang, kakausapin ko muna si Ate.
examples.en: Hold on, I'll talk to Ate first.

notes.taglish: Kaya mo yan! Isang interview lang yun.
notes.notes: 'Kaya' here = able. Standard encouragement for exams, workouts, breakups. 'Laban lang' (keep fighting) is the gritty version. Neutral.

examples.tl: Kaya mo yan, nag-aral ka naman.
examples.en: You can do it, you studied anyway.

notes.taglish: Wag na, okay lang, ako na lang magbabayad.
notes.notes: 'Huwag' (don't) clipped to 'wag'. 'Wag na lang' = forget it, never mind. 'Wag kang ganun' = don't be like that. Casual-neutral.

examples.tl: Wag na, nakakahiya.
examples.en: Don't bother, I'd feel bad.

examples.tl: Wag na lang, bukas na natin gawin.
examples.en: Never mind, let's do it tomorrow.

notes.taglish: Okay ka lang? Ang tahimik mo today.
notes.notes: Caring check-in. Answer 'okay lang' or 'medyo' (kind of). 'Okay ka lang ba?' adds concern. Neutral.

examples.tl: Okay ka lang? Parang pagod ka.
examples.en: You okay? You seem tired.

notes.en: Keep dreaming / don't count on it.
notes.taglish: Libre mo ako? Asa ka pa, KKB tayo.
notes.notes: From 'umasa' (to hope). Sarcastic shutdown. 'Asa!' alone is sharper. Casual, friends only.

examples.tl: Magigising siya ng 6 AM? Asa ka pa.
examples.en: He'll wake up at 6 AM? Keep dreaming.

notes.taglish: Saka na yung movie, tired ako today.
notes.notes: 'Saka' (then/later) + 'na'. Postpones politely. 'Saka na lang' = let's just do it some other time. Casual-neutral.

examples.tl: Saka na natin pag-usapan.
examples.en: Let's talk about it later.

notes.notes: ANG-form (subject/topic) of 'I'. Set: ako (ang) / ko (ng) / akin (sa). Comes after the predicate: 'Pagod ako.'

examples.tl: Pagod na ako.
examples.en: I'm tired already.
examples.taglish: Pagod na ako, grabe ang traffic.

examples.tl: Ako ang magbabayad.
examples.en: I'll be the one to pay.

notes.notes: NG-form of 'I': possessor ('kotse ko' = my car) or actor of an object-focus verb ('Binili ko' = I bought it). Never starts a sentence.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang phone ko?
examples.en: Where's my phone?

examples.tl: Binili ko na ang tiket.
examples.en: I already bought the ticket.

notes.taglish: sa akin / sa'kin
notes.notes: SA-form of 'I'. 'sa akin' = to/for me; 'akin ito' = this is mine. Often said 'sa'kin'.

examples.tl: Ibigay mo sa akin.
examples.en: Give it to me.
examples.taglish: Send mo sa'kin yung link.

examples.tl: Akin na lang yan.
examples.en: I'll just take that.

notes.notes: ANG-form of 'you' used at the START of a sentence or standing alone; after the predicate use 'ka'. Set: ikaw/ka (ang) / mo (ng) / iyo (sa).

examples.tl: Ikaw ang bahala.
examples.en: It's up to you.

examples.tl: Ikaw? Kumain ka na?
examples.en: You? Have you eaten?

notes.notes: Enclitic ANG-form of 'you'; goes right after the first word of the predicate: 'Saan ka?' 'Okay ka lang?' Use 'ikaw' at sentence start.

examples.tl: Saan ka ngayon?
examples.en: Where are you now?

examples.tl: Okay ka lang ba?
examples.en: Are you okay?

notes.notes: NG-form of 'you': 'bag mo' = your bag; 'Kinain mo?' = Did you eat it? Also softens commands: 'Buksan mo.'

examples.tl: Ano ang pangalan mo?
examples.en: What's your name?

examples.tl: Nakita mo ba yung susi?
examples.en: Did you see the key?

notes.taglish: sa'yo
notes.notes: SA-form of 'you'. Almost always 'sa iyo', pronounced and texted 'sa'yo'. 'Iyo na' = it's yours now.

examples.tl: Para sa iyo ito.
examples.en: This is for you.
examples.taglish: Para sa'yo to.

examples.tl: Sa iyo ba ang jacket na ito?
examples.en: Is this jacket yours?

notes.notes: ANG-form; gender-neutral (he or she). Set: siya (ang) / niya (ng) / kanya (sa). Texted 'sya'. Not used for things ('it' is ito/iyon or dropped).

examples.tl: Nasa office pa siya.
examples.en: He/she is still at the office.

examples.tl: Siya ang kapatid ko.
examples.en: That's my sibling.

notes.en: his / her / by him or her
notes.notes: NG-form of siya: 'bahay niya' = his/her house; 'Sinabi niya' = he/she said. Texted 'nya'.

examples.tl: Sinabi niya na late siya.
examples.en: He/she said they'll be late.

examples.tl: Ito ang number niya.
examples.en: This is his/her number.

notes.en: his / hers / to him or her
notes.notes: SA-form of siya; usually 'sa kanya'. 'Kanya ito' = this is his/hers. Formal spelling 'kaniya'.

examples.tl: Ibinigay ko sa kanya ang resibo.
examples.en: I gave him/her the receipt.

examples.tl: Kanya yung puting kotse.
examples.en: The white car is his/hers.

notes.notes: EXCLUSIVE 'we' = me and others, NOT the listener. Set: kami / namin / amin. Compare tayo (includes you).

examples.tl: Pupunta kami sa BGC mamaya.
examples.en: We're going to BGC later.

examples.tl: Kami na ang bahala.
examples.en: We'll take care of it.

notes.notes: NG-form of kami (exclusive). 'condo namin' = our condo (not yours). 'Kinain namin' = we ate it.

examples.tl: Malapit lang ang condo namin.
examples.en: Our condo is just nearby.

examples.tl: Inorder namin lahat ng ulam.
examples.en: We ordered all the dishes.

notes.notes: SA-form of kami. 'sa amin' also means 'at our place/hometown': 'Sa amin, walang traffic.'

examples.tl: Pumunta ka sa amin sa Sabado.
examples.en: Come to our place on Saturday.

examples.tl: Sa amin sa probinsya, mas mura ang isda.
examples.en: Back home in the province, fish is cheaper.

notes.notes: INCLUSIVE 'we' = me + you. After a verb root it means 'let's': 'Kain tayo!' Set: tayo / natin / atin.

examples.tl: Kain tayo sa labas mamaya.
examples.en: Let's eat out later.

examples.tl: Tayo ang susunod.
examples.en: We're next.

notes.notes: NG-form of tayo (inclusive). 'Order natin' = let's order it. 'bayan natin' = our country (yours and mine).

examples.tl: Ano ang order natin?
examples.en: What are we ordering?

examples.tl: Hatiin natin ang bill.
examples.en: Let's split the bill.

notes.notes: SA-form of tayo. 'sa atin' = to us / here in our place (incl. you): 'Mahal ang gas sa atin.'

examples.tl: Para sa atin lahat ito.
examples.en: This is for all of us.

examples.tl: Sa atin sa Pilipinas, lagi may rice.
examples.en: Here in the Philippines, there's always rice.

notes.notes: ANG-form plural 'you'. Also POLITE singular to elders/strangers: 'Saan po kayo?' Set: kayo / ninyo / inyo.

examples.tl: Kumain na ba kayo?
examples.en: Have you (all) eaten?

examples.tl: Saan po kayo galing?
examples.en: Where did you come from, sir/ma'am?

notes.notes: NG-form of kayo; spoken/texted 'niyo' or 'nyo'. Also polite singular: 'Ano po ang order niyo?'

examples.tl: Ano po ang order ninyo?
examples.en: What's your order, sir/ma'am?
examples.taglish: Ano po order nyo?

examples.tl: Nakita niyo ba si Marco?
examples.en: Did you guys see Marco?

notes.notes: SA-form of kayo. 'sa inyo' = to you all / at your place. Polite: 'Para sa inyo po.'

examples.tl: Pupunta kami sa inyo sa Linggo.
examples.en: We'll come to your place on Sunday.

examples.tl: Sa inyo na lang yung natira.
examples.en: You guys just keep the leftovers.

notes.notes: ANG-form 'they'. Set: sila / nila / kanila. Also polite singular in some contexts ('sila' for a respected person).

examples.tl: Nasa Tagaytay sila ngayon.
examples.en: They're in Tagaytay now.

examples.tl: Sila ang nag-invite sa akin.
examples.en: They were the ones who invited me.

notes.notes: NG-form of sila. 'bahay nila' = their house; 'Ginawa nila' = they did it. Also used for 'X and company': 'kina/sila Ana'.

examples.tl: Malaki ang bahay nila.
examples.en: Their house is big.

examples.tl: Kinansel nila ang flight.
examples.en: They cancelled the flight.

notes.notes: SA-form of sila; usually 'sa kanila' = to them / at their place.

examples.tl: Sabihin mo sa kanila na late ako.
examples.en: Tell them I'm late.

examples.tl: Kakain kami sa kanila mamaya.
examples.en: We'll eat at their place later.

notes.notes: Replaces 'ko ikaw' (I = actor, you = object) in one word: 'Mahal kita' = I love you. 'Tawagan kita' = I'll call you.

examples.tl: Mahal kita.
examples.en: I love you.

examples.tl: Susunduin kita sa mall.
examples.en: I'll pick you up at the mall.
examples.taglish: Susunduin kita sa Glorietta, wait ka lang.

notes.notes: Demonstrative, near the speaker. Spoken/texted 'to': 'Ano to?' NG-form: nito. Location: dito.

examples.tl: Magkano ito?
examples.en: How much is this?
examples.taglish: Magkano to, ate?

examples.tl: Ito ang bahay namin.
examples.en: This is our house.

notes.notes: Demonstrative, near the LISTENER. Almost always spoken 'yan'. NG-form: niyan. Location: diyan.

examples.tl: Ano yan?
examples.en: What's that (you have)?

examples.tl: Akin na yan.
examples.en: Give me that.

notes.notes: Demonstrative, far from both. Spoken 'yun'. Linked form 'yung' (iyong) works like 'the': 'yung bag ko'. NG-form: niyon/noon. Location: doon.

examples.tl: Sino yun?
examples.en: Who's that?

examples.tl: Kunin mo yung bag ko.
examples.en: Get my bag (that bag of mine).

notes.notes: Location near speaker. 'Dito lang' = just here. 'Taga-dito' = from here. Spelling 'rito' after a vowel is formal.

examples.tl: Dito lang ako sa condo.
examples.en: I'm just here at the condo.

examples.tl: Para dito, kuya!
examples.en: Stop here, driver!

examples.tl: Dito ka bumaba, malapit na ang mall.
examples.en: Get off here, the mall is close.
examples.taglish: Dito ka bumaba, tapos tawid ka, nandoon ang mall.

notes.taglish: Dito ka lang, wait mo ako.

notes.notes: Location near listener. Texted 'dyan' or 'jan'. 'Nandiyan' = it's there with you. 'Diyan lang' = right there.

examples.tl: Ilagay mo diyan sa mesa.
examples.en: Put it there on the table.

examples.tl: Nandiyan ba si Mama?
examples.en: Is Mom there (with you)?

examples.tl: Diyan ka lang, papunta na ako.
examples.en: Stay right there, I'm on my way.
examples.taglish: Dyan ka lang, papunta na ako, 5 mins.

notes.taglish: Diyan ka lang, susunduin kita.

notes.notes: Location far from both. Spoken 'dun'. 'Nandoon/nandun' = it's over there. 'Doon tayo kumain.'

examples.tl: Doon tayo kumain sa Poblacion.
examples.en: Let's eat over there in Poblacion.

examples.tl: Nandun ba yung ATM?
examples.en: Is the ATM over there?

examples.tl: Doon ang sakayan, sa may overpass.
examples.en: The loading area is over there, by the footbridge.
examples.taglish: Dun yung sakayan, sa may overpass, tawid ka lang.

notes.taglish: Doon tayo sumakay, sa kabila.

notes.notes: 'In this manner'. Often opens an explanation: 'Ganito kasi...' = Here's the thing...

examples.tl: Ganito kasi, na-cancel ang flight ko.
examples.en: Here's the thing, my flight got cancelled.

examples.tl: Ganito ang gawin mo.
examples.en: Do it like this.

notes.notes: Spoken 'ganun'. 'Ganun ba?' = Oh, is that so? 'Ganun talaga' = that's life. Very common reaction word.

examples.tl: Ganun ba? Hindi ko alam yun.
examples.en: Is that so? I didn't know that.

examples.tl: Ganun talaga, wala tayong magagawa.
examples.en: That's just how it is, nothing we can do.

notes.notes: NG-form of ito: 'presyo nito' = the price of this. Also 'recently': 'kamakailan lang nito'.

examples.tl: Magkano ang presyo nito?
examples.en: How much is the price of this?

examples.tl: Ano ang gamit nito?
examples.en: What's this used for?

notes.notes: NG-form of iyan. 'Ano ang lasa niyan?' = What does that taste like? Spoken 'nyan'.

examples.tl: Masarap ba ang lasa niyan?
examples.en: Does that taste good?

examples.tl: Bigyan mo ako niyan.
examples.en: Give me some of that.

notes.notes: NG-form of iyon, but mostly used as 'back then / at that time'. 'Noong' before a time word: 'noong Lunes' = last Monday.

examples.tl: Noon, mura pa ang pamasahe.
examples.en: Back then, fares were still cheap.

examples.tl: Umuwi ako noong Linggo.
examples.en: I went home last Sunday.

examples.tl: Noong bata ako, walang Grab, jeep lang.
examples.en: When I was a kid, there was no Grab, just jeeps.

notes.notes: Presentative 'here (is)'. Spoken 'eto'. 'Eto na' = here it comes / here you go. 'Eto, o' when handing something over.

examples.tl: Heto ang sukli mo.
examples.en: Here's your change.
examples.taglish: Eto, o. Sukli mo.

examples.tl: Eto na ang Grab natin.
examples.en: Here comes our Grab.

notes.notes: 'Sino siya?' Plural form 'sino-sino'. NG form: 'nino' (rare); SA form: 'kanino'.

examples.tl: Sino ang kasama mo?
examples.en: Who are you with?

examples.tl: Sino yung tumawag?
examples.en: Who was the one who called?

examples.tl: Sino 'yan? Kilala mo?
examples.en: Who's that? Do you know them?

notes.notes: 'Where' with verbs: 'Saan ka pupunta?' For 'where IS something', use 'nasaan'. 'Taga-saan ka?' = Where are you from?

examples.tl: Saan ka pupunta?
examples.en: Where are you going?

examples.tl: Saan tayo kakain?
examples.en: Where shall we eat?

examples.tl: Saan ang sakayan ng bus papuntang Pasay?
examples.en: Where do you catch the bus to Pasay?

notes.taglish: Saan ka? Otw na ako.

notes.notes: 'Where is (a thing/person)?' Answer with nasa / nandito / nandiyan / nandoon. Casual 'Asan?'

examples.tl: Nasaan ang susi?
examples.en: Where's the key?
examples.taglish: Asan yung charger ko?

examples.tl: Nasaan ka na?
examples.en: Where are you now?

examples.tl: Nasaan ang CR?
examples.en: Where's the restroom?
examples.taglish: Nasaan ang CR? Sa 2nd floor ba?

notes.taglish: Nasaan ka na? 10 minutes na ako dito.

notes.notes: Spoken 'kelan'. 'Kailan ka uuwi?' Future or past. 'Kailan pa?' = since when?

examples.tl: Kailan ang flight mo?
examples.en: When is your flight?

examples.tl: Kelan ka babalik sa Manila?
examples.en: When are you coming back to Manila?

examples.tl: Kailan ang flight mo pabalik ng States?
examples.en: When is your flight back to the States?

notes.notes: Answer usually starts with 'Kasi...'. 'Bakit naman?' = But why? 'Bakit hindi?' = Why not?

examples.tl: Bakit ka late?
examples.en: Why are you late?

examples.tl: Bakit naman wala siya?
examples.en: Why isn't he/she here?

notes.notes: Spoken 'pano'. 'Paano pumunta sa...' = How to get to... 'Paano kung...' = What if...

examples.tl: Paano pumunta sa Ayala mula dito?
examples.en: How do I get to Ayala from here?

examples.tl: Paano kung umulan?
examples.en: What if it rains?

notes.notes: 'Ilan kayo?' = How many are you? Also 'a few': 'ilang araw' = a few days. Linker: 'ilang'.

examples.tl: Ilan kayo?
examples.en: How many are you (in the group)?

examples.tl: Ilang oras ang byahe?
examples.en: How many hours is the trip?

examples.tl: Ilan kayo? Para ma-reserve ko ang table.
examples.en: How many of you? So I can reserve the table.

notes.notes: Only for prices. For amount/degree use 'gaano'. 'Magkano lahat?' = How much in total?

examples.tl: Magkano ang isang kilo ng mangga?
examples.en: How much is a kilo of mangoes?

examples.tl: Magkano lahat, ate?
examples.en: How much for everything, miss?

examples.tl: Magkano po ang sinigang?
examples.en: How much is the sinigang?

notes.notes: 'Alin ang gusto mo?' = Which do you want? Plural 'alin-alin'.

examples.tl: Alin ang mas mura?
examples.en: Which one is cheaper?

examples.tl: Alin dito ang sa'yo?
examples.en: Which of these is yours?

notes.notes: SA-form of sino. 'Kanino ito?' = Whose is this? 'Kay' + name answers it: 'Kay Ana.'

examples.tl: Kanino itong bag?
examples.en: Whose bag is this?

examples.tl: Kanino mo ibinigay?
examples.en: To whom did you give it?

notes.notes: Degree question used with ka- adjectives: 'Gaano kalayo?' = How far? 'Gaano katagal?' = How long?

examples.tl: Gaano kalayo ang airport mula dito?
examples.en: How far is the airport from here?

examples.tl: Gaano katagal ang byahe?
examples.en: How long is the trip?

notes.notes: Marks the sentence topic/subject (ANG-phrase). 'Masarap ang adobo.' Also for exclamations: 'Ang ganda!' = So pretty!

examples.tl: Masarap ang adobo dito.
examples.en: The adobo here is delicious.

examples.tl: Ang mahal ng Grab ngayon!
examples.en: Grab is so expensive right now!

notes.notes: Pronounced 'nang'. Marks possessor ('bahay ng kaibigan ko') or indefinite object ('Bumili ako ng tubig'). Not the same as 'nang' (adverb linker).

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng kape.
examples.en: I bought (some) coffee.

examples.tl: Ito ang bahay ng kaibigan ko.
examples.en: This is my friend's house.

notes.notes: All-purpose location/direction marker; also future time ('sa Lunes' = on Monday) and definite object with some verbs.

examples.tl: Nasa trabaho ako hanggang 6.
examples.en: I'm at work until 6.

examples.tl: Pupunta ako sa Makati sa Lunes.
examples.en: I'm going to Makati on Monday.

notes.notes: ANG-marker for personal names: 'Si Ana ang boss.' Plural 'sina' (Ana and others). Set: si / ni / kay.

examples.tl: Nandito na si Kuya.
examples.en: Big brother is here now.

examples.tl: Si Lloyd ang bisita namin.
examples.en: Lloyd is our guest.

notes.notes: NG-marker for names: 'kotse ni Ana' = Ana's car; 'Binili ni Ana' = Ana bought it. Plural 'nina'.

examples.tl: Ito ang bahay ni Tita.
examples.en: This is Auntie's house.

examples.tl: Niluto ni Mama ang sinigang.
examples.en: Mom cooked the sinigang.

notes.notes: SA-marker for names: 'Ibigay mo kay Ana' = Give it to Ana. 'kay Ana' also = at Ana's. Plural 'kina'.

examples.tl: Ibigay mo ito kay Marco.
examples.en: Give this to Marco.

examples.tl: Para kay Lola ang cake.
examples.en: The cake is for Grandma.

notes.notes: Pronounced 'manga'. Pluralizes nouns: 'mga tao' = people. Before numbers/times = 'around': 'mga alas-7' = about 7.

examples.tl: Marami ang mga tao sa mall.
examples.en: There are a lot of people at the mall.

examples.tl: Dadating ako mga alas-8.
examples.en: I'll arrive around 8.

notes.notes: Joins modifier + noun. After a vowel/n: -ng ('malaking bahay'); after a consonant: 'na' ('masarap na ulam'). Not the 'na' meaning 'already'.
