examples.tl: Masarap na ulam at malamig na beer.
examples.en: Tasty food and cold beer.

examples.tl: Yung lalaking nakaputi ang driver.
examples.en: The man in white is the driver.

notes.notes: Lets the topic come first: 'Ako ay pagod' = I am tired. Formal/written; speech prefers 'Pagod ako'. Also an exclamation 'Ay!' = Oh!

examples.tl: Ang Pilipinas ay may mahigit 7,000 isla.
examples.en: The Philippines has over 7,000 islands.

examples.tl: Ay! Nakalimutan ko ang wallet ko.
examples.en: Oh! I forgot my wallet.

notes.en: is at / is in / is on
notes.notes: na + sa = 'is located at'. 'Nasa bahay ako' = I'm at home. Answers 'Nasaan?'. With names: 'nakay' (rare).

examples.tl: Nasa bahay lang ako buong araw.
examples.en: I was just at home all day.

examples.tl: Nasa mesa ang susi.
examples.en: The key is on the table.

notes.notes: Plural of si: 'sina Ana at Marco' = Ana and Marco; 'sina Ana' alone = Ana and her group. NG: nina. SA: kina.

examples.tl: Dumating na sina Ana at Marco.
examples.en: Ana and Marco have arrived.

examples.tl: Kasama ko sina Tita.
examples.en: I'm with Auntie and them.

notes.notes: Plural of kay. 'kina Ana' = at Ana's place / to Ana and company. Very common for 'at X's house'.

examples.tl: Pupunta kami kina Ana mamaya.
examples.en: We're going to Ana's place later.

examples.tl: Ibigay mo kina Marco ang susi.
examples.en: Give the key to Marco and them.

notes.notes: Enclitic: change of state ('Tapos na' = done already). With commands = 'now/go ahead': 'Kain na.' Opposite of 'pa'.

examples.tl: Kumain na ako.
examples.en: I've already eaten.

examples.tl: Tara na, late na tayo.
examples.en: Let's go now, we're already late.

notes.notes: Enclitic: ongoing state ('Nasa office pa siya'), 'not yet' with hindi/wala ('Hindi pa'), or 'more' ('isa pa' = one more).

examples.tl: Hindi pa ako kumakain.
examples.en: I haven't eaten yet.

examples.tl: Isa pa po, kuya.
examples.en: One more please, boss.

notes.notes: Turns a statement into a yes/no question. Goes after the first word or after short pronouns: 'Okay ka ba?' 'Tapos na ba?'

examples.tl: Pupunta ka ba sa party?
examples.en: Are you going to the party?

examples.tl: May GCash ba kayo dito?
examples.en: Do you accept GCash here?

notes.notes: Reports what someone else said: 'Late daw siya' = He says he'll be late. 'raw' after vowels in careful speech; 'daw' is fine casually.

examples.tl: Uulan daw mamaya.
examples.en: They say it'll rain later.

examples.tl: Cancelled daw ang meeting.
examples.en: The meeting is cancelled, apparently.

notes.notes: 'Ako din' = me too. 'rin' after vowels in careful speech ('ako rin'); casual speech uses 'din' everywhere.

examples.tl: Gusto ko din ng kape.
examples.en: I want coffee too.

examples.tl: Taga-Makati din ako.
examples.en: I'm also from Makati.

notes.notes: Softener and limiter: 'Dito lang' = just here; 'Okay lang' = it's fine; 'Isa lang' = only one. Formal: lamang.

examples.tl: Okay lang ako.
examples.en: I'm fine (just okay).

examples.tl: Tubig lang po.
examples.en: Just water, please.

notes.notes: Surprise/realization: 'Ikaw pala!' = Oh, it's you! 'Oo nga pala' = Oh, by the way / that reminds me.

examples.tl: Ikaw pala yun!
examples.en: Oh, that was you!

examples.tl: Oo nga pala, may meeting tayo bukas.
examples.en: Oh right, by the way, we have a meeting tomorrow.

notes.notes: 'Do X first / for the time being': 'Sandali muna' = just a moment. 'Dito muna ako' = I'll stay here for now.

examples.tl: Kain muna tayo bago umalis.
examples.en: Let's eat first before leaving.

examples.tl: Teka muna, kukuha lang ako ng wallet.
examples.en: Wait a sec, I'll just get my wallet.

examples.tl: Kain muna tayo bago mag-meeting.
examples.en: Let's eat first before the meeting.

notes.notes: Uncertainty: 'Wala yata siya' = I think he's not here. Weaker than 'siguro'. Common in texts.

examples.tl: Closed na yata ang bangko.
examples.en: I think the bank is closed already.

examples.tl: Nakalimutan ko yata ang susi.
examples.en: I think I forgot the key.

notes.notes: In questions = speculation: 'Uulan kaya?' = I wonder if it'll rain. Different from kaya 'so' (conj) and kaya 'can' (stress on first syllable).

examples.tl: Sino kaya yun?
examples.en: I wonder who that is.

examples.tl: Open pa kaya ang 7-Eleven?
examples.en: Do you think 7-Eleven is still open?

notes.notes: Hope or unrealized wish: 'Sana okay ka' = hope you're okay; 'Pupunta sana ako' = I was going to go (but didn't). 'Sana all' = wish that were me.

examples.tl: Sana hindi umulan bukas.
examples.en: Hopefully it won't rain tomorrow.

examples.tl: Pupunta sana ako, kaso may trabaho.
examples.en: I would have gone, but I have work.

notes.notes: Polite 'oo'. Use with elders, officials, guards, staff. 'Hindi po' for polite no.

examples.tl: Opo, kakain na po ako.
examples.en: Yes, I'm about to eat (polite).

examples.tl: Opo, ako po si Lloyd.
examples.en: Yes, I'm Lloyd (polite).

examples.tl: Opo, kumain na po ako.
examples.en: Yes, I've already eaten.

notes.notes: Enclitic marking a consequence (often unwanted): 'Na-late tuloy ako' = So I ended up late. Also the verb 'to continue/go on' ('Tuloy ang party').

examples.tl: Traffic, na-late tuloy ako sa meeting.
examples.en: Traffic, so I ended up late for the meeting.

examples.tl: Tuloy pa ba ang lakad bukas?
examples.en: Is the plan tomorrow still on?

notes.notes: 'Kahit ano man' = anything at all; 'Wala man lang' = not even one; 'Mahal man, masarap' = even if pricey, it's good.

examples.tl: Wala man lang pasalubong?
examples.en: Not even a little gift for me?

examples.tl: Mahal man, sulit naman.
examples.en: Even if it's expensive, it's worth it.

notes.notes: Sentence-final 'e' adds mild excuse or reluctance: 'Wala akong pera e' = I don't have money, you see. Sentence-initial 'E, ano ngayon?' = So what?

examples.tl: Hindi ako makakapunta e, may trabaho.
examples.en: I can't come, you see, I've got work.

examples.tl: E di ikaw na ang magaling.
examples.en: Well then, you're the smart one (sarcastic).

notes.notes: 'kanin at ulam' = rice and dish. In speech, lists often use 'tapos' or 'saka' instead. Contracts to 't after vowels (formal).

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng kanin at ulam.
examples.en: I bought rice and a dish.

examples.tl: Si Ana at si Marco ang kasama ko.
examples.en: Ana and Marco are with me.

notes.notes: The everyday 'but' (Spanish loan). 'Kaso' = 'but the problem is'. Formal 'ngunit/subalit' only in writing.

examples.tl: Gusto ko, pero mahal.
examples.en: I like it, but it's expensive.

examples.tl: Pupunta ako pero late ako.
examples.en: I'll come but I'll be late.

notes.notes: 'But' with a catch or obstacle: 'Gusto ko sana, kaso wala akong pera.' Very common in casual speech.

examples.tl: Masarap dun, kaso malayo.
examples.en: The food there is good, but it's far.

examples.tl: Sasama ako, kaso may shift ako.
examples.en: I'd join, but I have a shift.

notes.notes: Slightly more formal than kasi. 'dahil sa' + noun = because of: 'dahil sa ulan'. 'Dahil' + clause: 'dahil umulan'.

examples.tl: Na-cancel ang flight dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: The flight was cancelled because of the typhoon.

examples.tl: Umuwi siya dahil may sakit siya.
examples.en: He/she went home because he/she was sick.

notes.notes: Conditions and indirect questions: 'Kung gusto mo' = if you want; 'Hindi ko alam kung saan' = I don't know where. 'Kung ako sa'yo' = if I were you.

examples.tl: Kung libre ka, kain tayo.
examples.en: If you're free, let's eat.

examples.tl: Hindi ko alam kung open pa sila.
examples.en: I don't know if they're still open.

notes.notes: For future or habitual 'when': 'Kapag umulan, baha.' Spoken 'pag'. Past 'when' uses 'noong' instead.

examples.tl: Kapag umulan, baha sa Espana.
examples.en: When it rains, Espana floods.

examples.tl: Text mo ako pag nandito ka na.
examples.en: Text me when you're here.

examples.tl: Pag umuulan, baha sa Taft.
examples.en: When it rains, Taft floods.

notes.en: for / so that / in order to
notes.notes: 'para sa' + noun = for; 'para' + verb = in order to. Also 'Para!' = stop (to a jeep/bus driver). 'parang' = like/seems.

examples.tl: Para sa'yo ito.
examples.en: This is for you.

examples.tl: Umaga ako umalis para hindi ma-traffic.
examples.en: I left in the morning so I wouldn't hit traffic.

notes.notes: Storytelling connector: 'Kumain kami, tapos nag-mall.' As adj = finished ('Tapos na'). 'Tapos?' = And then what?

examples.tl: Nag-gym ako, tapos kumain sa Poblacion.
examples.en: I went to the gym, then ate in Poblacion.

examples.tl: Tapos na ba ang meeting?
examples.en: Is the meeting over?

examples.tl: Nag-gym ako, tapos kumain, tapos natulog.
examples.en: I went to the gym, then ate, then slept.

notes.notes: 'Kape o tsaa?' Also an attention marker at sentence end: 'Eto, o!' = Here, look!

examples.tl: Grab o jeep tayo?
examples.en: Shall we take a Grab or a jeep?

examples.tl: Cash o GCash po?
examples.en: Cash or GCash?

notes.notes: 'Habang naghihintay' = while waiting. 'Habang buhay' = for life. 'Habang maaga' = while it's early.

examples.tl: Kumain ako habang naghihintay ng Grab.
examples.en: I ate while waiting for the Grab.

examples.tl: Umuwi na tayo habang maaga pa.
examples.en: Let's go home while it's still early.

examples.tl: Kain muna tayo habang naghihintay ng Grab.
examples.en: Let's eat first while waiting for the Grab.

notes.notes: As conjunction: 'bago umalis' = before leaving. Same word as adjective 'new'. Not 'noon/dati' (before = in the past).

examples.tl: Tumawag ka muna bago ka pumunta.
examples.en: Call first before you go.

examples.tl: Kain muna bago mag-gym.
examples.en: Eat first before the gym.

examples.tl: Tawagan mo ako bago ka umalis.
examples.en: Call me before you leave.

notes.notes: 'pagkatapos ng trabaho' = after work; 'pagkatapos kumain' = after eating. Casual speech often just uses 'tapos'.

examples.tl: Pagkatapos ng trabaho, gym ako.
examples.en: After work, I go to the gym.

examples.tl: Umuwi kami pagkatapos kumain.
examples.en: We went home after eating.

examples.tl: Pagkatapos ng trabaho, gym muna ako.
examples.en: After work, I hit the gym first.

notes.notes: 'Kahit umulan' = even if it rains. 'Kahit ano' = anything; 'kahit saan' = anywhere; 'kahit sino' = anyone.

examples.tl: Pupunta ako kahit umulan.
examples.en: I'll go even if it rains.

examples.tl: Kahit ano, okay lang sa akin.
examples.en: Anything is fine with me.

notes.notes: Spoken 'tsaka'. Adds an item or a next step: 'Isang kape, tsaka tubig.' 'Saka na' = later / some other time.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng tinapay, tsaka itlog.
examples.en: Buy bread, and also eggs.

examples.tl: Saka na natin pag-usapan.
examples.en: Let's talk about it some other time.

notes.notes: Time or place: 'hanggang bukas' = until tomorrow; 'hanggang Cubao' = as far as Cubao. 'Hanggang dito lang' = this is as far as it goes.

examples.tl: Nasa office ako hanggang alas-6.
examples.en: I'm at the office until 6.

examples.tl: Hanggang Ayala lang ang jeep na ito.
examples.en: This jeep only goes as far as Ayala.

examples.tl: Hanggang alas-diyes lang bukas ang 7-Eleven? Hindi, 24 hours 'yon.
examples.en: Is 7-Eleven only open until ten? No, it's 24 hours.

notes.notes: After a negative: 'Hindi si Ana kundi si Marco' = not Ana but Marco. 'Walang iba kundi' = none other than.

examples.tl: Hindi ako kundi siya ang nagluto.
examples.en: It wasn't me but him/her who cooked.

examples.tl: Wala akong magagawa kundi maghintay.
examples.en: I have nothing to do but wait.

notes.notes: Comparison: 'mas mura kesa sa Grab' = cheaper than Grab. Standard spelling 'kaysa'; spoken 'kesa'.

examples.tl: Mas mabilis ang MRT kesa sa bus.
examples.en: The MRT is faster than the bus.

examples.tl: Mas gusto ko ang sinigang kesa adobo.
examples.en: I prefer sinigang over adobo.

notes.notes: Existential, directly before a noun: 'May tao' = there's someone; 'May pera ako' = I have money. Before pronouns/adverbs use 'mayroon'.

examples.tl: May ATM ba dito?
examples.en: Is there an ATM here?

examples.tl: May meeting ako mamaya.
examples.en: I have a meeting later.

notes.notes: Spoken 'meron'. Used when a pronoun/particle follows ('Meron akong...') or alone as the answer 'Yes, there is.' 'Meron pa?' = Any more?

examples.tl: May tubig pa? Meron.
examples.en: Is there water left? There is.

examples.tl: Meron akong extra na charger.
examples.en: I have an extra charger.

notes.en: none / there is no / not have
notes.notes: Negative existential: 'Wala akong pera' = I have no money; 'Wala siya' = he's not here. Linker: 'walang tao'. 'Wala lang' = nothing, never mind.

examples.tl: Wala akong load.
examples.en: I don't have any phone credit.

examples.tl: Wala pa yung Grab.
examples.en: The Grab isn't here yet.

notes.notes: 'Ngayon' = right now or today. 'ngayong gabi' = tonight; 'ngayong araw' = today. Contrast with 'na' (already/now).

examples.tl: Busy ako ngayon.
examples.en: I'm busy right now.

examples.tl: May lakad ka ba ngayong gabi?
examples.en: Do you have plans tonight?

examples.tl: Busy ako ngayon, mamaya na lang.
examples.en: I'm busy now, maybe later.

notes.notes: Earlier the same day. 'Kanina lang' = just now. 'Kanina pa' = for a while already (been waiting).

examples.tl: Kumain na ako kanina.
examples.en: I already ate earlier.

examples.tl: Kanina pa ako naghihintay dito.
examples.en: I've been waiting here for a while.

examples.tl: Kumain na ako kanina, salamat.
examples.en: I already ate earlier, thanks.

notes.notes: Later the same day. 'mamayang gabi' = tonight (later). 'Mamaya na' = later, not now. For a later day use 'sa susunod'.

examples.tl: Tawagan kita mamaya.
examples.en: I'll call you later.

examples.tl: Mamaya na ako kakain.
examples.en: I'll eat later.

examples.tl: Mamaya na ako mag-reply, nasa meeting ako.
examples.en: I'll reply later, I'm in a meeting.

notes.notes: Stress on first syllable. 'Bukás' (last syllable) = open. 'Bukas ng umaga' = tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: May pasok ka ba bukas?
examples.en: Do you have work/school tomorrow?

examples.tl: Bukas na lang tayo mag-usap.
examples.en: Let's just talk tomorrow.

examples.tl: Bukas na lang natin tapusin, pagod na ako.
examples.en: Let's just finish it tomorrow, I'm tired.

notes.notes: 'Kahapon ng gabi' or 'kagabi' = last night. 'Noong isang araw' = the other day.

examples.tl: Umulan nang malakas kahapon.
examples.en: It rained hard yesterday.

examples.tl: Nakita ko siya kahapon sa Greenbelt.
examples.en: I saw him/her yesterday at Greenbelt.

examples.tl: Nag-Grab ako kahapon kasi umuulan.
examples.en: I took a Grab yesterday because it was raining.

notes.notes: ka- + gabi. Same pattern: 'kaninang umaga' = this morning (earlier).

examples.tl: Late ako natulog kagabi.
examples.en: I slept late last night.

examples.tl: Umuwi ka ba kagabi?
examples.en: Did you go home last night?

examples.tl: Ang lakas ng ulan kagabi, hindi ako nakatulog.
examples.en: The rain was so loud last night, I couldn't sleep.

notes.notes: 'Lagi' and 'palagi' are interchangeable; 'lagi' is shorter and more common in speech. Linker: 'laging late'.

examples.tl: Lagi siyang late.
examples.en: He/she is always late.

examples.tl: Lagi may traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: There's always traffic on EDSA.

examples.tl: Lagi na lang may traffic sa EDSA pag Biyernes.
examples.en: There's always traffic on EDSA on Fridays.

notes.notes: Same meaning as lagi, slightly more emphatic. 'Palaging' before a word it modifies.

examples.tl: Palagi akong nag-gym sa umaga.
examples.en: I always go to the gym in the morning.

examples.tl: Palaging puno ang MRT.
examples.en: The MRT is always full.

notes.notes: 'Minsan' = sometimes; 'minsan lang' = just once / rarely; 'paminsan-minsan' = once in a while.

examples.tl: Minsan nagje-jeep ako, minsan Grab.
examples.en: Sometimes I take a jeep, sometimes Grab.

examples.tl: Minsan lang ako uminom.
examples.en: I only drink once in a while.

examples.tl: Minsan nag-jeep ako, minsan nag-Grab, depende sa ulan.
examples.en: Sometimes I take the jeep, sometimes Grab, depending on the rain.

notes.notes: 'Madalas akong...' = I often... 'Kadalasan' = usually/most of the time.

examples.tl: Madalas akong kumain sa Poblacion.
examples.en: I often eat in Poblacion.

examples.tl: Madalas ba umulan dito sa Hunyo?
examples.en: Does it often rain here in June?

examples.tl: Madalas akong mag-order sa Grab Food pag weekend.
examples.en: I often order on Grab Food on weekends.

notes.notes: 'Bihira lang' = only rarely. Opposite of madalas.

examples.tl: Bihira na akong mag-jeep.
examples.en: I rarely take the jeep anymore.

examples.tl: Bihira lang siyang umuwi sa probinsya.
examples.en: He/she seldom goes home to the province.

examples.tl: Bihira akong magluto, mas madalas take-out.
examples.en: I rarely cook, more often take-out.

notes.notes: Reduplication = 'every': 'gabi-gabi' = every night, 'linggo-linggo' = every week, 'buwan-buwan' = monthly.

examples.tl: Araw-araw akong nag-gym.
examples.en: I go to the gym every day.

examples.tl: Araw-araw may traffic sa Makati.
examples.en: Every day there's traffic in Makati.

examples.tl: Araw-araw akong nag-jogging sa Ayala Triangle.
examples.en: I jog at Ayala Triangle every day.

notes.notes: Enclitic-like, after the verb: 'Umuwi agad' = went home right away. 'Agad-agad' = immediately (emphatic).

examples.tl: Umuwi ako agad pagkatapos ng shift.
examples.en: I went home right after my shift.

examples.tl: Reply ka agad, ha?
examples.en: Reply right away, okay?

examples.tl: Nag-reply siya agad, buti pa siya.
examples.en: She replied right away, good for her.

notes.notes: 'Biglang umulan' = it suddenly rained. 'Bigla-bigla' = out of nowhere. Linker -ng: 'biglang'.

examples.tl: Biglang umulan kanina.
examples.en: It suddenly rained earlier.

examples.tl: Bigla siyang umalis.
examples.en: He/she suddenly left.

examples.tl: Biglang umulan kanina, maaraw pa kanina-kanina lang.
examples.en: It suddenly rained earlier, it was sunny just a moment before.

notes.notes: 'Masyadong mahal' = too expensive. 'Hindi masyado' = not that much. 'Masyado ka naman' = you're too much!

examples.tl: Masyadong malayo ang Antipolo.
examples.en: Antipolo is too far.

examples.tl: Hindi masyadong maanghang.
examples.en: Not too spicy.

examples.tl: Masyadong maaga ang alas-singko, alas-sais na lang.
examples.en: Five is too early, let's make it six instead.

notes.notes: 'Halos lahat' = almost everyone/everything; 'halos araw-araw' = almost daily. Casual alternative: 'muntik' (almost did something).

examples.tl: Halos lahat ng tindahan sarado ngayon.
examples.en: Almost all the shops are closed today.

examples.tl: Halos isang oras ang byahe.
examples.en: The trip is almost an hour.

examples.tl: Halos araw-araw umuulan sa Agosto.
examples.en: It rains almost every day in August.

notes.notes: Possibility, often worried: 'Baka umulan' = it might rain. Also 'baka' = cow (stress 'báka'). 'Baka naman' = maybe, hopefully.

examples.tl: Baka late ako, traffic kasi.
examples.en: I might be late, because of traffic.

examples.tl: Baka wala na siya sa office.
examples.en: He/she might not be at the office anymore.

notes.notes: More confident than 'baka'. 'Siguro nga' = I suppose so. 'Oo siguro' = yeah, probably. From Spanish seguro.

examples.tl: Siguro mga alas-7 ako dadating.
examples.en: I'll probably arrive around 7.

examples.tl: Siguro sarado na sila ngayon.
examples.en: They're probably closed by now.

notes.notes: Casual yes (two syllables: o-o). Polite: 'opo'. 'Oo nga' = yeah, right. 'Oo naman' = of course.

examples.tl: Oo, pupunta ako.
examples.en: Yes, I'm going.

examples.tl: Oo naman, sama ako.
examples.en: Of course, I'm coming along.

notes.notes: Negates verbs/adjectives: 'Hindi masarap.' Casual 'di'. Use 'wala' for 'none/not have'. Polite 'hindi po'.

examples.tl: Hindi ako pupunta bukas.
examples.en: I'm not going tomorrow.

examples.tl: Hindi mahal, mura lang.
examples.en: Not expensive, just cheap.

notes.notes: Negative command. Spoken 'wag'. 'Huwag na' = no need / don't bother. 'Wag kang...' = don't you...

examples.tl: Huwag mo akong tawagan mamaya.
examples.en: Don't call me later.

examples.tl: Wag na, okay lang.
examples.en: No need, it's fine.

notes.notes: Opposite of gusto. Takes ng/ko: 'Ayaw ko' = I don't want to; 'Ayaw ko ng gulay' = I don't like vegetables. 'Ayaw ko na' = I quit.

examples.tl: Ayaw ko ng maanghang.
examples.en: I don't like spicy food.

examples.tl: Ayaw niyang sumama.
examples.en: He/she doesn't want to come along.

examples.tl: Ayaw ng tatay niya sa akin.
examples.en: Her dad doesn't like me.

notes.notes: Pseudo-verb with ng-pronouns: 'Gusto ko' = I want/like; 'Gusto mo ba?' = Do you want? 'Gusto kita' = I like you.

examples.tl: Gusto ko ng kape.
examples.en: I want some coffee.

examples.tl: Gusto mo bang sumama sa Tagaytay?
examples.en: Do you want to come to Tagaytay?

examples.tl: Gusto ko ang mga kaibigan mo, mababait sila.
examples.en: I like your friends, they're nice.

notes.notes: Pseudo-verb: 'Kailangan ko ng...' = I need...; 'Kailangan umalis' = need to leave. Spoken 'kelangan'.

examples.tl: Kailangan ko ng bagong SIM.
examples.en: I need a new SIM.

examples.tl: Kailangan kong umuwi nang maaga.
examples.en: I need to go home early.

notes.notes: 'Dapat kang magpahinga' = you should rest. 'Dapat sana' = should have. 'Dapat lang' = as it should be / serves you right.

examples.tl: Dapat maaga ka bukas.
examples.en: You should be early tomorrow.

examples.tl: Dapat sana nag-Grab na lang tayo.
examples.en: We should have just taken a Grab.

notes.notes: Stress on FIRST syllable (unlike kayâ 'so/I wonder'). 'Kaya ko' = I can handle it. 'Kaya mo yan!' = You can do it!

examples.tl: Kaya mo yan!
examples.en: You can do it!

examples.tl: Hindi ko kayang maglakad hanggang Ayala.
examples.en: I can't manage to walk all the way to Ayala.

notes.notes: Past habit or former state: 'Dati, mura ang pamasahe.' 'dating' = former/ex ('dating boss ko').

examples.tl: Dati, naglalakad lang ako papuntang office.
examples.en: Before, I used to just walk to the office.

examples.tl: Yan ang dating condo ko.
examples.en: That's my former condo.

examples.tl: Dati nakatira ako sa Pasig, ngayon sa Makati na.
examples.en: I used to live in Pasig, now I'm in Makati.

notes.notes: 'Saglit lang' = just a moment. 'Sandali' is the same. 'Teka' = wait (from hintay ka).

examples.tl: Saglit lang, kukunin ko yung wallet ko.
examples.en: Just a sec, I'll get my wallet.

examples.tl: Dadaan lang ako saglit sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: I'll just drop by 7-Eleven briefly.

examples.tl: Saglit lang, kukuha lang ako ng tubig.
examples.en: Just a sec, I'll just get some water.

notes.notes: Makes comparatives: 'mas mura' = cheaper; 'mas gusto ko' = I prefer. Pair with 'kesa (sa)' = than.

examples.tl: Mas mura ang jeep kesa sa Grab.
examples.en: The jeep is cheaper than Grab.

examples.tl: Mas gusto ko ang mainit na kape.
examples.en: I prefer hot coffee.

examples.tl: Mas mura sa palengke kaysa sa supermarket.
examples.en: It's cheaper at the market than at the supermarket.

notes.notes: Prefix for superlatives: 'pinakamura' = cheapest; 'pinakamasarap' = tastiest. Often 'ang pinaka-' + adj.

examples.tl: Ito ang pinakamurang SIM.
examples.en: This is the cheapest SIM.

examples.tl: Ano ang pinakamasarap dito?
examples.en: What's the best dish here?

examples.tl: Abril ang pinakamainit na buwan sa Manila.
examples.en: April is the hottest month in Manila.

notes.notes: ma- + ganda. Also 'good' in greetings: 'Magandang umaga.' For people, 'maganda' = pretty (fem.); 'gwapo' = handsome.

examples.tl: Maganda ang view sa condo mo.
examples.en: The view from your condo is beautiful.

examples.tl: Magandang umaga po.
examples.en: Good morning (polite).

examples.tl: Ang ganda ng ate mo!
examples.en: Your sister is so pretty!

notes.notes: Two meanings: expensive ('Mahal ang Grab') and love/dear ('Mahal kita', 'mahal ko' = my love).

examples.tl: Ang mahal ng rent sa BGC!
examples.en: Rent in BGC is so expensive!

examples.tl: Mahal kita.
examples.en: I love you.

examples.tl: Ang mahal ng kape sa BGC, 250 isang cup.
examples.en: Coffee in BGC is so expensive, 250 a cup.

notes.notes: 'Mura lang' = it's cheap. 'Pamura' / 'murang-mura' = very cheap. 'Mura' (stress murá) also = curse word.

examples.tl: Mura lang ang pagkain sa carinderia.
examples.en: Food at the carinderia is cheap.

examples.tl: Mas mura kung cash.
examples.en: It's cheaper if you pay cash.

examples.tl: Ang mura ng ulam dito, 70 lang.
examples.en: The dishes here are so cheap, only 70.

notes.notes: ma- + laki. 'Malaking bahay' (linker -ng). 'Malaki ang discount' = big discount.

examples.tl: Malaki ang mall sa Ortigas.
examples.en: The mall in Ortigas is big.

examples.tl: Malaking tulong ito.
examples.en: This is a big help.

notes.notes: ma- + liit. 'Maliit lang' = it's just small. 'Maliit na studio' = a small studio unit.

examples.tl: Maliit lang ang unit ko, studio type.
examples.en: My unit is just small, studio type.

examples.tl: Maliit na problema lang yan.
examples.en: That's just a small problem.

examples.tl: Maliit si Lola pero malakas pa.
examples.en: Grandma is small but still strong.

notes.notes: 'Malayo pa' = still far. 'Malayo-layo' = quite far. 'Gaano kalayo?' = how far?

examples.tl: Malayo ang airport mula sa Makati.
examples.en: The airport is far from Makati.

examples.tl: Malayo pa ba tayo?
examples.en: Are we still far?

examples.tl: Malayo ang Quezon City mula sa Makati pag traffic.
examples.en: Quezon City is far from Makati when there's traffic.
examples.taglish: Malayo ang QC pag traffic, two hours minsan.

notes.taglish: Malayo pa yan, mag-Grab ka na lang.

notes.notes: 'Malapit lang' = just nearby. 'Malapit na' = almost there / coming soon. 'malapit sa' = near to.

examples.tl: Malapit lang ang gym sa condo ko.
examples.en: The gym is just near my condo.

examples.tl: Malapit na ako, 5 minutes.
examples.en: I'm almost there, 5 minutes.

examples.tl: Malapit lang ang MRT sa condo ko.
examples.en: The MRT is near my condo.
examples.taglish: Malapit lang ang MRT sa condo ko, 5 minutes walk.

notes.taglish: Malapit lang, walking distance.

notes.notes: 'Mabilis lang' = it's quick. 'Bilisan mo' = hurry up. 'Dali' is also used for 'quick!'.

examples.tl: Mabilis ang MRT kung walang aberya.
examples.en: The MRT is fast if there's no glitch.

examples.tl: Mabilis lang ang process sa bangko.
examples.en: The process at the bank was quick.

examples.tl: Ang bilis ng delivery, kahapon lang ako nag-order.
examples.en: The delivery was so fast, I only ordered yesterday.

notes.notes: 'Mabagal ang internet' = the internet is slow. 'Bagal' alone as complaint: 'Bagal!'

examples.tl: Mabagal ang wifi dito.
examples.en: The wifi here is slow.

examples.tl: Mabagal ang usad ng traffic.
examples.en: The traffic is moving slowly.

examples.tl: Ang bagal ng internet pag umuulan.
examples.en: The internet is so slow when it rains.

notes.notes: ma- + sarap. 'Sarap!' alone = yum. Also for pleasant feelings: 'masarap matulog' = it's nice to sleep.

examples.tl: Masarap ang lechon dito.
examples.en: The lechon here is delicious.

examples.tl: Ang sarap ng tulog ko kagabi.
examples.en: I slept so well last night.

examples.tl: Ang sarap ng sinigang dito!
examples.en: The sinigang here is so good!

notes.notes: Weather, food, drink. 'Ang init!' = It's so hot! 'Mainit ang ulo' = short-tempered. Spicy is 'maanghang'.

examples.tl: Sobrang init sa labas, mag-aircon tayo.
examples.en: It's so hot outside, let's get some aircon.

examples.tl: Gusto ko ng mainit na kape.
examples.en: I want hot coffee.

examples.tl: Mainit pa yung pandesal, bagong luto.
examples.en: The pandesal is still hot, fresh from the oven.

notes.taglish: Mainit sa jeep, walang aircon.

notes.notes: 'Malamig na tubig' = cold water. 'Ang lamig!' = So cold! Tagaytay/Baguio are 'malamig'.

examples.tl: Malamig sa Baguio sa Disyembre.
examples.en: It's cold in Baguio in December.

examples.tl: Isang malamig na beer, please.
examples.en: One cold beer, please.

examples.tl: May malamig na beer ba kayo?
examples.en: Do you have cold beer?

notes.notes: 'Bagong phone' = new phone (linker -ng). 'Bago lang' = brand new / just recently. Also the conjunction 'before'.

examples.tl: Bago ang phone mo?
examples.en: Is your phone new?

examples.tl: May bagong restaurant sa Salcedo.
examples.en: There's a new restaurant in Salcedo.

notes.notes: For objects only. Old PEOPLE = 'matanda'. 'Lumang building' = old building.

examples.tl: Luma na ang laptop ko.
examples.en: My laptop is old now.

examples.tl: Lumang building yun pero maganda pa.
examples.en: That's an old building but still nice.

notes.notes: 'Madali lang' = it's easy. Related 'dali' = hurry ('Dali!' = quick!). 'Madaling araw' = early morning/dawn.

examples.tl: Madali lang mag-GCash.
examples.en: Using GCash is easy.

examples.tl: Madali lang pumunta dun, isang jeep lang.
examples.en: It's easy to get there, just one jeep.

examples.tl: Madali lang mag-GCash, scan lang ng QR.
examples.en: GCash is easy, just scan the QR.

notes.notes: Two meanings: difficult ('mahirap ang exam') and poor ('mahirap na pamilya'). 'Hirap' alone = it's a struggle.

examples.tl: Mahirap mag-drive sa Manila.
examples.en: It's hard to drive in Manila.

examples.tl: Mahirap makahanap ng Grab kapag umuulan.
examples.en: It's hard to find a Grab when it's raining.

notes.notes: 'Maraming tao' = lots of people. 'Ang dami!' = So many! 'Maraming salamat' = thank you very much.

examples.tl: Maraming tao sa Divisoria.
examples.en: There are lots of people in Divisoria.

examples.tl: Maraming salamat po.
examples.en: Thank you very much.

examples.tl: Maraming tao sa MRT pag alas-sais ng hapon.
examples.en: There are a lot of people on the MRT at six in the evening.

notes.notes: Standard 'kaunti'; spoken 'konti'. 'Konti lang' = just a little. 'Konting-konti' = very little.

examples.tl: Konti lang ang pera ko ngayon.
examples.en: I only have a little money right now.

examples.tl: Konting kanin lang po.
examples.en: Just a little rice, please.

examples.tl: Konti lang ang kanin ko, diet ako.
examples.en: Just a little rice for me, I'm on a diet.

notes.notes: Containers, vehicles, venues: 'Puno ang jeep' = the jeep is full. Stressed 'púno' = tree. Full stomach = 'busog'.

examples.tl: Puno na ang MRT, next train na lang.
examples.en: The MRT is full, let's take the next train.

examples.tl: Puno ang parking sa mall.
examples.en: The mall parking is full.

examples.tl: Puno na ang jeep, hintay tayo ng susunod.
examples.en: The jeep is full, let's wait for the next one.

notes.taglish: Puno na ang jeep, next na lang.

notes.notes: Fully adopted. 'Okay lang' = it's fine / I'm fine. 'Okay na' = it's good now. 'Okay ka lang?' = you alright?

examples.tl: Okay lang ba kung late ako ng konti?
examples.en: Is it okay if I'm a little late?

examples.tl: Okay na, nabayaran ko na.
examples.en: It's okay now, I've paid it.

notes.notes: People or events: 'Masaya ako' = I'm happy; 'Masaya ang party' = the party was fun. 'Ang saya!' = so fun!

examples.tl: Masaya ang Christmas sa Pilipinas.
examples.en: Christmas in the Philippines is fun.

examples.tl: Masaya akong nandito ka.
examples.en: I'm happy you're here.

examples.tl: Masaya ako para sa inyo!
examples.en: I'm happy for you guys!

notes.notes: People or places/moods. 'Nalulungkot ako' = I'm feeling sad. 'Ang lungkot' = how sad.

examples.tl: Malungkot siya kasi umalis ang kaibigan niya.
examples.en: He/she is sad because their friend left.

examples.tl: Malungkot ang condo kapag mag-isa ka.
examples.en: The condo is lonely when you're alone.

examples.tl: Malungkot siya kasi umalis ang kaibigan niya papuntang Canada.
examples.en: She's sad because her friend left for Canada.

notes.notes: 'Pagod na ako' = I'm tired already. 'Nakakapagod' = tiring. 'Pahinga' = rest.

examples.tl: Pagod ako galing sa trabaho.
examples.en: I'm tired from work.

examples.tl: Nakakapagod ang byahe pauwi.
examples.en: The trip home is tiring.

examples.tl: Pagod na ako, uwi na tayo.
examples.en: I'm tired, let's go home.

notes.notes: 'Gutom na ako' = I'm hungry. 'Nagugutom ako' (verb form) is also common. 'Gutom ka ba?' = hungry?

examples.tl: Gutom na ako, kain tayo.
examples.en: I'm hungry, let's eat.

examples.tl: Gutom ka na ba?
examples.en: Are you hungry yet?

examples.tl: Gutom na ako, order na tayo sa Grab.
examples.en: I'm hungry, let's order on Grab.

notes.notes: Full after eating. 'Busog na ako' = I'm full. Not 'puno' (that's for containers). 'Nakakabusog' = filling.

examples.tl: Busog na ako, salamat.
examples.en: I'm full, thanks.

examples.tl: Nakakabusog ang unli rice.
examples.en: Unlimited rice is filling.

examples.tl: Busog na ako, ikaw na ang tumapos.
examples.en: I'm full, you finish it.

notes.notes: ma- + linis. 'Maglinis' = to clean. Opposite: 'madumi'. 'Malinis ang CR' = the restroom is clean.

examples.tl: Malinis ang CR sa mall na ito.
examples.en: The restrooms in this mall are clean.

examples.tl: Malinis na ang unit ko.
examples.en: My unit is clean now.

notes.notes: Spoken 'madumi'; formal 'marumi'. 'Dumi' = dirt. 'Madumi ang tubig' = the water is dirty.

examples.tl: Madumi ang sapatos ko dahil sa baha.
examples.en: My shoes are dirty because of the flood.

examples.tl: Madumi pa ang mesa, pakilinis.
examples.en: The table is still dirty, please clean it.

notes.notes: Height or amount: 'mataas ang presyo' = prices are high; 'mataas na building' = tall building. Tall person = 'matangkad'.

examples.tl: Mataas ang rent sa Makati.
examples.en: Rent in Makati is high.

examples.tl: Mataas ang building na yun.
examples.en: That building is tall.

notes.notes: 'Mababa ang presyo' = low price. 'Mababang grade' = low grade. Short person = 'maliit' or 'pandak' (casual).

examples.tl: Mababa ang sweldo pero okay ang work.
examples.en: The salary is low but the work is fine.

examples.tl: Mababa ang kisame dito.
examples.en: The ceiling here is low.

notes.notes: For people and pets. 'Mabait siya' = he/she is nice. 'Ang bait!' = so kind! Opposite: 'masama' or 'salbahe'.

examples.tl: Mabait ang guard sa building namin.
examples.en: The guard in our building is nice.

examples.tl: Mabait na tao si Tita.
examples.en: Auntie is a kind person.

examples.tl: Mabait ang mga magulang ng jowa ko, swerte ako.
examples.en: My partner's parents are kind, I'm lucky.

notes.notes: 'Masama ang panahon' = the weather is bad. 'Masama ang pakiramdam ko' = I feel sick. 'Masamang balita' = bad news.

examples.tl: Masama ang pakiramdam ko ngayon.
examples.en: I don't feel well today.

examples.tl: Masama ang traffic kapag umuulan.
examples.en: Traffic is bad when it rains.

notes.notes: 'Tama!' = Correct! 'Tama ka' = you're right. 'Tama na' = that's enough, stop. 'Tama lang' = just right.

examples.tl: Tama ka, mas mura dun.
examples.en: You're right, it's cheaper there.

examples.tl: Tama na, busog na ako.
examples.en: That's enough, I'm full.

notes.notes: 'Sira ang aircon' = the aircon is broken. 'Nasira' = got broken. 'Sira-ulo' = crazy (slang).

examples.tl: Sira ang elevator, hagdan muna tayo.
examples.en: The elevator is broken, let's take the stairs for now.

examples.tl: Nasira ang phone ko sa ulan.
examples.en: My phone got damaged in the rain.

examples.tl: Sira yung lock ng pinto, pa-ayos sa landlord.
examples.en: The door lock is broken, have the landlord fix it.

notes.notes: Formal; most Manileños just say 'busy'. Common in 'Sorry sa abala' = sorry for the bother/inconvenience.

examples.tl: Sorry sa abala, pwede bang magtanong?
examples.en: Sorry to bother you, can I ask something?

examples.tl: Abala siya ngayon, busy sa trabaho.
examples.en: He/she is busy right now, busy with work.

notes.notes: Also 'home' in general ('uwi sa bahay'), even when you live in a condo.

examples.tl: Nasa bahay lang ako buong araw.
examples.en: I was just at home all day.
examples.taglish: Nasa bahay lang ako buong araw, WFH.

examples.tl: Uwi na tayo sa bahay, traffic na mamaya.
examples.en: Let's go home, it'll be traffic later.

notes.notes: Said as in English. 'Unit' = your apartment; 'tower'/'building' for the block. 'Apartment' usually means a cheaper walk-up.

examples.tl: Punta ka sa condo ko mamaya, mag-order tayo.
examples.en: Come to my condo later, let's order food.

examples.tl: Ilang floor ang unit mo?
examples.en: What floor is your unit on?

notes.notes: Formal spelling 'kuwarto'. Bedroom = kwarto; 'silid' is literary.

examples.tl: Nasa kwarto ko ang charger, kunin mo lang.
examples.en: The charger is in my room, just get it.

examples.tl: Isang kwarto lang ang unit namin, studio type.
examples.en: Our unit has just one room, studio type.

examples.tl: Nasa kusina si Ate, nagluluto ng ulam.
examples.en: Ate is in the kitchen cooking the main dish.

examples.tl: Maliit ang kusina sa condo, induction lang ang gamit namin.
examples.en: The condo kitchen is small, we only use an induction stove.

examples.tl: Maliit ang kusina sa condo pero okay na.
examples.en: The condo kitchen is small but it's fine.

notes.notes: 'Dirty kitchen' = outdoor/secondary kitchen for frying and grilling (Philippine English). 'Kusinero/a' = cook.
The bathroom at home. In public places people say 'CR'.

examples.tl: Nasa banyo pa siya, naliligo.
examples.en: She's still in the bathroom, showering.

examples.tl: Barado ang drain sa banyo, tumawag ka sa admin.
examples.en: The bathroom drain is clogged, call the admin.

notes.notes: From 'comfort room'. The everyday word for any toilet outside the home; 'banyo' is the one at home.

examples.tl: Saan ang CR dito?
examples.en: Where's the restroom here?

examples.tl: Pupunta lang ako ng CR, bantayan mo ang bag ko.
examples.en: I'm just going to the restroom, watch my bag.

notes.taglish: Mag-CR lang ako, wait ka diyan.
notes.notes: Nag-CR, nagsi-CR. Very common and polite enough for any setting.

examples.tl: Mag-CR lang ako, sandali.
examples.en: I'll just use the restroom, one sec.

examples.tl: Pwede ba akong mag-CR sa inyo?
examples.en: Can I use your bathroom?

examples.tl: Nasa sala ang TV at ang mga bisita.
examples.en: The TV and the guests are in the living room.

examples.tl: Matulog ka na lang sa sala, may sofa bed.
examples.en: Just sleep in the living room, there's a sofa bed.

notes.notes: 'Pintuan' = doorway, also used for the door itself.

examples.tl: Isara mo ang pinto, lalabas ang lamig ng aircon.
examples.en: Close the door, the aircon cold will get out.

examples.tl: May kumakatok sa pinto, baka delivery.
examples.en: Someone's knocking at the door, maybe a delivery.

examples.tl: Buksan mo ang bintana, amoy luto sa loob.
examples.en: Open the window, it smells of cooking inside.

examples.tl: Hindi nabubuksan ang bintana sa condo namin.
examples.en: The windows in our condo can't be opened.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang susi sa loob, tawagin natin ang guard.
examples.en: I left the key inside, let's call the guard.
examples.taglish: Naiwan ko ang susi sa loob, na-lock out ako!

examples.tl: Nasaan ang susi ng unit? Hindi ko mahanap.
examples.en: Where's the unit key? I can't find it.

examples.tl: Hindi ko pa naaayos ang kama ko.
examples.en: I haven't made my bed yet.

examples.tl: Queen size ang kama namin, kasya pa sa kwarto.
examples.en: Our bed is queen size, it still fits in the room.

notes.notes: Root upo (sit). 'Silya' also used for a chair.

examples.tl: Kulang ang upuan, may bisita tayo mamaya.
examples.en: We don't have enough chairs, we have guests later.

examples.tl: May upuan ba sa labas ng clinic?
examples.en: Are there seats outside the clinic?

examples.tl: Ilagay mo lang sa mesa ang grocery.
examples.en: Just put the groceries on the table.

examples.tl: Walang mesa sa unit, sa sofa kami kumakain.
examples.en: There's no table in the unit, we eat on the sofa.

notes.notes: Lights are 'buksan' (open) and 'patayin' (kill), not 'isara'. 'Bukas ang ilaw' = the light is on.

examples.tl: Patayin mo ang ilaw bago ka matulog.
examples.en: Turn off the light before you sleep.

examples.tl: Buksan mo ang ilaw, madilim na.
examples.en: Turn on the light, it's dark already.

notes.notes: Always 'aircon', never 'AC'. Hinaan = turn down, lakasan = turn up.

examples.tl: Ang init! Buksan natin ang aircon.
examples.en: It's so hot! Let's turn on the aircon.

examples.tl: Mahal ang kuryente kapag maghapon ang aircon.
examples.en: Electricity is expensive if the aircon runs all day.

notes.notes: Many people just say 'electric fan' or 'fan'.

examples.tl: Bentilador lang muna, mahal ang kuryente.
examples.en: Just the fan for now, electricity is expensive.

examples.tl: Itutok mo sa akin ang bentilador, pawis na ako.
examples.en: Point the fan at me, I'm sweating.

notes.notes: 'Nawalan ng kuryente' = power went out. Meralco is the Manila provider.

examples.tl: Nawalan ng kuryente kagabi, grabe ang init.
examples.en: The power went out last night, the heat was terrible.

examples.tl: Mahal ang kuryente ngayong buwan, 4,000 ang bill ko.
examples.en: Electricity is expensive this month, my bill is 4,000.

examples.tl: Nagbayad ka na ba ng kuryente? Due na bukas.
examples.en: Have you paid the electricity? It's due tomorrow.

notes.notes: Filipinos say 'brownout' for any outage; 'blackout' is rare.

examples.tl: May brownout sa Makati kanina, dalawang oras.
examples.en: There was a power outage in Makati earlier, two hours.

examples.tl: Brownout ulit? Walang wifi tuloy.
examples.en: Power outage again? So no wifi.

examples.tl: Brownout kanina ng dalawang oras, nainitan ako sa condo.
examples.en: Power was out for two hours earlier, I got hot in the condo.

notes.taglish: Brownout sa amin, walang aircon, init!

notes.notes: 'Magtapon ng basura' = take out the trash. Condos have a garbage room per floor.

examples.tl: Ilabas mo na ang basura, mabaho na.
examples.en: Take out the trash now, it stinks already.

examples.tl: Saan ang tapunan ng basura dito sa floor?
examples.en: Where's the trash chute on this floor?

notes.notes: Labahan = clothes to be washed, or the washing area. 'Labada' = a batch of laundry. 'Laundry' also common.

examples.tl: Dami ng labahan, dalhin na natin sa laundry shop.
examples.en: So much laundry, let's take it to the laundry shop.

examples.tl: Nasa labahan pa ang jeans mo.
examples.en: Your jeans are still in the laundry.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Labahan = laundry shop; labandera = laundrywoman. Root from Spanish lavar.

examples.tl: Naglalaba siya tuwing Sabado.
examples.en: He does laundry every Saturday.

examples.tl: Maglalaba ako bukas, Sabado.
examples.en: I'll do laundry tomorrow, Saturday.

examples.tl: Naglaba si Ate kanina, nasa sampayan ang mga damit.
examples.en: Ate did the laundry earlier, the clothes are on the line.

examples.tl: Pakiplantsa ang polo ko para bukas.
examples.en: Please iron my polo shirt for tomorrow.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang plantsa? Gusot ang damit ko.
examples.en: Where's the iron? My clothes are wrinkled.

notes.notes: 'Ipaplantsa' = have it ironed (at the laundry shop).

examples.tl: Hindi ako marunong magplantsa, dinadala ko sa laundry.
examples.en: I don't know how to iron, I take it to the laundry.

examples.tl: Nagplantsa si Ate ng mga polo ko kanina.
examples.en: Ate ironed my polos earlier.

notes.notes: Walis tambo = soft indoor broom; walis tingting = stiff outdoor broom.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang walis? Natapon ang bigas.
examples.en: Where's the broom? The rice spilled.

examples.tl: Walis tambo sa sala, walis tingting sa labas.
examples.en: Soft broom for the living room, stiff broom for outside.

notes.notes: 'Walisin' = sweep (it/the floor).

examples.tl: Magwalis ka muna bago mag-mop.
examples.en: Sweep first before you mop.

examples.tl: Nagwalis na ako ng sala, ikaw na sa kusina.
examples.en: I already swept the living room, you do the kitchen.

notes.notes: The surface you walk on. A building level is 'floor' or 'palapag'.

examples.tl: Basa ang sahig, mag-ingat ka.
examples.en: The floor is wet, be careful.

examples.tl: Mag-mop tayo ng sahig, madumi na.
examples.en: Let's mop the floor, it's dirty already.

examples.tl: Pwede bang magbutas sa dingding? Tanong muna sa admin.
examples.en: Can we drill into the wall? Ask the admin first.

examples.tl: Manipis ang dingding, rinig ang kapitbahay.
examples.en: The wall is thin, you can hear the neighbor.

examples.tl: Sira ang elevator, hagdan muna tayo.
examples.en: The elevator is broken, let's take the stairs.

examples.tl: Nasa 3rd floor lang ako, hagdan na lang.
examples.en: I'm just on the 3rd floor, I'll take the stairs.

notes.notes: 'Lift' is not used. Also just 'elev'.

examples.tl: Ang tagal ng elevator sa building namin tuwing umaga.
examples.en: The elevator in our building takes forever in the morning.

examples.tl: Isa lang ang gumaganang elevator ngayon.
examples.en: Only one elevator is working right now.

examples.tl: Nasa lobby na ang Grab mo.
examples.en: Your Grab is already in the lobby.

examples.tl: Pakikuha ang package ko sa lobby.
examples.en: Please pick up my package at the lobby.

examples.tl: Hintayin mo ako sa lobby, bababa ako.
examples.en: Wait for me in the lobby, I'm coming down.
examples.taglish: Wait mo ako sa lobby, bababa na ako, 2 mins.

notes.taglish: Nasa lobby na ako, baba ka na.
notes.notes: Default meeting point in condos and offices. 'Sa lobby na lang tayo magkita.'
Address as 'Kuya guard' or 'Sir'. 'Gwardya' is understood, 'sekyu' is slang.

examples.tl: Iwan mo lang sa guard ang package ko.
examples.en: Just leave my package with the guard.

examples.tl: Tanungin mo ang guard kung saan ang visitor parking.
examples.en: Ask the guard where the visitor parking is.

examples.tl: Iwan mo lang sa guard yung package, kukunin ko mamaya.
examples.en: Just leave the package with the guard, I'll get it later.

notes.taglish: Tanungin mo ang guard kung saan ang Tower 2.

notes.notes: The polite term. 'Katulong' still common; 'yaya' = nanny. Address her as 'Ate' or 'Manang'.

examples.tl: Tuwing Sabado lang pumupunta ang kasambahay namin.
examples.en: Our helper only comes on Saturdays.

examples.tl: Masipag ang kasambahay nila, pati plantsa gawa niya.
examples.en: Their helper is hardworking, she even does the ironing.

examples.tl: Day off ng kasambahay namin tuwing Linggo.
examples.en: Our house helper's day off is every Sunday.

examples.tl: Maingay ang kapitbahay namin tuwing gabi, may karaoke.
examples.en: Our neighbors are noisy every night, they have karaoke.

examples.tl: Mabait ang kapitbahay ko, binigyan ako ng ulam.
examples.en: My neighbor is kind, she gave me some food.

examples.tl: Maingay ang kapitbahay namin tuwing weekend.
examples.en: Our neighbor is noisy every weekend.

notes.notes: In condos people also say 'neighbor' or 'katabi namin' (the one next to us).
'Nagre-rent' or 'nangungupahan' = renting. Most people just say 'rent'.

examples.tl: Kailan ang due ng upa mo?
examples.en: When is your rent due?

examples.tl: Tumaas ang upa namin ng 2,000 ngayong taon.
examples.en: Our rent went up by 2,000 this year.

examples.tl: Dalawang buwan nang hindi nagbabayad ng upa yung kapitbahay.
examples.en: The neighbor hasn't paid rent for two months.

notes.notes: Monthly condo fees, often just 'dues'. Separate from rent and Meralco.

examples.tl: Nagtaas ulit ang association dues sa condo.
examples.en: The condo association dues went up again.

examples.tl: Kasama na ba sa upa ang dues?
examples.en: Are the dues included in the rent?

examples.tl: Tumaas ulit ang association dues sa building namin.
examples.en: The association dues in our building went up again.

notes.notes: The condo management office. Also 'admin office'.

examples.tl: Mag-report ka sa admin, tumutulo ang tubo sa banyo.
examples.en: Report it to the admin, the bathroom pipe is leaking.

examples.tl: Sarado ang admin office tuwing Linggo.
examples.en: The admin office is closed on Sundays.

examples.tl: Sa admin mo i-report yung tumutulo sa CR.
examples.en: Report the leak in the bathroom to the admin.

notes.notes: 'Nakakandado' = locked. For door locks people also say 'naka-lock'.

examples.tl: Nakakandado ang gate pagkatapos ng alas-diyes.
examples.en: The gate is padlocked after ten o'clock.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng kandado para sa bike mo.
examples.en: Buy a padlock for your bike.

examples.tl: Nasa gate na ang delivery mo.
examples.en: Your delivery is at the gate.

examples.tl: Kailangan ng ID sa gate ng village.
examples.en: You need an ID at the village gate.

examples.tl: Barado ang lababo, tawagan natin ang maintenance.
examples.en: The sink is clogged, let's call maintenance.

examples.tl: Tambak na ang hugasan sa lababo.
examples.en: The dishes are piled up in the sink.

notes.notes: Filipinos say 'ref', not 'fridge'. 'Tira' = leftovers.

examples.tl: May tira pa sa ref, i-microwave mo lang.
examples.en: There are leftovers in the fridge, just microwave them.

examples.tl: Ilagay mo sa ref ang gatas, masisira.
examples.en: Put the milk in the fridge, it'll spoil.

examples.tl: Ilagay mo sa ref yung tira, baka mapanis.
examples.en: Put the leftovers in the fridge, they might spoil.

notes.notes: Many condos ban gas, so 'induction' is common.

examples.tl: Patayin mo ang kalan, kumukulo na.
examples.en: Turn off the stove, it's boiling already.

examples.tl: Walang gas na kalan dito, induction ang gamit.
examples.en: No gas stove here, we use induction.

examples.tl: Induction lang ang kalan sa condo, bawal ang gasul.
examples.en: The condo stove is induction only, LPG isn't allowed.

examples.tl: Hugasan mo na ang kaldero, may natirang kanin.
examples.en: Wash the pot now, there's leftover rice in it.

examples.tl: Malaking kaldero ang gamitin mo sa sinigang.
examples.en: Use the big pot for the sinigang.

examples.tl: Nasa kaldero pa ang sinigang, painitin mo.
examples.en: The sinigang is still in the pot, heat it up.

notes.notes: Big pot for rice or soup. Kaserola = casserole/saucepan. Rice cooker is said in English.

examples.tl: Painitin mo muna ang kawali bago ilagay ang itlog.
examples.en: Heat the pan first before putting in the egg.

examples.tl: Non-stick ang kawali, huwag kang gumamit ng metal.
examples.en: The pan is non-stick, don't use metal.

examples.tl: Initin mo muna ang kawali bago ilagay ang mantika.
examples.en: Heat the pan first before adding the oil.

notes.notes: Any frying pan. 'Lechon kawali' = pork belly fried in a kawali. Non-stick = non-stick.

examples.tl: Kuha ka ng plato, kain na tayo.
examples.en: Get a plate, let's eat.

examples.tl: Dalawang plato lang ang malinis, hugasan mo na ang iba.
examples.en: Only two plates are clean, wash the rest.

examples.tl: Isa pang plato po, mag-share kami.
examples.en: One more plate please, we're sharing.

notes.notes: Pinggan is the Tagalog synonym, also common ('maghugas ng pinggan'). 'Platito' = saucer/small plate.

examples.tl: Nabasag ang baso, ingat sa bubog.
examples.en: The glass broke, careful of the shards.

examples.tl: Kuha ka ng baso, may Coke sa ref.
examples.en: Get a glass, there's Coke in the fridge.

examples.tl: Isang basong tubig lang, salamat.
examples.en: Just a glass of water, thanks.

notes.notes: Glass for drinks. 'Isang basong tubig' = a glass of water. 'May baso po?' when you get a bottle.
Filipinos eat with spoon and fork; the spoon does the cutting.

examples.tl: Kutsara at tinidor lang, walang kutsilyo.
examples.en: Just spoon and fork, no knife.

examples.tl: Pahingi ng kutsara, pang-sabaw.
examples.en: Can I have a spoon, for the soup.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng kutsara at tinidor.
examples.en: May I have a spoon and fork, please.

examples.tl: Wala akong tinidor, kutsara lang ang binigay.
examples.en: I don't have a fork, they only gave a spoon.

examples.tl: Ilagay mo sa mesa ang tinidor at kutsara.
examples.en: Put the forks and spoons on the table.

examples.tl: Walang tinidor sa take-out, nakalimutan nila.
examples.en: There's no fork in the take-out, they forgot.

notes.notes: Partner of the spoon. Chopsticks = chopsticks. Eating with hands = kamayan (boodle fight).
Every household has one. Said in English.

examples.tl: Isaksak mo ang rice cooker, magsaing na tayo.
examples.en: Plug in the rice cooker, let's cook rice.

examples.tl: Naka-warm pa ang rice cooker, may kanin pa.
examples.en: The rice cooker is still on warm, there's rice left.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Everyday household verb. Kanin = cooked rice; bigas = uncooked rice.

examples.tl: Nagsaing ka na ba? Wala na tayong kanin.
examples.en: Did you cook rice yet? We have no rice left.

examples.tl: Magsaing ka na, uuwi si Mama ng alas-sais.
examples.en: Cook rice now, Mom is coming home at six.

examples.tl: Nagsaing ako ng dalawang tasa, sapat na sa atin.
examples.en: I cooked two cups of rice, that's enough for us.

examples.tl: Isara mo ang kurtina, sobrang init sa hapon.
examples.en: Close the curtain, it's so hot in the afternoon.

examples.tl: Blackout curtain ang binili ko para makatulog.
examples.en: I bought blackout curtains so I can sleep.

examples.tl: Dalawa ang unan ko, hindi ako makatulog sa isa.
examples.en: I use two pillows, I can't sleep with one.

examples.tl: Palitan mo ang punda ng unan, Linggo na.
examples.en: Change the pillowcase, it's Sunday already.

examples.tl: Kumot pa, malamig ang aircon.
examples.en: More blanket please, the aircon is cold.

examples.tl: Nasa labahan ang kumot, gamitin mo muna ang isa.
examples.en: The blanket is in the wash, use the other one for now.

notes.notes: Most people just say 'towel'.

examples.tl: Nasa banyo ang malinis na tuwalya.
examples.en: The clean towel is in the bathroom.

examples.tl: Pahiram ng towel, nakalimutan ko sa condo.
examples.en: Lend me a towel, I forgot mine at the condo.

notes.notes: Sabong panlaba = laundry detergent; sabong panghugas = dish soap.

examples.tl: Ubos na ang sabon sa banyo.
examples.en: The soap in the bathroom is used up.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng sabong panlaba, yung powder.
examples.en: Buy laundry detergent, the powder kind.

notes.notes: Sold in tiny sachets at sari-sari stores.

examples.tl: Ubos na ang shampoo, isama mo sa grocery list.
examples.en: The shampoo is finished, add it to the grocery list.

examples.tl: Sachet lang ng shampoo ang binili ko, pang-isang linggo.
examples.en: I only bought shampoo sachets, enough for a week.

notes.notes: 'Colgate' is used as the generic word by many.

examples.tl: Pabili ng toothpaste, kahit anong brand.
examples.en: Please buy toothpaste, any brand.

examples.tl: Wala nang Colgate, konti na lang.
examples.en: There's almost no toothpaste left.

notes.notes: Many public CRs have no tissue; bring your own.

examples.tl: Walang tissue sa CR, magdala ka ng sarili mo.
examples.en: There's no tissue in the restroom, bring your own.

examples.tl: Pahingi ng tissue, natapon ang kape.
examples.en: Can I have a tissue, the coffee spilled.

examples.tl: Mag-ipon tayo ng tubig sa timba, may water interruption bukas.
examples.en: Let's store water in the bucket, there's a water cut tomorrow.

examples.tl: Timba at tabo lang, walang shower sa boarding house.
examples.en: Just a bucket and dipper, no shower at the boarding house.

notes.notes: The plastic dipper beside every Filipino toilet; used for washing and bucket baths.

examples.tl: Walang bidet dito, tabo lang ang gamit.
examples.en: No bidet here, we just use the dipper.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang tabo? Sira ang shower.
examples.en: Where's the dipper? The shower is broken.

notes.notes: 'Isampay' = hang up to dry. Many condos ban drying on the balcony.

examples.tl: Isampay mo sa sampayan, bawal sa balcony sabi ng admin.
examples.en: Hang it on the drying rack, the admin says the balcony is off limits.

examples.tl: Puno na ang sampayan, dami ng nilabhan.
examples.en: The clothesline is full, so much got washed.

examples.tl: May washing machine na kami, hindi na kailangan ng laundry shop.
examples.en: We have a washing machine now, no need for the laundry shop.

examples.tl: Sira ang washing machine, umiikot pero hindi nag-spin.
examples.en: The washing machine is broken, it turns but won't spin.

notes.notes: Drop-off wash-dry-fold, charged per kilo. Every condo area has several.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo sa laundry shop, per kilo ang bayad.
examples.en: Take it to the laundry shop, they charge per kilo.

examples.tl: Kukunin ko ang labada sa laundry shop mamaya.
examples.en: I'll pick up the laundry from the shop later.

notes.notes: Root gising. Gumising, gumigising, gigising. 'Gisingin mo ako' = wake me up.

examples.tl: Gumising ako ng alas-sais para hindi ma-late.
examples.en: I woke up at six so I wouldn't be late.

examples.tl: Gisingin mo ako ng alas-singko, may flight ako.
examples.en: Wake me up at five, I have a flight.

notes.notes: Different from gumising (wake up). 'Ayaw kong bumangon' = I don't want to get up.

examples.tl: Gising na ako pero ayaw ko pang bumangon.
examples.en: I'm awake but I don't want to get up yet.

examples.tl: Bumangon ka na, alas-otso na!
examples.en: Get up, it's eight already!

notes.notes: Actor focus (ma-, not mag-). Naliligo = is showering. 'Ligo muna ako' = let me shower first.

examples.tl: Maliligo lang ako tapos alis na tayo.
examples.en: I'll just shower and then we'll leave.

examples.tl: Maligo ka muna bago tayo umalis.
examples.en: Shower first before we leave.

examples.tl: Naligo na ako, bihis na lang.
examples.en: I've showered, I just need to get dressed.

notes.taglish: Mag-toothbrush muna ako bago matulog.
notes.notes: The everyday form. 'Magsipilyo' is the native word, less used in Manila.

examples.tl: Nag-toothbrush na ako, tulog na ako.
examples.en: I've brushed my teeth, I'm going to sleep.

examples.tl: Mag-toothbrush ka muna bago lumabas, amoy bawang.
examples.en: Brush your teeth before going out, you smell of garlic.

notes.en: to get dressed; to change clothes
notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). 'Magbibihis lang ako' = let me just change. Bihisan = dress someone.

examples.tl: Nagbihis muna siya bago lumabas.
examples.en: She changed first before going out.

examples.tl: Magbihis ka na, nasa lobby na ang Grab.
examples.en: Get dressed, the Grab is already in the lobby.

examples.tl: Magbibihis lang ako, basa ako sa ulan.
examples.en: I'll just change, I got wet in the rain.

notes.notes: 'Mag-almusal' = to eat breakfast. 'Agahan' is also used.

examples.tl: Ano ang almusal natin? Tapsilog?
examples.en: What's our breakfast? Tapsilog?

examples.tl: Hindi ako nag-almusal, kape lang.
examples.en: I didn't have breakfast, just coffee.

examples.tl: Nag-almusal ka na ba?
examples.en: Have you had breakfast yet?

notes.notes: 'Mananghalian' = to eat lunch. 'Lunch' itself is very common in Taglish.

examples.tl: Saan tayo mananghalian? Sa food court?
examples.en: Where shall we have lunch? The food court?

examples.tl: Baon ko ang tanghalian ko, tira kagabi.
examples.en: I packed my lunch, last night's leftovers.

examples.tl: Saan tayo mananghalian? Sa Glorietta?
examples.en: Where are we having lunch? At Glorietta?
examples.taglish: Saan tayo mag-lunch? Glorietta?

notes.notes: 'Maghapunan' = to eat dinner. 'Dinner' is also common.

examples.tl: Ano ang hapunan? Mag-order na lang tayo.
examples.en: What's for dinner? Let's just order.

examples.tl: Maghapunan ka muna bago umuwi.
examples.en: Have dinner first before going home.

examples.tl: Ano'ng ulam sa hapunan?
examples.en: What's the dish for dinner?

notes.notes: Actor focus (ma-). Natutulog = is sleeping. Makatulog = to fall asleep. Tulog = asleep.

examples.tl: Natulog ako ng alas-dos kagabi.
examples.en: I went to sleep at 2 a.m. last night.

examples.tl: Matulog ka na, maaga ka bukas.
examples.en: Go to sleep, you're up early tomorrow.

examples.tl: Alas-dos na ako natulog kagabi, antok ako ngayon.
examples.en: I slept at two last night, I'm sleepy now.

notes.notes: Actor focus (um-). 'Alis!' alone is a blunt 'move/get out'. 'Aalis na ako' = I'm off.

examples.tl: Kanina pa umalis si Marco.
examples.en: Marco left a while ago.

examples.tl: Umalis ako ng condo ng alas-siyete, late pa rin.
examples.en: I left the condo at seven, still late.

examples.tl: Aalis na ako, lock mo ang pinto.
examples.en: I'm leaving now, lock the door.

notes.taglish: Alis na tayo, baka ma-traffic.

notes.notes: Actor focus (um-). 'Uwi na tayo' = let's head home. Object focus iuwi = take something home.

examples.tl: Uuwi na ako, traffic na kasi.
examples.en: I'm heading home now, traffic is building up.

examples.tl: Uuwi na ako, traffic na mamaya.
examples.en: I'm going home now, it'll be traffic later.

examples.tl: Anong oras ka umuwi kagabi?
examples.en: What time did you get home last night?

notes.taglish: Uwi na ako, gabi na.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: lutuin. Nagluluto = is cooking. Luto = cooked.

examples.tl: Nagluto si Ate ng adobo para sa lunch.
examples.en: Ate cooked adobo for lunch.

examples.tl: Magluluto ako ng adobo mamaya, kain ka dito.
examples.en: I'll cook adobo later, eat here.

examples.tl: Hindi ako nagluluto, puro Grab food lang.
examples.en: I don't cook, just Grab food all the time.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: linisin. Malinis = clean (adj).

examples.tl: Naglinis kami ng condo buong Linggo.
examples.en: We cleaned the condo all Sunday.

examples.tl: Maglilinis ako ng unit bukas, Linggo.
examples.en: I'll clean the unit tomorrow, Sunday.

examples.tl: Linisin mo ang banyo, may amag na.
examples.en: Clean the bathroom, there's mold already.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). For dishes, hands, cars; clothes are maglaba. Object focus: hugasan.

examples.tl: Ako na maghuhugas ng plato.
examples.en: I'll wash the dishes.

examples.tl: Maghugas ka ng kamay bago kumain.
examples.en: Wash your hands before eating.

examples.tl: Ako na ang maghuhugas ng plato, ikaw na sa basura.
examples.en: I'll wash the dishes, you take out the trash.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Pahinga (pa- + hinga 'breath') acts as the root. 'Pahinga muna' = rest first.

examples.tl: Nagpahinga muna kami sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: We rested a bit at the 7-Eleven first.

examples.tl: Magpahinga ka muna, mukhang pagod ka.
examples.en: Rest for a while, you look tired.

examples.tl: Day off ko bukas, magpapahinga lang ako sa condo.
examples.en: It's my day off tomorrow, I'll just rest at the condo.

notes.notes: Root ayos. 'Ayusin mo' = fix/arrange it. Also 'mag-ayos' = get ready (hair, face).

examples.tl: Mag-ayos ka ng kwarto mo, nagkalat.
examples.en: Tidy up your room, it's a mess.

examples.tl: Mag-aayos lang ako, five minutes.
examples.en: I'll just get ready, five minutes.

notes.notes: Root ligpit. Putting things back in place; 'ligpitin mo' = put it away. Also for clearing the table.

examples.tl: Magligpit ka ng mga damit mo sa sala.
examples.en: Put away your clothes in the living room.

examples.tl: Ligpitin na natin ang mesa, tapos na kumain.
examples.en: Let's clear the table, we're done eating.

notes.notes: 'Magkalat' = make a mess; 'nagkalat' = messy / scattered. 'Makalat' = messy (adj).

examples.tl: Dami ng kalat, dumating ang mga pamangkin ko.
examples.en: What a mess, my nieces and nephews came over.

examples.tl: Huwag kang magkalat sa sala, may bisita tayo.
examples.en: Don't make a mess in the living room, we have guests.

notes.taglish: Nag-grocery kami sa Landmark kanina.
notes.notes: Nag-grocery, naggo-grocery, maggo-grocery. 'Grocery' also means the supermarket itself.

examples.tl: Mag-grocery tayo mamaya, wala nang laman ang ref.
examples.en: Let's do groceries later, the fridge is empty.

examples.tl: Nag-grocery ako sa SM, 3,000 ang nagastos ko.
examples.en: I did groceries at SM, I spent 3,000.

notes.notes: Root palengke (wet market). Namalengke, namamalengke, mamamalengke.

examples.tl: Namalengke si Ate ng gulay at isda sa Guadalupe.
examples.en: Ate went to the market in Guadalupe for vegetables and fish.

examples.tl: Mas mura kung mamalengke ka kesa sa grocery.
examples.en: It's cheaper to shop at the market than the grocery.

notes.taglish: Mag-nap lang ako, 30 minutes.
notes.notes: Root idlip. In Taglish people say 'mag-nap' or 'power nap'; 'siesta' also understood.

examples.tl: Umidlip lang ako pagkatapos ng lunch, tapos balik sa trabaho.
examples.en: I just napped after lunch, then back to work.

examples.tl: Iidlip muna ako, gisingin mo ako ng alas-tres.
examples.en: I'll nap for a bit, wake me at three.

notes.notes: 'Buong araw' also means all day. 'Magdamag' = all night.

examples.tl: Maghapon akong nasa bahay, nag-WFH.
examples.en: I was home all day, working from home.

examples.tl: Maghapon na nakabukas ang aircon, patayin mo na.
examples.en: The aircon has been on all day, turn it off now.

notes.notes: Tuwing umaga = every morning; tuwing Sabado = every Saturday. Also 'kada'.

examples.tl: Tuwing umaga, kape muna bago lahat.
examples.en: Every morning, coffee first before anything.

examples.tl: Tuwing Linggo kami naglilinis ng unit.
examples.en: We clean the unit every Sunday.

examples.tl: Tuwing Sabado, palengke ako nang maaga.
examples.en: Every Saturday, I go to the market early.

notes.taglish: WFH ako bukas, kaya nasa condo lang ako.
notes.notes: 'Nag-WFH ako' = I worked from home. Said as letters. Also just 'WFH ako bukas'.

examples.tl: Mag-WFH ako bukas, may inspection sa unit.
examples.en: I'll work from home tomorrow, there's an inspection in the unit.

examples.tl: Nag-WFH ako buong linggo, hindi ako lumabas.
examples.en: I worked from home all week, I didn't go out.

notes.en: to go to work or school / enter
accept: to enter; to go to work/school
notes.notes: The everyday verb for going to work. 'Hindi ako pumasok' = I didn't go in / I was absent.

examples.tl: Papasok ako ng 9, pero traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: I go in at 9, but EDSA has traffic.

examples.tl: Hindi ako pumasok kahapon, may sakit ako.
examples.en: I didn't go to work yesterday, I was sick.

examples.tl: Pumasok ka ba kahapon o nag-leave ka?
examples.en: Did you go to work yesterday or did you take leave?

notes.notes: Object focus (-an). Irregular: bukas + -an drops a vowel: buksan. Also 'turn on' (buksan mo ang ilaw).

examples.tl: Binuksan ko ang aircon pagdating ko.
examples.en: I turned on the aircon when I arrived.

examples.tl: Buksan mo ang aircon, ang init.
examples.en: Turn on the aircon, it's hot.

examples.tl: Pakibuksan ang pinto, wala akong susi.
examples.en: Please open the door, I don't have a key.

notes.notes: Object focus (i-). 'Isara mo ang pinto' = close the door. For lights/appliances, 'turn off' is patayin.

examples.tl: Isinara niya ang bintana kasi umuulan.
examples.en: She closed the window because it was raining.

examples.tl: Isara mo ang bintana, uulan.
examples.en: Close the window, it's going to rain.

examples.tl: Isinara na ng guard ang gate, late na tayo.
examples.en: The guard already closed the gate, we're late.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). In daily life mostly 'turn off' (patayin mo ang ilaw/aircon). Pinatay = turned off / killed.

examples.tl: Pinatay ko na ang aircon bago umalis.
examples.en: I turned off the aircon before leaving.

examples.tl: Patayin mo ang aircon kapag aalis ka.
examples.en: Turn off the aircon when you leave.

examples.tl: Pinatay ko ang cellphone ko sa sinehan.
examples.en: I turned off my phone in the cinema.

notes.taglish: Na-lock ko ba ang pinto? Hindi ko maalala.
notes.notes: 'I-lock mo' = lock it; 'naka-lock' = locked; 'na-lock out' = locked out. Native 'ikandado' is rarer in Manila.

examples.tl: I-lock mo ang pinto bago matulog.
examples.en: Lock the door before sleeping.

examples.tl: Naka-lock ang unit, nasa guard ang spare key.
examples.en: The unit is locked, the spare key is with the guard.

notes.notes: Prepaid credit for Globe/Smart. 'Wala akong load' = I have no credit. Bought via GCash or sari-sari store.

examples.tl: Wala akong load, hindi ako maka-text.
examples.en: I have no credit, I can't text.

examples.tl: Pabili ng load, 100 Globe.
examples.en: Please buy me credit, 100 pesos Globe.

examples.tl: Wala akong load, pa-text naman.
examples.en: I have no phone credit, can you text for me?

notes.taglish: Mag-load muna ako sa GCash, wala na akong data.
notes.notes: Nag-load, naglo-load, maglo-load. 'Pa-load' = please top me up.

examples.tl: Mag-load muna ako, wala na akong data.
examples.en: Let me top up first, I'm out of data.

examples.tl: Nag-load ako ng 99 para sa isang linggong promo.
examples.en: I topped up 99 pesos for the one-week promo.

notes.notes: 'Magpalit ng dolyar' = change dollars; 'magpalit ng damit' = change clothes. Object focus 'palitan' / 'ipalit'.

examples.tl: Magpapalit ako ng 200 dollars, pwede sa mall.
examples.en: I'll exchange 200 dollars, can do it at the mall.

examples.tl: Nagpalit ako ng SIM, Smart na ako.
examples.en: I changed SIM, I'm on Smart now.

examples.tl: Magpalit ka ng damit, pawis ka.
examples.en: Change your clothes, you're sweaty.

examples.tl: Magdamag akong hindi nakatulog, maingay ang kapitbahay.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep all night, the neighbors were noisy.

examples.tl: Magdamag na nakabukas ang ilaw sa sala.
examples.en: The living room light was on all night.

examples.tl: Masakit ang ulo ko, baka kulang sa tulog.
examples.en: My head hurts, maybe I lack sleep.

examples.tl: Naumpog ang ulo ko sa cabinet.
examples.en: I bumped my head on the cabinet.

examples.tl: Namumula ang mata mo, puyat ka ba?
examples.en: Your eyes are red, did you stay up late?

examples.tl: Masakit ang mata ko sa screen, maghapon sa laptop.
examples.en: My eyes hurt from the screen, all day on the laptop.

examples.tl: Barado ang ilong ko, may sipon ako.
examples.en: My nose is blocked, I have a cold.

examples.tl: Dumudugo ang ilong niya dahil sa init.
examples.en: His nose is bleeding because of the heat.

examples.tl: May singaw ako sa bibig, hindi ako makakain ng maanghang.
examples.en: I have a mouth sore, I can't eat spicy food.

examples.tl: Takpan mo ang bibig mo kapag umuubo.
examples.en: Cover your mouth when you cough.

examples.tl: Masakit ang ngipin ko, kailangan ko ng dentista.
examples.en: My tooth hurts, I need a dentist.

examples.tl: Magtoothbrush ka, may bawang sa ngipin mo.
examples.en: Brush your teeth, there's garlic in your teeth.

examples.tl: Masakit ang tiyan ko, baka sa kinain ko sa karinderya.
examples.en: My stomach hurts, maybe from what I ate at the eatery.

examples.tl: Kumukulo ang tiyan ko, gutom na ako.
examples.en: My stomach is growling, I'm hungry.

examples.tl: Maghugas ka ng kamay, galing ka sa jeep.
examples.en: Wash your hands, you came from the jeep.

examples.tl: Nasugatan ang kamay ko sa kutsilyo.
examples.en: I cut my hand on the knife.

notes.notes: Covers foot and often the whole leg; 'binti' = lower leg, 'hita' = thigh.

examples.tl: Masakit ang paa ko, maghapon akong nakatayo.
examples.en: My feet hurt, I was standing all day.

examples.tl: Alisin mo ang sapatos, basa ang paa mo.
examples.en: Take off your shoes, your feet are wet.

notes.notes: Also 'behind': 'sa likod ng building' = behind the building.

examples.tl: Masakit ang likod ko sa upuan sa office.
examples.en: My back hurts from the office chair.

examples.tl: Pakihilot ang likod ko, ang sakit.
examples.en: Please massage my back, it hurts.

examples.tl: Nasa likod ng simbahan ang palengke.
examples.en: The market is behind the church.
examples.taglish: Nasa likod ng simbahan yung palengke, dumaan ka sa gilid.

notes.taglish: Nasa likod ng mall ang parking.

examples.tl: Masakit ang balikat ko sa bag, sobrang bigat.
examples.en: My shoulder hurts from the bag, it's so heavy.

examples.tl: Stiff ang balikat ko, kailangan ko ng massage.
examples.en: My shoulders are stiff, I need a massage.

notes.notes: Head hair only; body hair is 'balahibo'.

examples.tl: Basa pa ang buhok ko, hintayin mo ako.
examples.en: My hair is still wet, wait for me.

examples.tl: Magpapagupit ako ng buhok sa barbero sa may Guadalupe.
examples.en: I'll get a haircut at the barber near Guadalupe.

examples.tl: May sakit sa puso ang tatay ko, kaya bawal ang maalat.
examples.en: My father has heart disease, so no salty food.

examples.tl: Mabilis ang tibok ng puso ko pagkatapos ng hagdan.
examples.en: My heart was beating fast after the stairs.

examples.tl: Masakit ang leeg ko, maling unan.
examples.en: My neck hurts, wrong pillow.

examples.tl: Namamaga ang leeg niya, may lagnat din.
examples.en: His neck is swollen, he has a fever too.

examples.tl: Masakit ang tuhod ko pag-akyat ng hagdan.
examples.en: My knee hurts going up the stairs.

examples.tl: Nagasgas ang tuhod ko nung nadapa ako sa Ayala.
examples.en: I scraped my knee when I tripped at Ayala.

examples.tl: Masakit ang braso ko sa gym kahapon.
examples.en: My arms hurt from the gym yesterday.

examples.tl: Sunog ang braso ko, nakalimutan ang sunblock.
examples.en: My arm is sunburned, I forgot the sunblock.

notes.notes: Also toes: 'daliri sa paa'.

examples.tl: Naipit ang daliri ko sa pinto.
examples.en: My finger got caught in the door.

examples.tl: Nahiwa ang daliri ko habang naghihiwa ng sibuyas.
examples.en: I cut my finger while slicing onions.

notes.notes: Also 'mukhang' = looks like: 'mukhang pagod ka' = you look tired.

examples.tl: Maghilamos ka ng mukha, mamantika.
examples.en: Wash your face, it's oily.

examples.tl: Namumula ang mukha mo, ang init ba?
examples.en: Your face is red, is it the heat?

notes.notes: Formal spelling 'tainga'; everyone says 'tenga'.

examples.tl: Masakit ang tenga ko pagkatapos ng flight.
examples.en: My ear hurts after the flight.

examples.tl: Nabingi ako sa karaoke ng kapitbahay, ang lakas sa tenga.
examples.en: The neighbor's karaoke deafened me, so loud in the ears.

examples.tl: Masakit ang lalamunan ko, baka sipon na ito.
examples.en: My throat hurts, this might be a cold coming.

examples.tl: May nakabara sa lalamunan ko, tinik ng bangus.
examples.en: Something's stuck in my throat, a milkfish bone.

notes.notes: 'Masakit ang X ko' = my X hurts. Also emotional: 'masakit' = it hurts.

examples.tl: Masakit ang ulo ko, may Biogesic ka?
examples.en: My head hurts, do you have Biogesic?

examples.tl: Masakit ba? Punta tayo sa clinic.
examples.en: Does it hurt? Let's go to the clinic.

notes.notes: 'Sakit ng ulo' = headache; 'may sakit' = sick. 'Ang sakit!' = ouch, it hurts!

examples.tl: Ang sakit! Naipit ang kamay ko.
examples.en: Ouch! My hand got caught.

examples.tl: Anong sakit niya? Dengue daw.
examples.en: What's his illness? They say dengue.

notes.notes: 'May sakit ako' = I'm sick. 'Nagkasakit' = got sick. Also 'masama ang pakiramdam ko'.

examples.tl: May sakit si Ate, hindi siya makakapunta ngayon.
examples.en: Ate is sick, she can't come today.

examples.tl: May sakit ka ba? Mag-leave ka na lang.
examples.en: Are you sick? Just take the day off.

notes.notes: Also figurative: a hassle ('sakit sa ulo' = pain in the neck).

examples.tl: May sakit ng ulo ako, uminom na ako ng gamot.
examples.en: I have a headache, I already took medicine.

examples.tl: Sakit sa ulo ang traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: The traffic on EDSA is a headache.

notes.notes: 'May lagnat ako' or 'nilalagnat ako' = I have a fever.

examples.tl: May lagnat ako, 38.5 kanina.
examples.en: I have a fever, 38.5 earlier.

examples.tl: Mataas pa ang lagnat niya, dalhin natin sa ospital.
examples.en: His fever is still high, let's take him to the hospital.

notes.notes: Verb form of lagnat. Nilagnat (had a fever), nilalagnat (has), lalagnatin (will).

examples.tl: Nilalagnat ako kaya hindi ako papasok.
examples.en: I have a fever so I won't go to work.

examples.tl: Nilagnat ako ng tatlong araw pagkatapos ng bakuna.
examples.en: I had a fever for three days after the vaccine.

notes.notes: 'Umubo' = to cough; 'inuubo ako' = I have a cough.

examples.tl: Inuubo ako, dalawang linggo na.
examples.en: I've had a cough for two weeks now.

examples.tl: May ubo at sipon ang anak ko, baka trangkaso.
examples.en: My child has a cough and cold, maybe flu.

notes.notes: 'May sipon ako' or 'sinisipon ako' = I have a cold. Not 'malamig'.

examples.tl: May sipon ako, dahil sa aircon sa office.
examples.en: I have a cold, because of the office aircon.

examples.tl: Sinisipon ako, pahingi ng tissue.
examples.en: I have a runny nose, can I have a tissue.

notes.notes: 'Inaantok ako' = I'm sleepy (the usual form). 'Antok na ako' also fine.

examples.tl: Inaantok ako sa meeting, kape muna.
examples.en: I'm sleepy in the meeting, coffee first.

examples.tl: Antok na ako, tulog na ako. Good night!
examples.en: I'm sleepy, going to sleep. Good night!

notes.notes: 'Uhaw ako' or 'nauuhaw ako'.

examples.tl: Uhaw ako, may tubig ka?
examples.en: I'm thirsty, do you have water?

examples.tl: Nauuhaw ako sa init, bili tayo ng buko juice.
examples.en: I'm thirsty from the heat, let's buy coconut juice.

examples.tl: Uhaw ako, pabili ng malamig na tubig.
examples.en: I'm thirsty, let me buy cold water.

notes.notes: 'Nahihilo ako' = I'm dizzy. Also for motion sickness.

examples.tl: Nahihilo ako sa bus, bukas mo ang bintana.
examples.en: I'm getting dizzy on the bus, open the window.

examples.tl: Nahihilo ako sa init, kailangan ko ng tubig.
examples.en: I'm dizzy from the heat, I need water.

notes.notes: Root suka (vomit). 'Sumuka' = to vomit, 'nagsuka' also.

examples.tl: Nasusuka ako, sobrang amoy ng usok ng jeep.
examples.en: I feel nauseous, the jeep fumes smell so strong.

examples.tl: Sumuka siya pagkatapos uminom kagabi.
examples.en: He threw up after drinking last night.

notes.notes: 'Uminom ng gamot' = take medicine (literally drink). Biogesic = paracetamol brand everyone names.

examples.tl: Uminom ka na ng gamot bago matulog.
examples.en: Take your medicine before you sleep.

examples.tl: May gamot ka ba sa sakit ng ulo?
examples.en: Do you have medicine for a headache?

notes.notes: Address as 'Doc'. 'Magpa-doktor' = see a doctor. 'Doktora' for a woman.

examples.tl: Magpa-doktor ka na, isang linggo ka nang inuubo.
examples.en: Go see a doctor, you've been coughing for a week.

examples.tl: Ano ang sabi ng doktor? Rest lang daw.
examples.en: What did the doctor say? Just rest, he said.

notes.notes: Makati Med, St. Luke's BGC, etc. 'Na-ospital' = got hospitalized.

examples.tl: Dinala siya sa ospital kagabi, dehydrated.
examples.en: He was taken to the hospital last night, dehydrated.

examples.tl: Malapit ang Makati Med sa condo, pwedeng lakarin.
examples.en: Makati Med is close to the condo, you can walk.

examples.tl: Saan ang pinakamalapit na ospital?
examples.en: Where's the nearest hospital?
examples.taglish: Saan ang pinakamalapit na hospital? Emergency ito.

notes.taglish: Dalhin natin siya sa Makati Med.

notes.notes: Many just say 'Mercury' (Mercury Drug) or 'drugstore'. 'Parmasya' is formal.

examples.tl: Bibili lang ako ng paracetamol sa botika.
examples.en: I'll just buy paracetamol at the pharmacy.

examples.tl: May 24-hour na Mercury sa Guadalupe.
examples.en: There's a 24-hour Mercury Drug in Guadalupe.

examples.tl: May botika ba malapit dito?
examples.en: Is there a pharmacy near here?
examples.taglish: May botika ba malapit dito? Mercury or Watsons?

notes.taglish: Dumaan tayo sa Mercury, bibili ako ng Biogesic.
Magpapa-check-up ako bukas, covered ng HMO.
notes.notes: 'Magpa-check-up' = get a check-up. HMO = health insurance card.

examples.tl: May check-up ako sa doktor bukas ng umaga.
examples.en: I have a check-up with the doctor tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: Magpa-check-up ka na, matagal na yang ubo mo.
