examples.en: Get a check-up, that cough has been going on a while.

notes.notes: Sumakit (hurt), sumasakit (hurts/is hurting), sasakit (will hurt).

examples.tl: Sumakit ang tiyan ko pagkatapos kumain ng street food.
examples.en: My stomach started hurting after eating street food.

examples.tl: Sumasakit ang ulo ko kapag kulang ako sa tubig.
examples.en: My head aches when I don't drink enough water.

notes.notes: 'Gumaling' = got well. 'Magaling' alone = skilled/good at something.

examples.tl: Magaling na ako, pwede na akong pumasok.
examples.en: I'm better now, I can go to work.

examples.tl: Gumaling na ba ang anak mo? Lagnat daw.
examples.en: Has your child recovered? He had a fever, you said.

notes.notes: 'Nasugatan' = got wounded. Betadine and Band-Aid are the usual words for fixing it.

examples.tl: May sugat ako sa paa, lagyan ko ng Betadine.
examples.en: I have a cut on my foot, I'll put Betadine on it.

examples.tl: Nasugatan ang kamay niya sa lata.
examples.en: His hand got cut on the can.

notes.notes: 'May allergy ako sa X' = I'm allergic to X. 'Allergic ako sa hipon' also used.

examples.tl: May allergy ako sa hipon, huwag mo lagyan.
examples.en: I'm allergic to shrimp, don't add any.

examples.tl: Nag-allergy siya sa alikabok, puro bahing.
examples.en: He had an allergy to the dust, kept sneezing.

notes.notes: 'Pawis na pawis ako' = I'm drenched in sweat. 'Pinagpapawisan' = sweating.

examples.tl: Pawis na pawis ako, ang init sa labas.
examples.en: I'm drenched in sweat, it's so hot outside.

examples.tl: Magpalit ka, basa ng pawis ang damit mo.
examples.en: Change, your shirt is wet with sweat.

notes.notes: Root ihi. Umihi, umiihi, iihi. 'Iihi lang ako' = I'll just pee. 'Mag-CR' is the polite way.

examples.tl: Iihi lang ako, saan ang CR?
examples.en: I'll just pee, where's the restroom?

examples.tl: Umihi muna ang bata bago umalis.
examples.en: The kid peed first before leaving.

notes.notes: 'Kumusta ang pakiramdam mo?' = how are you feeling? 'Pakiramdam ko' = I feel like.

examples.tl: Kumusta ang pakiramdam mo? Okay na ba?
examples.en: How are you feeling? Okay now?

examples.tl: Pakiramdam ko lalagnatin ako.
examples.en: I feel like I'm coming down with a fever.

notes.notes: The standard way to say you feel sick. Opposite: 'maganda ang pakiramdam ko'.

examples.tl: Masama ang pakiramdam ko, mag-leave ako ngayon.
examples.en: I don't feel well, I'll take leave today.

examples.tl: Masama ang pakiramdam ni Ate, hindi siya makakapaglinis.
examples.en: Ate feels unwell, she won't be able to clean.

examples.tl: Masama ang pakiramdam ko. — Uminom ka ng gamot, magpahinga ka.
examples.en: I don't feel well. — Take some medicine, get some rest.

notes.notes: Root ginaw. Say this, not 'malamig ako'. 'Nilalamig' is also heard.

examples.tl: Giniginaw ako, hinaan mo ang aircon.
examples.en: I'm cold, turn down the aircon.

examples.tl: Giniginaw siya pero may lagnat, baka trangkaso.
examples.en: He feels cold but has a fever, might be flu.

notes.notes: Root init. Say this, not 'mainit ako' (which sounds odd). 'Ang init!' = it's so hot!

examples.tl: Naiinitan ako, buksan natin ang aircon.
examples.en: I'm hot, let's turn on the aircon.

examples.tl: Naiinitan ang bata, patayin mo ang kalan.
examples.en: The kid is hot, turn off the stove.

notes.notes: Very common word with no English equivalent. 'Napuyat ako' = I stayed up late / lacked sleep.

examples.tl: Puyat ako, alas-tres na natulog dahil sa deadline.
examples.en: I'm sleep-deprived, slept at three because of the deadline.

examples.tl: Mukhang puyat ka, kape ka muna.
examples.en: You look like you lack sleep, have coffee first.

notes.notes: Any garment or clothes in general. 'Magdamit' = to dress.

examples.tl: Dami ng damit sa sala, ligpitin mo.
examples.en: So many clothes in the living room, put them away.

examples.tl: Bili ako ng bagong damit sa Uniqlo, sale.
examples.en: I bought new clothes at Uniqlo, there was a sale.

notes.notes: 'Jeans' is also just 'jeans'. 'Maong' = denim.

examples.tl: Basa ang pantalon ko sa ulan, magpapalit ako.
examples.en: My pants got wet in the rain, I'll change.

examples.tl: Bawal ang shorts sa office, pantalon dapat.
examples.en: Shorts aren't allowed at the office, must be pants.

notes.notes: Said in English. Standard condo and weekend wear in the heat.

examples.tl: Shorts at tsinelas lang ako, lalabas lang sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: Just shorts and slippers for me, only going out to 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: Bawal ang shorts sa simbahan.
examples.en: Shorts are not allowed in church.

notes.notes: 'Rubber shoes' = sneakers. Take them off at the door in most homes.

examples.tl: Alisin mo ang sapatos sa pinto, bago ang sahig.
examples.en: Take off your shoes at the door, the floor is new.

examples.tl: Basa ang sapatos ko, baha sa Buendia.
examples.en: My shoes are wet, there was flooding on Buendia.

notes.notes: Flip-flops; everyone has a pair by the door. 'Pang-bahay' = house slippers.

examples.tl: Magtsinelas ka sa loob, malamig ang sahig.
examples.en: Wear slippers inside, the floor is cold.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang tsinelas ko? Nasa may pinto?
examples.en: Where are my slippers? By the door?

examples.tl: Wala akong malinis na medyas, hindi pa nalabhan.
examples.en: I have no clean socks, they haven't been washed.

examples.tl: Nawawala ang isang medyas ko, baka sa washing machine.
examples.en: One of my socks is missing, maybe in the washing machine.

notes.notes: For a baseball cap people say 'cap'. Sombrero = any hat, often a wide one.

examples.tl: Magsuot ka ng sombrero, sobrang init ng araw.
examples.en: Wear a hat, the sun is really hot.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang cap ko sa Grab.
examples.en: I left my cap in the Grab.

notes.notes: Both wristwatch and wall clock. 'Anong oras na sa relo mo?'

examples.tl: Anong oras na sa relo mo? Patay ang cellphone ko.
examples.en: What time is it on your watch? My phone is dead.

examples.tl: Nakalimutan ko ang relo ko sa banyo.
examples.en: I forgot my watch in the bathroom.

notes.notes: Both eyeglasses and mirror. 'Shades' = sunglasses.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang salamin ko? Hindi ko mabasa ang menu.
examples.en: Where are my glasses? I can't read the menu.

examples.tl: May salamin sa pinto ng aparador.
examples.en: There's a mirror on the wardrobe door.

notes.notes: Said in English. 'Bantayan mo ang bag ko' = watch my bag.

examples.tl: Bantayan mo ang bag ko, mag-CR lang ako.
examples.en: Watch my bag, I'll just use the restroom.

examples.tl: Nasa bag ko ang susi at wallet.
examples.en: The key and wallet are in my bag.

notes.notes: Said in English. 'Pitaka' is the native word, still used by older people.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang wallet ko sa condo, pahiram muna ng pamasahe.
examples.en: I left my wallet at the condo, lend me fare money.

examples.tl: Wala akong cash sa wallet, GCash lang.
examples.en: I have no cash in my wallet, just GCash.

notes.notes: Carry one always: for rain and for the sun. 'Magpayong' = use an umbrella.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo ang payong, uulan mamaya.
examples.en: Bring the umbrella, it'll rain later.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ulit ang payong ko sa jeep, ilang beses na ito.
examples.en: I left my umbrella in the jeep again, this has happened several times.

examples.tl: Dala ka ng payong, baka umulan mamayang hapon.
examples.en: Bring an umbrella, it might rain this afternoon.

notes.taglish: Dala ka ng payong, uulan daw mamaya.

notes.notes: 'Shirt' or 't-shirt' in English. 'Sando' = sleeveless undershirt.

examples.tl: T-shirt at shorts lang ako sa bahay.
examples.en: I just wear a t-shirt and shorts at home.

examples.tl: Puro puting t-shirt ang binili ko, mura sa Divisoria.
examples.en: I bought all white t-shirts, cheap in Divisoria.

notes.notes: In the Philippines 'polo' = a collared button-down, not a polo shirt. 'Polo shirt' = the golf type.

examples.tl: Polo ang suot ko sa office, hindi t-shirt.
examples.en: I wear a collared shirt at the office, not a t-shirt.

examples.tl: Paki-plantsa ang polo ko, may meeting ako bukas.
examples.en: Please iron my shirt, I have a meeting tomorrow.

notes.notes: Worn mostly for aircon in malls, cinemas and offices, not for weather.

examples.tl: Magdala ka ng jacket, malamig sa sinehan.
examples.en: Bring a jacket, it's cold in the cinema.

examples.tl: Bakit may jacket ka, 35 degrees sa labas?
examples.en: Why do you have a jacket on, it's 35 degrees outside?

notes.notes: Root suot. Nagsuot, nagsusuot, magsusuot. 'Isuot mo' = wear it. 'Suot' = outfit.

examples.tl: Magsuot ka ng jacket, malamig sa office.
examples.en: Wear a jacket, it's cold at the office.

examples.tl: Anong isusuot ko sa party? Smart casual daw.
examples.en: What should I wear to the party? Smart casual, they said.

notes.notes: For clothes, furniture, people in a car. 'Hindi kasya' = doesn't fit. 'Kumasya' = did fit.

examples.tl: Hindi na kasya ang jeans ko, dami ng kinain sa Pasko.
examples.en: My jeans don't fit anymore, I ate too much at Christmas.

examples.tl: Kasya ba ang sofa sa elevator?
examples.en: Will the sofa fit in the elevator?

notes.notes: Filipinos say 'cellphone' or 'phone', texted as 'cp'. Never 'mobile'.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang cellphone ko? Nasa kama?
examples.en: Where's my phone? On the bed?

examples.tl: Nabasag ang screen ng cellphone ko, nalaglag sa jeep.
examples.en: My phone screen cracked, it fell in the jeep.

notes.notes: Said in English. 'Pahiram ng charger' is a daily phrase.

examples.tl: Pahiram ng charger, lowbat na ako.
examples.en: Lend me a charger, my battery's low.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang charger ko sa office.
examples.en: I left my charger at the office.

notes.taglish: Mag-charge muna ako, 5% na lang.
notes.notes: Nag-charge, nagcha-charge, magcha-charge. 'I-charge mo' = charge it. 'Naka-charge' = charging/plugged in.

examples.tl: Mag-charge muna ako, lowbat na ako.
examples.en: Let me charge first, my battery's low.

examples.tl: I-charge mo ang powerbank bago tayo umalis.
examples.en: Charge the powerbank before we leave.

notes.notes: From 'low battery'. Also jokingly for a tired person: 'lowbat na ako'.

examples.tl: Lowbat na ako, mag-text ka lang kung saan tayo magkikita.
examples.en: My battery's low, just text me where we'll meet.

examples.tl: Lowbat ang cellphone ko kaya hindi ako nakasagot.
examples.en: My phone was low on battery so I couldn't answer.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo ang laptop, mag-WFH tayo sa coffee shop.
examples.en: Bring the laptop, let's work from a coffee shop.

examples.tl: Namatay ang laptop ko sa gitna ng meeting.
examples.en: My laptop died in the middle of the meeting.

notes.notes: Pronounced 'tee-vee'. 'Manood ng TV' = watch TV.

examples.tl: Patayin mo ang TV, walang nanonood.
examples.en: Turn off the TV, nobody's watching.

examples.tl: Nanood lang kami ng TV buong Linggo.
examples.en: We just watched TV all Sunday.

notes.notes: For the TV and the aircon. 'Nasaan ang remote?' is heard in every Filipino home.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang remote ng aircon?
examples.en: Where's the aircon remote?

examples.tl: Ubos na ang baterya ng remote, bili ka ng AA.
examples.en: The remote's batteries are dead, buy some AA.

notes.notes: 'Mabagal ang wifi' = the wifi is slow. PLDT, Globe, Converge are the providers.

examples.tl: Mabagal ang wifi, umuulan kasi.
examples.en: The wifi is slow, because it's raining.

examples.tl: Ano ang password ng wifi niyo?
examples.en: What's your wifi password?

notes.notes: Pronounced 'day-ta'. 'Wala akong data' = I'm out of mobile data. Bought as 'promo' with load.

examples.tl: Wala akong data, hindi ako maka-Grab.
examples.en: I have no data, I can't book a Grab.

examples.tl: Mag-data ka lang, walang wifi sa jeep.
examples.en: Just use your data, there's no wifi on the jeep.

notes.notes: Root saksak (also 'stab'). 'Nakasaksak' = plugged in. 'Tanggalin sa saksakan' = unplug.

examples.tl: Isaksak mo ang charger sa extension.
examples.en: Plug the charger into the power strip.

examples.tl: Nakasaksak pa ba ang plantsa? Tanggalin mo.
examples.en: Is the iron still plugged in? Unplug it.

notes.notes: Also just 'outlet'. Philippines uses 220V with US-style flat plugs.

examples.tl: May saksakan ba malapit sa mesa? Kailangan ko mag-charge.
examples.en: Is there an outlet near the table? I need to charge.

examples.tl: Kulang ang saksakan sa kwarto, bili ka ng extension.
examples.en: Not enough outlets in the room, buy a power strip.

notes.notes: 'Extension' or 'extension cord' = power strip. Every condo desk has one.

examples.tl: Pahiram ng extension, isa lang ang saksakan dito.
examples.en: Lend me a power strip, there's only one outlet here.

examples.tl: Huwag mong isaksak ang aircon sa extension, delikado.
examples.en: Don't plug the aircon into the extension, it's dangerous.

examples.tl: Ano ang password ng wifi? Nasa router?
examples.en: What's the wifi password? On the router?

examples.tl: Nakalimutan ko ang password ng GCash ko.
examples.en: I forgot my GCash password.

notes.notes: Essential for brownouts and long commutes.

examples.tl: Dala ka ng powerbank, mahaba ang biyahe.
examples.en: Bring a power bank, it's a long trip.

examples.tl: Naka-charge na ang powerbank, nasa mesa.
examples.en: The power bank is charged, it's on the table.

notes.notes: Standing wardrobe or cabinet. Many just say 'cabinet' or 'closet'.

examples.tl: Ilagay mo sa aparador ang mga naplantsang damit.
examples.en: Put the ironed clothes in the wardrobe.

examples.tl: Puno na ang aparador, mag-donate ka ng damit.
examples.en: The wardrobe is full, donate some clothes.

notes.notes: The condo unit phone to the lobby or guard.

examples.tl: Tumawag ang guard sa intercom, may bisita ka.
examples.en: The guard called on the intercom, you have a visitor.

examples.tl: Sira ang intercom namin, text na lang sa guard.
examples.en: Our intercom is broken, we just text the guard.

notes.notes: Root kalat. Nagkalat, nagkakalat, magkakalat. 'Nagkalat' also = is lying around everywhere.

examples.tl: Huwag kang magkalat sa kusina, kakalinis lang ni Ate.
examples.en: Don't make a mess in the kitchen, Ate just cleaned.

examples.tl: Nagkalat ang mga damit sa sahig.
examples.en: Clothes are scattered on the floor.

notes.taglish: Nag-sick leave ako, nilalagnat ako.
notes.notes: 'Mag-leave' = take a day off; 'SL' = sick leave, 'VL' = vacation leave.

examples.tl: Mag-sick leave ka na lang, may lagnat ka.
examples.en: Just take sick leave, you have a fever.

examples.tl: Nag-SL ako kahapon, masama ang pakiramdam ko.
examples.en: I took sick leave yesterday, I felt unwell.

notes.notes: Traditional Filipino massage; also the masseuse. 'Magpahilot' = get a massage. Spas say 'massage'.

examples.tl: Magpapahilot ako, masakit ang likod ko.
examples.en: I'll get a massage, my back hurts.

examples.tl: May hilot sa may palengke, 300 lang.
examples.en: There's a masseuse near the market, only 300.

notes.notes: 'Magpa-dentista' = go to the dentist. Also 'dentist'.

examples.tl: Magpa-dentista ka na, matagal nang masakit ang ngipin mo.
examples.en: Go to the dentist, your tooth has hurt for a long time.

examples.tl: May appointment ako sa dentista sa Sabado, cleaning lang.
examples.en: I have a dentist appointment on Saturday, just a cleaning.

notes.notes: Said in English. 'Uminom ng vitamins' = take vitamins.

examples.tl: Uminom ka ng vitamins araw-araw para hindi magkasakit.
examples.en: Take vitamins every day so you don't get sick.

examples.tl: Nakalimutan ko ang vitamins ko ngayong umaga.
examples.en: I forgot my vitamins this morning.

notes.notes: Root hilamos. Specific to the face; hands = maghugas, body = maligo.

examples.tl: Maghilamos ka muna, may muta ka pa.
examples.en: Wash your face first, you still have eye gunk.

examples.tl: Naghilamos lang ako, hindi na ako naligo.
examples.en: I just washed my face, I didn't shower anymore.

notes.notes: Native word; 'sipilyo' = toothbrush. In Manila 'mag-toothbrush' is more common.

examples.tl: Magsipilyo ka bago matulog.
examples.en: Brush your teeth before sleeping.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng bagong sipilyo, luma na yan.
examples.en: Buy a new toothbrush, that one's old.

notes.taglish: Nag-mop na ako ng sahig, huwag kang tumapak muna.
notes.notes: Nag-mop, nagmo-mop, magmo-mop. The mop itself is 'mop'.

examples.tl: Mag-mop ka ng sahig pagkatapos magwalis.
examples.en: Mop the floor after sweeping.

examples.tl: Basa pa ang sahig, kaka-mop lang.
examples.en: The floor is still wet, it was just mopped.

notes.notes: Said in English. 'Sapin' = sheet/lining; 'kobre-kama' is old-fashioned.

examples.tl: Palitan mo ang bedsheet, Linggo na.
examples.en: Change the bedsheet, it's Sunday.

examples.tl: Nasa labahan ang bedsheet, gamitin mo muna ang luma.
examples.en: The bedsheet is in the wash, use the old one for now.

notes.notes: Said in English. 'Balkonahe' is the Tagalog word, rarely used in Manila.

examples.tl: Bawal magsampay sa balcony, sabi ng admin.
examples.en: No hanging laundry on the balcony, says the admin.

examples.tl: Nag-kape ako sa balcony, ganda ng view ng BGC.
examples.en: I had coffee on the balcony, great view of BGC.

notes.taglish: Kain tayo!
notes.notes: Root of kumain. Said alone as an invitation; 'Kain tayo' / 'Tara, kain' = let's eat. Polite reply if declining: 'Busog pa po.'

examples.tl: Kain na! Lumalamig na ang ulam.
examples.en: Eat now! The food is getting cold.

examples.tl: Tara, kain muna tayo bago umuwi.
examples.en: Come on, let's eat first before going home.
examples.taglish: Tara, kain muna tayo sa BGC bago umuwi.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Object focus: kainin. The bare root 'Kain tayo!' is the everyday invitation.

examples.tl: Kumain na kami sa Jollibee kanina.
examples.en: We already ate at Jollibee earlier.
examples.taglish: Kumain na kami, nag-Jollibee lang.

examples.tl: Kumain na ba kayo?
examples.en: Have you (all) eaten yet?
examples.taglish: Kumain na ba kayo? Order na tayo kung hindi pa.

examples.tl: Kakain kami sa labas mamaya.
examples.en: We're eating out later.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). Completed uses the -in- infix: kinain. 'Kainin mo na' = eat it now.

examples.tl: Kinain ng pusa ang tira.
examples.en: The cat ate the leftovers.

examples.tl: Kainin mo na yung tira, masisira pa.
examples.en: Eat the leftovers already, they'll spoil.

examples.tl: Hindi ko kinain yung sili.
examples.en: I didn't eat the chili.

notes.notes: Also means a meal event ('may kainan sa office'). 'Kainan' is any eating place, from carinderia to restaurant.

examples.tl: May bagong kainan sa may Kalayaan, subukan natin.
examples.en: There's a new eatery near Kalayaan, let's try it.

examples.tl: May kainan mamaya sa office, free lunch.
examples.en: There's a meal thing later at the office, free lunch.
examples.taglish: May kainan mamaya sa office, free lunch daw.

notes.notes: Core concept: anything eaten with kanin. 'Ano'ng ulam?' is the daily question. Carinderias display ulam in trays.

examples.tl: Ano'ng ulam natin ngayong gabi?
examples.en: What's our dish for tonight?

examples.tl: Dalawang ulam at isang kanin po.
examples.en: Two dishes and one rice, please.

notes.notes: Cooked rice. Uncooked is bigas; the plant is palay. 'Extra rice' and 'unli rice' are used as-is.

examples.tl: Isa pang kanin po.
examples.en: One more rice, please.

examples.tl: Wala akong kanin, keto ako ngayon.
examples.en: No rice for me, I'm doing keto now.
examples.taglish: No rice ako ngayon, keto kasi.

notes.notes: Sold by the kilo at the palengke or grocery. Kanin once cooked.

examples.tl: Bumili ka ng limang kilo ng bigas sa palengke.
examples.en: Buy five kilos of rice at the market.

notes.notes: Spanish loan, a real meal slot around 3-4 PM (and ~10 AM). Verb: mag-merienda. Pancit, turon, halo-halo are typical.

examples.tl: Merienda muna tayo, ang tagal pa ng dinner.
examples.en: Let's have a snack first, dinner is still far off.

examples.tl: Ano'ng merienda ninyo sa office?
examples.en: What's your snack at the office?
examples.taglish: Ano'ng merienda niyo sa office? Pa-order ako.

notes.notes: Noun from kain. 'Foods' as a plural is common Philippine English.

examples.tl: Masarap ang pagkain dito pero mahal.
examples.en: The food here is good but expensive.

examples.tl: May natirang pagkain pa sa ref.
examples.en: There's still leftover food in the fridge.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in); o becomes u: inumin. Vowel root takes in- prefix: ininom. Inumin as a noun = a drink.

examples.tl: Ininom ko na yung gamot kanina.
examples.en: I already took the medicine earlier.

examples.tl: Ano'ng inumin niyo? Iced tea o softdrinks?
examples.en: What will you have to drink? Iced tea or soda?

examples.tl: May inumin ba sa package na ito?
examples.en: Does this package include a drink?

notes.notes: Actor focus (um- before a vowel root). Object focus: inumin. Said alone it often means drinking alcohol.

examples.tl: Umiinom siya ng kape tuwing umaga.
examples.en: He drinks coffee every morning.

examples.tl: Uminom ka ng maraming tubig, mainit ngayon.
examples.en: Drink lots of water, it's hot today.

examples.tl: Inom tayo sa Poblacion sa Friday.
examples.en: Let's go drinking in Poblacion on Friday.

notes.notes: 'Umorder' also common. 'I-order' = order it. 'Order na tayo' = let's order.

examples.tl: Nag-order ako sa GrabFood, 30 minutes daw.
examples.en: I ordered on GrabFood, 30 minutes they said.

examples.tl: Mag-oorder pa ba kayo o bill out na?
examples.en: Are you ordering more or shall we get the bill?

examples.tl: Nag-order na ako ng Grab Food, darating sa 30 minutes.
examples.en: I already ordered Grab Food, it arrives in 30 minutes.

notes.taglish: Order na tayo.

notes.notes: 'Pa-' + verb = request to have something done. Follow with 'ng' + item. Used in person and in chat/Viber group orders.

examples.tl: Pa-order po ng isang tapsilog at isang kape.
examples.en: I'd like to order one tapsilog and one coffee, please.

notes.notes: paki- + bigay. Add 'po' for politeness. Follow with 'ng' + thing and 'sa' + person. Also 'pakiabot' (pass, hand over).

examples.tl: Pakibigay po ng toyo.
examples.en: Please give me the soy sauce.

examples.tl: Pakibigay sa kanya yung sukli.
examples.en: Please hand him the change.

notes.en: may I have; please give me
notes.notes: pa- + hingi (ask for). Softer than pakibigay; add 'po' and 'ng'. Used for both free and paid items.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng tubig.
examples.en: May I have some water, please.

examples.tl: Pahingi ng isang kagat ng burger mo.
examples.en: Give me one bite of your burger.

notes.notes: 'Isa pa po' to the waiter; 'isa pa nga' casual. 'Isa pa' also means 'also/another thing' in conversation.

examples.tl: Isa pa pong kanin.
examples.en: One more rice, please.

examples.tl: Isa pa, ate! Yung beer.
examples.en: One more, miss! The beer.

examples.tl: Isa pa pong kanin. — Sige po.
examples.en: One more rice, please. — Okay.

notes.notes: Standard way to ask for the check in Manila restaurants. Often with a hand gesture of writing in the air. 'Chit' is the older word.

examples.tl: Ate, bill out po.
examples.en: Miss, the bill please.

examples.tl: Bill out na tayo, late na.
examples.en: Let's get the bill, it's late.

notes.notes: Older/colloquial word for the bill, still heard ('Pakikuha ng chit'). Younger staff say 'bill'.

examples.tl: Pakikuha po ng chit.
examples.en: Please bring the bill.

notes.notes: Said as-is. Cashiers ask 'Dine-in or take-out?' Also 'pabalot' for wrapping leftovers.

examples.tl: Take-out po, isang chickenjoy.
examples.en: To go, please, one chickenjoy.

examples.tl: Take-out na lang, wala nang upuan.
examples.en: Let's just take out, there are no more seats.

notes.notes: The standard counter question is 'Dine-in or take-out po?' Answer with either word plus 'po'.

examples.tl: Dine-in po, para sa dalawa.
examples.en: Dine in, please, for two.

notes.en: I'd like to buy (at a counter)
accept: I'd like to buy / please buy for me
notes.notes: pa- + bili. The opener at a sari-sari store, 7-Eleven or street stall. Follow with 'ng' + item. Also = please buy for me ('Pabili ako ng yelo').

examples.tl: Pabili po ng isang Coke at yelo.
examples.en: I'd like one Coke and ice, please.

examples.tl: Pabili ako ng pandesal pag-uwi mo.
examples.en: Buy me pandesal on your way home.

examples.tl: Pabili po ng isang Coke sakto at yelo.
examples.en: I'd like a Coke sakto and some ice please.

notes.taglish: Libre ko.
notes.notes: 'Libre ko' = my treat. 'Ilibre mo ako' = treat me. 'Libre' also means free time (libre ka ba bukas?).

examples.tl: Libre ko ngayon, birthday ko kasi.
examples.en: My treat today, it's my birthday.

examples.tl: Libre ang tubig pero bayad ang yelo.
examples.en: The water is free but the ice costs.

examples.tl: Libre ko kayo ng kape mamaya, sahod ko.
examples.en: Coffee's on me later, it's my payday.

notes.notes: Not expected when there is a service charge; small tips are welcome in carinderias and for riders. 'Keep the change' = 'Sa iyo na ang sukli.'

examples.tl: May service charge na, pero nag-iwan pa rin ako ng tip.
examples.en: There's already a service charge, but I still left a tip.

examples.tl: Bigyan mo ng tip yung rider, umulan e.
examples.en: Give the rider a tip, it rained.

examples.tl: Bigyan mo ng tip yung rider, umulan pa.
examples.en: Give the rider a tip, it even rained.

notes.notes: Most sit-down restaurants add 10% on top of VAT. Check the receipt before tipping.

examples.tl: May service charge ba dito? Tingnan mo sa resibo.
examples.en: Is there a service charge here? Check the receipt.

notes.notes: 'Hati tayo' = let's split (the bill or the food). 'Kalahati' = a half. 'Paghatian' = share among.

examples.tl: Hati tayo sa isang order ng sisig, malaki e.
examples.en: Let's share one order of sisig, it's big.

notes.notes: 'Unli' = unlimited, used for rice, wings, samgyupsal. 'Extra rice' = one extra serving.

examples.tl: Unli rice dito, kaya sulit.
examples.en: Unlimited rice here, so it's worth it.

examples.tl: Extra rice po, isa.
examples.en: Extra rice please, one.

notes.notes: 'Pakidagdag' = please add more. 'Dagdag bayad' = additional charge. 'Dagdagan mo' = add to it.

examples.tl: Pakidagdag ng sabaw, ate.
examples.en: Please add more soup, miss.

examples.tl: May dagdag na bayad ang extra sauce.
examples.en: Extra sauce has an additional charge.

notes.notes: Ask the server or anyone at the next table. Also 'Ano'ng bestseller niyo?'

examples.tl: Kuya, ano'ng masarap dito? First time ko.
examples.en: Sir, what's good here? It's my first time.

examples.tl: Anong masarap dito? — Yung crispy pata po, bestseller.
examples.en: What's good here? — The crispy pata, it's the bestseller.

notes.notes: Standard at a carinderia where there's no menu. 'Meron' is the spoken form of mayroon.

examples.tl: Ate, ano pong meron? Wala na bang sinigang?
examples.en: Miss, what do you have? No more sinigang?

notes.notes: 'Ubos na po' = we've run out. 'Naubos' = got used up. 'Ubusin mo' = finish it (all).

examples.tl: Ubos na po ang lechon kawali.
examples.en: The lechon kawali is sold out.

examples.tl: Ubusin mo yung kanin mo, sayang.
examples.en: Finish your rice, it'd be a waste.

notes.notes: From Spanish exacto. 'Sakto lang ang anghang' = the spice is just right. Also means 'just enough money'.

examples.tl: Sakto lang ang alat, hindi sobra.
examples.en: The saltiness is just right, not too much.

examples.tl: Sakto lang yung pera ko, walang sukli. — Okay lang, kuya.
examples.en: My money is just exact, no change needed. — That's fine.

examples.tl: Sakto po, bente.
examples.en: Exact amount, twenty.

notes.notes: 'Patikim' = let me try some / here, try some. 'Tikman mo' = taste it. Common at the palengke for fruit.

examples.tl: Patikim naman ng kare-kare mo.
examples.en: Let me have a taste of your kare-kare.

examples.tl: Tikman mo muna bago ka maglagay ng patis.
examples.en: Taste it first before you add fish sauce.

notes.notes: 'Tira' as a noun = what's left. 'Natira' = was left over. 'Pabalot' to take leftovers home.

examples.tl: Yung tira kagabi, iprito mo lang bukas.
examples.en: Last night's leftovers, just fry them tomorrow.

notes.notes: pa- + balot (wrap). The way to ask for leftovers to be packed. Also used at the counter: 'Pabalot na lang' = make it to go.

examples.tl: Ate, pabalot po itong natira.
examples.en: Miss, please wrap up these leftovers.

examples.tl: Pabalot na lang, kakainin ko sa condo.
examples.en: Just wrap it, I'll eat it at the condo.

notes.notes: Change the number: para sa tatlo, para sa apat. For portions: 'good for two' is used as-is on menus.

examples.tl: Table para sa dalawa po.
examples.en: A table for two, please.

examples.tl: Yung platter, good for two daw.
examples.en: The platter is good for two, they say.

examples.tl: Ilan po kayo? — Para sa dalawa po.
examples.en: How many are you? — For two.

notes.notes: 'Sawa na ako sa manok' = I'm sick of chicken. 'Nakakasawa' = gets tiring. 'Hindi nakakasawa' = never gets old.

examples.tl: Sawa na ako sa Jollibee, iba naman tayo.
examples.en: I'm tired of Jollibee, let's go somewhere else.

examples.tl: Hindi nakakasawa ang adobo.
examples.en: Adobo never gets old.

notes.notes: Cheap, home-style ulam in trays; you point at what you want. 'Turo-turo' is the same idea (turo = point).

examples.tl: Kain tayo sa carinderia, 80 pesos lang ang ulam at kanin.
examples.en: Let's eat at the carinderia, rice and a dish is only 80 pesos.

notes.notes: From turo (point): you point at the dishes in trays. Same as carinderia; slightly more casual term.

examples.tl: Sa turo-turo, tinuturo mo lang yung gusto mong ulam.
examples.en: At a turo-turo, you just point at the dish you want.

notes.notes: pa- + English verb, very common Taglish. 'Mag-Grab Food' also works. Rider = delivery driver.

examples.tl: Pa-deliver na lang tayo, umuulan.
examples.en: Let's just have it delivered, it's raining.

examples.tl: Nandito na daw yung rider sa lobby.
examples.en: The rider is already in the lobby, they say.

notes.notes: Used as a verb too: 'mag-Grab Food', 'nag-Grab ako'. Foodpanda is the other big app.

examples.tl: Mag-Grab Food na lang tayo, tamad akong lumabas.
examples.en: Let's just order Grab Food, I'm too lazy to go out.

examples.tl: Ang mahal ng delivery fee sa Grab ngayon.
examples.en: The delivery fee on Grab is expensive right now.

notes.en: adobo (meat stewed in soy, vinegar, garlic)
notes.notes: The unofficial national dish. Chicken (manok) or pork (baboy). 'Adobong manok', 'adobong baboy'. Keeps well; classic baon.

examples.tl: Adobong manok ang baon ko ngayon.
examples.en: Chicken adobo is my packed lunch today.

examples.tl: Mas masarap ang adobo kinabukasan.
examples.en: Adobo tastes better the next day.

notes.notes: Sour (maasim) soup with pork, shrimp or fish and vegetables. 'Sinigang na baboy', 'sinigang na hipon'. Comfort food on rainy days.

examples.tl: Umuulan, perfect sa sinigang na baboy.
examples.en: It's raining, perfect for pork sinigang.

examples.tl: Pakidagdag ng sabaw ng sinigang.
examples.en: Please add more sinigang broth.

notes.notes: Clear chicken soup with ginger (luya), green papaya or sayote, and malunggay or chili leaves. The go-to when sick.

examples.tl: May sipon ako, tinola ang hanap ko.
examples.en: I have a cold, I'm craving tinola.

notes.notes: Peanut-based stew, usually oxtail and tripe, always served with bagoong on the side. Fiesta/Sunday dish.

examples.tl: Hindi kumpleto ang kare-kare kung walang bagoong.
examples.en: Kare-kare isn't complete without bagoong.

notes.notes: Chopped pork (face/ears), onion, kalamansi, chili, often with egg on a sizzling plate. The number one pulutan.

examples.tl: Isang sisig at dalawang beer, kuya.
examples.en: One sisig and two beers, sir.

examples.tl: Pakilagay ng itlog sa sisig.
examples.en: Please put an egg on the sisig.

notes.notes: Centerpiece of fiestas, Christmas and birthdays. 'Lechon kawali' is deep-fried pork belly, a different dish. 'Lechon manok' = roast chicken.

examples.tl: May lechon sa birthday ni Tita.
examples.en: There's lechon at Auntie's birthday.

examples.tl: Lechon kawali at kanin, tapos sawsawan na Mang Tomas.
examples.en: Lechon kawali with rice, then Mang Tomas sauce.

notes.notes: 'Lumpiang Shanghai' = small fried meat rolls (party staple). 'Lumpiang sariwa' = fresh (unfried). 'Lumpiang gulay/togue' = vegetable rolls.

examples.tl: Laging may lumpiang Shanghai sa handaan.
examples.en: There's always lumpiang Shanghai at a party.

notes.notes: Any noodle dish: pancit canton (stir-fried), bihon (rice noodles), palabok (with orange sauce). Served on birthdays for long life.

examples.tl: Pancit para sa mahabang buhay, birthday ko kasi.
examples.en: Noodles for long life, since it's my birthday.

examples.tl: Pancit canton at itlog, tapos na ang merienda.
examples.en: Instant pancit canton and an egg, that's my snack done.

notes.en: garlic rice + fried egg combo meal
notes.notes: SInangag + itLOG. Add the meat as a prefix: tapsilog, longsilog, tosilog, bangsilog, hotsilog, cornsilog. A 'tapsihan' sells them 24/7.

examples.tl: Ano'ng silog mo? Tapsilog o longsilog?
examples.en: Which silog do you want? Tapsilog or longsilog?

examples.tl: Open 24 hours yung tapsihan sa may corner.
examples.en: The tapsilog place at the corner is open 24 hours.

notes.en: beef tapa, garlic rice, fried egg
notes.notes: TAPa + SInangag + itLOG. The most common silog. Comes with sawsawan of suka and sibuyas.

examples.tl: Isang tapsilog po, over easy yung itlog.
examples.en: One tapsilog please, egg over easy.

notes.notes: LONGganisa + SInangag + itLOG.

examples.tl: Longsilog ang favorite ko, matamis yung longganisa.
examples.en: Longsilog is my favorite, the sausage is sweet.

notes.notes: TOcino + SInangag + itLOG. Sweet cured pork.

examples.tl: Tosilog para sa bata, hindi maanghang.
examples.en: Tosilog for the kid, it's not spicy.

notes.notes: Thin beef marinated in soy, garlic, kalamansi, then fried. The 'tap' in tapsilog. Not the Spanish tapas.

examples.tl: Masarap ang tapa nila, hindi matigas.
examples.en: Their tapa is good, not tough.

notes.notes: Regional styles: sweet (hamonado, e.g. Pampanga) or garlicky-sour (recado, e.g. Vigan, Lucban). Breakfast staple.

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng Vigan longganisa sa palengke.
examples.en: I bought Vigan longganisa at the market.

notes.notes: Red, sweet, cured pork slices, fried for breakfast. Sold in packs in every grocery.

examples.tl: Tocino at sinangag, tapos kape, solb na ang umaga.
examples.en: Tocino and garlic rice, then coffee, and the morning is sorted.

notes.notes: Pritong itlog = fried egg; nilagang itlog = boiled egg; itlog na maalat = salted duck egg (red shell). Also slang for zero/nothing.

examples.tl: Dalawang itlog po, sunny side up.
examples.en: Two eggs please, sunny side up.

examples.tl: Wala na tayong itlog, bili ka sa tindahan.
examples.en: We're out of eggs, buy some at the store.

notes.notes: Common fish: bangus (milkfish), tilapia, galunggong (GG), tuna. 'Pritong isda' = fried fish; 'inihaw na isda' = grilled.

examples.tl: Pritong isda at kamatis, ulam ng probinsya.
examples.en: Fried fish and tomatoes, a provincial meal.

examples.tl: Sariwa pa ba itong isda?
examples.en: Is this fish still fresh?

notes.notes: Also the live bird. 'Pritong manok' = fried chicken; 'inihaw na manok' = grilled; 'lechon manok' = roast chicken.

examples.tl: Manok na lang ulit? Sawa na ako.
examples.en: Chicken again? I'm sick of it.

examples.tl: Isang kilo ng manok, pakihiwa na.
examples.en: One kilo of chicken, please cut it up.

notes.notes: Both the animal and the meat. Liempo = belly, kasim = shoulder, pata = hock. Also slang for messy/greedy.

examples.tl: Baboy o manok ang adobo niyo?
examples.en: Is your adobo pork or chicken?

examples.tl: Hindi ako kumakain ng baboy.
examples.en: I don't eat pork.

notes.notes: Stress matters: báka = cow/beef; bakâ = maybe. 'Karne ng baka' = beef. Bulalo and tapa are beef dishes.

examples.tl: Mahal ang baka ngayon sa palengke.
examples.en: Beef is expensive at the market now.

examples.tl: Baka? Baka hindi, baboy yan.
examples.en: Beef? Maybe not, that's pork.

notes.notes: 'Sinigang na hipon', 'halabos na hipon' (steamed in salt water). Say 'allergic ako sa hipon' if needed.

examples.tl: Allergic ako sa hipon, may hipon ba dito?
examples.en: I'm allergic to shrimp, is there shrimp in this?

notes.notes: Inihaw na pusit (grilled stuffed squid) and calamares (fried rings) are common pulutan.

examples.tl: Order tayo ng inihaw na pusit, pampulutan.
examples.en: Let's order grilled squid as bar food.

notes.notes: 'Ginisang gulay' = sauteed vegetables; 'lumpiang gulay'. 'Vegetarian' is said in English.

examples.tl: Kain ka ng gulay, hindi puro karne.
examples.en: Eat vegetables, not just meat.

examples.tl: May gulay lang ba kayo na ulam? Vegetarian ako.
examples.en: Do you have a vegetable-only dish? I'm vegetarian.

notes.notes: Sold by the kilo at the palengke or from a cart. Ask 'Hinog na ba?' (is it ripe?).

examples.tl: Bumili tayo ng prutas pang-dessert.
examples.en: Let's buy fruit for dessert.

notes.notes: Hinog (ripe, yellow) or hilaw (green, eaten with bagoong). Guimaras and Cebu mangoes are famous. 'Mango' is also said.

examples.tl: Manggang hilaw at bagoong, favorite ko.
examples.en: Green mango with bagoong, my favorite.

examples.tl: Magkano kilo ng mangga?
examples.en: How much per kilo of mangoes?

notes.notes: Varieties: lakatan (sweet yellow), latundan, saba (cooking banana, used in turon and banana cue).

examples.tl: Saging ang baon ko para sa gym.
examples.en: I packed a banana for the gym.

notes.notes: Mature coconut, grated for gata (coconut milk) and kakanin. Young coconut for drinking is buko.

examples.tl: May gata ng niyog ang laing at Bicol express.
examples.en: Laing and Bicol express have coconut milk.

notes.notes: Drinking coconut. Buko juice, buko pandan (dessert), buko pie (Laguna). Sold fresh from carts and 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: Pabili ng buko juice, ang init.
examples.en: Let me buy coconut juice, it's so hot.

examples.tl: Pasalubong na buko pie galing Laguna.
examples.en: Buko pie from Laguna as a homecoming gift.

notes.notes: Tiny sour citrus squeezed into sawsawan, pancit, sisig, and juice. 'Kalamansi juice' is on most menus.

examples.tl: Pigain mo ang kalamansi sa pancit.
examples.en: Squeeze the kalamansi onto the noodles.

examples.tl: Isang kalamansi juice, walang asukal.
examples.en: One kalamansi juice, no sugar.

notes.notes: Stress: sukà = vinegar, súka = vomit. Used in adobo, paksiw, and as dip with garlic and chili (sukang may sili).

examples.tl: Pahingi ng suka para sa chicharon.
examples.en: Give me some vinegar for the pork rinds.

notes.notes: Toyo + kalamansi = toyomansi, the all-purpose dip. 'May toyo' also slangily means someone is acting crazy.

examples.tl: Toyo at kalamansi ang sawsawan ng inihaw.
examples.en: Soy sauce and kalamansi is the dip for grilled food.

notes.notes: Salty fermented fish sauce. Seasoning for sinigang, tinola, and as a dip with kalamansi and sili.

examples.tl: Lagyan mo ng kaunting patis ang sinigang.
examples.en: Put a little fish sauce in the sinigang.

notes.notes: Bagoong alamang (shrimp) goes with kare-kare and green mango; bagoong isda is for pinakbet. Strong smell, strong love.

examples.tl: Ang bagoong ay para sa kare-kare at manggang hilaw.
examples.en: Bagoong is for kare-kare and green mango.

notes.notes: 'Maalat' = salty. 'Pakiabot ng asin' at the table. Rock salt is used for itlog na maalat.

examples.tl: Kulang sa asin yung sabaw.
examples.en: The soup needs more salt.

notes.notes: Whole peppercorns (buong paminta) go in adobo. Bell pepper is 'bell pepper'; chili is sili.

examples.tl: Lagyan mo ng buong paminta ang adobo.
examples.en: Put whole peppercorns in the adobo.

notes.notes: 'Walang asukal' = no sugar. 'Matamis' = sweet. Coffee shops ask 'sugar level?' in English.

examples.tl: Kape na walang asukal, gatas lang.
examples.en: Coffee with no sugar, just milk.

examples.tl: Ubos na ang asukal, bili ka sa Seven.
examples.en: We're out of sugar, buy some at 7-Eleven.

notes.notes: 'Mamantika' = oily/greasy. Sold tingi in small bags at sari-sari stores.

examples.tl: Sobrang mamantika ang pritong manok nila.
examples.en: Their fried chicken is very greasy.

examples.tl: Pabili ng mantika, pang-prito.
examples.en: Buy cooking oil, for frying.

notes.notes: From sawsaw (to dip). Toyomansi, suka with garlic, Mang Tomas, bagoong. Diners mix their own.

examples.tl: Ano'ng sawsawan mo sa lumpia? Suka o sweet chili?
examples.en: What's your dip for lumpia? Vinegar or sweet chili?

examples.tl: Pakilagay ng sawsawan sa take-out.
examples.en: Please include dipping sauce with the take-out.

notes.notes: From pulot (pick up). Sisig, chicharon, mani, inihaw. 'Pampulutan' = something to serve as pulutan.

examples.tl: Ano'ng pulutan natin? Sisig at chicharon?
examples.en: What's our bar food? Sisig and pork rinds?

notes.notes: Umbrella word: puto, kutsinta, suman, bibingka, biko, sapin-sapin. Sold at the palengke and as pasalubong.

examples.tl: Bumili ng kakanin si Lola para sa merienda.
examples.en: Grandma bought rice cakes for the afternoon snack.

notes.notes: Literally 'mix-mix'. Shaved ice, milk, beans, jellies, ube, leche flan. Summer staple; Chowking and Razon's are popular.

examples.tl: Ang init! Halo-halo tayo sa Chowking.
examples.en: It's so hot! Let's get halo-halo at Chowking.

examples.tl: Haluin mo muna bago kainin.
examples.en: Mix it first before eating.

notes.en: warm silken tofu with syrup and sago
notes.notes: Sold by the magtataho shouting 'Tahooo!' in the morning. Served in a cup, 20-30 pesos. Also in 7-Eleven now.

examples.tl: Tumawag ka sa magtataho, gusto ko ng mainit na taho.
examples.en: Call the taho vendor, I want warm taho.

notes.notes: Saba banana (and sometimes langka) in a lumpia wrapper, fried with caramelized sugar. Street merienda, 15-25 pesos.

examples.tl: Pabili ng dalawang turon, merienda ko.
examples.en: Two turon please, my afternoon snack.

notes.notes: Sold at night by vendors calling 'Baluuut!'. Eaten with salt or spiced vinegar. Penoy is the unfertilized version.

examples.tl: Try mo ang balut, may asin at suka.
examples.en: Try the balut, with salt and vinegar.

notes.notes: Slightly sweet rolls sold hot from bakeries at dawn. Dipped in coffee; filled with kesong puti, palaman, or Spam.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng pandesal sa panaderya, mainit pa.
examples.en: Buy pandesal at the bakery, it's still hot.

examples.tl: Pandesal at kape, almusal ng bayan.
examples.en: Pandesal and coffee, the nation's breakfast.

notes.notes: General word for bread. Sliced loaf is often just 'tasty' (from a brand). Panaderya = bakery.

examples.tl: Wala na tayong tinapay para sa almusal.
examples.en: We have no more bread for breakfast.

notes.notes: Leftover rice fried with garlic. The 'si' in silog. 'Fried rice' is also understood.

examples.tl: Gawin nating sinangag ang tirang kanin.
examples.en: Let's make the leftover rice into garlic fried rice.

notes.notes: Plain rice porridge; arroz caldo (with chicken, ginger) and goto (with tripe) are the loaded versions. Sick-day and late-night food.

examples.tl: Lugaw at tokwa't baboy, tapos kape.
examples.en: Rice porridge with tofu and pork, then coffee.

notes.notes: Lugaw with chicken, ginger, safflower, fried garlic and kalamansi. Rainy-day and sick-day food.

examples.tl: Lagnat ako kahapon, arroz caldo ang kinain ko.
examples.en: I had a fever yesterday, I ate arroz caldo.

notes.notes: Beef shank and marrow boiled for hours. Famous in Tagaytay; a cold-weather and drinking food.

examples.tl: Bulalo sa Tagaytay, worth it ang byahe.
examples.en: Bulalo in Tagaytay, the trip is worth it.

notes.notes: Grilled (inihaw na liempo) or fried (lechon kawali). Sold by the kilo at the palengke.

examples.tl: Inihaw na liempo at kanin, tapos toyomansi.
examples.en: Grilled pork belly with rice, then soy-kalamansi dip.

notes.notes: Crispy fried pork skin, dipped in spiced vinegar. Also chicharon bulaklak (intestine). Classic pulutan.

examples.tl: Chicharon na may suka, pulutan natin.
examples.en: Pork rinds with vinegar, our bar snack.

notes.notes: From dugo (blood). Dark savory stew, eaten with puto. Jokingly called 'chocolate meat' to foreigners.

examples.tl: Dinuguan at puto, classic combo.
examples.en: Dinuguan and puto, a classic combo.

notes.notes: Pork, chilies, bagoong and gata. One of the few genuinely spicy Filipino dishes. Laing is the vegetable cousin.

examples.tl: Maanghang talaga ang Bicol express nila, ingat.
examples.en: Their Bicol express is really spicy, careful.

notes.notes: Ilocano dish: squash, eggplant, okra, bitter gourd, string beans, with bagoong and often pork or bagnet.

examples.tl: Pinakbet ang gulay ko ngayon, may ampalaya.
examples.en: Pinakbet is my vegetable dish today, it has bitter gourd.

notes.notes: National fish. Boneless bangus is sold marinated (daing na bangus) for frying. Bangsilog = bangus silog.

examples.tl: Daing na bangus, sinangag at itlog: bangsilog.
examples.en: Marinated milkfish, garlic rice and egg: bangsilog.

notes.notes: Literally 'dry'. Smelly when fried, loved with sinangag, kamatis and suka. Not for the condo kitchen if neighbors complain.

examples.tl: Bawal magprito ng tuyo sa condo, umaamoy sa hallway.
examples.en: Frying dried fish is banned in the condo, it smells up the hallway.

notes.notes: 'Walang sibuyas' = no onions. Red onions are the default; 'sibuyas Tagalog' = small red shallots.

examples.tl: Walang sibuyas po sa burger ko.
examples.en: No onions on my burger, please.

notes.notes: Base of almost every dish (gisa = saute in garlic, onion, tomato). Fried garlic bits top lugaw and sinangag.

examples.tl: Maraming bawang ang sinangag nila, masarap.
examples.en: Their garlic rice has lots of garlic, delicious.

notes.notes: Sliced raw tomatoes with salt or bagoong are a side for fried fish and tuyo.

examples.tl: Pritong tuyo at kamatis, tapos sinangag.
examples.en: Fried dried fish and tomatoes, then garlic rice.

notes.notes: Siling labuyo = tiny very hot chili. Siling haba = long green mild chili. 'May sili ba?' = does it have chili?

examples.tl: May sili ba ito? Hindi ako kumakain ng maanghang.
examples.en: Does this have chili? I don't eat spicy food.

examples.tl: Lagyan mo ng sili ang suka.
examples.en: Put chili in the vinegar.

notes.notes: Purple yam used in halaya (jam), halo-halo, ice cream, and the ube-cheese pandesal craze.

examples.tl: Ube cheese pandesal, uso pa ba yan?
examples.en: Ube cheese pandesal, is that still trendy?

notes.notes: Sold roasted or fried with garlic (adobong mani) by street vendors. Base of kare-kare sauce.

examples.tl: Pabili ng mani sa manong, pampulutan.
examples.en: Buy peanuts from the vendor, for bar snacks.

notes.notes: Kesong puti = fresh white carabao cheese, eaten with pandesal. 'Cheese' is said just as often.

examples.tl: Pandesal na may kesong puti, galing Laguna.
examples.en: Pandesal with white cheese from Laguna.

notes.notes: Chinese-Filipino steamed bun: asado (sweet pork) or bola-bola (meatball with egg). Sold hot at 7-Eleven and Chowking.

examples.tl: Isang siopao asado, pang-merienda.
examples.en: One asado siopao, for a snack.

notes.notes: Pork dumplings with toyo, kalamansi and chili garlic oil. 'Siomai rice' is a cheap meal; sold at stalls and malls.

examples.tl: Siomai rice na lang ako, 60 pesos.
examples.en: I'll just have siomai rice, 60 pesos.

notes.notes: Fried on a cart, speared with a stick, dipped in sweet, spicy or vinegar sauce. Kwek-kwek (orange battered quail eggs) and kikiam share the cart.

examples.tl: Fishball at kwek-kwek sa labas ng school, 5 pesos each dati.
examples.en: Fishball and kwek-kwek outside the school, 5 pesos each back then.

notes.notes: Street barbecue skewer, dipped in vinegar. Other skewers: betamax (blood), adidas (chicken feet), helmet (head).

examples.tl: Isaw at betamax, ihaw-ihaw sa kanto.
examples.en: Isaw and betamax, grilled skewers on the corner.

notes.notes: Filipino barbecue = sweet soy-marinated pork on sticks, grilled. 'Ihaw-ihaw' = street grill stand. Also inihaw.

examples.tl: Tatlong stick ng barbecue at isang kanin.
examples.en: Three sticks of barbecue and one rice.

notes.notes: Small white steamed cakes, often with cheese on top. Partner of dinuguan. Careful: means something else in Spanish.

examples.tl: Puto't dinuguan sa handaan.
examples.en: Puto and dinuguan at the party.

notes.en: rice cake baked in clay pot (Christmas)
notes.notes: Sold outside churches during Simbang Gabi (December), topped with butter, cheese, itlog na maalat and niyog.

examples.tl: Bibingka at puto bumbong pagkatapos ng Simbang Gabi.
examples.en: Bibingka and puto bumbong after the dawn mass.

notes.notes: 'Magkape tayo' = let's have coffee. 3-in-1 sachets at home, barako from Batangas, Starbucks/Bo's in malls. 'Kapeng mainit' = hot coffee.

examples.tl: Kape muna ako bago mag-work.
examples.en: Coffee first before I work.

examples.tl: Magkape tayo sa Bo's mamaya?
examples.en: Coffee at Bo's later?
examples.taglish: Coffee tayo sa Bo's mamaya? Libre ko.

notes.notes: Most people say 'tea' or the specific drink (iced tea, milk tea). 'Salabat' = ginger tea. Iced tea is the default restaurant drink.

examples.tl: Mainit na tsaa para sa sipon.
examples.en: Hot tea for a cold.

examples.tl: Milk tea na lang ako, less sugar.
examples.en: I'll just have milk tea, less sugar.

notes.notes: 'May gatas' = with milk. Condensed milk (condensada) and evaporated milk are pantry staples for coffee and desserts.

examples.tl: Kape na may gatas, walang asukal.
examples.en: Coffee with milk, no sugar.

examples.tl: Ubos na ang gatas ng bata.
examples.en: The kid's milk is finished.

notes.notes: Said in English. Popular: buko juice, kalamansi juice, mango shake, 'juice' also covers powdered Tang-style drinks.

examples.tl: Anong juice meron? Mango o pineapple?
examples.en: What juice do you have? Mango or pineapple?

notes.notes: Always 'softdrinks', even for one. Coke is the default; 'Coke' can mean any cola. Sold in glass bottles (bote) and 'mismo' small bottles.

examples.tl: Softdrinks na lang ako, Coke Zero kung meron.
examples.en: I'll just have a soda, Coke Zero if you have it.

notes.notes: Everyone says 'beer'; serbesa is the old Spanish word (San Miguel's full name). Order: 'Isang Pale, kuya.' Red Horse is the strong one.

examples.tl: Dalawang San Mig Light, malamig ha.
examples.en: Two San Mig Lights, cold ones okay.

examples.tl: Beer tayo mamaya sa Poblacion?
examples.en: Beers later in Poblacion?

notes.notes: Any alcoholic drink, especially hard liquor (gin, brandy like Emperador, rum like Tanduay). 'Inom' = drinking session.

examples.tl: Hindi ako umiinom ng alak, driver ako ngayon.
examples.en: I don't drink alcohol, I'm the driver tonight.

notes.notes: 'Walang yelo' = no ice. 'Maraming yelo' = lots of ice. Ice is sold in bags at sari-sari stores and 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: Iced tea po, walang yelo.
examples.en: Iced tea please, no ice.

examples.tl: Pabili ng yelo para sa inuman.
examples.en: Buy ice for the drinking session.

notes.notes: Ask for a glass with your bottle: 'May baso po?' or 'Sa baso po'. 'Sa tasa' = in a cup; 'sa bote' = in the bottle.

examples.tl: Yung Coke, sa baso po, may yelo.
examples.en: The Coke in a glass please, with ice.

notes.notes: Traditionally one shared glass passed around the table (tagayan). 'Tagay!' = drink up / cheers. 'Tagayan mo siya' = pour him one.

examples.tl: Tagay! Para sa bagong trabaho mo.
examples.en: Cheers! To your new job.

notes.notes: From asin/alat. 'Sobrang maalat' = too salty. 'Alat' is the noun (saltiness).

examples.tl: Medyo maalat yung tapa pero okay lang.
examples.en: The tapa is a bit salty but it's fine.

notes.notes: Filipino spaghetti, longganisa and tocino are all matamis. 'Tamis' = sweetness. 'Panghimagas' = dessert (formal; people say dessert).

examples.tl: Masyadong matamis ang spaghetti ng Jollibee para sa akin.
examples.en: Jollibee's spaghetti is too sweet for me.

notes.notes: Sinigang and green mango are maasim. 'Asim' = sourness. 'Pa-asim' = make it more sour.

examples.tl: Gusto ko maasim talaga ang sinigang.
examples.en: I like my sinigang really sour.

notes.notes: 'Maanghang ba?' is the key question before ordering. 'Anghang' = spiciness. 'Hindi maanghang' = not spicy. Levels: mild/medium/spicy in English.

examples.tl: Maanghang ba ito? Hindi ako kaya ng maanghang.
examples.en: Is this spicy? I can't handle spicy.

examples.tl: Pakibawasan ng anghang, konting sili lang.
examples.en: Please make it less spicy, just a little chili.

notes.notes: Ampalaya (bitter gourd) is the classic mapait food. 'Pait' = bitterness; also used for heartbreak.

examples.tl: Mapait ang ampalaya pero masarap sa itlog.
examples.en: Bitter gourd is bitter but good with eggs.

notes.notes: Rich, deep, satisfying taste (umami). 'Linamnam' = that savory quality. Used in food ads and by titos describing broth.

examples.tl: Malinamnam ang sabaw ng bulalo, matagal na pinakuluan.
examples.en: The bulalo broth is savory, it was boiled a long time.

notes.notes: For meat = tender; for bread = soft. 'Lambot' = softness. Opposite: matigas.

examples.tl: Malambot ang baka, hindi chewy.
examples.en: The beef is tender, not chewy.

notes.notes: Tough meat, stale bread, hard rice. 'Matigas ang ulo' = stubborn (idiom).

examples.tl: Matigas yung tapa, parang goma.
examples.en: The tapa is tough, like rubber.

notes.notes: Lechon skin, chicharon, fried chicken. 'Lutong' = crunch. 'Crispy' is used just as much.

examples.tl: Malutong pa ang balat ng lechon, sarap!
examples.en: The lechon skin is still crispy, delicious!

notes.notes: Literally brave. For coffee or liquor = strong. Barako coffee is matapang. Opposite for drinks: matabang (weak/bland).

examples.tl: Matapang ang kape dito, hindi ako makakatulog.
examples.en: The coffee here is strong, I won't be able to sleep.

examples.tl: Matapang si Lolo noong giyera.
examples.en: Grandpa was brave during the war.

examples.tl: Matapang siya, nag-resign nang walang backup job.
examples.en: She's bold, resigned without a backup job.

notes.notes: Needs salt or patis. Also = weak coffee. 'Tabang' = blandness. Not to be confused with mataba (fat).

examples.tl: Matabang yung sabaw, lagyan mo ng patis.
examples.en: The soup is bland, add some fish sauce.

notes.notes: Unripe fruit (manggang hilaw) or undercooked food. Opposite: hinog (ripe) / luto (cooked).

examples.tl: Hilaw pa yung kanin, dagdagan mo ng tubig.
examples.en: The rice is still undercooked, add water.

examples.tl: Hinog na ba ang mangga o hilaw pa?
examples.en: Is the mango ripe yet or still green?

notes.notes: 'Ano'ng lasa?' = what does it taste like? 'Lasang ...' = tastes like ... 'Walang lasa' = tasteless. 'Lasahan mo' = taste it.

examples.tl: Lasang pizza yung chichirya na ito.
examples.en: These chips taste like pizza.

examples.tl: Ano'ng lasa ng ube? Parang matamis na kamote.
examples.en: What does ube taste like? Like a sweet potato.

notes.notes: From prito (Spanish frito). 'Pritong manok/isda/itlog' before a noun; 'magprito' = to fry; 'iprito mo' = fry it. 'Pinirito' = was fried.

examples.tl: Pritong itlog at sinangag, mabilis lang.
examples.en: Fried egg and garlic rice, it's quick.

examples.tl: Iprito mo na lang yung tirang adobo.
examples.en: Just fry the leftover adobo.

notes.notes: From ihaw (grill). 'Inihaw na liempo/pusit/isda'. 'Ihaw-ihaw' = street grill. 'Mag-ihaw tayo' = let's grill (condo rooftop BBQ).

examples.tl: Inihaw na liempo at toyomansi, tapos kanin.
examples.en: Grilled pork belly with soy-kalamansi, then rice.

examples.tl: Mag-ihaw tayo sa roof deck sa Sunday.
examples.en: Let's grill on the roof deck on Sunday.

notes.notes: From laga (boil). 'Nilagang baka' = boiled beef soup with potatoes and cabbage; 'nilagang itlog' = boiled egg. Clear, mild, comforting.

examples.tl: Nilagang baka ang ulam, may repolyo at patatas.
examples.en: Boiled beef soup is the dish, with cabbage and potatoes.

notes.notes: Gisa = saute. The base step of most Filipino dishes. 'Ginisang gulay/monggo/corned beef'. 'Igisa mo' = saute it.

examples.tl: Ginisang corned beef at sibuyas, ulam ng wala nang budget.
examples.en: Sauteed corned beef and onions, the end-of-budget meal.

notes.notes: Table or kitchen knife. Rarely on a Filipino table since the spoon does the cutting. 'Pakihiwa' = please cut/slice.

examples.tl: Mapurol ang kutsilyo, hindi makahiwa ng kamatis.
examples.en: The knife is dull, it can't slice a tomato.

notes.notes: Cup with a handle. 'Isang tasang kape' = a cup of coffee. Also a measuring cup in recipes (1 tasa ng bigas).

examples.tl: Dalawang tasa ng bigas para sa apat na tao.
examples.en: Two cups of rice for four people.

notes.notes: Literally 'house-cooked'. Carinderias advertise 'lutong bahay'. 'Lutong Pinoy' = Filipino cooking.

examples.tl: Miss ko na ang lutong bahay, puro Grab ako buong linggo.
examples.en: I miss home-cooked food, I've been on Grab all week.

notes.notes: Hugas = wash (things, hands). Laundry is labahan. 'Ikaw na maghugas' = you do the dishes. Household rule: the one who cooks doesn't wash.

examples.tl: Ako nagluto, ikaw na maghugas ng plato.
examples.en: I cooked, you wash the dishes.

notes.notes: magpa- + init. Object focus: painitin mo (heat it). Taglish: 'pa-heat mo'. At 7-Eleven: 'Pakiinit po' = please microwave it.

examples.tl: Painitin mo yung ulam sa microwave, isang minuto.
examples.en: Heat up the dish in the microwave, one minute.

examples.tl: Pakiinit po yung siopao.
examples.en: Please heat up the siopao.

notes.notes: The standard 7-Eleven / Ministop request for ready meals. Staff will also ask 'Painitin po?'

examples.tl: Pakiinit po itong rice meal, tapos isang kutsara.
examples.en: Please heat this rice meal, and one spoon.

notes.notes: Everyone says 'Seven'. On every Makati corner: siopao, hot rice meals, coffee, beer, bills payment, GCash cash-in. Ministop and Alfamart are the others.

examples.tl: Daan muna tayo sa Seven, bibili ako ng tubig.
examples.en: Let's stop by 7-Eleven first, I'll buy water.

examples.tl: Open 24/7 ang Seven sa baba ng condo, sulit.
examples.en: The 7-Eleven below the condo is open 24/7, so handy.

notes.notes: Fresh meat, fish, vegetables, fruit by the kilo. Go early. 'Mamalengke' = to go marketing. Haggling (tawad) is normal; having a suki helps.

examples.tl: Mamalengke tayo nang maaga, sariwa pa ang isda.
examples.en: Let's go to the market early, the fish is still fresh.

examples.tl: Mas mura sa palengke kaysa sa grocery.
examples.en: It's cheaper at the market than at the grocery.

examples.tl: Mas mura ang gulay sa palengke kaysa sa supermarket.
examples.en: Vegetables are cheaper at the market than the supermarket.

notes.taglish: Namalengke ako kaninang umaga.

notes.notes: From tinda (goods for sale). Usually a small neighborhood store. 'Tindera/tindero' = shopkeeper (f/m). 'Nagtitinda' = sells.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng yelo sa tindahan sa kanto.
examples.en: Buy ice at the store on the corner.

examples.tl: Bumili ka ng yelo sa tindahan sa kanto.
examples.en: Buy ice at the store on the corner.

examples.tl: Sarado na ang tindahan, 10 PM na.
examples.en: The store is closed, it's 10 PM.

notes.taglish: May tindahan sa kanto, bili ka ng load.

notes.notes: Tiny home-front store selling tingi: single sachets, cigarettes by the stick, cold drinks, load. Often with a window grille. Backbone of barangay life.

examples.tl: May sari-sari store sa tabi ng building, open hanggang 11.
examples.en: There's a sari-sari store next to the building, open till 11.

notes.notes: Two-way loyalty: you're the vendor's suki and they're yours. Gets you better prices, extra pieces and credit. Vendors call anyone 'suki' to be friendly.

examples.tl: Suki na ako sa manok vendor, laging may dagdag.
examples.en: I'm a regular at the chicken vendor, there's always extra.

examples.tl: Suki, bili ka na, mura lang!
examples.en: Hey regular, buy some, it's cheap!

examples.tl: Suki na ako dun, binibigyan ako ng tawad.
examples.en: I'm a regular there, they give me a discount.

notes.en: retail in small portions; by the piece
notes.notes: Buying one sachet of shampoo, one egg, one cigarette, a small bag of oil. 'Tingi-tingi' = in bits. Sari-sari stores run on tingi.

examples.tl: Tingi lang ang bili ko ng kape, tatlong sachet.
examples.en: I only buy coffee by the sachet, three sachets.

examples.tl: May tingi kayong mantika?
examples.en: Do you sell cooking oil in small portions?

examples.tl: Tingi lang ang bili ko ng shampoo, sachet.
examples.en: I buy shampoo by the piece, in sachets.

notes.notes: 'Sukli po' = your change (said by cashier). 'Wala pong sukli' = no change available. 'Sa iyo na ang sukli' = keep the change.

examples.tl: Kuya, kulang yung sukli ko.
examples.en: Sir, my change is short.

examples.tl: Sa iyo na ang sukli, salamat.
examples.en: Keep the change, thanks.

examples.tl: Kuya, yung sukli ko po.
examples.en: Sir, my change please.

notes.taglish: Kuya, may sukli po ba sa 500?

notes.notes: 'Pahingi ng resibo' or 'May resibo?' 'OR' = official receipt (for reimbursement). Check for service charge on it.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng resibo, ire-reimburse ko.
examples.en: Receipt please, I'll get reimbursed.

examples.tl: Pwede pa-resibo?
examples.en: Can I get a receipt?

examples.tl: Itago mo yung resibo para sa warranty.
examples.en: Keep the receipt for the warranty.

notes.taglish: Pa-receipt po.

notes.notes: Plastic = plastic bag. Many Metro Manila cities restrict plastic bags, so stores charge for paper or offer eco bags. 'May plastic?' also works.

examples.tl: Pa-plastic po, marami akong dala.
examples.en: A bag please, I'm carrying a lot.

examples.tl: Wala pong plastic, bawal sa Makati. Paper bag lang.
examples.en: No plastic bags, they're banned in Makati. Only paper bags.

notes.notes: What a cashier, jeepney driver or taho vendor asks when you hand over a 1000. Reply: 'Wala, sorry' or 'Meron, teka'. Carry barya.

examples.tl: Wala kang barya? Wala akong sukli sa isang libo.
examples.en: Don't you have smaller bills? I can't change a thousand.

notes.notes: Coins and small bills. Essential for jeeps, sari-sari stores and street food. 'Pabarya' = please break this bill.

examples.tl: Pabarya ng isang libo, pambayad sa jeep.
examples.en: Please break this thousand, for the jeepney fare.

examples.tl: May barya ka ba? Pambili ng taho.
examples.en: Do you have coins? To buy taho.

examples.tl: Puro barya ang laman ng wallet ko.
examples.en: My wallet is full of coins.

notes.taglish: May barya ka? Pang-jeep lang.

notes.notes: 'Bayad po' when handing money. 'Magbayad' = to pay. 'Bayaran mo' = pay for it. 'Bayad na' = already paid. 'Kanya-kanyang bayad' = KKB.

examples.tl: Bayad po, dalawang tapsilog.
examples.en: Here's payment, two tapsilog.

examples.tl: Bayad na ba yung Grab? Cash o GCash?
examples.en: Is the Grab paid already? Cash or GCash?

examples.tl: Magkano ang bayad sa parking dito?
examples.en: How much is the parking fee here?

notes.notes: GCash (and Maya) QR payments work at most stalls and carinderias now. Look for the QR Ph sign. 'Scan lang po' = just scan.

examples.tl: Pwede GCash? Wala akong cash.
examples.en: Can I pay with GCash? I don't have cash.

examples.tl: Scan lang po dito, tapos ipakita ang confirmation.
examples.en: Just scan here, then show the confirmation.

examples.tl: Pwede GCash? — Pwede po, i-scan niyo lang yung QR.
examples.en: Can I pay with GCash? — Yes, just scan the QR.

notes.notes: 'Pwede pa-tawad?' / 'Tawad naman' = can you give a discount? 'Tumawad' = to haggle. Works at the palengke, not at 7-Eleven. Also = forgiveness in church.

examples.tl: Ate, tawad naman, tatlong kilo kukunin ko.
examples.en: Miss, give me a discount, I'm taking three kilos.

examples.tl: Pwede pa-tawad? Last price na ba yan?
examples.en: Can you lower it? Is that your last price?

examples.tl: Wala bang tawad, ate? Tatlo ang kukunin ko.
examples.en: No discount, miss? I'm taking three.

notes.notes: Actor focus. Object focus is 'bilhin'. 'Pabili' = please buy for me / I'd like to buy (at a counter).

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng ulam sa carinderia, tapos umuwi.
examples.en: I bought food at the carinderia, then went home.

examples.tl: Bibili ako ng tubig sa 7-Eleven, gusto mo?
examples.en: I'll buy water at 7-Eleven, want some?

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng prutas sa palengke kanina.
examples.en: I bought fruit at the market earlier.

notes.notes: 'Mag-grocery' = to do grocery shopping. SM Supermarket, Landers, S&R, Robinsons. 'Grocery' means both the store and the trip.

examples.tl: Mag-grocery tayo sa SM mamaya, wala nang laman ang ref.
examples.en: Let's do groceries at SM later, the fridge is empty.

examples.tl: Mahal mag-grocery sa Landers pero bulk.
examples.en: Groceries at Landers are expensive but you buy in bulk.

notes.prompt: Order: ba / ka / na  (→ 'are you ... yet?')
notes.explanation: Enclitic order: monosyllabic pronoun (ka) → na/pa → ba.

notes.prompt: Order: kumain / ba / na / kayo  (→ 'Have you all eaten yet?')
notes.explanation: na before ba; the two-syllable pronoun kayo goes after all monosyllabic particles.

notes.prompt: Order: umalis / siya / na / daw  (→ 'They say he already left.')
notes.explanation: na → daw (monosyllabic particles) → siya (two-syllable pronoun) last.

notes.prompt: Order: gusto / lang / ko  (→ 'I just want (it).')
notes.explanation: Monosyllabic pronoun ko comes right after the predicate, before lang (two syllables).

notes.prompt: Order: bakit / tinanong / mo / pa / ba  (→ 'Why did you even still ask?')
notes.explanation: Enclitics attach to the first word (bakit): mo → pa → ba, then the verb.

notes.prompt: Order: hindi / ako / pa / nakakain  (→ 'I haven't eaten yet.')
notes.explanation: After hindi: pa (na/pa slot) before the two-syllable pronoun ako, then the verb.

notes.prompt: Order: pupunta / din / ako  (→ 'I'm going too.')
notes.explanation: Monosyllabic particle din before two-syllable pronoun ako. rin after vowels is the textbook form; din is common in speech.

notes.prompt: Order: kain / na / tayo  (→ 'Let's eat now.')
notes.explanation: na comes before the two-syllable pronoun tayo. Root 'kain' alone works as an invitation.

notes.prompt: Order: nandito / na / ba / siya  (→ 'Is he here already?')
notes.explanation: na → ba → siya: monosyllabic particles first, two-syllable pronoun last.

notes.prompt: Order: ikaw / pala / 'yan  (→ 'Oh, it's you!')
notes.explanation: pala (surprise/realization) follows the first word. 'yan = iyan (that).

notes.prompt: Order: ayaw / ko / nga  (→ 'I said I don't want to.')
notes.en: I said I don't want to.
notes.explanation: ko (monosyllabic pronoun) first, then nga (two-syllable particle: insistence).

notes.prompt: Order: ano / ba / 'yan  (→ 'What is that?!')
notes.explanation: ba sits right after the question word; here it adds exasperation, not a yes/no question.

notes.prompt: Order: nasaan / na / ba / siya  (→ 'Where is he now?')
notes.explanation: Question word first, then na → ba → siya.

notes.prompt: Order: kumain / ka / na / ba  (→ 'Have you eaten yet?')
notes.explanation: Full order: ka → na → ba. Compare 'Kumain na ba kayo?' where two-syllable kayo goes last.

notes.prompt: Order: sinabi / ko / na / sa'yo  (→ 'I already told you.')
notes.explanation: ko → na; the non-enclitic phrase sa'yo (sa iyo) comes after all enclitics.

notes.prompt: Order: hindi / mo / ba / alam  (→ 'Don't you know?')
notes.explanation: Enclitics attach to hindi: mo → ba, then the predicate alam.

notes.prompt: Order: late / na / naman / ako  (→ 'I'm late again.')
notes.explanation: na → naman (two-syllable particle) → ako (two-syllable pronoun). 'na naman' = again, as usual.

notes.prompt: Order: wala / kasi / ako / pera  (→ 'Because I have no money.')
notes.explanation: Two-syllable particle kasi before two-syllable pronoun ako; ako takes -ng before pera.

notes.prompt: Order: sige / na / nga  (→ 'Oh fine, go ahead.')
notes.explanation: na (monosyllabic) → nga (two syllables). 'Sige na nga' = giving in reluctantly.

notes.prompt: Order: tapos / ka / na / ba  (→ 'Are you done yet?')
notes.explanation: ka → na → ba after the predicate tapos.

notes.prompt: Order: uuwi / daw / siya / na / bukas  (→ 'He's going home tomorrow, they say.')
notes.explanation: na → daw → siya; the adverb bukas is not an enclitic, so it comes last.

notes.prompt: Order: ako / na / lang  (→ 'I'll just do it.')
notes.explanation: Ako is the fronted predicate here; enclitics na → lang follow it.

notes.prompt: Choose ang / ng / sa: Natutulog ___ bata.
notes.explanation: ang marks the focus (topic) of the sentence: the thing the sentence is about.

notes.prompt: Choose ang / ng / sa: Kumain ako ___ mangga.
notes.explanation: With an actor-focus verb (kumain) the object is non-focus and takes ng.

notes.prompt: Choose ang / ng / sa: Pupunta ako ___ mall.
notes.explanation: sa marks location, direction, time and recipients.

notes.prompt: Choose ang / ng / sa: Kinain ko ___ mangga.
notes.explanation: Object-focus verb (kinain): the object is the focus → ang; the actor is in ng-form (ko).

notes.prompt: Choose si / ni / kay: Dumating na ___ Marco.
notes.explanation: si = ang for personal names. Plural: sina Marco at Ana.

notes.prompt: Choose si / ni / kay: Ito ang kotse ___ Marco.
notes.explanation: ni = ng for names: possessor or non-focus actor (Binili ni Marco).

notes.prompt: Choose si / ni / kay: Ibinigay ko ___ Ana ang susi.
notes.explanation: kay = sa for names: recipient or location ('kay Ana' = at Ana's place).

notes.prompt: Make plural: Nakita ko ang bata.  (→ 'I saw the children.')
notes.explanation: mga goes right after the marker: ang mga / ng mga / sa mga. The noun itself never changes.

notes.prompt: Choose ng mga / sa mga: Nagbigay siya ng pagkain ___ bata.
notes.explanation: Recipient = sa; plural adds mga after it: sa mga bata.

notes.prompt: Choose ng mga / sa mga: Bumili ako ___ regalo para sa kanila.
notes.explanation: Non-focus object = ng; plural adds mga: ng mga regalo.

notes.prompt: Choose nasa / sa: ___ mall ako ngayon.
notes.explanation: nasa = 'is at/in'; it is the predicate, no verb needed. Plain sa follows a verb: Pupunta ako sa mall.

notes.prompt: Choose nasa / sa: Pupunta ako ___ Makati bukas.
notes.explanation: After a motion verb use sa. nasa only when the location itself is the predicate: Nasa Makati ako.

notes.prompt: Choose nasa / sa: ___ bag ko ang wallet ko.
notes.explanation: Location predicate: Nasa bag ko ang wallet ko = my wallet is in my bag.

notes.prompt: Rewrite with ay-inversion: Mabait ang titser.
notes.explanation: ay puts the topic first; formal/written. Spoken Manila Tagalog is predicate-first: Mabait ang titser.

notes.prompt: Fill: ___ pera ako.  (I have money.)
notes.explanation: may + bare noun directly, no ng: May pera ako. Meron/mayroon instead takes a linker: Meron akong pera.

notes.prompt: Rewrite with meron: May pera ako.
notes.explanation: meron/mayroon stands alone, so the pronoun moves next to it and takes -ng. 'Meron' is the spoken form.

notes.prompt: Fill: ___ akong pera.  (I have no money.)
notes.explanation: wala = none/not have; the pronoun gets the -ng linker: Wala akong pera.

notes.prompt: Choose ng / nang: Kumain siya ___ mabilis.
notes.explanation: nang links a verb to how it's done (adverb of manner) and means 'when'. ng marks nouns: kumain ng kanin.

notes.prompt: Choose ng / nang: Bumili ako ___ kape.
notes.explanation: ng before a noun (object or possessor). nang only for manner, 'when', and na+ng contractions.

notes.prompt: Choose ng / nang: Wala ___ tao sa opisina.  (No one is at the office anymore.)
notes.explanation: nang here is 'na' (already) + linker -ng: wala na + ng tao → wala nang tao. Not the noun marker ng.

notes.prompt: Choose ng / nang: Umalis siya ___ dumating ako.
notes.explanation: nang = 'when' joining two clauses in the past. Spoken Manila often says 'noong dumating ako' too.

notes.prompt: Choose ang / ng: Gusto ko ___ kape.  (I want some coffee.)
notes.explanation: ng = coffee in general / some coffee; ang = that specific coffee (Gusto ko ang kape na 'to). ng is the default.

notes.prompt: Convert: ako (ang-form) → ng-form
notes.explanation: Sets: ako / ko / akin. The ng-form marks possessor or non-focus actor: bahay ko, ginawa ko.

notes.prompt: Convert: ikaw / ka → ng-form
notes.explanation: Sets: ikaw(ka) / mo / iyo. Bahay mo = your house; ginawa mo = you did it.

notes.prompt: Convert: siya → ng-form
notes.explanation: Sets: siya / niya / kanya. Spoken and texted as nya.

notes.prompt: Convert: kami → sa-form
notes.explanation: Sets: kami / namin / amin. 'Sa amin' = to us / at our place.

notes.prompt: Convert: sila → ng-form
notes.explanation: Sets: sila / nila / kanila. Bahay nila = their house.

notes.prompt: Convert: tayo → sa-form
notes.explanation: Sets: tayo / natin / atin. 'Sa atin' = to us (including you); 'atin 'to' = this is ours.

notes.prompt: Convert: kayo → ng-form
notes.explanation: ninyo is the full form; spoken Manila says niyo / nyo. Also the polite singular 'you'.

notes.prompt: Say 'I love you' using the one word that replaces ko + ikaw
notes.explanation: kita = ko + ka/ikaw (I → you). Never 'mahal ko ikaw'. Also: Tatawagan kita = I'll call you.

notes.prompt: Fill: Tatawagan ___ bukas.  (I'll call you tomorrow.)
notes.explanation: Whenever the actor is 'I' (ko) and the focus is 'you' (ka), they fuse into kita.

notes.prompt: Choose kami / tayo: Kain ___!  (Let's eat — including the listener)
notes.explanation: tayo = we including you; kami = we but not you.

notes.prompt: Choose kami / tayo: Aalis na ___, bye!  (We're leaving — not you)
notes.explanation: kami excludes the listener: we're leaving, you stay. tayo would mean 'let's leave'.

notes.prompt: Choose niya / nila: Binili ___ ang bahay.  (They bought the house.)
notes.explanation: niya = he/she, nila = they. Object-focus verb binili → actor takes ng-form.

notes.prompt: Rewrite with aking: ang bahay ko
notes.explanation: Two possessives: noun + ko/mo/niya (everyday) or aking/iyong/kanyang + noun (formal, emphatic). Default: bahay ko.

notes.prompt: Choose ikaw / ka: ___ ba si Lloyd?  (Are you Lloyd?)
notes.explanation: ikaw starts a sentence or stands alone as predicate; ka is the enclitic form after the predicate: Lloyd ka ba?

notes.prompt: Choose ikaw / ka: Saan ___ pupunta?
notes.explanation: After a predicate or question word, use enclitic ka, never ikaw.

notes.prompt: Fill: Para ___ ito.  (This is for you.)
notes.explanation: sa-form pronouns after para/sa: para sa'yo, para sa akin, para sa kanya. sa'yo = sa iyo.

notes.prompt: Fill: ___ ba 'to?  (Is this yours?)
notes.explanation: Possession as predicate uses sa-forms: Sa'yo ba 'to? Akin 'to. Kanya 'yun.

notes.prompt: Translate (everyday form): his phone
notes.explanation: Everyday possessive: noun + niya. 'Kanyang phone' is formal. Texted: phone nya.

notes.prompt: Join with the linker: maganda + babae
notes.explanation: After a vowel, add -ng to the first word: maganda → magandang.

notes.prompt: Join with the linker: masarap + pagkain
notes.explanation: After a consonant other than n, use a separate 'na'.

notes.prompt: Join with the linker: bago + kotse
notes.explanation: Vowel ending → -ng. Works with any modifier + noun pair.

notes.prompt: Join with the linker: mabait + tao
notes.explanation: Consonant ending (t) → separate na.

notes.prompt: Join (noun first): bata + mabait
notes.explanation: Order can flip; the linker always goes on the first word: mabait na bata = batang mabait.

notes.prompt: Join: gusto ko + kumain
notes.explanation: The linker also joins pseudo-verbs to verbs; it lands on the pronoun: gusto kong, ayaw niyang, pwede bang.

notes.prompt: Join: kailangan ko + umuwi
notes.explanation: kailangan + ko + -ng + infinitive. Same with dapat: Dapat kang matulog.

notes.prompt: Join: iyon + bata  (→ 'that child' / spoken 'yung')
notes.explanation: After n, the n becomes ng: iyon → iyong. Spoken Manila: 'yung bata. Same with iyan → iyang ('yang bata).

notes.prompt: Join: wala + ako + pera
notes.explanation: The linker attaches to the word right before the noun. Enclitic ako slips in: Wala akong pera, not 'Walang ako pera'.

notes.prompt: Join: dalawa + anak
notes.explanation: Numbers take the linker like adjectives: isang, dalawang, tatlong, apat na, limang.

notes.prompt: Join: pwede ba + sumama ako
notes.explanation: Enclitics ba and ako go after pwede; ako takes -ng before the verb.

notes.prompt: Form the adjective from the root ganda (beauty)
notes.explanation: ma- + root = adjective: ganda→maganda, sarap→masarap, bait→mabait, init→mainit.

notes.prompt: Compare: 'Makati is more expensive than Pasig.'
notes.tl: Mas mahal ang Makati kaysa sa Pasig.
notes.en: Makati is more expensive than Pasig.
notes.explanation: mas + adjective ... kaysa sa + noun. Spoken: 'Mas mahal sa Makati kaysa sa Pasig' (it's pricier in Makati).
accept_tl: Mas mahal ang Makati kaysa Pasig.
Mas mahal sa Makati kaysa sa Pasig.

notes.prompt: Superlative: 'the most delicious'
notes.explanation: pinaka- + full adjective (keep ma-): pinakamasarap, pinakamaganda, pinakamahal.

notes.prompt: Intensify with napaka-: maganda → 'very beautiful'
notes.explanation: napaka- + ROOT (drop ma-): napakaganda, napakasarap, napakainit.

notes.prompt: Intensify with sobrang: mahal → 'super expensive'
notes.explanation: sobrang + adjective is the everyday spoken intensifier: sobrang init, sobrang traffic, sobrang sarap.

notes.prompt: Exclaim 'How beautiful!' using ang + root
notes.explanation: Ang + root = exclamation: Ang ganda! Ang sarap! Ang mahal! Add ng/ni for the thing: Ang ganda ng view.

notes.prompt: Pluralize the adjective: maganda (several beautiful girls)
notes.explanation: Plural ma- adjectives double the first syllable of the root: magaganda, masasarap, mababait. Optional; mga alone is fine.

notes.prompt: Translate: 'the beautiful girls'
notes.explanation: Plural adjective + linker + noun. 'Ang mga magandang babae' is also fine; don't double up both unless emphatic.

notes.prompt: Translate: 'a bit expensive'
notes.explanation: medyo + adjective = somewhat/kind of. Medyo malayo, medyo late.

notes.prompt: Translate: 'super delicious' (use napaka-)
notes.explanation: napaka- takes the root sarap, not masarap. Spoken alternative: sobrang sarap.

notes.prompt: Compare with a name: 'Marco is taller than Lloyd.'
notes.tl: Mas matangkad si Marco kaysa kay Lloyd.
notes.explanation: kaysa sa + common noun, kaysa kay + name (kaysa kina + several names). Spoken often drops to 'kaysa kay'.

notes.prompt: Translate: 'It's more delicious here.'
notes.explanation: mas works alone without kaysa when the comparison is understood from context.

notes.prompt: Make it a yes/no question: Pupunta ka.
notes.explanation: ba makes a yes/no question; it sits after the first enclitics (ka).

notes.prompt: Choose hindi / wala / huwag / ayaw: ___ ako pupunta.  (I'm not going.)
notes.explanation: hindi negates verbs, adjectives, identity. wala = none/not have. huwag = don't (command). ayaw = don't want.

notes.prompt: Choose hindi / wala / huwag / ayaw: ___ akong pera.
notes.explanation: Existence and possession are negated with wala, never hindi.

notes.prompt: Choose hindi / wala / huwag / ayaw: ___ kang umalis.  (Don't leave.)
