notes.explanation: huwag + pronoun with -ng + infinitive: Huwag kang umalis. Spoken Manila: 'Wag kang umalis.

notes.prompt: Choose hindi / wala / huwag / ayaw: ___ ko ng kape.  (I don't want coffee.)
notes.explanation: ayaw + ko/mo/niya + ng noun, or -ng + verb: Ayaw kong kumain. Opposite: gusto.

notes.prompt: Choose hindi / wala: ___ siya dito.  (He isn't here.)
notes.explanation: Absence uses wala (Wala siya dito). 'Hindi siya dito' contrasts location: not here but somewhere else.

notes.prompt: Add the tag 'right?': Mahal, ___?
notes.explanation: 'di ba (hindi ba) = right? Goes at the end or the start: Di ba mahal 'yun?

notes.prompt: Fix the word order: Pupunta ka saan?
notes.explanation: Question words come first; the enclitic pronoun follows right after. 'Pupunta ka saan?' is only an echo question.

notes.prompt: Ask 'What time?' (clock time)
notes.explanation: kailan = when (day/date); anong oras = what time (clock). Anong oras ka uuwi?

notes.prompt: Choose kailan / anong oras: ___ ang flight mo?  (which day)
notes.explanation: kailan asks for a day or date; anong oras asks for a clock time.

notes.prompt: Answer yes to: May pera ka ba?
notes.explanation: may/meron questions are answered meron/wala, not oo/hindi. oo/hindi answer verb and adjective questions.

notes.prompt: Answer no to: May pera ka ba?
notes.explanation: wala answers may/meron questions in the negative. 'Wala, eh' softens it.

notes.prompt: Answer no to: Pupunta ka ba?
notes.explanation: hindi answers verb/adjective yes-no questions. Often with eh: Hindi, eh.

notes.prompt: Answer yes to: Kumain ka na ba?
notes.explanation: oo = yes; opo = polite yes (to elders/strangers). Natural answers repeat the verb with na: Kumain na.

notes.prompt: Ask 'Who is that?' (a person)
notes.explanation: sino = who (people), ano = what (things). Sino siya? Ano 'to?

notes.prompt: Ask 'Where is the CR?'
notes.explanation: nasaan = where is (location of something); saan = where + verb (Saan ka pupunta?). Manila speech also says 'Saan ang CR?'

notes.prompt: Ask 'How much?' (price)
notes.explanation: magkano = how much (price); ilan = how many. Magkano 'to? Ilan kayo?

notes.prompt: Choose hindi / wala: ___ pa tapos.  (It's not done yet.)
notes.explanation: hindi pa = not yet (verb/adjective). wala pa = none yet / not here yet: Wala pa siya.

notes.prompt: Choose hindi / wala: ___ pa siya.  (He's not here yet.)
notes.explanation: wala pa = hasn't arrived / none yet. Also 'Wala pa akong sahod' = I haven't been paid yet.

notes.en: I'm just at the condo right now.
I bought a viand at the carinderia.

notes.tl: Binili {{niya}} ang bagong phone sa Lazada.
notes.en: He bought the new phone on Lazada.
I'm late again, the traffic is crazy.
Because I have no phone load.
I was late because of traffic on EDSA.
I'm going to the party too.
I have no money, lend me some first.

notes.tl: Kumain siya {{nang}} mabilis kasi late na.
notes.en: He ate quickly because it was late.
There's no one at the office anymore.
I went home when Mom called.

notes.tl: Nakita ko ang {{mga}} bata sa park.
notes.en: I saw the children at the park.
I'm not going to the meeting.
He's not here, he's in Cebu.
When are you coming back to the Philippines?
How much is a kilo of mangoes?
Who was that with you earlier?
The baby is still sleeping, don't be noisy.
We went to Tagaytay last weekend.

notes.tl: Mas mahal ang Grab {{kaysa}} sa jeep.
notes.en: Grab is more expensive than the jeep.

notes.tl: Ito ang {{pinakamasarap}} na sisig sa Makati.
notes.en: This is the best sisig in Makati.
The view from the rooftop is so beautiful!
The flowers in Baguio are beautiful.

notes.notes: The everyday word. 'Walang pera' = broke. 'Pera-pera lang yan' = it's just a matter of money.

examples.tl: Wala akong pera ngayon, sa sahod na lang.
examples.en: I have no money right now, after payday instead.

examples.tl: May pera ka ba pang-Grab?
examples.en: Do you have money for the Grab?

notes.notes: 'Piso' = one peso / a one-peso coin. In Taglish amounts are usually 'X pesos' (bente pesos, 500 pesos).

examples.tl: Kulang ng piso, okay lang ba?
examples.en: It's one peso short, is that okay?

examples.tl: Dalawang daang pesos ang pamasahe sa Grab.
examples.en: The Grab fare was two hundred pesos.

examples.tl: Piso lang ang dagdag sa pamasahe? Ok lang 'yan.
examples.en: Only a one-peso fare increase? That's fine.

notes.notes: Rarely handled now; prices get rounded. 25 sentimo coins still show up as sukli in supermarkets.

examples.tl: Bente-singko sentimo lang ang sukli, 'wag na.
examples.en: The change is only twenty-five centavos, never mind.

notes.notes: Asked by drivers, cashiers and vendors when you hand over a big bill. 'Wala akong barya' = I have no change.

examples.tl: Boss, may barya ka? Wala akong sukli sa limang daan.
examples.en: Boss, got any change? I don't have change for five hundred.
examples.taglish: Boss, may barya ka? Wala akong sukli sa 500.

notes.notes: Said when handing fare to a jeepney driver, often passed forward by other passengers. Add destination and headcount: 'Bayad po, dalawa, Ayala.'

examples.tl: Bayad po, isa lang, hanggang Guadalupe.
examples.en: Fare please, just one, to Guadalupe.

examples.tl: Pakiabot po ng bayad.
examples.en: Please pass my fare forward.

examples.tl: Bayad po, dalawa, hanggang Ayala.
examples.en: Fare please, two people, to Ayala.
examples.taglish: Bayad po, dalawa, hanggang Ayala. Salamat po.

notes.taglish: Bayad po, isa lang, Guadalupe.

notes.notes: Actor focus. 'Magbayad ng kuryente' = pay the electric bill.

examples.tl: Nagbayad na ako ng kuryente kanina sa GCash.
examples.en: I already paid the electricity earlier on GCash.

examples.tl: Saan ako magbabayad, sa kahera?
examples.en: Where do I pay, at the cashier?

examples.tl: Nagbayad na ako ng kuryente sa GCash.
examples.en: I already paid the electric bill on GCash.

notes.notes: Object focus: the thing or person paid is the topic. 'Bayaran mo ako' = pay me.

examples.tl: Babayaran ko na yung utang ko sa 'yo sa Friday.
examples.en: I'll pay you back what I owe on Friday.

examples.tl: Binayaran ko na yung internet, 1,699 ulit.
examples.en: I paid the internet already, 1,699 again.

examples.tl: Babayaran ko na lang yung kuryente sa GCash.
examples.en: I'll just pay the electric bill on GCash.

notes.notes: 'May utang ako sa 'yo' = I owe you. 'Utang na loob' = debt of gratitude, a big cultural concept.

examples.tl: May utang pa ako kay Mark, dalawang libo.
examples.en: I still owe Mark two thousand.

examples.tl: Ilista mo muna, utang.
examples.en: Put it on my tab for now (sari-sari store).

notes.notes: Specifically money or credit. 'Mangutang' is the same meaning, slightly more formal.

examples.tl: Umutang siya sa akin, hindi pa nagbabayad.
examples.en: He borrowed money from me, hasn't paid yet.

examples.tl: Ayokong umutang sa online lending app, ang laki ng interest.
examples.en: I don't want to borrow from an online lending app, the interest is huge.

notes.notes: pa- + utang = 'let me borrow'. Casual, between friends; 'naman' softens it.

examples.tl: Pautang muna, bro, limang daan lang, babayaran ko sa sahod.
examples.en: Lend me five hundred for now, bro, I'll pay you on payday.

notes.notes: Root for borrowing things. 'Hiram lang' = just borrowed, not mine.

examples.tl: Hiram lang 'tong charger, ibalik mo ha.
examples.en: This charger is just borrowed, return it okay.

notes.notes: For objects. For money 'umutang' is more usual, though 'humiram ng pera' is fine too.

examples.tl: Pwede ba akong humiram ng payong? Umuulan.
examples.en: Can I borrow an umbrella? It's raining.

examples.tl: Humiram ako ng pera sa kapatid ko para sa deposit.
examples.en: I borrowed money from my sibling for the deposit.

notes.notes: Object focus of humiram.

examples.tl: Hihiramin ko lang yung ballpen mo, saglit.
examples.en: I'll just borrow your pen for a sec.

notes.notes: Causative: let someone borrow. Object focus is 'ipahiram' (Ipahiram mo sa kanya).

examples.tl: Nagpahiram ako ng pera sa kapatid ko, hindi pa bumabalik.
examples.en: I lent money to my sibling, it hasn't come back.

examples.tl: Ayaw niyang magpahiram ng motor.
examples.en: He doesn't want to lend his motorbike.

notes.notes: pa- request form. Very common: 'Pahiram ng charger.' Not for money (use 'pautang').

examples.tl: Pahiram ng charger, lowbat na 'ko.
examples.en: Let me borrow your charger, my battery's dying.
examples.taglish: Pahiram ng charger, lowbat na 'ko.

notes.notes: Both the pay and the day it arrives. Government and many companies pay on the 15th and 30th.

examples.tl: Kailan ang sahod mo?
examples.en: When is your payday?

examples.tl: Sa 15 at 30 ang sahod namin.
examples.en: We get paid on the 15th and 30th.

notes.notes: From Spanish sueldo. Interchangeable with sahod.

examples.tl: Maliit ang sweldo pero malapit sa bahay.
examples.en: The salary is small but it's close to home.

notes.notes: From Spanish quincena. Pair: kinsenas (15th) and katapusan (end of month).

examples.tl: Sa kinsenas na lang ako magbabayad ng renta.
examples.en: I'll pay the rent on the 15th payday instead.

notes.notes: Literally 'the end'. As payday talk: 'Katapusan na bukas.'

examples.tl: Katapusan na bukas, may pera na ulit.
examples.en: Tomorrow is month-end payday, money again.

notes.notes: Also the pronoun kita (I...you: mahal kita) and 'see' (nakita). Context decides.

examples.tl: Malaki ang kita niya sa online selling.
examples.en: She earns a lot from online selling.

examples.tl: Kumikita siya ng mga 30k kada buwan sa BPO.
examples.en: He earns about 30k a month at the BPO.

notes.notes: 'Magastos' = costly to keep / a big spender. 'Gastusin' = expenses (noun) too.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng gastos ko this month, ang dami kong binili.
examples.en: My expenses are huge this month, I bought so much.

examples.tl: Kasama na ba ang tubig sa gastos sa renta?
examples.en: Is water included in the rent costs?

notes.notes: Object focus 'gastusin' (Gastusin mo na).

examples.tl: Huwag ka nang gumastos, ako na ang magbabayad.
examples.en: Don't spend anymore, I'll pay.

notes.notes: 'Matipid' = thrifty (person or car). 'Tipid-tips' is a common magazine phrase.

examples.tl: Tipid na lang muna tayo hanggang sahod.
examples.en: Let's just be frugal until payday.

examples.tl: Matipid sa gas yung kotse ko.
examples.en: My car is fuel-efficient.

examples.tl: Nagtitipid ako kasi may babayaran akong visa extension.
examples.en: I'm cutting back because I have a visa extension to pay for.

notes.notes: Senior citizens and PWDs get 20 percent off by law, so 'senior discount' is heard everywhere.

examples.tl: May diskwento ba kung cash?
examples.en: Is there a discount if I pay cash?

examples.tl: May senior citizen discount po kami, ID lang.
examples.en: We have a senior citizen discount, just show ID.

examples.tl: Tumawad ka, mahal masyado yung presyo niya.
examples.en: Haggle, her price is too high.

examples.tl: Hindi ako marunong tumawad, nahihiya ako.
examples.en: I don't know how to haggle, I get shy.

notes.notes: The standard haggling opener. Follow with 'Last price?' or 'Kung dalawa, magkano?'

examples.tl: Wala bang tawad, kuya? Suki na 'ko dito.
examples.en: No discount, kuya? I'm a regular here already.

examples.tl: Wala bang tawad? Last price na ba yan?
examples.en: No discount? Is that your last price?

notes.notes: 'Presyuhan' = to put a price on. 'Last price' is the haggling phrase, said in English.

examples.tl: Tumaas ulit ang presyo ng bigas.
examples.en: The price of rice went up again.

examples.tl: Magkano ang presyo nito kung wholesale?
examples.en: What's the price of this wholesale?

notes.notes: 'Maningil' = to collect payment; 'singilin' = bill someone. 'Ang laki ng singil' = the bill is huge.

examples.tl: Magkano ang singil sa kuryente mo this month?
examples.en: How much is your electric charge this month?

examples.tl: May singil sa delivery, 49 pesos.
examples.en: There's a delivery charge, 49 pesos.

notes.notes: Object focus; the person billed is the topic. Actor focus is 'maningil'.

examples.tl: Sinisingil na ako ng admin para sa association dues.
examples.en: The admin is already billing me for the association dues.

notes.notes: The dominant e-wallet; accepted at carinderias, tricycle drivers, bills. Verb-ified: 'i-GCash', 'mag-GCash', 'na-GCash'.

examples.tl: GCash ka ba? I-send ko na lang.
examples.en: Are you on GCash? I'll just send it.

examples.tl: Na-GCash ko na, check mo.
examples.en: I've GCashed it already, check it.
examples.taglish: Na-GCash ko na, check mo.

notes.notes: To a vendor: asks to pay by GCash. To a friend: asks them to send via GCash. Look for the QR code sign.

examples.tl: Pa-GCash na lang ako, wala akong cash.
examples.en: I'll just pay by GCash, I have no cash.

examples.tl: Pa-GCash na lang ng share mo sa dinner.
examples.en: Just GCash me your share of the dinner.

notes.notes: Formerly PayMaya; the second big e-wallet, also a digital bank with high savings interest.

examples.tl: May Maya ka? Dun ako mag-send, wala akong GCash.
examples.en: Do you have Maya? I'll send there, I have no GCash.

notes.taglish: Punta muna ako sa bank.
notes.notes: Also 'bench' (stress on the last syllable). Manila speakers say 'bank' or just the bank's name (BPI, BDO).

examples.tl: Pupunta ako sa bangko bukas para mag-open ng account.
examples.en: I'm going to the bank tomorrow to open an account.

examples.tl: Sarado ang bangko sa Sabado hapon.
examples.en: Banks are closed Saturday afternoon.

examples.tl: Pupunta muna ako sa bangko bago tayo umalis.
examples.en: I'll go to the bank first before we leave.
examples.taglish: Dadaan muna ako sa bangko, mag-withdraw, bago tayo umalis.

notes.notes: Said letter by letter. 'ATM card' = debit card. Non-bank ATMs charge a fee; 'may service fee'.

examples.tl: May ATM ba dito malapit? Mag-withdraw lang ako.
examples.en: Is there an ATM near here? I just need to withdraw.

examples.tl: Offline yung ATM, try natin sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: The ATM is offline, let's try the 7-Eleven.

notes.notes: Standard Taglish verb. 'Pa-withdraw' at a GCash outlet = cash out.

examples.tl: Nag-withdraw ako kanina pero may 250 na fee.
examples.en: I withdrew earlier but there was a 250 fee.

examples.tl: Magwi-withdraw lang ako sa BPI sa Glorietta.
examples.en: I'll just withdraw at the BPI in Glorietta.

notes.notes: 'I-deposit' (object focus) = deposit it. Spelled 'deposito' in Tagalog but spoken as English.

examples.tl: Mag-deposit ka sa account ko, i-send ko sa 'yo yung details.
examples.en: Deposit to my account, I'll send you the details.

notes.notes: Covers money sent home and parcels. 'Pinadala' = what was sent. OFW culture word.

examples.tl: May padala ang anak niya galing Dubai buwan-buwan.
examples.en: Her child sends money from Dubai every month.

examples.tl: Kukunin ko yung padala sa Palawan Express.
examples.en: I'll pick up the remittance at Palawan Express.

notes.notes: Object focus 'ipadala' (Ipadala mo sa akin). Used for money, parcels, and 'send me the file'.

examples.tl: Nagpadala ako ng pera sa kapatid ko sa probinsya.
examples.en: I sent money to my sibling in the province.

examples.tl: Magpapadala ako ng balikbayan box sa December.
examples.en: I'll send a balikbayan box in December.

examples.tl: Nagpadala siya ng pera sa pamilya niya sa probinsya.
examples.en: He sent money to his family in the province.

notes.notes: Said in English. 'Remittance center' = Palawan, Cebuana Lhuillier, Western Union; also pawnshops.

examples.tl: Dumaan ako sa remittance center para kunin yung padala.
examples.en: I stopped by the remittance center to get the money sent.

notes.notes: magpa- because you have someone load you. 'Mag-load' also heard for loading yourself via app.

examples.tl: Magpapa-load lang ako sa tindahan, 50 lang.
examples.en: I'll just buy 50 of load at the store.

examples.tl: Nagpa-load ako ng 100 sa sari-sari store.
examples.en: I topped up 100 pesos at the corner store.

notes.notes: Said by cashiers in English. Reply 'Card po' or 'Cash po'. Many small places are 'cash lang' or GCash only.

examples.tl: Cash or card po? — Card po, debit.
examples.en: Cash or card? — Card please, debit.

examples.tl: Cash lang po tanggap namin, walang card.
examples.en: We only accept cash, no cards.

notes.notes: Said in English. 'Cash lang' = cash only. 'Cash out' at a GCash outlet = withdraw e-money.

examples.tl: May cash ka? Walang GCash yung tindahan.
examples.en: Do you have cash? The store has no GCash.

notes.notes: 'Kulang ng bente' = twenty short. 'Kulang-kulang' = roughly, a bit short. 'Nagkulang' = fell short.

examples.tl: Kulang ng bente yung bayad mo, boss.
examples.en: Your payment is twenty short, boss.

examples.tl: Kulang pa ako ng 2k para sa renta.
examples.en: I'm still 2k short for the rent.

examples.tl: Kulang ng singko ang bayad mo, kuya.
examples.en: Your payment is five pesos short, kuya.

notes.notes: 'Isang libo' = 1,000; 'tatlong libo' = 3,000. Taglish: '3k', 'three thousand'. Linker: dalawang libo.

examples.tl: Tatlong libo ang renta kada linggo? Mahal.
examples.en: Three thousand rent per week? Expensive.

examples.tl: Sampung libo ang deposit.
examples.en: The deposit is ten thousand.

notes.notes: 'Isang daan' = 100, 'dalawang daan' = 200. Becomes 'raan' after a vowel: apat na raan, anim na raan. Also 'road / way'.

examples.tl: Limang daan ang bayad sa labada.
examples.en: The laundry costs five hundred.

examples.tl: Apat na raan lang ang Grab galing airport.
examples.en: The Grab from the airport was only four hundred.

notes.notes: Spanish numbers are normal for money and time: uno, dos, tres... singko (5), diyes (10), kinse (15), bente (20), trenta (30), singkwenta (50), siyento (100).

examples.tl: Bente pesos ang pamasahe sa jeep? Ang mahal na.
examples.en: Twenty pesos for the jeep? That's gotten expensive.

examples.tl: Bente-singko ang isang pandesal dito.
examples.en: A pandesal is twenty-five here.

examples.tl: Bente isang tumpok ang kamatis.
examples.en: Tomatoes are twenty pesos a pile.

notes.notes: Prices in markets are nearly always quoted in Spanish numbers. 'Isang daan' usually replaces 'siyento' though.

examples.tl: Singkwenta lang po ang isang kilo ng kamatis.
examples.en: A kilo of tomatoes is just fifty.

examples.tl: Singkwenta ang isang kilo ng kamote ngayon.
examples.en: A kilo of sweet potato is fifty right now.

notes.notes: Kanya-kanyang bayad. Pronounced 'kay-kay-bee'. Opposite of 'libre ko' or 'sagot ko'.

examples.tl: KKB tayo mamaya ha, wala pa akong sahod.
examples.en: We each pay our own later okay, I haven't been paid yet.

notes.notes: Sagot = answer / responsibility. 'Sagot ko na yan' = I'll cover that. 'Ako na' also means 'let me pay'.

examples.tl: Sagot ko na yung dinner, birthday ko naman.
examples.en: Dinner's on me, it's my birthday anyway.

notes.notes: Also 'pipe' (same stress) and 'sugarcane' (stress on last syllable). In Taglish 'interest' is more common for loans; 'tubo' for profit.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng tubo ng credit card kung minimum lang ang bayad.
examples.en: Credit card interest is huge if you only pay the minimum.

examples.tl: Maliit lang ang tubo sa pag-reselling ng load.
examples.en: The profit from reselling load is small.

examples.tl: Kailangan ko ng puhunan para sa maliit na milk tea business.
examples.en: I need capital for a small milk tea business.

notes.notes: 'Naipon' = accumulated. 'Ipon challenge' is a popular savings game.

examples.tl: May ipon ako para sa emergency, konti lang.
examples.en: I have some savings for emergencies, just a little.

examples.tl: Naubos ang ipon ko sa hospital bill.
examples.en: My savings got used up on the hospital bill.

notes.notes: Hyphen because the root starts with a vowel. Object focus 'ipunin' (Ipunin mo yung barya).

examples.tl: Nag-iipon ako para sa bakasyon sa Palawan.
examples.en: I'm saving up for a vacation in Palawan.

examples.tl: Mag-ipon ka na, malapit na ang Pasko.
examples.en: Start saving, Christmas is near.

examples.tl: Nag-iipon ako para sa bagong motor.
examples.en: I'm saving up for a new motorbike.

notes.notes: Said in English; 'badyet' in formal spelling. 'Budget meal' = cheap set meal. 'Over budget' as-is.

examples.tl: Ang budget ko lang for rent ay 25k.
examples.en: My budget for rent is only 25k.
examples.taglish: 25k lang ang budget ko for rent.

examples.tl: May budget meal dito, 99 pesos with drinks.
examples.en: They have a budget meal here, 99 pesos with drinks.

notes.notes: 'Hulog' = one installment / a deposit. Appliances and phones are often 'hulugan' at Home Credit.

examples.tl: Hulugan lang yung cellphone ko, 12 months, zero interest.
examples.en: My phone is on installment, 12 months, zero interest.

examples.tl: Pwede bang hulugan 'to?
examples.en: Can I pay for this in installments?

notes.notes: Literally 'to drop'. Used for SSS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth contributions and for installment payments.

examples.tl: Maghuhulog ako sa SSS bukas, voluntary ako.
examples.en: I'll pay my SSS contribution tomorrow, I'm a voluntary member.

notes.notes: 'Palitan ng pera' = money changer. Also the verb 'palitan' (to replace/change) and 'palitan' with mid stress (swap with each other).

examples.tl: Saan ang magandang palitan ng dolyar dito sa Makati?
examples.en: Where's a good dollar changer here in Makati?

examples.tl: Mas maganda ang rate sa palitan kaysa sa bangko.
examples.en: The rate is better at the money changer than the bank.

notes.notes: Everyday speech often just says 'dollar(s)'. 'Ilan ang dolyar?' = what's the dollar rate.

examples.tl: Ilan ang dolyar ngayon? — Mga 57 na.
examples.en: What's the dollar at now? — About 57.

examples.tl: Magpapalit ako ng dolyar sa Sanry's.
examples.en: I'll change dollars at Sanry's.

notes.notes: Said in English, or just 'rate'. 'Mataas ang dolyar' = the peso is weak.

examples.tl: Mataas ang exchange rate ngayon, magpapalit na ako.
examples.en: The exchange rate is high today, I'll exchange now.

examples.tl: Anong rate niyo sa dollar?
examples.en: What's your dollar rate?

notes.notes: Said in English. 'Mag-open ng account'. 'Account number' is asked for transfers; 'account name' too.

examples.tl: May account ka ba sa BPI? Dun ko i-transfer.
examples.en: Do you have a BPI account? I'll transfer there.

examples.tl: Anong account name, para hindi ma-bounce?
examples.en: What's the account name, so it doesn't bounce?

notes.notes: English pronunciation. 'Check balance' at ATMs. Also for load: 'balance ng load'.

examples.tl: Check mo muna yung balance mo bago mag-withdraw.
examples.en: Check your balance first before withdrawing.

examples.tl: Maintaining balance ang hinahanap ng bangko, 3k.
examples.en: The bank requires a maintaining balance, 3k.

notes.taglish: I-transfer mo na lang sa GCash ko.
notes.notes: Used as noun and Taglish verb: 'i-transfer', 'nag-transfer', 'na-transfer na'. InstaPay = instant, PESONet = same day.

examples.tl: I-transfer mo na lang sa GCash ko, same number.
examples.en: Just transfer it to my GCash, same number.

examples.tl: Na-transfer na ba? Wala pa akong notification.
examples.en: Has it been transferred? I haven't gotten a notification.

notes.taglish: Nag-invest ako sa mutual fund.
notes.notes: Said in English. 'Mag-invest', 'nag-invest'. Scam warning: 'investment scam' is a common news phrase.

examples.tl: Nag-invest ako sa mutual fund, maliit lang, 5k monthly.
examples.en: I invested in a mutual fund, just small, 5k monthly.

examples.tl: Baka scam yan, ang laki ng promised return.
examples.en: That might be a scam, the promised return is huge.

notes.notes: 'Tax' is more common in speech; 'buwis' in news and formal. VAT is 12 percent and usually included in the price.

examples.tl: Kasama na ba ang buwis sa presyo?
examples.en: Is tax already included in the price?

examples.tl: Ang laki ng tax na kinakaltas sa sahod ko.
examples.en: The tax deducted from my salary is huge.

notes.notes: 'Kinaltas' = was deducted. 'Bawas' is the general word for 'less/reduced'.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng kaltas sa sahod ko: tax, SSS, PhilHealth.
examples.en: The deductions from my salary are huge: tax, SSS, PhilHealth.

notes.notes: You paid from your own money, usually unexpectedly. 'Mag-abono' = to advance the money.

examples.tl: Abonado ako sa dinner kagabi, hindi nagbayad si Mark.
examples.en: I was out of pocket for dinner last night, Mark didn't pay.

notes.notes: Prefix: pang-jeep, pang-gas, pang-kain, pang-rent = money for that. Spelling shifts: pam- before b/p (pambayad), pan- before d/t/s.

examples.tl: Wala akong pang-jeep, pahiram ng bente.
examples.en: I have no jeep money, lend me twenty.

examples.tl: Eto, pang-gas mo.
examples.en: Here, for your gas.

notes.notes: Fare for jeep, bus, tricycle, Grab. 'Pamasahe' also = money you give someone for their trip.

examples.tl: Magkano ang pamasahe papuntang Cubao?
examples.en: How much is the fare to Cubao?

examples.tl: Tumaas ang pamasahe sa jeep, 15 na ang minimum.
examples.en: Jeep fare went up, minimum is 15 now.

examples.tl: Magkano ang pamasahe hanggang Ayala?
examples.en: How much is the fare to Ayala?
examples.taglish: Kuya, magkano po ang pamasahe hanggang Ayala?

notes.taglish: Magkano ang pamasahe papuntang Cubao?

notes.notes: Often softened with 'ngayon' or 'muna'. 'Broke ako' and 'petsa de peligro' (days before payday) are common jokes.

examples.tl: Wala akong pera hanggang kinsenas, KKB tayo.
examples.en: I have no money until the 15th, we each pay our own.

examples.tl: Petsa de peligro na, wala na akong pera.
examples.en: Danger days before payday, I'm out of money.

notes.notes: Say it to the guard or rider when a delivery is prepaid, or to a cashier when the app already charged you.

examples.tl: Bayad na yung order, kuya, GCash. — Okay, thank you po.
examples.en: The order's already paid, via GCash. — Okay, thank you.

notes.notes: Ask before assuming something is free: parking, delivery, printing at the admin office.

examples.tl: May bayad ba yung delivery? — Wala, free na.
examples.en: Is there a delivery charge? — No, it's free.

examples.tl: May bayad ba ang pag-xerox dito sa admin?
examples.en: Is there a charge for photocopying here at the admin?

notes.notes: Metro Manila's electric utility; the name stands for the bill itself. Pay via GCash, Bayad Center or 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng Meralco namin, 6k, dahil sa aircon.
examples.en: Our electric bill is huge, 6k, because of the aircon.

notes.notes: Providers: PLDT, Globe, Converge. 'Mabagal ang internet' is a daily complaint. 'Wi-Fi' said 'wai-fai'.

examples.tl: Ang bagal ng internet, tatawag ako sa Converge.
examples.en: The internet is so slow, I'll call Converge.

examples.tl: Kasama na ba ang internet sa renta?
examples.en: Is internet included in the rent?

notes.notes: 'Bayarin' is the Tagalog, but speech uses 'bill(s)'. In a restaurant: 'Bill out po' or 'Chit po'.

examples.tl: Ang dami kong bills this month: Meralco, tubig, internet.
examples.en: I have so many bills this month: electric, water, internet.

examples.tl: Bill out na po tayo.
examples.en: Can we have the bill please.

examples.tl: Ang dami kong bayarin bago mag-Pasko.
examples.en: I have so many bills to pay before Christmas.

notes.notes: Said in English; 'due na' = it's due. 'Overdue' and 'penalty' also English.

examples.tl: Kailan ang due date ng credit card mo?
examples.en: When is your credit card due date?

examples.tl: Due na bukas yung Meralco, bayaran ko na ngayon.
examples.en: The electric bill is due tomorrow, I'll pay it now.

notes.notes: 'Upa' is the Tagalog; 'renta' and 'rent' are what Manila says. 'Magrenta' = to rent.

examples.tl: Magkano ang renta sa condo mo sa BGC?
examples.en: How much is the rent on your condo in BGC?

examples.tl: Kasama na sa renta ang dues at parking.
examples.en: Dues and parking are included in the rent.

notes.notes: Taglish 'mag-rent' is just as common. 'Magpaupa' = to rent out.

examples.tl: Umuupa lang kami, hindi amin yung unit.
examples.en: We're just renting, the unit isn't ours.

notes.notes: Seen on signs: 'Paupahan: Room for rent'. 'Apartment for rent' also as-is.

examples.tl: May paupahan daw sa Poblacion, 15k kada buwan, studio.
examples.en: There's a place for rent in Poblacion, 15k a month, studio.

notes.notes: Lease, job contract, phone plan. 'Kontraktwal' = contractual worker, a political buzzword.

examples.tl: One year ang kontrata, tapos renewable.
examples.en: The contract is one year, then renewable.

examples.tl: Basahin mo muna ang kontrata bago pumirma.
examples.en: Read the contract first before signing.

notes.notes: Standard lease ask: 'two months deposit, one month advance'. In speech it's 'deposit', English pronunciation.

examples.tl: Two months deposit at one month advance ang hinihingi ng landlord.
examples.en: The landlord is asking for two months deposit and one month advance.

examples.tl: Ibabalik ba ang deposito pagkatapos ng kontrata?
examples.en: Will the deposit be returned after the contract?

notes.notes: may + ari (possession). Used for unit owners, store owners, dog owners. 'Sino ang may-ari?' = whose is this?

examples.tl: Tatawagan ko ang may-ari, sira yung aircon.
examples.en: I'll call the owner, the aircon is broken.

examples.tl: Nasa abroad ang may-ari, broker ang kausap ko.
examples.en: The owner is abroad, I deal with the broker.

notes.notes: Said in English; 'landlady' for women. 'Kasera/kasero' is the old Tagalog word, now mainly in boarding houses.

examples.tl: Strict yung landlord ko sa visitors, pa-register sa guard.
examples.en: My landlord is strict about visitors, they register with the guard.

notes.notes: From Spanish casera. 'Kasero' for a man. Mostly in bedspace and boarding house talk, less for condos.

examples.tl: Si Aling Nena ang kasera namin, mabait pero mahigpit sa bayad.
examples.en: Aling Nena is our landlady, kind but strict about payment.

notes.notes: Both 'broker' and 'agent' used. Many condo units are listed by agents on Facebook groups.

examples.tl: May kilala kang broker? Naghahanap ako ng unit sa Salcedo.
examples.en: Do you know a broker? I'm looking for a unit in Salcedo.

notes.notes: 'Lipat-bahay' = house move; 'lipat-bahay truck' is the moving service. Also change jobs: 'lumipat ng company'.

examples.tl: Lilipat kami sa Makati next month, mas malapit sa trabaho.
examples.en: We're moving to Makati next month, closer to work.

examples.tl: Lumipat siya ng kumpanya, mas mataas ang offer.
examples.en: He moved companies, the offer was higher.

examples.tl: Lumipat kami ng tren sa Cubao.
examples.en: We switched trains at Cubao.
examples.taglish: Lumipat kami ng train sa Cubao, MRT to LRT-2.

notes.taglish: Lipat tayo ng LRT sa Taft.

accept_tl: May package ba para sa akin?
notes.notes: Ask the lobby guard or receptionist. Add unit number: 'para sa 1204'. 'Dumating' = arrived.

examples.tl: Kuya, may dumating ba na package para sa Unit 1204?
examples.en: Kuya, did a package arrive for Unit 1204?

examples.tl: May dumating ba na Lazada? Pirma lang ako.
examples.en: Did a Lazada delivery come? I'll just sign.

notes.notes: Building handymen for plumbing, electrical, aircon. Request through admin; small tip appreciated.

examples.tl: Tumawag ako sa maintenance para sa aircon cleaning.
examples.en: I called maintenance for the aircon cleaning.

notes.notes: Also 'to sort out' paperwork: 'Aayusin ko ang visa ko.' 'Pa-ayos' = have it fixed. 'Ayos' = okay, in order.

examples.tl: Aayusin daw ng maintenance yung gripo bukas.
examples.en: Maintenance will fix the faucet tomorrow.

examples.tl: Aayusin ko muna ang papeles ko sa immigration.
examples.en: I'll sort out my immigration papers first.

examples.tl: Inaayos pa ng technician ang internet.
examples.en: The technician is still fixing the internet.

notes.notes: 'Ma-cut' / 'na-cut' for utilities and internet; 'naputol' is the Tagalog. 'Disconnection notice' comes in English.

examples.tl: Bayaran mo na ang internet, baka ma-cut.
examples.en: Pay the internet now, it might get cut off.

examples.tl: Na-cut yung Meralco namin, hindi nabayaran.
examples.en: Our electricity got cut, it didn't get paid.

notes.notes: Object focus; the item is the topic. Irregular: bilhin, not bilihin.

examples.tl: Bibilhin ko yung sapatos kung may sale.
examples.en: I'll buy the shoes if there's a sale.

examples.tl: Saan mo binili yung bag mo? Ganda.
examples.en: Where did you buy your bag? Nice.

examples.tl: Binili ko yung sapatos online kasi sale.
examples.en: I bought those shoes online since they were on sale.

notes.notes: Vendors shout 'Bili na kayo!' 'Magkano bili mo?' = how much did you pay. 'Pabili' = please buy.

examples.tl: Magkano bili mo dito? Mukhang mahal.
examples.en: How much did you pay for this? Looks expensive.

notes.notes: Actor focus (ma-/mang-). Root bili: b becomes m (ma-mili). Also 'to choose' (mamili ka).

examples.tl: Namili kami sa Divisoria para sa Pasko.
examples.en: We went shopping in Divisoria for Christmas.

examples.tl: Mamimili ako sa Landmark mamaya, may kulang sa kusina.
examples.en: I'll go shopping at Landmark later, the kitchen is missing some things.

examples.tl: Mamili ka, alin ang gusto mo?
examples.en: Choose, which one do you want?

notes.notes: Tindero for a man. Address them as 'ate' / 'kuya', or 'ma'am/sir' in malls.

examples.tl: Tanong mo sa tindera kung may size 10.
examples.en: Ask the saleslady if they have size 10.

notes.notes: 'Cashier' is just as common. 'Sa kahera' / 'sa counter' = pay over there.

examples.tl: Sa kahera na po kayo magbayad, dun po.
examples.en: Please pay at the cashier, over there.

notes.notes: 'Mag-mall' = hang out at the mall, the national pastime. SM, Ayala (Glorietta, Greenbelt), Robinsons.

examples.tl: Tara sa Greenbelt, mag-mall tayo, ang init sa labas.
examples.en: Let's go to Greenbelt, hang out at the mall, it's hot outside.

examples.tl: Magkita tayo sa mall mamaya, sa Glorietta.
examples.en: Let's meet at the mall later, at Glorietta.
examples.taglish: Meet tayo sa mall mamaya, Glorietta 4, sa may cinema.

examples.tl: Nag-mall lang kami buong hapon kasi ang init.
examples.en: We just hung out at the mall all afternoon because of the heat.

notes.taglish: Mag-mall tayo, ang init sa labas.

notes.notes: 'Naka-sale' = on sale. '3-day sale', 'midnight sale', '11.11' online. 'Sale' pronounced as in English.

examples.tl: May sale sa SM, 50% off ang mga damit.
examples.en: There's a sale at SM, clothes are 50% off.

notes.notes: 'Naka-' = in the state of. Also 'Kasama ba sa sale?' = is this included in the sale.

examples.tl: Ate, naka-sale ba 'to o regular price?
examples.en: Miss, is this on sale or regular price?

notes.notes: English word. 'Anong size mo?' Shoe sizes are US sizes; clothes run small, so XL is normal for Americans.

examples.tl: May size medium ba nito?
examples.en: Do you have this in medium?

examples.tl: Anong size mo sa sapatos? — 10.
examples.en: What's your shoe size? — 10.

notes.notes: 'Anong kulay?' 'May ibang kulay?' Colors: pula, asul/blue, berde/green, dilaw, itim, puti.

examples.tl: May ibang kulay ba? Ayoko ng pula.
examples.en: Is there another color? I don't want red.

examples.tl: Anong kulay ng kotse ng Grab? Puti daw.
examples.en: What color is the Grab car? White, they say.

notes.notes: 'Sukatin' = measure; 'magsukat/isukat' = try on. 'Sakto ang sukat' = fits exactly.

examples.tl: Sakto ang sukat, hindi masikip.
examples.en: The fit is just right, not tight.

examples.tl: Anong sukat ng kama? Queen?
examples.en: What's the bed size? Queen?

notes.notes: Object focus 'isukat' (Isukat mo muna). 'Pwede bang magsukat?' is the fitting room ask.

examples.tl: Pwede bang magsukat? Saan ang fitting room?
examples.en: Can I try it on? Where's the fitting room?

examples.tl: Isukat mo muna bago bilhin, baka masikip.
examples.en: Try it on first before buying, it might be tight.

notes.notes: English. Staff may limit items: 'tatlo lang po'.

examples.tl: Saan po ang fitting room? Isusukat ko lang.
examples.en: Where's the fitting room? I'll just try it on.

notes.notes: Clothes fit and crowding: 'masikip sa MRT'. 'Sikip' root.

examples.tl: Masikip sa baywang, may mas malaki ba?
examples.en: It's tight at the waist, is there a bigger one?

examples.tl: Ang sikip sa jeep, siksikan.
examples.en: The jeep is so cramped, packed.

notes.notes: Opposite of masikip. Also 'relaxed, lenient' (maluwag ang boss) and 'traffic is light'.

examples.tl: Maluwag yung large, kunin ko na lang yung medium.
examples.en: The large is loose, I'll just take the medium.

notes.taglish: Pwede ba mag-refund?
notes.notes: 'No return, no exchange' signs are illegal under consumer law but exchange-only is common in practice. Keep the resibo.

examples.tl: Pwede ba mag-refund kung may defect?
examples.en: Can I get a refund if it's defective?

examples.tl: Store credit lang daw, walang cash refund.
examples.en: They said store credit only, no cash refund.

notes.taglish: Pwede bang i-exchange?
notes.notes: 'I-exchange', 'pa-exchange'. Usually within 7 days with receipt and tags.

examples.tl: Pwede bang i-exchange, mali yung size?
examples.en: Can I exchange it, the size is wrong?

examples.tl: Seven days lang ang exchange, dalhin mo yung resibo.
examples.en: Exchange is only within seven days, bring the receipt.

notes.notes: Ask about stock or seconds. 'Meron' is spoken 'mayroon'. Answer: 'Meron pa' / 'Ubos na'.

examples.tl: Meron pa ba nito sa size large? — Ubos na po.
examples.en: Do you still have this in large? — All sold out.

examples.tl: Meron pa bang kanin? Pa-extra rice.
examples.en: Is there more rice? Extra rice please.

notes.notes: 'Naubusan ako' = I missed out, they ran out on me. 'Out of stock' also said in English.

examples.tl: Ubos na po yung pandesal, bukas na ulit.
examples.en: The pandesal is all gone, tomorrow again.

examples.tl: Naubusan ako ng tickets, ang bilis.
examples.en: I missed out on tickets, they went so fast.

notes.notes: Greenhills, Divisoria 168, Christmas bazaars. Haggling expected. Pronounced chang-ge.

examples.tl: Sa tiangge sa Greenhills, tumawad ka lagi, mataas ang unang presyo.
examples.en: At the Greenhills bazaar, always haggle, the first price is high.

notes.notes: Market pricing is per kilo. 'Kalahating kilo' = half kilo. 'Isang kilo ng...' with linker ng.

examples.tl: Magkano ang kilo ng bangus?
examples.en: How much per kilo for bangus?

examples.tl: Kalahating kilo lang ng baboy, pakigiling.
examples.en: Just half a kilo of pork, please grind it.

examples.tl: Magkano ang kilo ng bangus, ate?
examples.en: How much is a kilo of bangus, ate?

notes.notes: A vendor's stall or anyone's assigned spot. 'Pumwesto' = take your spot.

examples.tl: May pwesto siya sa tiangge sa Baclaran, damit.
examples.en: She has a stall at the Baclaran market, clothes.

notes.notes: Default payment for Shopee and Lazada. Pronounced see-oh-dee. Have exact cash ready for the rider.

examples.tl: COD na lang yung order ko sa Shopee, wala akong card.
examples.en: My Shopee order is cash on delivery, I have no card.

examples.tl: COD po ba 'to? Magkano babayaran?
examples.en: Is this COD? How much do I pay?

notes.notes: Grab, Lalamove, Shopee, J&T riders on motorbikes. They call or text 'nasa lobby na po ako'. Tip: 'pang-tip'.

examples.tl: Nasa lobby na daw yung rider, may bayad ba?
examples.en: The rider's in the lobby, is there payment due?

examples.tl: Tumawag yung rider, hindi makahanap ng building.
examples.en: The rider called, he can't find the building.

examples.tl: Tumawag ang rider, nasa gate na siya.
examples.en: The rider called, he's at the gate.
examples.taglish: Tumawag yung rider, nasa gate na, kunin mo yung order.

notes.taglish: Nasa labas na ang rider, kunin mo ang order.

notes.notes: paki- = please. For leftovers or gifts. 'Take-out' is the usual word for food to go; 'balot' for wrapping.

examples.tl: Pakibalot po yung natira, iuuwi ko.
examples.en: Please wrap up the leftovers, I'll take them home.

examples.tl: Pakibalot na pang-gift, may ribbon.
examples.en: Please gift-wrap it, with a ribbon.

notes.notes: 'Anong trabaho mo?' = what do you do. Taglish uses 'work' heavily: 'nagwo-work ako', 'may work ako bukas'.

examples.tl: Anong trabaho mo? — Nagwo-work ako remote, IT.
examples.en: What's your job? — I work remote, IT.

examples.tl: Maraming trabaho sa BPO sa Ortigas at BGC.
examples.en: There are lots of jobs at BPOs in Ortigas and BGC.

notes.notes: Taglish equivalent 'mag-work / nag-work / nagwo-work'. 'Pumasok' is more common for 'go to work'.

examples.tl: Nagtatrabaho siya sa BPO sa Ortigas, night shift.
examples.en: She works at a BPO in Ortigas, night shift.

examples.tl: Nagtrabaho ako sa Saudi ng limang taon.
examples.en: I worked in Saudi for five years.

examples.tl: Nagtatrabaho siya sa isang BPO sa Ortigas.
examples.en: He works at a BPO in Ortigas.

notes.notes: 'Office' is what most people say. 'Officemate' = coworker.

examples.tl: Nasa opisina pa ako, late na uuwi.
examples.en: I'm still at the office, I'll go home late.

examples.tl: Saan ang office niyo? — Sa Ayala Avenue.
examples.en: Where's your office? — On Ayala Avenue.

notes.notes: Also a friendly address for strangers: guards, drivers, vendors ('Boss, magkano?'). 'Bossing' is the jokey version.

examples.tl: Mabait ang boss ko, pero strict sa deadline.
examples.en: My boss is nice, but strict about deadlines.

examples.tl: Boss, pakibukas ng gate.
examples.en: Boss, please open the gate.

examples.tl: Boss, magkano 'to?
examples.en: Boss, how much is this?

notes.notes: Used for employers of household staff, drivers, OFWs abroad. For office bosses, 'boss'. 'Maamo' (different word) = tame.

examples.tl: Mabait ang amo ng kasambahay namin dati.
examples.en: Our helper's former employer was kind.

examples.tl: Hindi nagbabayad ng tama ang amo niya sa Dubai.
examples.en: Her employer in Dubai doesn't pay properly.

notes.notes: ka- = companion in. Taglish: 'kawork', 'officemate', 'teammate'.

examples.tl: Katrabaho ko siya dati sa Makati, magkaibigan na kami.
examples.en: He was my coworker before in Makati, we're friends now.

examples.tl: Kasama sa trabaho ko si Jen, kaya kilala ko.
examples.en: Jen works with me, that's why I know her.

examples.tl: Katrabaho ko siya dati sa BPO.
examples.en: He was my coworker before at the BPO.

notes.notes: English. 'May meeting ako', 'nasa meeting'. 'Mag-meeting' = hold a meeting.

examples.tl: May meeting ako ng 10, tawagan na lang kita pagkatapos.
examples.en: I have a meeting at 10, I'll just call you after.

notes.notes: English. 'Bukas ang deadline', 'lagpas sa deadline' = past the deadline.

examples.tl: Bukas ang deadline, kaya mag-OT ako ngayon.
examples.en: The deadline is tomorrow, so I'm doing overtime today.

notes.notes: 'Mag-leave' = take leave; 'mag-file ng leave'. SL = sick leave, VL = vacation leave. Pronounced as in English.

examples.tl: Mag-leave ako sa Friday, may lakad kami sa Tagaytay.
examples.en: I'm taking leave on Friday, we have a trip to Tagaytay.

examples.tl: Nag-file na ako ng VL, approved na.
examples.en: I filed my vacation leave, it's approved.

notes.notes: 'Off ako bukas' = I'm off tomorrow. 'Rest day' used in shift work.

examples.tl: Day off ko bukas, matutulog lang ako buong araw.
examples.en: It's my day off tomorrow, I'll just sleep all day.

examples.tl: Anong off mo? — Lunes at Martes.
examples.en: What are your days off? — Monday and Tuesday.

notes.notes: Almost always 'OT' (oh-tee). 'Nag-OT', 'may OT pay', 'forced OT'.

examples.tl: Nag-OT ako kagabi hanggang 10, grabe.
examples.en: I did overtime last night until 10, intense.

examples.tl: May OT pay ba kayo o wala?
examples.en: Do you get overtime pay or not?

notes.notes: Standard Taglish verb. 'Applicant' and 'application' as-is.

examples.tl: Nag-apply ako sa tatlong kumpanya, isa ang tumawag.
examples.en: I applied to three companies, one called back.

examples.tl: Mag-aapply ako ng credit card sa BPI.
examples.en: I'll apply for a credit card at BPI.

notes.notes: English, usually pronounced 'rez-yoo-may'. Jobs sites: JobStreet, Indeed, LinkedIn.

examples.tl: I-send mo yung resume mo sa HR email, i-refer kita.
examples.en: Send your resume to the HR email, I'll refer you.

notes.notes: English. 'Ma-interview' = get interviewed. 'Final interview', 'initial interview'.

examples.tl: May interview ako bukas, kinakabahan ako.
examples.en: I have an interview tomorrow, I'm nervous.

notes.notes: The key admin word. Every office posts a list of requirements; bring photocopies of everything. 'Kumpleto ba ang requirements mo?'

examples.tl: Ano ang requirements para sa barangay clearance?
examples.en: What are the requirements for a barangay clearance?

examples.tl: Kulang ang requirements ko, bumalik ako bukas.
examples.en: My documents were incomplete, I'll come back tomorrow.

notes.notes: Pronounced eye-dee. 'Valid ID' = government-issued. Guards ask 'ID po' for visitors and often keep it until you leave.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo ang dalawang valid ID at photocopy.
examples.en: Bring two valid IDs and photocopies.

examples.tl: ID po, sir, para sa visitor pass.
examples.en: ID please, sir, for the visitor pass.

notes.notes: 'Lagda' is the formal word on forms. 'Pirma dito' = sign here.

examples.tl: Pirma dito, tapos petsa sa tabi.
examples.en: Sign here, then the date next to it.

notes.notes: Object focus 'pirmahan' (Pirmahan mo ang kontrata). Taglish 'mag-sign' also common.

examples.tl: Pumirma ka dito sa baba ng form.
examples.en: Sign here at the bottom of the form.

examples.tl: Pirmahan mo muna ang logbook sa guard.
examples.en: Sign the logbook at the guard first.

notes.notes: 'Fill-out-an mo yung form' or 'i-fill out' are standard Taglish. 'Application form', 'ballpen' needed, black ink.

examples.tl: Fill-out-an mo yung form tapos ibigay sa window 3.
examples.en: Fill out the form then give it to window 3.

notes.notes: 'Punan' is the Tagalog for fill in. Forms: 'Punan ang lahat ng patlang' = fill in all blanks.

examples.tl: I-fill out mo muna 'to bago pumila.
examples.en: Fill this out first before lining up.

examples.tl: Na-fill out ko na, kulang lang ng pirma.
examples.en: I've filled it out, it just needs a signature.

notes.notes: 'Ang haba ng pila' = the line is long. 'Pumila' = to line up. 'Singit' = cutting in line, a big sin.

examples.tl: Ang haba ng pila sa BIR, umaga pa ako dito.
examples.en: The line at the BIR is so long, I've been here since morning.

examples.tl: Saan ang pila para sa renewal?
examples.en: Where's the line for renewals?

examples.tl: Pumila ka muna dun para kumuha ng number.
examples.en: Line up over there first to get a number.

examples.tl: Pumipila na ako sa labas ng 6 AM.
examples.en: I was already lining up outside at 6 AM.

examples.tl: Pumila kami ng isang oras sa MRT.
examples.en: We lined up for an hour at the MRT.
examples.taglish: Pumila kami ng one hour sa MRT, grabe.

notes.taglish: Pumila ka sa taxi lane, bawal mag-hail sa labas.
notes.notes: Root pila = line. 'Mahaba ang pila' = long line. 'Pumila ka' is a common instruction at malls and terminals.
Government offices and banks give a queue number first. 'Kumuha ng number', 'tinawag na ang number ko'.

examples.tl: Kumuha ka muna ng number sa guard sa entrance.
examples.en: Get a number from the guard at the entrance first.

examples.tl: Tinawag na ba ang number ko? 47.
examples.en: Has my number been called? 47.

notes.notes: Clerks call 'Sunod!' 'Susunod' = the next one / upcoming (susunod na linggo = next week). 'Sumunod' = to follow.

examples.tl: Sunod! — Ako po.
examples.en: Next! — That's me.

examples.tl: Sino ang susunod sa pila?
examples.en: Who's next in line?

notes.notes: Government offices route you by numbered windows. 'Sa window 5 ang releasing.'

examples.tl: Sa window 5 po ang releasing, dun kayo pumila.
examples.en: Releasing is at window 5, line up there.

notes.notes: Pronounced bee-eye-ar. TIN = tax ID number; 'RDO' = your revenue district office. Freelancers register here.

examples.tl: Kukuha ako ng TIN sa BIR, kailangan sa bank account.
examples.en: I'll get a TIN at the BIR, it's needed for the bank account.

notes.notes: Private-sector pension system; 'hulog sa SSS' = contribution. GSIS is the government-employee version. Pag-IBIG = housing fund.

examples.tl: Automatic ang hulog ko sa SSS, kinakaltas sa payroll.
examples.en: My SSS contribution is automatic, deducted from payroll.

notes.notes: Covers part of hospital bills; foreigners with ACR can enroll voluntarily. 'May PhilHealth ka ba?' is asked at admission.

examples.tl: Gamitin mo ang PhilHealth mo sa hospital para may bawas.
examples.en: Use your PhilHealth at the hospital so there's a deduction.

notes.notes: Barangay = smallest local government unit. Get it at the barangay hall; needed for leases, jobs, police clearance. 'Cedula' often with it.

examples.tl: Kailangan ng barangay clearance para sa lease at sa bangko.
examples.en: You need a barangay clearance for the lease and the bank.

examples.tl: Saan ang barangay hall ng Poblacion?
examples.en: Where's the Poblacion barangay hall?

notes.notes: Pronounced en-bee-eye. Online appointment required; 'hit' means a name match delays release. Needed for jobs and visas.

examples.tl: May appointment ako para sa NBI clearance sa Lunes, sa Robinsons.
examples.en: I have an appointment for my NBI clearance Monday, at Robinsons.

examples.tl: May hit daw ang NBI ko, balik after one week.
examples.en: My NBI had a name hit, come back after a week.

notes.notes: Say it to the guard to skip the walk-in line. Add time and office: 'ng 9 AM sa immigration'. 'Walk-in' is also said.

examples.tl: May appointment ako sa immigration ng 9 AM, saan ang pila?
examples.en: I have a 9 AM appointment at immigration, where's the line?

examples.tl: Walk-in po ba kayo o may appointment?
examples.en: Are you a walk-in or do you have an appointment?

notes.notes: Main office in Intramuros; satellite offices in SM Aura, Robinsons and others handle extensions. 'BI' pronounced bee-eye.

examples.tl: Pupunta ako sa immigration sa Intramuros para sa extension.
examples.en: I'm going to immigration in Intramuros for the extension.

examples.tl: Mas mabilis sa BI satellite office sa mall.
examples.en: It's faster at the BI satellite office in the mall.

notes.notes: English. 'Tourist visa', '9(a)', '13(a)' spouse visa, 'SRRV' retiree visa, 'expired na ang visa'.

examples.tl: Kailan expire ang visa mo?
examples.en: When does your visa expire?

examples.tl: Nag-apply ako ng 13(a) visa kasi kasal ako sa Pilipina.
examples.en: I applied for a 13(a) visa because I'm married to a Filipina.

notes.taglish: Mag-e-extend ako ng visa.
notes.notes: 'Mag-extend', 'nag-extend', 'mag-e-extend' = extend the visa. Tourist extensions run 1 or 2 months at a time.

examples.tl: Mag-e-extend ako ng visa, dalawang buwan ulit.
examples.en: I'll extend my visa, two months again.

examples.tl: Magkano ang extension ngayon? Tumaas daw.
examples.en: How much is the extension now? They say it went up.

notes.notes: Alien Certificate of Registration. Required after 59 days; renew yearly with the annual report in January. Guards accept it as valid ID.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo ang ACR I-Card mo pag magre-renew ka.
examples.en: Bring your ACR I-Card when you renew.

examples.tl: January ang annual report, dalhin ang ACR.
examples.en: The annual report is in January, bring the ACR.

notes.notes: 'Expired' said in English for IDs, visas, food. 'Paso' is the Tagalog but rare in speech. 'Ma-expire' = to expire.

examples.tl: Expired na yung ID ko, kailangan i-renew.
examples.en: My ID has expired, it needs renewing.

examples.tl: Baka ma-expire ang visa ko bago makuha ang ACR.
examples.en: My visa might expire before I get the ACR.

notes.notes: Passports (DFA), licenses (LTO), leases, ACR. Object focus 'i-renew'.

examples.tl: Magre-renew ako ng lease, pero hihingi ako ng tawad sa renta.
examples.en: I'll renew the lease, but I'll ask for a discount on rent.

examples.tl: Nag-renew siya ng passport sa DFA Aseana.
examples.en: She renewed her passport at DFA Aseana.

notes.notes: Every government and bank transaction has one. 'Express lane fee' at immigration is a legit extra for faster service.

examples.tl: May processing fee na 500 pesos, cash lang.
examples.en: There's a processing fee of 500 pesos, cash only.

notes.notes: 'Releasing' is the pickup window. 'Kailan ang release?' = when can I pick it up. 'Na-release na' = ready.

examples.tl: Release daw ng clearance sa Wednesday, balik ako.
examples.en: The clearance is released Wednesday, I'll come back.

examples.tl: Na-release na ang ACR mo, pwede nang kunin.
examples.en: Your ACR has been released, you can pick it up.

notes.notes: Generic for photocopy, pronounced 'seroks'. 'Pa-xerox' = please copy. Xerox stalls sit outside every government office.

examples.tl: Pa-xerox ng ID, dalawang kopya, front and back.
examples.en: Photocopy my ID please, two copies, front and back.

examples.tl: May xerox sa labas, 3 pesos per page.
examples.en: There's a photocopier outside, 3 pesos per page.

notes.notes: 'Dalawang kopya' = two copies. 'Kumopya' = to copy / cheat on a test.

examples.tl: Dalawang kopya ng form, isa sa 'yo, isa sa kanila.
examples.en: Two copies of the form, one for you, one for them.

notes.notes: 'Pa-notaryo' / 'i-notarize'. Leases, affidavits and authorization letters need it; notaries cluster near city halls.

examples.tl: Pa-notaryo ng kontrata, 200 pesos lang sa tabi ng city hall.
examples.en: Get the contract notarized, just 200 pesos next to city hall.

notes.notes: Someone who offers to speed up paperwork for a fee, illegal under the Anti-Red Tape Act. Signs say 'No to fixers'.

examples.tl: Wag kang kumuha ng fixer, bawal yan at baka ma-scam ka.
examples.en: Don't get a fixer, it's illegal and you might get scammed.

notes.notes: 'Company' more common in speech. 'Pinapasukan' = the company you work at.

examples.tl: Anong kumpanya ang pinapasukan mo?
examples.en: What company do you work for?

notes.notes: 'May pasok' = there's work/class; 'walang pasok' = suspended (holiday, typhoon). Also 'come in': 'Pasok!'

examples.tl: May pasok ba bukas? — Wala, holiday.
examples.en: Is there work tomorrow? — No, it's a holiday.

examples.tl: Walang pasok sa Metro Manila dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: No work or classes in Metro Manila because of the typhoon.

notes.notes: English. 'Regular holiday' = double pay; 'special non-working'. Government offices and banks close; malls stay open.

examples.tl: Holiday sa Lunes, sarado ang mga government office.
examples.en: Monday is a holiday, government offices are closed.

examples.tl: Long weekend! Holiday sa Friday.
examples.en: Long weekend! Friday is a holiday.

notes.notes: Mandatory extra month of salary paid by December 24. Pronounced 'thirteenth month'. 'Pang-Pasko' money.

examples.tl: Sa December ang 13th month, pang-Pasko at pang-ipon.
examples.en: The 13th month pay comes in December, for Christmas and savings.

notes.notes: English. HMO (health card), rice allowance, 13th month, SL/VL. 'Regular' status after six months probation unlocks them.

examples.tl: May HMO at rice allowance sa benefits, kaya tinanggap ko.
examples.en: The benefits include an HMO and rice allowance, so I accepted.

notes.notes: From 'racket' but neutral: a side job or one-off paid gig. 'May raket ako' = I've got a gig. 'Nagraraket' = hustling.

examples.tl: May raket ako sa weekends, nagtuturo ng English online.
examples.en: I have a side gig on weekends, teaching English online.

notes.notes: Filipino English for a second income source. 'Sideline ko' = my side job.

examples.tl: Sideline ko ang pag-Grab tuwing gabi, pandagdag sa renta.
examples.en: Driving Grab at night is my side job, to help with rent.

notes.notes: 'Mag-negosyo' = go into business. 'Negosyante' = businessperson. Small businesses: milk tea, sari-sari store, online selling.

examples.tl: Gusto kong mag-negosyo, maliit na cafe sa Poblacion.
examples.en: I want to start a business, a small cafe in Poblacion.

notes.notes: 'Nawalan ng' = lost (something). 'Natanggal' = got removed/fired. 'Na-laid off' and 'na-retrench' also heard.

examples.tl: Nawalan siya ng trabaho noong pandemic, ngayon nag-Grab.
examples.en: He lost his job during the pandemic, now he drives Grab.

notes.notes: Key admin verb: kumuha ng number, ng clearance, ng ID. Object focus 'kunin' (Kunin mo). 'Pakuha' = please get.

examples.tl: Kukuha ako ng barangay clearance bukas ng umaga.
examples.en: I'll get a barangay clearance tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: Kumuha ka ng number sa guard bago pumila.
examples.en: Get a number from the guard before lining up.

examples.tl: Kumuha ako ng tubig sa ref.
examples.en: I got some water from the fridge.

notes.notes: Object focus of kumuha. Irregular: kunin, not kuhain. 'Kukunin ko mamaya' = I'll pick it up later.

examples.tl: Kukunin ko yung package sa guard mamaya.
examples.en: I'll pick up the package from the guard later.

examples.tl: Kinuha na ba niya ang sukli?
examples.en: Did he take the change already?

examples.tl: Kinuha ko na ang package sa lobby.
examples.en: I already picked up the package from the lobby.

notes.notes: Forms, requirements, reports: 'ipasa sa window 2'. Also pass the ball / the salt. 'Mag-submit' is the Taglish option.

examples.tl: Ipasa mo yung form sa window 2, tapos hintayin ang pangalan mo.
examples.en: Submit the form at window 2, then wait for your name.

examples.tl: Ipinasa ko na ang requirements ko sa HR.
examples.en: I already submitted my requirements to HR.

notes.notes: Offices, stores, roads. 'Sarado pag lunch' = closed at lunch, common in government offices. 'Isara' = to close.

examples.tl: Sarado ang BIR pag lunch, 12 to 1, kumain muna tayo.
examples.en: The BIR is closed at lunch, 12 to 1, let's eat first.

examples.tl: Sarado na ang bangko, 3 PM lang.
examples.en: The bank is already closed, only until 3 PM.

notes.notes: Stress distinguishes: bukas with final stress (open) vs first-syllable stress (tomorrow). Context clears it. 'Buksan' = to open.

examples.tl: Bukas ba ang bangko sa Sabado? — Bukas, hanggang 12.
examples.en: Is the bank open Saturday? — Open, until 12.

examples.tl: Bukas pa ang tindahan, bilis.
examples.en: The store is still open, hurry.

notes.notes: On forms: 'Petsa' next to 'Lagda'. 'Anong petsa ngayon?' = what's the date. 'Petsa de peligro' = broke days before payday.

examples.tl: Lagay mo ang petsa ngayon sa tabi ng pirma.
examples.en: Put today's date next to the signature.

examples.tl: Anong petsa ang flight mo? Para ma-check ko ang schedule ko.
examples.en: What date is your flight? So I can check my schedule.

notes.notes: English. 'Performance bonus', 'Christmas bonus' (separate from the mandatory 13th month). 'May bonus ba kayo?'

examples.tl: May bonus kami sa December kung maabot ang target.
examples.en: We get a bonus in December if we hit the target.

notes.notes: English for the bank product; 'ipon' for the money itself. Digital banks (Maya, GoTyme, CIMB) pay higher interest than BDO/BPI.

examples.tl: Mag-open ka ng savings sa digital bank, mataas ang interest.
examples.en: Open a savings account at a digital bank, the interest is high.

notes.notes: English in everyday talk; 'tubo' in Tagalog. 'Zero interest' installment deals are everywhere. 'Patubuan' = money lending at interest.

examples.tl: Zero interest kung 6 months installment sa card.
examples.en: Zero interest if it's 6 months installment on the card.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng interest ng 5-6, iwasan mo.
examples.en: The interest on 5-6 lending is huge, avoid it.

notes.notes: Core cultural value: a favor creates a lasting obligation to repay. 'Walang utang na loob' = ungrateful, a serious insult.

examples.tl: Malaki ang utang na loob ko sa kanya, tinulungan niya ako nung wala akong trabaho.
examples.en: I owe him a big debt of gratitude, he helped me when I had no job.

notes.en: Put it on my tab for now.
notes.notes: Sari-sari store credit: the owner keeps a 'listahan' (notebook) of what you owe, paid on payday. Only for suki.

examples.tl: Ate, ilista mo muna, sa Sabado ko babayaran.
examples.en: Ate, put it on my tab for now, I'll pay Saturday.

notes.notes: 'Chit' is an old Filipino English word for the restaurant bill. 'Bill out' is the common alternative. Make a signing gesture in the air.

examples.tl: Chit po, tapos pa-separate yung sa amin.
examples.en: The bill please, and separate ours.

notes.notes: Spanish loan. 'Family' itself is just as common in Taglish ('family day', 'family dinner').

examples.tl: Malapit ako sa pamilya ko.
examples.en: I'm close to my family.

examples.tl: May family dinner kami sa Sunday, kaya hindi ako makakasama.
examples.en: We have a family dinner on Sunday, so I can't join.

notes.notes: Usually plural 'mga magulang'. 'Parents' is also fine in Taglish.

examples.tl: Nasa probinsya pa ang mga magulang ko.
examples.en: My parents are still in the province.

examples.tl: Strict ang magulang niya, kaya laging may curfew.
examples.en: Her parents are strict, so there's always a curfew.

notes.notes: Formal or written (forms, prayers: 'Ama Namin'). In speech people say tatay, papa, daddy.

examples.tl: Pangalan ng ama: isulat sa form.
examples.en: Father's name: write it on the form.

examples.tl: Namatay ang ama niya noong bata pa siya.
examples.en: His father died when he was still young.

notes.notes: Address form: 'Tay'. Many Manila families say 'Papa' or 'Daddy'. Old slang: 'erpat'.

examples.tl: Si Tatay ang nagluto ng ulam.
examples.en: Dad was the one who cooked the ulam.

examples.tl: Tay, pahiram ng kotse mamaya.
examples.en: Dad, can I borrow the car later?

notes.notes: Formal or written. In speech: nanay, mama, mommy. 'Ina' also appears in 'Inang Bayan' (motherland).

examples.tl: Pangalan ng ina bago mag-asawa: Reyes.
examples.en: Mother's maiden name: Reyes.

examples.tl: Single mom siya, siya lang ang ina at ama ng mga bata.
examples.en: She's a single mom, both mother and father to the kids.

notes.notes: Address form: 'Nay'. 'Mama'/'Mommy' very common in Manila. Old slang: 'ermat'.

examples.tl: Tumawag si Nanay, kumusta daw ako.
examples.en: Mom called, asking how I am.

examples.tl: Nay, uuwi ako sa Sabado.
examples.en: Mom, I'm coming home on Saturday.

notes.notes: Offspring, not age (compare 'bata' = kid). Also used as address: 'Anak, kain na.'

examples.tl: Ilan ang anak mo?
examples.en: How many kids do you have?

examples.tl: Nag-graduate na ang panganay kong anak.
examples.en: My eldest child already graduated.

notes.notes: Gender-neutral. 'Kapatid na lalaki/babae' when you need the gender; or just kuya/ate/bunso.

examples.tl: Tatlo kaming magkakapatid.
examples.en: There are three of us siblings.

examples.tl: Nasa Dubai ang kapatid ko, OFW.
examples.en: My sibling is in Dubai, an OFW.

notes.notes: Also the default address for any slightly older guy: waiter, Grab driver, guard. See the Kuya/Ate address note.

examples.tl: Si Kuya ang nagbayad ng kuryente.
examples.en: My older brother paid the electric bill.

examples.tl: Close ako sa kuya ko kahit lagi kaming nag-aaway dati.
examples.en: I'm close to my big brother even though we used to fight all the time.

notes.notes: Also address for any slightly older woman (cashier, server). Pronounced AH-teh, two syllables.

examples.tl: Nasa Canada na ang ate ko.
examples.en: My older sister is in Canada now.

examples.tl: Si Ate ang laging nag-aayos ng gulo namin.
examples.en: My big sister is the one who always fixes our mess.

notes.notes: The baby of the family, at any age. 'Spoiled bunso' is a running joke.

examples.tl: Ako ang bunso, kaya ako ang laging inuutusan.
examples.en: I'm the youngest, so I'm always the one sent on errands.

examples.tl: Spoiled talaga ang bunso nila.
examples.en: Their youngest is really spoiled.

notes.notes: Culturally expected to help support younger siblings ('panganay pressure').

examples.tl: Panganay ako, kaya ako ang breadwinner.
examples.en: I'm the eldest, so I'm the breadwinner.

examples.tl: Si panganay ang pinakamatured sa kanila.
examples.en: The eldest is the most mature of them.

notes.notes: Address: 'Lolo' or 'Lo'. Also used for any elderly man, jokingly for friends who act old.

examples.tl: Beterano rin ang lolo ko.
examples.en: My grandfather is also a veteran.

examples.tl: Si Lolo ang nagturo sa akin mag-chess.
examples.en: Grandpa taught me how to play chess.

notes.notes: Address: 'Lola' or 'La'. 'Lola mo!' is a playful retort.

examples.tl: Masarap magluto si Lola.
examples.en: Grandma cooks well.

examples.tl: Dadalawin namin si Lola sa Bulacan ngayong weekend.
examples.en: We're visiting Grandma in Bulacan this weekend.

notes.notes: Also for parents' friends and any man of that generation. 'Tito jokes' = dad jokes.

examples.tl: Si Tito Ben ang nagsundo sa amin sa airport.
examples.en: Uncle Ben picked us up at the airport.

examples.tl: Ang dami niyang tito, ang laki ng pamilya.
examples.en: He has so many uncles, it's a huge family.

notes.notes: Also for mom's friends and your partner's aunts. 'Tita' jokingly = nosy middle-aged-lady energy ('tita questions').

examples.tl: Nakilala ko na ang mga tita ng jowa ko, grabe ang tanong.
examples.en: I met my partner's aunts, wow, the questions.

examples.tl: Tita, salamat po sa pasalubong!
examples.en: Auntie, thank you for the gift!

notes.notes: Cousins are often as close as siblings; 'pinsang buo' = first cousin.

examples.tl: Kasal ng pinsan ko sa Tagaytay next month.
examples.en: My cousin's wedding is in Tagaytay next month.

examples.tl: Magpinsan sila pero parang magkapatid.
examples.en: They're cousins but they're like siblings.

notes.notes: Gender-neutral. Titos and titas are expected to bring pasalubong for pamangkin.

examples.tl: Birthday ng pamangkin ko bukas, bibili ako ng regalo.
examples.en: My niece's birthday is tomorrow, I'll buy a gift.

examples.tl: Ang cute ng pamangkin mo!
examples.en: Your nephew is so cute!

notes.notes: Gender-neutral. 'Mister'/'misis' also common in speech. 'May asawa' = married.

examples.tl: May asawa na ba siya?
examples.en: Is he married already?

examples.tl: Taga-Cebu ang asawa ko.
examples.en: My spouse is from Cebu.

notes.notes: A bit formal/old-fashioned. In Manila speech 'boyfriend', 'BF' or 'jowa' are more common.

examples.tl: May nobyo na si ate, dati pa.
examples.en: Big sister has a boyfriend, for a while now.

examples.tl: Boyfriend mo ba 'yun?
examples.en: Is that your boyfriend?

notes.notes: Same register as nobyo. 'Girlfriend'/'GF' far more common in speech.

examples.tl: Ipakilala mo naman ang nobya mo sa amin.
examples.en: Introduce your girlfriend to us, come on.

examples.tl: Three years na silang mag-GF-BF.
examples.en: They've been girlfriend and boyfriend for three years.

notes.notes: Casual slang, gender-neutral, extremely common. 'May jowa ka na?' = are you seeing someone?

examples.tl: May jowa ka na ba?
examples.en: Do you have a partner now?

examples.tl: Date night namin ng jowa ko sa BGC.
examples.en: My partner and I have date night in BGC.

notes.notes: Formal/literary (songs, forms, news). Rare in speech; people say jowa, boyfriend, girlfriend.

examples.tl: Kasintahan niya ang kasama niya sa litrato.
examples.en: The one with him in the photo is his sweetheart.

notes.notes: 'Friend' is just as common in Taglish. Close friend: 'bestfriend', 'bes', 'beshie'.

examples.tl: Matagal na kaming kaibigan, since college.
examples.en: We've been friends a long time, since college.

examples.tl: Kaibigan ko siya, hindi jowa.
examples.en: He's my friend, not my partner.

notes.notes: Your crew. 'Kabarkada' = a member of your group. 'Barkada trip' = group outing.

examples.tl: Inuman kami ng barkada ko sa Poblacion sa Friday.
examples.en: My friends and I are drinking in Poblacion on Friday.

examples.tl: Kabarkada ko siya noong high school.
examples.en: He was part of my group in high school.

notes.notes: Slang, slightly more 'bro' than barkada. Also address: 'Tropa!' / 'tropz'.

examples.tl: Kasama ko ang tropa sa gym mamaya.
examples.en: I'm with the squad at the gym later.

examples.tl: Tropa, tara, kain tayo!
examples.en: Guys, come on, let's eat!

notes.notes: Noun and quasi-verb. 'Kasama ko siya' = I'm with him. 'Sama ka?' = coming along? 'Kasama sa bahay' = housemate.

examples.tl: Sino ang kasama mo kagabi?
examples.en: Who were you with last night?

examples.tl: Kasama ba ang jowa mo sa trip?
examples.en: Is your partner coming on the trip?

notes.notes: 'May bisita kami' = we have company. Verb: bumisita/dumalaw = to visit. Guests are always fed.

examples.tl: May bisita kami, kaya nagluto si Mama ng marami.
examples.en: We have guests, so Mom cooked a lot.

examples.tl: Bisita lang ako dito, hindi ako taga-rito.
examples.en: I'm just a visitor here, I'm not from here.

notes.notes: Also a wedding sponsor. Expected to give aguinaldo (cash gift) at Christmas; running joke that ninongs hide in December.

examples.tl: Ninong ako sa binyag ng anak ng kaibigan ko.
examples.en: I'm godfather at my friend's child's baptism.

examples.tl: Nagtatago na ang mga ninong, Pasko na.
examples.en: The godfathers are hiding now, it's Christmas.

notes.notes: Female counterpart of ninong. Being asked to be ninang is an honor (and an expense).

examples.tl: Tinanong ako kung gusto kong maging ninang.
examples.en: I was asked if I'd like to be godmother.

examples.tl: Ninang ko si Tita Marie.
examples.en: Auntie Marie is my godmother.

notes.notes: Your godson/goddaughter. Plural 'mga inaanak'.

examples.tl: Lima ang inaanak ko, mahal ang Pasko.
examples.en: I have five godchildren, Christmas is expensive.

notes.notes: Originally the godfather of your child (or vice versa); now also any close male friend. Female: kumare. Address: 'pare'.

examples.tl: Kumpare ko siya, ninong siya ng anak ko.
examples.en: He's my compadre, he's my kid's godfather.

examples.tl: Mga kumpare ni Tatay ang nag-inuman sa garahe.
examples.en: Dad's buddies were drinking in the garage.

notes.notes: Related: manugang = child-in-law, bayaw = brother-in-law, hipag = sister-in-law. 'In-laws' is common in Taglish.

examples.tl: Mabait ang biyenan ko, swerte ako.
examples.en: My mother-in-law is kind, I'm lucky.

examples.tl: Lunch kami sa mga biyenan ko sa Sunday.
examples.en: We're having lunch at my in-laws' on Sunday.

notes.notes: Gender-neutral. The classic 'biyenan vs manugang' tension is a teleserye staple.

examples.tl: Gusto ng nanay niya ang bagong manugang.
examples.en: His mom likes her new daughter-in-law.

notes.notes: Also address from grandparents: 'Apo, halika.'

examples.tl: Ang dami nang apo ni Lola.
examples.en: Grandma has so many grandchildren now.

examples.tl: Spoiled si bunso kasi favorite na apo.
examples.en: The youngest is spoiled because he's the favorite grandchild.

notes.notes: 'Magkambal' = twins (as a pair). Also a nickname/address between twins.

examples.tl: Kambal sila pero magkaiba ang ugali.
examples.en: They're twins but have different personalities.

notes.notes: Blunt gossip/teleserye register, any gender. Softer: 'ang third party', 'may iba'. Use with care.

examples.tl: Chismis daw, may kabit ang asawa niya.
examples.en: Rumor is her husband has a mistress.

notes.notes: Used exactly as in English, very common. 'Dating jowa' also works.

examples.tl: Nakita ko ang ex ko sa mall, awkward.
examples.en: I saw my ex at the mall, awkward.

examples.tl: Hindi pa siya nakaka-move on sa ex niya.
examples.en: He hasn't moved on from his ex yet.

notes.notes: 'Maraming tao' = crowded. 'Walang tao' = nobody's there. 'Tao po!' = anybody home? (said at a gate).

examples.tl: Ang daming tao sa MRT kanina.
examples.en: There were so many people on the MRT earlier.

examples.tl: Mabait siyang tao.
examples.en: He's a kind person.

notes.notes: Also spelled/said 'lalake'. 'Anak na lalaki' = son. 'Mga lalaki' = the guys.

examples.tl: Sino 'yung lalaking kasama ni ate?
examples.en: Who's that guy with big sister?

examples.tl: Mga lalaki ang nag-asikaso ng ihaw.
examples.en: The guys handled the grilling.

notes.notes: 'Anak na babae' = daughter. 'Mga babae' = the girls/ladies. 'Girl' itself is common in Taglish.

examples.tl: Puro babae ang officemate ko.
examples.en: My officemates are all women.

examples.tl: Ang babaeng 'yun ang bagong manager.
examples.en: That woman is the new manager.

notes.notes: About age (vs anak = offspring). Also adj 'young': 'bata pa siya' = he's still young. 'Mga bata' = the kids.

examples.tl: Maraming bata sa pool tuwing Sabado.
examples.en: There are lots of kids at the pool on Saturdays.

examples.tl: Bata pa siya pero manager na.
examples.en: She's still young but already a manager.

notes.notes: Noun and adj. 'Matanda na' = already old. 'Mas matanda sa akin' = older than me. Polite: 'nakatatanda'.

examples.tl: Mas matanda siya sa akin ng tatlong taon.
examples.en: He's three years older than me.

examples.tl: Pauupo mo ang matanda sa jeep.
examples.en: Let the elderly person sit on the jeep.

notes.notes: Unmarried young man. 'Binata na siya' = he's grown up now. Titas love asking 'binata pa?' (still single?).

examples.tl: Binata pa ba ang kuya mo?
examples.en: Is your older brother still single?

examples.tl: Ang laki na ng pamangkin ko, binata na.
examples.en: My nephew is so grown up now, a young man already.

notes.notes: Counterpart of binata. 'Dalaga na' = she's grown up. 'Dalagang Pilipina' is a cultural ideal/song.

examples.tl: Dalaga na ang anak ni Tita, college na.
examples.en: Auntie's daughter is a young woman now, in college already.

examples.tl: Dalaga pa siya, walang jowa.
examples.en: She's still single, no partner.

notes.notes: Formal: 'Ginoong Santos' (G.) = Mr. Santos. 'Mga ginoo at binibini' = ladies and gentlemen. In speech people say 'sir'.

examples.tl: Ginoong Cruz, puwede po kayong pumasok.
examples.en: Mr. Cruz, you may come in.

notes.notes: Formal: 'Ginang Reyes' (Gng.). Miss = 'Binibini' (Bb.). In speech: 'ma'am', 'misis'.

examples.tl: Para kay Ginang Reyes ang sulat.
examples.en: The letter is for Mrs. Reyes.

notes.en: polite address to customers or strangers
notes.notes: Default polite address by guards, cashiers, Grab drivers, in offices. 'Mamser' jokingly merges both. Reply politely with 'po'.

examples.tl: Sir, bawal po ang shorts dito.
examples.en: Sir, shorts aren't allowed here.

examples.tl: Ma'am, GCash po ba o cash?
examples.en: Ma'am, GCash or cash?

notes.notes: From kumpare. Men to men, very common. Shortened 'pre'. Similar: 'tol', 'bro', 'tsong', 'dude'.

examples.tl: Pare, tara, inom tayo mamaya.
examples.en: Bro, come on, let's drink later.

examples.tl: Pre, nasaan ka na? Late ka na.
examples.en: Dude, where are you? You're late.

notes.notes: Used as in English, also 'brad' / 'bruh'. Women friends: 'sis', 'bes', 'girl', 'mars'.

examples.tl: Bro, salamat sa libre ha.
examples.en: Bro, thanks for the treat, okay.

examples.tl: Sis, kita tayo sa Glorietta.
examples.en: Sis, let's meet at Glorietta.

notes.en: address for staff or slightly older strangers
notes.notes: Polite-friendly for waiters, drivers, cashiers, guards, vendors, roughly your age or older. Add 'po'. Never rude.

examples.tl: Kuya, para po sa tabi.
examples.en: Kuya, please stop at the side (getting off a jeep).

examples.tl: Ate, isang iced coffee po, less sugar.
examples.en: Ate, one iced coffee please, less sugar.

accept: sir (address for a driver, older man)
notes.notes: For noticeably older working men: tricycle driver, guard, vendor, plumber. Respectful, not rude. Female: manang.

examples.tl: Manong, sa 7-Eleven lang po.
examples.en: Manong, just to the 7-Eleven please.

examples.tl: Si Manong guard ang tumanggap ng package.
examples.en: Manong the guard received the package.

examples.tl: Manong, para po sa kanto.
examples.en: Sir, please stop at the corner.
examples.taglish: Manong, para po sa kanto, salamat.

notes.taglish: Manong, sa Ayala po.

notes.notes: For older working women (vendors, helpers). Also adj 'manang' = old-fashioned/prudish in dress or attitude.

examples.tl: Manang, pabili po ng dalawang itlog.
examples.en: Manang, two eggs please.

examples.tl: Manang ang damit niya, parang pang-simba.
examples.en: Her outfit is so old-fashioned, like church clothes.

notes.notes: Calling an elderly vendor or stranger 'Nay' or 'Tay' (from nanay/tatay) is warm and respectful. Also 'Nanay'/'Tatay' in full.

examples.tl: Nay, magkano po ang saging?
examples.en: Ma'am, how much are the bananas?

examples.tl: Tay, dito lang po ako bababa.
examples.en: Sir, I'll get off right here.

notes.notes: Also 'schoolmate', 'batchmate' (same graduating year), 'kabatch'.

examples.tl: Kaklase ko siya noong high school.
examples.en: She was my classmate in high school.

examples.tl: Reunion ng mga kaklase ko sa December.
examples.en: My classmates' reunion is in December.

notes.notes: Someone you know but not a friend. 'Kakilala ko lang siya' = I just know him.

examples.tl: Hindi kami close, kakilala ko lang siya.
examples.en: We're not close, he's just an acquaintance.

examples.tl: May kakilala ako sa BIR, tanungin ko.
examples.en: I know someone at the BIR, I'll ask.

notes.notes: Live-in or daytime nanny, very common in middle-class Manila households. Address: 'Yaya' or 'Ate'.

examples.tl: Umalis ang yaya nila, kaya WFH si misis.
examples.en: Their nanny quit, so the wife is working from home.

examples.tl: Mahal na ang sweldo ng yaya sa Makati.
examples.en: Nanny salaries are expensive in Makati now.

notes.notes: 60+. Senior ID gives 20% discount; 'senior lane' at banks and pharmacies. 'Senior na si Tatay.'

examples.tl: May senior discount po ba kayo?
examples.en: Do you have a senior discount?

examples.tl: Pumila si Lola sa senior lane.
examples.en: Grandma lined up in the senior lane.

notes.notes: Collective. 'Mga kabataan ngayon' = kids these days (classic tito line). Also 'kabataan' = youth (time of life).

examples.tl: Puro cellphone ang mga kabataan ngayon.
examples.en: Young people today are all on their phones.

notes.notes: Used as-is: 'Sad ako', 'nakaka-sad', 'na-sad ako'. Lighter than malungkot.

examples.tl: Sad ako, cancelled ang trip namin.
examples.en: I'm sad, our trip got cancelled.

examples.tl: Nakaka-sad 'yung balita tungkol sa lolo niya.
examples.en: The news about his grandfather is saddening.

notes.notes: 'Galit ka ba sa akin?' = are you mad at me? 'Nagalit' = got angry; 'nagagalit' = is getting angry.

examples.tl: Galit si Mama kasi late ako umuwi.
examples.en: Mom's angry because I came home late.

examples.tl: Huwag ka nang magalit, nag-sorry na ako.
examples.en: Don't be angry anymore, I already said sorry.

notes.notes: Incompleted aspect of magalit. 'Nagalit' = got angry (done). 'Magagalit' = will get angry.

examples.tl: Nagagalit si boss kapag late ang report.
examples.en: The boss gets angry when the report is late.

examples.tl: Magagalit ang jowa ko kung makalimutan ko ang monthsary.
examples.en: My partner will get mad if I forget our monthsary.

notes.notes: 'Takot ako sa ipis' = I'm scared of cockroaches. 'Natatakot' = feeling afraid (now). 'Nakakatakot' = scary.

examples.tl: Takot siya sa aso.
examples.en: She's afraid of dogs.

examples.tl: Takot akong mag-drive sa EDSA.
examples.en: I'm scared to drive on EDSA.

notes.notes: From matakot. 'Natakot ako' = I got scared. 'Natatakot ako na...' = I'm afraid that...
