examples.tl: Natatakot akong mag-isa sa condo kapag may bagyo.
examples.en: I'm scared being alone in the condo when there's a typhoon.

examples.tl: Natakot ako sa lindol kanina.
examples.en: The earthquake earlier scared me.

notes.notes: From kaba (nervousness). 'Kinabahan ako' = I got nervous. Texting: 'kinakabahan ako huhu'.

examples.tl: Kinakabahan ako sa interview ko bukas.
examples.en: I'm nervous about my interview tomorrow.

examples.tl: Kinabahan ako nang makilala ko ang parents niya.
examples.en: I got nervous when I met her parents.

notes.notes: Used as-is: 'Excited ako', 'na-excite ako', 'nakaka-excite'. Tagalog 'nasasabik' is formal.

examples.tl: Excited na ako sa trip natin sa Palawan!
examples.en: I'm excited for our Palawan trip!

examples.tl: Na-excite ang mga bata sa bagong puppy.
examples.en: The kids got excited about the new puppy.

notes.notes: 'Inis ako sa kanya' = I'm annoyed at him. 'Nakakainis' = annoying. 'Naiinis' = getting annoyed.

examples.tl: Inis ako kasi laging late ang Grab.
examples.en: I'm annoyed because the Grab is always late.

examples.tl: Inis na inis siya sa kapitbahay namin.
examples.en: She's super annoyed at our neighbor.

notes.notes: From mainis. 'Nainis ako' = I got annoyed. Super common in GC rants.

examples.tl: Naiinis ako sa traffic sa EDSA araw-araw.
examples.en: I get annoyed with the EDSA traffic every day.

examples.tl: Nainis siya kasi hindi ako nag-reply.
examples.en: She got annoyed because I didn't reply.

notes.notes: From hiya (shame/shyness), a core Filipino concept. 'Nahiya ako' = I was embarrassed. 'Nakakahiya' = embarrassing.

examples.tl: Nahihiya akong humingi ng tulong sa kanila.
examples.en: I'm shy about asking them for help.

examples.tl: Nahiya ako, nakalimutan ko ang pangalan niya.
examples.en: I was embarrassed, I forgot her name.

notes.notes: Also 'Nakakahiya naman' when someone gives you something = oh, you shouldn't have. Slang: 'nakakahiya', 'shems'.

examples.tl: Nakakahiya, nadapa ako sa harap ng crush ko.
examples.en: So embarrassing, I tripped in front of my crush.

examples.tl: Nakakahiya naman, ikaw na naman ang nag-libre.
examples.en: Oh you shouldn't have, you treated us again.

notes.notes: 'Stress ako' / 'na-stress ako' / 'nakaka-stress'. Also 'stressed' as-is.

examples.tl: Na-stress ako sa trabaho buong linggo.
examples.en: I was stressed from work all week.

examples.tl: Nakaka-stress ang pag-renew ng visa.
examples.en: Renewing the visa is stressful.

notes.notes: Nakaka- + root = 'causes X'. Common with people too: 'nakakapagod kausap' = tiring to talk to.

examples.tl: Nakakapagod ang commute mula Cavite hanggang Makati.
examples.en: The commute from Cavite to Makati is exhausting.

examples.tl: Nakakapagod siyang kausap, puro reklamo.
examples.en: He's tiring to talk to, all complaints.

notes.notes: 'Bored ako' / 'nabo-bored ako' / 'nakaka-bored'. Tagalog: 'naiinip' (impatient/bored waiting).

examples.tl: Bored ako, walang magawa sa condo.
examples.en: I'm bored, nothing to do in the condo.

examples.tl: Nabo-bored ang mga bata sa misa.
examples.en: The kids get bored at mass.

notes.notes: From inip. Specifically the boredom of waiting. 'Nainip ako' = I got tired of waiting.

examples.tl: Naiinip na ako, isang oras na akong naghihintay sa Grab.
examples.en: I'm getting impatient, I've been waiting an hour for the Grab.

examples.tl: Nainip ang mga bisita, late ang celebrant.
examples.en: The guests got restless, the celebrant was late.

notes.notes: Taglish verb: 'Na-miss kita', 'na-miss ko ang adobo ni Lola'. 'Nami-miss' = currently missing. Tagalog 'nangungulila' is formal.

examples.tl: Na-miss kita! Ang tagal nating hindi nagkita.
examples.en: I missed you! It's been so long since we saw each other.

examples.tl: Nami-miss ko na ang pamilya ko sa probinsya.
examples.en: I'm missing my family in the province.

notes.notes: Everyday text to partner/family. 'Miss ko na kayo' to a group. 'Miss kita' alone also works.

examples.tl: Miss na kita, kailan ka uuwi?
examples.en: I miss you already, when are you coming home?

examples.tl: Miss ko na kayo, tropa. Inuman soon!
examples.en: I miss you guys, squad. Drinks soon!

notes.notes: Taglish nakaka- form. Said when something brings back fond memories: old photos, a reunion, hometown food.

examples.tl: Nakakamiss ang college days natin.
examples.en: Our college days make me miss them.

examples.tl: Nakakamiss 'yung tambay natin sa kanto dati.
examples.en: I miss how we used to hang out at the corner.

notes.notes: Also 'expensive'. 'Mahal' as address = dear/babe. 'Mahal kita' = I love you. 'Mahal ko siya' = I love him/her.

examples.tl: Mahal, nasaan ka na?
examples.en: Babe, where are you now?

examples.tl: Mahal niya talaga ang pamilya niya.
examples.en: He really loves his family.

notes.notes: Romantic or family. 'Mahal ko kayo' to parents/kids. 'Love you' / 'lab yu' also common in text.

examples.tl: Mahal kita, ingat ka sa biyahe.
examples.en: I love you, take care on the trip.

examples.tl: Mahal ko kayo, Ma, Pa. Happy anniversary!
examples.en: I love you, Mom, Dad. Happy anniversary!

notes.notes: Object focus (-in): the loved one is the subject. 'Mahal kita' is the usual 'I love you'; minamahal = beloved.

examples.tl: Minahal niya ang Pilipinas na parang sariling bayan.
examples.en: He loved the Philippines like his own country.

examples.tl: Mahalin mo ang sarili mo muna.
examples.en: Love yourself first.

examples.tl: Minahal ko siya pero hindi kami para sa isa't isa.
examples.en: I loved her but we weren't meant for each other.

notes.notes: A confession, lighter than 'Mahal kita'. 'May gusto ako sa 'yo' = I have feelings for you. 'Type kita' = I'm into you.

examples.tl: Gusto kita. Puwede ba kitang ligawan?
examples.en: I like you. Can I court you?

examples.tl: Umamin siya: may gusto raw siya sa akin.
examples.en: He confessed: he said he has feelings for me.

notes.notes: 'Nagseselos' = is jealous (now). 'Nagselos' = got jealous. 'Seloso/selosa' = jealous type. 'Inggit' = envy (of things).

examples.tl: Nagseselos ang jowa ko sa officemate ko.
examples.en: My partner is jealous of my officemate.

examples.tl: Selos lang 'yun, hindi galit.
examples.en: That's just jealousy, not anger.

notes.notes: Used as-is: 'Proud ako sa 'yo'. 'Ipinagmamalaki' is formal. Compare 'mayabang' = arrogant (negative).

examples.tl: Proud ako sa 'yo, anak.
examples.en: I'm proud of you, my child.

examples.tl: Proud parents sila sa graduation.
examples.en: They were proud parents at the graduation.

notes.notes: From mag-alala. 'Nag-alala ako' = I got worried. 'Huwag kang mag-alala' = don't worry. Text: 'worried ako'.

examples.tl: Nag-aalala si Mama kasi hindi ako nag-text.
examples.en: Mom is worried because I didn't text.

examples.tl: Huwag kang mag-alala, okay lang ako.
examples.en: Don't worry, I'm fine.

notes.notes: From kilig, the untranslatable romantic thrill. 'Nakakakilig' = so sweet it gives you butterflies. 'Kinikilig' = currently giddy.

examples.tl: Kinilig ako nang hawakan niya ang kamay ko.
examples.en: I got butterflies when he held my hand.

examples.tl: Kinikilig si ate sa text ng crush niya.
examples.en: Big sister is giddy over her crush's text.

notes.notes: 'Nakakatawa siya' = he's funny. Text: 'HAHAHA nakakatawa'. 'Natawa ako' = I laughed.

examples.tl: Nakakatawa ang mga tito jokes niya.
examples.en: His dad jokes are funny.

examples.tl: Natawa ako sa meme na sinend mo sa GC.
examples.en: I laughed at the meme you sent to the group chat.

examples.tl: Nakita mo yung meme? — Oo, nakakatawa, totoo pa.
examples.en: Did you see the meme? — Yeah, it's funny, and it's true.

notes.notes: About people or situations. Slang short form: 'nakakaloka', 'nakaka-badtrip'.

examples.tl: Nakakainis, cancelled ulit ang booking ko.
examples.en: So annoying, my booking got cancelled again.

examples.tl: Nakakainis siya kausap kapag lasing.
examples.en: He's annoying to talk to when drunk.

examples.tl: Na-cancel ulit yung Grab ko. — Nakakainis, third time na.
examples.en: My Grab got cancelled again. — So annoying, third time already.

notes.notes: 'Nakakatakot sa Quiapo kapag gabi' = Quiapo is scary at night. Also 'creepy'.

examples.tl: Nakakatakot ang balita tungkol sa bagyo.
examples.en: The news about the typhoon is scary.

examples.tl: Nakakatakot maglakad diyan kapag madilim.
examples.en: It's scary to walk there when it's dark.

examples.tl: Nakakatakot ang eskinita pag gabi, walang ilaw.
examples.en: The alley is scary at night, there are no lights.
examples.taglish: Nakakatakot yung eskinita pag gabi, walang ilaw, walang tao.

notes.taglish: Nakakatakot dito pag gabi, walang tao.

notes.notes: From loka (crazy). Originally gay lingo, now mainstream. Reaction to anything shocking, good or bad.

examples.tl: Nakakaloka, 500 pesos ang isang kape!
examples.en: Insane, one coffee is 500 pesos!

examples.tl: Nakakaloka ang chismis sa GC namin.
examples.en: The gossip in our group chat is wild.

notes.notes: From gulat. 'Gulat ako' = I'm surprised. 'Nakakagulat' = surprising. 'Surprise party' is 'surprise' as-is.

examples.tl: Nagulat ako nang bumisita ang pinsan ko galing Dubai.
examples.en: I was surprised when my cousin visited from Dubai.

examples.tl: Nagulat siya sa surprise party niya.
examples.en: She was surprised at her surprise party.

notes.notes: Untranslatable: withdrawing quietly because someone let you down, expecting them to make it up. 'Nagtatampo' = is sulking. 'Suyuin' = to coax out of tampo.

examples.tl: Nagtatampo si Lola kasi hindi kami dumalaw sa birthday niya.
examples.en: Grandma is sulking because we didn't visit on her birthday.

examples.tl: May tampo pa siya sa akin, kaya hindi nag-reply.
examples.en: She's still hurt at me, so she isn't replying.

notes.notes: Physical or emotional. 'Nasaktan ako sa sinabi mo' = what you said hurt me. 'Masakit' = painful.

examples.tl: Nasaktan siya sa sinabi ng ate niya.
examples.en: She was hurt by what her sister said.

examples.tl: Nasaktan ako noong nag-break kami.
examples.en: I got hurt when we broke up.

notes.notes: Taglish; mostly about exes and love life. 'Bitter ka lang' = you're just bitter. Also 'bitter sa love'.

examples.tl: Bitter pa siya sa ex niya kaya ayaw niyang mag-date.
examples.en: He's still bitter about his ex so he doesn't want to date.

examples.tl: Bitter ka lang kasi walang ka-date sa Valentine's.
examples.en: You're just bitter because you have no date on Valentine's.

notes.notes: 'Badtrip ako' = I'm in a bad mood. 'Nakaka-badtrip' = what a bummer. 'Na-badtrip ako sa kanya' = he put me off.

examples.tl: Badtrip, na-late ako kasi baha sa Taft.
examples.en: Ugh, I was late because Taft was flooded.

examples.tl: Na-badtrip ako sa waiter, ang sungit.
examples.en: The waiter put me in a bad mood, so grumpy.

notes.notes: Gana = appetite/drive. 'Wala akong gana' = I'm not feeling it. 'Nawalan ako ng gana' = I lost interest.

examples.tl: Wala akong gana kumain, broken-hearted.
examples.en: I have no appetite, I'm broken-hearted.

examples.tl: Walang gana mag-work si bes, Monday.
examples.en: Bestie has no drive to work, it's Monday.

notes.notes: Taglish verb from enjoy. 'Mag-enjoy ka!' = have fun! 'Nag-e-enjoy' = is enjoying. Tagalog 'nasiyahan' is formal.

examples.tl: Nag-enjoy ba kayo sa Boracay?
examples.en: Did you guys have fun in Boracay?

examples.tl: Mag-enjoy kayo sa date, ingat!
examples.en: Enjoy your date, take care!

notes.notes: From 'paranoid'. 'Napapraning ako' = I'm getting paranoid. Common for overthinking a text that got seen-zoned.

examples.tl: Napapraning ako, hindi pa siya nag-reply since kahapon.
examples.en: I'm getting paranoid, she hasn't replied since yesterday.

examples.tl: Praning siya sa mga chismis sa office.
examples.en: He's paranoid about the office gossip.

notes.notes: From hypertension. 'Na-high blood ako' = I got worked up. 'Nakaka-high blood' = infuriating. Jokey tone.

examples.tl: Na-high blood si Tatay sa bill ng Meralco.
examples.en: Dad got worked up over the Meralco bill.

examples.tl: Nakaka-high blood ang customer service nila.
examples.en: Their customer service is infuriating.

notes.notes: Opposite of mabait. 'Sungit' = grumpiness. 'Nagsusungit' = being grumpy right now. Common for staff reviews.

examples.tl: Masungit ang cashier sa 7-Eleven kanina.
examples.en: The cashier at the 7-Eleven earlier was grumpy.

examples.tl: Masungit si boss kapag Monday.
examples.en: The boss is cranky on Mondays.

notes.notes: Root arte (acting). Fussy about food, clothes, cleanliness, or overly dramatic. Mild tease among friends.

examples.tl: Maarte siya sa pagkain, ayaw ng street food.
examples.en: She's fussy with food, won't eat street food.

examples.tl: Huwag kang maarte, sakay na sa jeep.
examples.en: Don't be fussy, just get on the jeep.

notes.notes: For people and places. 'Tahimik lang siya' = he's the quiet type. 'Tumahimik ka' = be quiet.

examples.tl: Tahimik siya sa GC pero madaldal in person.
examples.en: She's quiet in the group chat but talkative in person.

examples.tl: Tahimik ang condo namin, walang maingay na kapitbahay.
examples.en: Our condo is quiet, no noisy neighbors.

notes.notes: Root daldal (chatter). Friendly tease. 'Ang daldal mo!' = you talk so much.

examples.tl: Madaldal ang tita niya, hindi ako nakapagsalita.
examples.en: Her aunt is so talkative, I couldn't get a word in.

examples.tl: Madaldal ang Grab driver ko, kuwento tungkol sa politika.
examples.en: My Grab driver was chatty, stories about politics.

notes.notes: Root talino. Plural: 'matatalino'. 'Matalino ka' is a sincere compliment; 'ang talino!' = so smart!

examples.tl: Matalino ang pamangkin ko, laging top sa klase.
examples.en: My niece is smart, always top of the class.

examples.tl: Matalino siya pero tamad mag-aral.
examples.en: He's smart but lazy about studying.

notes.notes: Harsh when aimed at someone; among close friends it's playful ('Tanga mo! HAHAHA'). Also self-directed: 'tanga ako sa love'. Avoid with strangers.

examples.tl: Ang tanga ko, naiwan ko ang wallet ko sa Grab.
examples.en: I'm so dumb, I left my wallet in the Grab.

examples.tl: Tanga ka ba? Niloko ka na niya nang dalawang beses.
examples.en: Are you stupid? He's cheated on you twice already.

notes.notes: 'Tinatamad ako' = I feel lazy / can't be bothered (very common). 'Katamaran' = laziness.

examples.tl: Tinatamad akong lumabas, uulan daw.
examples.en: I don't feel like going out, it's going to rain.

examples.tl: Tamad ang kapatid ko, hindi tumutulong sa bahay.
examples.en: My brother is lazy, doesn't help around the house.

notes.notes: Root sipag. Classic praise for OFWs, students, employees. 'Ang sipag mo!' = you're so hardworking.

examples.tl: Masipag ang mga Pilipino sa abroad.
examples.en: Filipinos abroad are hardworking.

examples.tl: Masipag ang kasambahay namin, maaga pa lang tapos na.
examples.en: Our helper is diligent, done early in the day.

notes.notes: Root yabang. 'Nagyayabang' = showing off. 'Yabang mo!' = you're so cocky. A serious social sin in PH culture.

examples.tl: Mayabang ang bagong officemate, puro kuwento ng achievements.
examples.en: The new officemate is arrogant, all stories about his achievements.

examples.tl: Huwag kang magyabang sa social media.
examples.en: Don't show off on social media.

notes.notes: Personality trait (vs 'nahihiya' = feeling shy right now). Root hiya.

examples.tl: Mahiyain ang anak nila, nagtatago sa likod ng mama.
examples.en: Their kid is shy, hiding behind her mom.

examples.tl: Mahiyain ako dati, pero na-train ako sa sales.
examples.en: I was shy before, but sales trained me out of it.

notes.notes: Pala- + kaibigan = tends to make friends. 'Friendly' as-is is also common.

examples.tl: Palakaibigan siya, kaya ang dami niyang kilala sa Makati.
examples.en: He's outgoing, so he knows tons of people in Makati.

examples.tl: Palakaibigan ang mga Pilipino sa mga foreigner.
examples.en: Filipinos are friendly toward foreigners.

notes.notes: Root alaga (to care for). High praise for a partner or parent. 'Alagang-alaga' = well taken care of.

examples.tl: Maalaga ang jowa ko, laging may baon akong tubig.
examples.en: My partner is caring, I always have water packed.

examples.tl: Maalaga si Ate sa mga pamangkin niya.
examples.en: Big sister is attentive to her nieces and nephews.

notes.notes: Insulting but also teasing: 'Duwag ka!' when a friend won't ride the roller coaster. 'Takot' is the feeling; duwag is the label.

examples.tl: Duwag siya, hindi siya umamin sa crush niya.
examples.en: He's a coward, he never confessed to his crush.

notes.notes: Spanish loan. 'Gwaping' is jokey. 'Pogi' is the casual synonym ('ang pogi!'). 'Gwapa' for women is Bisaya, not Tagalog.

examples.tl: Gwapo ang bago nilang manager.
examples.en: Their new manager is handsome.

examples.tl: Pogi ang jowa ni Ate, parang artista.
examples.en: Big sister's boyfriend is handsome, like an actor.

notes.notes: As in English, for babies, pets, crushes. 'Ang cute!' 'Cute siya' can also mean 'he's a bit attractive'.

examples.tl: Ang cute ng baby ng pinsan ko!
examples.en: My cousin's baby is so cute!

examples.tl: Cute 'yung barista sa coffee shop sa Salcedo.
examples.en: The barista at the Salcedo coffee shop is cute.

notes.notes: For people. 'Mataas' = tall/high for things. 'Tangkad' = height. Common first observation about foreigners.

examples.tl: Matangkad ang tatay niya, basketball player dati.
examples.en: Her dad is tall, a basketball player before.

examples.tl: Ang tangkad mo! Ilang feet ka?
examples.en: You're so tall! How many feet are you?

notes.notes: Said more openly than in the US (relatives will comment: 'tumaba ka!' = you gained weight). Softer: 'chubby', 'malusog' (healthy).

examples.tl: Tumaba ka! Masarap siguro ang buhay sa Makati.
examples.en: You gained weight! Life in Makati must be good.

examples.tl: Mataba ang pusa nila, spoiled.
examples.en: Their cat is fat, spoiled.

notes.notes: 'Pumayat ka' = you lost weight (compliment or concern). 'Slim' / 'sexy' for the flattering version.

examples.tl: Pumayat ka, nag-gym ka ba?
examples.en: You lost weight, have you been going to the gym?

examples.tl: Payat siya noong high school, ngayon jacked na.
examples.en: He was skinny in high school, now he's jacked.

notes.notes: Root puti (white). Often meant as a compliment in PH, which can feel odd to Americans. 'Pumuti ka' = you got lighter.

examples.tl: Maputi ang nanay niya, half-Spanish.
examples.en: Her mom is fair-skinned, half-Spanish.

examples.tl: Maputi ka kasi laging aircon.
examples.en: You're pale because you're always in the aircon.

notes.notes: Root itim (black). Can be blunt; 'morena/moreno' or 'kayumanggi' are the flattering words. 'Umitim ka' = you got tan (after a beach trip).

examples.tl: Umitim ako sa Boracay, sunog.
examples.en: I got dark in Boracay, sunburned.

examples.tl: Maitim siya pero maganda ang kutis.
examples.en: She's dark-skinned but has beautiful skin.

notes.notes: Morena (f) / moreno (m). The complimentary word for brown skin, 'morena beauty'. Kayumanggi = brown (formal).

examples.tl: Morena ang jowa ko, ayaw niya ng whitening.
examples.en: My partner is morena, she won't use whitening.

examples.tl: Moreno siya, laging nasa beach.
examples.en: He's tan, always at the beach.

notes.notes: Suplado (m) / suplada (f). Someone who seems too cool to talk to you. Very common label.

examples.tl: Suplada ang bagong neighbor, hindi bumabati.
examples.en: The new neighbor is snobbish, doesn't say hi.

examples.tl: Suplado siya sa una pero mabait pala.
examples.en: He seemed aloof at first but turned out nice.

notes.notes: Root lambing (affection/sweet-talk). 'Naglalambing' = being affectionate / sweet-talking to get something.

examples.tl: Malambing ang anak nila, laging nakayakap.
examples.en: Their kid is affectionate, always hugging.

examples.tl: Naglalambing si ate kay Papa kasi may hihingin.
examples.en: Big sister is sweet-talking Dad because she wants something.

notes.notes: Root kulit. Kids who won't stop, friends who keep nagging. 'Ang kulit mo!' Also 'kulit' = horsing around.

examples.tl: Makulit ang pamangkin ko, hindi natatahimik.
examples.en: My nephew is pesky, never settles down.

examples.tl: Ang kulit mo, sinabi ko nang hindi ako puwede.
examples.en: You're so persistent, I already said I can't.

notes.notes: Someone who ignores rules or warnings. Used for kids, friends, and rule-breaking citizens ('mga pasaway').

examples.tl: Pasaway ang kuya ko noong bata, laging napapagalitan.
examples.en: My brother was a troublemaker as a kid, always getting scolded.

examples.tl: Pasaway ang mga driver dito, hindi sumusunod sa lane.
examples.en: Drivers here are rule-breakers, they don't stay in lane.

notes.notes: Teasing or critical. Opposite: 'galante' (generous). 'Matipid' = thrifty (positive).

examples.tl: Kuripot si kuya, hindi nag-libre sa birthday niya.
examples.en: My brother is stingy, didn't treat us on his birthday.

examples.tl: Hindi ako kuripot, matipid lang.
examples.en: I'm not cheap, just thrifty.

notes.notes: Spanish loan. Someone who always picks up the tab. 'Mapagbigay' = generous (formal).

examples.tl: Galante si Tito Jun, siya ang nagbayad ng buong dinner.
examples.en: Uncle Jun is generous, he paid for the whole dinner.

notes.notes: Root galang (respect). Using po/opo and mano makes you 'magalang'. Top compliment for a partner meeting the family.

examples.tl: Magalang ang jowa ni ate, laging po at opo.
examples.en: Big sister's boyfriend is respectful, always po and opo.

examples.tl: Magalang ang mga bata nila.
examples.en: Their kids are polite.

notes.notes: Strong. Rude manners or vulgar jokes/behavior. 'Ang bastos!' = how rude! 'Walang galang' = no respect.

examples.tl: Bastos ang lalaki sa jeep, sinisiksik ang mga babae.
examples.en: The guy on the jeep was rude, crowding the women.

examples.tl: Bastos ang joke niya sa harap ng mga bata.
examples.en: His joke was vulgar in front of the kids.

notes.notes: Chismosa (f) / chismoso (m). 'Chismis' = gossip (noun). 'Mag-chismis tayo' = let's catch up on gossip. Playful among friends.

examples.tl: Chismosa ang kapitbahay namin, alam niya lahat.
examples.en: Our neighbor is a gossip, she knows everything.

examples.tl: Chismoso ang GC ng barkada, may update araw-araw.
examples.en: The barkada group chat is gossipy, there's an update every day.

notes.notes: As in English, for partners and gestures. 'Sweet niyo!' = you two are so sweet. Tagalog: malambing.

examples.tl: Sweet ng jowa mo, hinatid ka hanggang condo.
examples.en: Your partner is sweet, took you all the way to the condo.

examples.tl: Ang sweet ng message ni Lola sa GC.
examples.en: Grandma's message in the group chat was so sweet.

notes.notes: Said 'kay-jay'. The friend who won't join or shuts down the fun. 'Huwag kang KJ!' = don't be a buzzkill.

examples.tl: Huwag kang KJ, sumama ka sa inuman.
examples.en: Don't be a killjoy, come to the drinking session.

notes.notes: Maki(pag)- = join in doing with others. 'Nakipag-usap ako sa landlord' = I talked with the landlord. Casual 'usap tayo' = let's talk.

examples.tl: Gusto kong makipag-usap sa admin ng condo tungkol sa parking.
examples.en: I want to talk with the condo admin about parking.

examples.tl: Usap tayo mamaya, may sasabihin ako.
examples.en: Let's talk later, I have something to tell you.

notes.notes: Object focus (ka- + usap + -in): the person spoken to is the subject. 'Kausapin mo siya' = talk to him.

examples.tl: Kinausap ko ang landlord tungkol sa deposit.
examples.en: I talked to the landlord about the deposit.

examples.tl: Kinausap ko na si boss tungkol sa leave ko.
examples.en: I already talked to the boss about my leave.

examples.tl: Kausapin mo ang kapatid mo, nagtatampo siya.
examples.en: Talk to your brother, he's sulking.

notes.notes: Directional focus (-an): the person called is the subject. Tawagin = call someone by name / summon.

examples.tl: Tatawagan kita mamaya pag free na ako.
examples.en: I'll call you later when I'm free.

examples.tl: Tawagan mo si Mama, nag-aalala siya.
examples.en: Call Mom, she's worried.

examples.tl: Tinawagan ako ng Grab driver, hindi niya mahanap ang gate.
examples.en: The Grab driver called me, he couldn't find the gate.

notes.notes: Taglish: i-text (to text), nag-text (texted), tine-text (is texting), 'text mo ako' = text me. Also 'mag-text'.

examples.tl: I-text mo ako kapag nakauwi ka na.
examples.en: Text me when you get home.

examples.tl: Nag-text si Tita, pupunta daw siya sa Sabado.
examples.en: Auntie texted, she says she's coming on Saturday.

notes.notes: Messenger/Viber/WhatsApp messages are 'chat', not 'text'. 'I-chat mo ako', 'nag-chat siya', 'chat lang kita'. 'GC' = group chat.

examples.tl: I-chat mo lang ako sa Messenger, wala akong load.
examples.en: Just message me on Messenger, I have no load.

examples.tl: Nag-chat ang ex ko kagabi. Hindi ko pa nire-reply.
examples.en: My ex messaged last night. I haven't replied yet.

notes.notes: Every barkada, family and office has one (Messenger/Viber). 'Nasa GC' = it's in the group chat. 'Nag-mute ako ng GC' = I muted the GC.

examples.tl: Nasa GC ng pamilya ang details ng reunion.
examples.en: The reunion details are in the family group chat.

examples.tl: Ang ingay ng GC ng barkada kagabi, 200 messages.
examples.en: The barkada group chat was so noisy last night, 200 messages.

notes.notes: Reciprocal actor focus (mag-). 'Nag-away kami' = we had a fight. Awayin = pick a fight with.

examples.tl: Nag-away sila dahil sa pera.
examples.en: They fought over money.

examples.tl: Nag-away kami ng jowa ko kagabi, LQ lang.
examples.en: My partner and I fought last night, just a lovers' quarrel.

examples.tl: Lagi silang nag-aaway tungkol sa pera.
examples.en: They always fight about money.

notes.notes: 'Kami' excludes the listener. 'Nag-away kami ni Mama' = Mom and I fought. 'Nag-usap na kami' usually follows when it's resolved.

examples.tl: Nag-away kami ni kuya dahil sa utang.
examples.en: My brother and I had a fight over a debt.

examples.tl: Nag-away kami pero okay na ulit kami.
examples.en: We fought but we're okay again.

notes.notes: 'Bati na kami' = we're on good terms again (very common). 'Hindi sila nagbabati' = they're not speaking. Root bati = greet / be on terms.

examples.tl: Nagkabati na kami ng ate ko after two weeks.
examples.en: My sister and I made up after two weeks.

examples.tl: Bati na ba kayo ng jowa mo?
examples.en: Are you and your partner good again?

notes.notes: Taglish, the everyday verb. Nag-sorry (apologized), 'mag-sorry ka' = say sorry. 'Sorry na' = come on, I'm sorry. Formal: humingi ng tawad.

examples.tl: Nag-sorry na ako, ano pa ba ang gusto mo?
examples.en: I already said sorry, what else do you want?

examples.tl: Mag-sorry ka kay Lola, nasaktan siya.
examples.en: Apologize to Grandma, she was hurt.

notes.notes: More serious/sincere than mag-sorry. 'Patawad' = forgive me / forgiveness. 'Patawarin mo ako' = forgive me.

examples.tl: Humingi siya ng tawad sa mga magulang niya.
examples.en: He asked his parents for forgiveness.

examples.tl: Patawad, hindi ko sinasadya.
examples.en: Forgive me, I didn't mean it.

notes.notes: Nagpasalamat (thanked). Everyday thanks is just 'salamat' / 'thank you'. 'Pasasalamat' = gratitude; 'thanksgiving party' is common after a blessing.

examples.tl: Nagpasalamat ako sa mga tumulong noong bagyo.
examples.en: I thanked those who helped during the typhoon.

examples.tl: Magpasalamat ka kay Tita, siya ang nagbayad ng tuition mo.
examples.en: Thank Auntie, she's the one who paid your tuition.

notes.notes: Binati (greeted), binabati (is greeting). 'Batiin mo si Tito' = say hi to Uncle. Also 'congratulate' and 'greet on a birthday'. 'Bati' = a greeting.

examples.tl: Batiin mo si Lola, birthday niya ngayon.
examples.en: Greet Grandma, it's her birthday today.

examples.tl: Hindi niya ako binati sa hallway, suplado.
examples.en: He didn't greet me in the hallway, snob.

notes.notes: Verbs: yumakap (to hug, actor), yakapin (to hug someone), nagyakapan (hugged each other). Text: 'yakap!' or 'virtual hug'.

examples.tl: Yakap muna bago umalis.
examples.en: Hug first before leaving.

examples.tl: Niyakap ako ni Mama sa airport, umiyak pa.
examples.en: Mom hugged me at the airport, even cried.

notes.notes: Often implies a serious talk ('nag-usap kami nang masinsinan'). 'Nag-usap na kami' = we've talked it out. 'Mag-usap tayo' = let's talk.

examples.tl: Nag-usap kami ng jowa ko tungkol sa future namin.
examples.en: My partner and I talked about our future.

examples.tl: Nag-usap na kami ni kuya, okay na.
examples.en: My brother and I already talked, it's fine now.

notes.notes: 'Kilala' = know a person (vs 'alam' = know a fact). 'Kilala mo ba siya?' = do you know her? 'Hindi ko siya kilala' = I don't know him.

examples.tl: Kilala ko siya, kaklase ko sa high school.
examples.en: I know her, she was my high school classmate.

examples.tl: Kilala mo ba 'yung bagong tenant sa 12th floor?
examples.en: Do you know the new tenant on the 12th floor?

notes.notes: From makilala. 'Nakilala ko siya sa...' = I met her at... 'Makilala' = to meet/get to know. Not for appointments (that's magkita).

examples.tl: Nakilala ko ang jowa ko sa gym sa Makati.
examples.en: I met my partner at a gym in Makati.

examples.tl: Gusto kong makilala ang pamilya mo.
examples.en: I want to meet your family.

notes.notes: Ipinakilala (introduced). 'Ipakilala mo ako' = introduce me. 'Magpakilala' = introduce yourself. 'Pakilala' = an introduction.

examples.tl: Ipakilala mo naman ako sa tita mo.
examples.en: Come on, introduce me to your aunt.

examples.tl: Ipinakilala niya ako sa parents niya noong Pasko.
examples.en: He introduced me to his parents at Christmas.

notes.en: to meet up; to see each other
notes.notes: Reciprocal actor focus (mag-): two people see each other. 'Kita tayo' = see you. Makita = to see.

examples.tl: Magkikita kami sa Glorietta mamaya.
examples.en: We're meeting up at Glorietta later.
examples.taglish: Magkikita kami sa Glorietta mamaya, around 6.

examples.tl: Kita tayo sa Greenbelt mamaya, 7 PM.
examples.en: Let's meet at Greenbelt later, 7 PM.

examples.tl: Nagkita kami ng barkada ko sa Poblacion.
examples.en: My friends and I met up in Poblacion.

notes.notes: Nag-date (went on a date), 'ka-date' = your date. 'Date night', 'dinner date' as-is. 'Nililigawan' = being courted.

examples.tl: Nag-date kami sa Salcedo market noong Sabado.
examples.en: We went on a date at the Salcedo market on Saturday.

examples.tl: Sino ang ka-date mo sa Valentine's?
examples.en: Who's your date on Valentine's?

notes.notes: Nanligaw (courted), nanliligaw (is courting). 'Ligaw' = courtship; 'manliligaw' = suitor; 'ligawan' = to court someone. Still a real stage before 'official'.

examples.tl: Nanligaw siya sa akin nang isang taon bago kami naging official.
examples.en: He courted me for a year before we became official.

examples.tl: May nanliligaw kay ate, officemate niya.
examples.en: Someone's courting big sister, her officemate.

notes.notes: The traditional stage: 'ligaw stage', 'nililigawan' (being courted). 'Sinagot' = she said yes (literally: answered).

examples.tl: Nasa ligaw stage pa sila, hindi pa sila.
examples.en: They're still in the courtship stage, not official yet.

examples.tl: Sinagot na niya ang nanliligaw sa kanya.
examples.en: She finally said yes to her suitor.

notes.notes: 'Crush ko siya' = I have a crush on him. 'May crush ako sa 'yo' = I have a crush on you. 'Crush ng bayan' = everyone's crush. 'Crush kita' is a confession.

examples.tl: Crush ko ang barista sa Salcedo, HAHAHA.
examples.en: I have a crush on the barista in Salcedo, haha.

examples.tl: Crush ng bayan ang bagong officemate.
examples.en: The new officemate is everyone's crush.

notes.notes: Nag-break (broke up), 'break na sila' = they're done. 'Nakipag-break' = broke up with someone. 'Hiwalay' = separated (also for married couples).

examples.tl: Nag-break sila after five years, nakakalungkot.
examples.en: They broke up after five years, it's sad.

examples.tl: Break na sila ng jowa niya, kaya bitter.
examples.en: She and her partner broke up, that's why she's bitter.

notes.notes: Root amin. 'Umamin siya sa crush niya' = he confessed to his crush. 'Aminin mo!' = admit it! 'Nag-confess' also common.

examples.tl: Umamin siya sa akin na may gusto siya sa akin.
examples.en: He confessed to me that he has feelings for me.

examples.tl: Aminin mo, crush mo siya!
examples.en: Admit it, you have a crush on her!

notes.notes: From 'standby'. 'Tambay' = hanging out / an idle person; 'tambayan' = hangout spot. 'Tambay tayo' = let's chill.

examples.tl: Tumambay kami sa condo ko, nag-Netflix lang.
examples.en: We hung out at my condo, just watched Netflix.

examples.tl: Tambay tayo sa coffee shop after work.
examples.en: Let's hang out at the coffee shop after work.

notes.notes: The barkada's main event. 'Mag-inuman' = to have drinks. 'Inom tayo' = let's drink. 'Pulutan' = bar food.

examples.tl: May inuman sa bahay ni Jake sa Friday, sama ka?
examples.en: There's a drinking session at Jake's on Friday, you coming?

examples.tl: Nag-inuman kami hanggang 3 AM, hangover ako ngayon.
examples.en: We drank until 3 AM, I'm hungover now.

notes.notes: Dumalaw (visited), dadalaw (will visit). 'Dalawin' = visit someone (object focus). 'Bumisita' is the synonym. Visiting the sick/elderly is a strong norm.

examples.tl: Dadalaw kami kay Lola sa ospital mamaya.
examples.en: We're visiting Grandma at the hospital later.

examples.tl: Dalawin mo naman ang parents mo, matagal ka nang hindi umuuwi.
examples.en: Visit your parents, you haven't gone home in a long time.

notes.notes: 'Ano ang chismis?' = what's the tea? 'Mag-chismis' / 'mag-chismisan' = to gossip. 'Marites' = a gossipy person (meme).

examples.tl: Ano ang latest chismis sa office?
examples.en: What's the latest gossip at the office?

examples.tl: Chismis lang 'yan, hindi totoo.
examples.en: That's just a rumor, it's not true.

notes.notes: Two uses: 'asar ako' = I'm irritated; 'inaasar niya ako' = he's teasing me. 'Asaran' = mutual teasing (barkada love language). 'Asar talo' = sore loser.

examples.tl: Lagi akong inaasar ng barkada ko tungkol sa crush ko.
examples.en: My friends always tease me about my crush.

examples.tl: Asar ako, nakalimutan ko ulit ang password ko.
examples.en: I'm irritated, I forgot my password again.

notes.notes: Messenger culture: 'Na-seen lang ako' = he saw it and didn't reply. 'Seen-zoned ako'. The source of much praning.

examples.tl: Na-seen lang ako ng crush ko. Sad.
examples.en: My crush just left me on read. Sad.

examples.tl: Huwag mo akong i-seen-zone, reply ka naman.
examples.en: Don't leave me on read, reply, come on.

notes.notes: Formal-ish; people mostly say 'birthday'. 'Maligayang kaarawan' = happy birthday (on cards). The celebrant treats everyone ('libre').

examples.tl: Kaarawan ni Mama sa Linggo, handaan sa bahay.
examples.en: It's Mom's birthday on Sunday, a party at the house.

examples.tl: Happy birthday, bes! Libre mo mamaya ha.
examples.en: Happy birthday, bestie! Your treat later, okay.

examples.tl: Kaarawan ni Mama sa a-bente ng Nobyembre, bibili ako ng cake sa Goldilocks.
examples.en: Mom's birthday is November 20, I'll buy a cake at Goldilocks.

notes.taglish: Birthday ko sa Sabado, libre ko kayo.

notes.notes: Reverse of the US custom: the celebrant pays. 'Pa-birthday mo!' = treat us for your birthday! 'Pa-blowout' is the older term.

examples.tl: Pa-birthday mo naman, boss!
examples.en: Treat us for your birthday, boss!

examples.tl: Pizza ang pa-birthday niya sa office.
examples.en: Her birthday treat for the office was pizza.

notes.notes: 'Kasal na sila' = they're married. 'Ikakasal' = getting married. 'Kasalan' = the wedding event. 'Ninong/ninang sa kasal' = wedding sponsors.

examples.tl: Kasal ng pinsan ko sa Tagaytay sa December.
examples.en: My cousin's wedding is in Tagaytay in December.

examples.tl: Ikakasal na si ate next year!
examples.en: Big sister is getting married next year!

notes.notes: Nagpakasal (got married), magpapakasal (will get married). 'Nag-propose' / 'engaged' as-is. Civil wedding = 'civil', church = 'church wedding'.

examples.tl: Nagpakasal sila sa civil muna, church wedding next year.
examples.en: They had a civil wedding first, church wedding next year.

examples.tl: Kailan kayo magpapakasal?
examples.en: When are you two getting married?

notes.notes: Big family event with many ninongs/ninangs. 'Bibinyagan' = will be baptized. Followed by a handaan.

examples.tl: Binyag ng anak ni kuya sa Sabado, ninong ako.
examples.en: My brother's kid's baptism is Saturday, I'm the godfather.

examples.tl: Puro bisita sa bahay after ng binyag.
examples.en: The house was full of guests after the christening.

notes.notes: From mamatay. 'Namatay na ang lolo ko' = my grandpa has passed. Softer: 'pumanaw', 'wala na' (is gone). 'Patay' = dead.

examples.tl: Namatay ang lola niya kagabi, kaya absent siya.
examples.en: Her grandmother died last night, so she's absent.

examples.tl: Wala na si Lolo, pero lagi ko siyang naaalala.
examples.en: Grandpa is gone, but I always remember him.

notes.notes: Multi-day wake, often at home or a funeral chapel, with food, coffee and card games. Showing up matters more than words. 'Makiramay' = to condole.

examples.tl: Pupunta ako sa lamay ng tatay ng officemate ko mamaya.
examples.en: I'm going to the wake of my officemate's dad later.

examples.tl: Three days ang lamay, tapos libing sa Sabado.
examples.en: The wake is three days, then the burial on Saturday.

notes.notes: 'Ililibing' = will be buried. 'Punerarya' = funeral home. People say 'funeral' too. Wear black or white.

examples.tl: Umuwi siya sa probinsya para sa libing ng lola niya.
examples.en: He went home to the province for his grandmother's funeral.

examples.tl: Sa Loyola Marikina ang libing.
examples.en: The burial is at Loyola Marikina.

notes.notes: 'Condolence' (singular) is what people actually text, plus 'praying for your family'. Tagalog: 'Nakikiramay ako/kami' (I/we share your grief).

examples.tl: Condolence sa inyo, pare. Nandito lang kami.
examples.en: Condolences to you all, bro. We're here for you.

examples.tl: Nakikiramay kami sa pamilya ni Tita Nena.
examples.en: We offer our condolences to Auntie Nena's family.

notes.notes: As-is. 'Nag-graduate' = graduated. 'Pagtatapos' is the formal word on programs. Whole family attends, then a celebratory lunch.

examples.tl: Graduation ng pamangkin ko sa UST sa June.
examples.en: My niece's graduation at UST is in June.

examples.tl: Nag-graduate na ang bunso, buong pamilya nag-Jollibee.
examples.en: The youngest graduated, the whole family went to Jollibee.

notes.notes: Taglish. 'Promotion' as-is. 'Na-regular' = became a regular employee (big deal after probation). Celebrant treats ('libre').

examples.tl: Na-promote si ate, team lead na siya!
examples.en: Big sister got promoted, she's a team lead now!

examples.tl: Libre mo, na-promote ka!
examples.en: Your treat, you got promoted!

notes.notes: People say 'anniversary' or 'anniv'. 'Monthsary' = monthly anniversary (young couples, taken seriously).

examples.tl: Anniversary ng parents ko sa Sabado, 30 years.
examples.en: My parents' anniversary is Saturday, 30 years.

examples.tl: Nakalimutan niya ang monthsary namin, nagtatampo ako.
examples.en: He forgot our monthsary, I'm sulking.

notes.notes: Every barangay/town has one. Open houses, everyone eats everywhere, 'kain lang'. Famous ones: Sinulog, Ati-Atihan, Pahiyas.

examples.tl: Fiesta sa barangay nila sa Mayo, inimbita ako.
examples.en: Their barangay fiesta is in May, I was invited.

examples.tl: Sa fiesta, puwede kang kumain sa kahit anong bahay.
examples.en: At the fiesta, you can eat at any house.

notes.notes: Season starts in September ('ber months'). 'Maligayang Pasko' = Merry Christmas. 'Aguinaldo' = cash gift from ninongs; 'Noche Buena' = Christmas Eve feast.

examples.tl: Uuwi ako sa probinsya sa Pasko.
examples.en: I'm going home to the province for Christmas.

examples.tl: Maligayang Pasko sa inyong lahat!
examples.en: Merry Christmas to all of you!

examples.tl: Uuwi ka ba sa States sa Pasko o dito ka lang?
examples.en: Are you going home to the States for Christmas or staying here?

notes.notes: 'Manigong Bagong Taon' = Happy New Year. 'Media Noche' = midnight feast; round fruits, polka dots, loud noise for luck.

examples.tl: Saan kayo mag-Bagong Taon? Sa amin ka na lang.
examples.en: Where are you spending New Year's? Just come to ours.

examples.tl: Manigong Bagong Taon, Tita! Ingat po kayo.
examples.en: Happy New Year, Auntie! Take care.

notes.notes: Families go to the cemetery, clean graves, light candles, eat. Heavy traffic out of Manila. 'Araw ng mga Patay' is the formal name.

examples.tl: Uuwi kami sa Bulacan sa Undas para dalawin si Lolo.
examples.en: We're going home to Bulacan for Undas to visit Grandpa's grave.

examples.tl: Traffic sa NLEX tuwing Undas.
examples.en: NLEX is jammed every Undas.

notes.notes: Manila empties out; Maundy Thursday and Good Friday are holidays, malls close. Visita Iglesia (church visits), 'Mahal na Araw' in Tagalog.

examples.tl: Tahimik ang Makati tuwing Holy Week, lahat umuuwi sa probinsya.
examples.en: Makati is quiet every Holy Week, everyone goes home to the province.

examples.tl: Bawal mag-ingay sa bahay ni Lola sa Good Friday.
examples.en: No noise allowed at Grandma's house on Good Friday.

notes.notes: Root handa (to prepare). Any celebration with lots of food: birthday, binyag, fiesta. 'May handaan' = there's a party. Guests take home 'baon'.

examples.tl: May handaan sa bahay ni Tita sa Sabado, 50th birthday niya.
examples.en: There's a party at Auntie's house on Saturday, her 50th birthday.

examples.tl: Ang dami ng pagkain sa handaan, may lechon!
examples.en: So much food at the party, there was lechon!

notes.notes: Spanish loan. Thrown for someone leaving (abroad, new job). Opposite: 'welcome party' or 'bienvenida' (rare).

examples.tl: Despedida ni Marco sa Friday, aalis siya papuntang Canada.
examples.en: Marco's farewell party is Friday, he's leaving for Canada.

examples.tl: Umiyak lahat sa despedida ni ate.
examples.en: Everyone cried at big sister's send-off.

notes.notes: Pronounced 'de-BOO'. Formal party with 18 roses, 18 candles. Boys' 21st is less of a thing. 'Debutante' = the celebrant.

examples.tl: Debut ng pamangkin ko sa November, may 18 roses.
examples.en: My niece's debut is in November, with the 18 roses.

examples.tl: Kasama ako sa 18 roses sa debut niya.
examples.en: I'm one of the 18 roses at her debut.

notes.notes: As-is. Family reunions at Christmas, batch reunions at homecoming. Expect 'tita questions' about weight and love life.

examples.tl: Family reunion sa Pasko, 60 tao sa bahay ni Lola.
examples.en: Family reunion at Christmas, 60 people at Grandma's house.

examples.tl: Hindi ako pupunta sa batch reunion, puro tanong kung may jowa na.
examples.en: I'm not going to the batch reunion, all questions about whether I have a partner.

notes.notes: 'Buntis si ate' = sis is pregnant. 'Nabuntis' = got pregnant. 'Preggy' is the cute Taglish version. 'Nanganak' = gave birth.

examples.tl: Buntis na ang asawa ni kuya, due sa March.
examples.en: My brother's wife is pregnant, due in March.

examples.tl: Nanganak na si ate kagabi, baby girl!
examples.en: Big sister gave birth last night, a baby girl!

notes.notes: Take an elder's hand and touch it to your forehead on arrival; they say 'God bless'. Expected at family gatherings. 'Magmano' = do the mano.

examples.tl: Mano po, Lola. Kumusta po kayo?
examples.en: Bless, Grandma. How are you?

examples.tl: Magmano ka kay Tito bago kumain.
examples.en: Do the mano to Uncle before eating.

notes.notes: Add 'po' with vendors older than you. 'Magkano lahat?' = how much all together.

examples.tl: Magkano po ito? — Dalawang daan lang po.
examples.en: How much is this? — Just two hundred.

notes.notes: For palengke, tiangge, Divisoria, Greenhills. Not for malls or restaurants. Root tawad = discount/haggle.

examples.tl: Pwede bang tumawad, ate? — Sige, bawas ko ng bente.
examples.en: Can I haggle, miss? — Okay, I'll take off twenty.

notes.notes: Pattern: 'Meron ba kayong ...?' for anything in a store or restaurant. 'Mayroon' is the full form; 'meron' is what you'll hear.

examples.tl: Meron ba kayong extra rice? — Meron po.
examples.en: Do you have extra rice? — Yes, we do.

notes.notes: CR = comfort room, universal in Manila. 'Banyo' is bathroom at home.

examples.tl: Saan po ang CR? — Diyan po sa likod, kanan.
examples.en: Where's the restroom? — Back there, to the right.

notes.notes: 'Pahingi ng ...' is the most natural way to ask for something at a table. Paki- + root = 'please do X'.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng tubig. — Service water or bottled?
examples.en: Can I have some water, please? — Service water or bottled?

notes.notes: 'Dalawang order ng ...' for two. Carinderia style: point and say 'Isa nito.'

examples.tl: Isang order ng sisig at dalawang kanin. — Sige po, dine-in?
examples.en: One order of sisig and two rice. — Okay, dine-in?

notes.notes: Opposite: 'Dine-in po.' Nobody says 'to go' in Manila.

examples.tl: Dine-in or take-out po? — Take-out po.
examples.en: Dine-in or take-out? — Take-out, please.

notes.notes: Sari-sari store opener. 'Pabili ng ...' = let me buy some ... Also 'Pabili po!' to call the tindera.

examples.tl: Ate, pabili ng tubig. — Malamig o hindi?
examples.en: Miss, I'd like to buy water. — Cold or not?

notes.notes: Drivers and tinderas ask 'May barya ka?' or 'Wala kang barya?'. 'Maliit' = small bills.

examples.tl: Wala po akong barya, isang libo lang. — Ay, wala akong panukli.
examples.en: I don't have change, only a thousand. — Oh, I don't have change for that.

notes.notes: 'Bill out' is the everyday Taglish verb. 'Chit' is older but still understood. Hand signal: write in the air.

examples.tl: Yung bill po. — Sige po, isang bill lang?
examples.en: The bill, please. — Sure, just one bill?

notes.notes: Answer to a driver's 'Saan po tayo?' (Where to?). Add a landmark: 'Sa Makati po, malapit sa Greenbelt.'

examples.tl: Saan po tayo? — Sa Makati po, Ayala Avenue.
examples.en: Where to? — Makati, Ayala Avenue.

notes.notes: Tells a driver to drop you here. On a jeep shout 'Para po!' instead.

examples.tl: Saan po kayo bababa? — Dito lang po, sa tabi.
examples.en: Where will you get off? — Just here, on the side.

notes.notes: 'Para!' (from Spanish parar) is the jeep/bus word; 'pakihinto' is fine for a car or Grab.

examples.tl: Kuya, pakihinto dito sa kanto. — Sige po.
examples.en: Sir, please stop here at the corner. — Okay.

notes.notes: Spelled diretso or deretso. Directions you'll hear: diretso, kaliwa, kanan, U-turn, sa kanto.

examples.tl: Kaliwa po ba dito? — Hindi, diretso lang, tapos kanan.
examples.en: Left here? — No, just go straight, then right.

notes.notes: Kanan = right. 'Sa susunod na kanto' = at the next corner.

examples.tl: Kaliwa sa kanto, tapos dito lang po. — Okay.
examples.en: Left at the corner, then just here. — Okay.

accept: Turn right at the next corner.
notes.notes: 'Susunod' = next. Also heard: 'Sa unahan, kanan' (up ahead, right).

examples.tl: Saan po? — Kanan sa susunod na kanto, sa may 7-Eleven.
examples.en: Where? — Right at the next corner, by the 7-Eleven.

notes.notes: 'Matagal pa ba?' = is it still a long wait? Useful for food, Grab, and queues.

examples.tl: Gaano katagal yung order? — Mga sampung minuto po.
examples.en: How long for the order? — About ten minutes.

examples.tl: Gaano katagal ang biyahe papuntang airport?
examples.en: How long is the trip to the airport?

notes.notes: 'Ilang minuto pa?' = how many more minutes. Common reply: 'Lima pa' or 'Malapit na' (almost).

examples.tl: Ilang minuto pa, kuya? — Lima pa po, traffic eh.
examples.en: How many more minutes? — Five more, there's traffic.

accept_tl: Sa inyo na po ang sukli.
notes.notes: Sukli = change (money back). 'Okay na yan' while waving off change also works.

examples.tl: Yung sukli niyo po. — Sa'yo na, kuya, salamat.
examples.en: Here's your change. — Keep it, thanks.

notes.notes: Resibo or receipt, both used. OR = official receipt.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng resibo. — Eto po.
examples.en: Can I have a receipt? — Here you go.

notes.notes: Say it while catching the server's eye. Solo: 'Order na ako.'

examples.tl: Order na po kami. — Sige po, ano pong sa inyo?
examples.en: We're ready to order. — Okay, what will you have?

notes.notes: Open: 'Anong oras kayo nagbubukas?' 'Bukas pa ba kayo?' = are you still open?

examples.tl: Anong oras po kayo nagsasara? — Alas-diyes po ng gabi.
examples.en: What time do you close? — Ten p.m.

notes.en: Do you have a bigger one?
notes.notes: Mas = more. Mas maliit = smaller, mas mura = cheaper, ibang kulay = other color.

examples.tl: May mas malaki po ba nito? — Wala na po, medium na lang.
examples.en: Do you have this in a bigger size? — None left, only medium.

notes.notes: Pinaka- = most, so pinakamalapit = nearest. Swap in ATM, botika (pharmacy), palengke, MRT.

examples.tl: Saan ang pinakamalapit na ATM? — Sa labas lang, sa tabi ng Jollibee.
examples.en: Where's the nearest ATM? — Just outside, next to Jollibee.

notes.en: Where do I catch a ride to BGC?
accept: Where do I ride to BGC?
accept_tl: Saan po ang sakayan papuntang BGC?
Saan ako pwedeng sumakay papuntang BGC?
notes.notes: Sakay = ride/board; sakayan = the stop or terminal. Papunta sa / papuntang = heading to.

examples.tl: Saan po ako sasakay papuntang BGC? — Doon po sa BGC Bus sa may Ayala.
examples.en: Where do I catch a ride to BGC? — Over there at the BGC Bus by Ayala.

notes.notes: 'Ako nga pala si ...' = by the way, I'm ... (natural when you forgot to introduce yourself).

examples.tl: Ako nga pala si Lloyd. — Ako si Jen. Nice to meet you!
examples.en: By the way, I'm Lloyd. — I'm Jen. Nice to meet you!

notes.notes: Taga- + place = from that place. People will often ask 'Kano ka?' (short for Amerikano).

examples.tl: Taga-saan ka? — Taga-Amerika ako, pero dito na ako nakatira.
examples.en: Where are you from? — I'm from America, but I live here now.

notes.notes: Nakatira = lives/resides. Casual: 'Sa Makati ako' is enough in context.

examples.tl: Saan ka nakatira? — Nakatira ako sa Makati, malapit sa Rockwell.
examples.en: Where do you live? — I live in Makati, near Rockwell.

accept: I've been here for two years.
accept_tl: Dalawang taon na ako sa Pilipinas.
Dalawang taon na ako sa Maynila.
notes.notes: 'Na' marks 'already/by now'. Numbers in English are common in Taglish: 'Three years na ako dito.'

examples.tl: Gaano ka na katagal dito? — Dalawang taon na ako dito.
examples.en: How long have you been here? — I've been here two years.

notes.notes: Konti is the spoken form of kaunti. Say it with a smile; it invites people to slow down.

examples.tl: Wow, Tagalog ka! — Konti lang ang alam ko, pakibagalan.
examples.en: Wow, you speak Tagalog! — I only know a little, please go slow.

accept: I used to be a soldier.
notes.notes: Dating = former. 'Beterano' is understood but evokes WWII vets; 'retired military' or 'ex-military' is what people actually say.

examples.tl: Anong trabaho mo dati? — Dating sundalo ako, retired na.
examples.en: What did you do before? — I was a soldier, retired now.

notes.notes: Kumusta and kamusta are both standard. Asking about family is expected small talk, not nosy.

examples.tl: Kumusta ang pamilya mo? — Okay naman, nasa probinsya sila.
examples.en: How's your family? — They're fine, they're in the province.

notes.notes: Asked far more freely than in the US. Answer: 'Kwarenta na ako' or 'Forty na ako.'

examples.tl: Ilang taon ka na? — Trenta'y singko na ako. Ikaw?
examples.en: How old are you? — I'm thirty-five. You?

notes.notes: Saan for 'where' with a verb; nasaan for 'where is' a thing or person.

examples.tl: Saan ka nakatira? — Sa Pasig, pero nagtatrabaho ako sa Makati.
examples.en: Where do you live? — In Pasig, but I work in Makati.

accept: What do you do for work?
notes.notes: 'Work' replaces trabaho in casual Taglish. 'Saan ka nagtatrabaho?' = where do you work.

examples.tl: Anong work mo? — Nasa BPO ako, night shift.
examples.en: What's your job? — I'm in a BPO, night shift.

notes.notes: 'Saan ka galing?' literally asks where you just came from, but is also used for hometown. Expect 'Taga-Batangas ako.'

examples.tl: Taga-saan ka? — Taga-Cebu ako, pero dito na ako nagtatrabaho.
examples.en: Where are you from? — I'm from Cebu, but I work here now.

notes.notes: Standard small talk here, even from strangers. 'Jowa' = boyfriend/girlfriend (slang).

examples.tl: May asawa ka na ba? — Wala pa, single pa ako.
examples.en: Are you married? — Not yet, I'm still single.

notes.notes: 'Pa' = still. Married: 'May asawa na ako.' Divorced/separated: 'Hiwalay na kami.'

examples.tl: May asawa ka na? — Single pa ako. Ikaw?
examples.en: Are you married? — I'm still single. You?

notes.en: How long have you been here?
notes.notes: 'Matagal ka na dito?' = you've been here long? is the most casual version.

examples.tl: Matagal ka na dito? — Oo, two years na.
examples.en: Have you been here long? — Yeah, two years now.

notes.notes: Textbook form; in real life nearly everyone just says 'Nice to meet you.' Saying the Tagalog gets a warm reaction.

examples.tl: Masaya akong makilala ka. — Ako rin! Ingat.
examples.en: Nice to meet you. — Me too! Take care.

notes.notes: Polite to elders: 'Ano pong pangalan ninyo?' With staff just read the name tag and use kuya/ate.

examples.tl: Anong pangalan mo? — Ako si Marco. Ikaw?
examples.en: What's your name? — I'm Marco. You?

notes.tl: Nagpa-practice lang ako ng Tagalog ko.
notes.notes: Nagpa-practice (incompleted) = am practicing. Good answer when someone laughs at your Tagalog, in a friendly way.

examples.tl: Bakit Tagalog ka? — Nagpa-practice lang ako ng Tagalog ko, pasensya na.
examples.en: Why are you speaking Tagalog? — I'm just practicing my Tagalog, sorry.

notes.notes: Add 'na' for 'tired now/already'. Haggard = exhausted and looking it (Taglish).

examples.tl: Pagod ako, traffic kanina. — Magpahinga ka muna.
examples.en: I'm tired, there was traffic earlier. — Rest first.

notes.notes: Swap the body part: tiyan (stomach), ngipin (tooth), likod (back), lalamunan (throat).

examples.tl: Masakit ang ulo ko. — May Biogesic ako, gusto mo?
examples.en: I have a headache. — I have Biogesic, want some?

notes.notes: 'Kailangan ko ng ...' + noun. With a verb: 'Kailangan kong umuwi' (I need to go home).

examples.tl: Kailangan ko ng tubig, ang init. — Bibili ako sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: I need water, it's so hot. — I'll buy some at 7-Eleven.

notes.notes: 'Gusto ko ng ...' + noun; 'Gusto kong ...' + verb. 'Gusto mo ng kape?' = want coffee?

examples.tl: Gusto mo ng kape? — Gusto ko ng kape, walang asukal.
examples.en: Want coffee? — I want coffee, no sugar.

notes.notes: Ayoko = ayaw ko, contracted. Soften with 'po' or 'salamat': 'Ayoko po, salamat.' 'Ayoko na' = I've had enough.

examples.tl: Gusto mo pa ng kanin? — Ayoko na, busog na ako.
examples.en: Want more rice? — No more, I'm full.

notes.notes: 'Ewan ko' is more offhand (dunno). 'Ewan' alone can sound dismissive.

examples.tl: Anong oras siya darating? — Hindi ko alam, di pa nag-reply.
examples.en: What time is she arriving? — I don't know, she hasn't replied yet.

notes.notes: 'Ano ulit?' = what again? is the quick casual version. Root ulit = repeat.

examples.tl: Pwede mo bang ulitin? Mabilis masyado. — Sige: sa kanto, kaliwa.
examples.en: Can you repeat that? Too fast. — Sure: at the corner, left.

notes.notes: For speech or a driver. 'Dahan-dahan lang po, kuya' to a speeding Grab driver. Root bagal = slow.

examples.tl: Pakibagalan po, nag-aaral pa ako ng Tagalog. — Ah, sige, dahan-dahan.
examples.en: Please slow down, I'm still learning Tagalog. — Oh, sure, slowly.

notes.notes: 'Okay lang' answers 'Kumusta?' and 'Okay ka lang?' (are you okay?). Lang softens it.

examples.tl: Okay ka lang? Parang pagod ka. — Okay lang ako, puyat lang.
examples.en: Are you okay? You look tired. — I'm okay, just didn't sleep much.

notes.taglish: Di ako sure.
notes.notes: 'Sure' has fully replaced sigurado in casual speech. 'Sure ka?' = are you sure?

examples.tl: Bukas ba ang Sunday? — Hindi ako sigurado, i-check ko.
examples.en: Is it open on Sunday? — I'm not sure, I'll check.

notes.notes: Siguro = maybe/probably; baka = maybe (less sure); malamang = most likely. 'Siguro nga' = yeah, probably.

examples.tl: Uulan ba mamaya? — Siguro, madilim na.
examples.en: Will it rain later? — Maybe, it's already dark.

notes.notes: Mamaya = later today. 'Mamaya na lang' = let's just do it later. Bukas = tomorrow.

examples.tl: Kakain ka na? — Baka mamaya, busog pa ako.
examples.en: Are you eating now? — Maybe later, I'm still full.

notes.notes: Pronounced 'tignan'. Non-committal answer to plans. 'Bahala na' = we'll see what happens / leave it to fate.

examples.tl: Sama ka sa Sabado? — Tingnan natin, may trabaho pa ako.
examples.en: Coming on Saturday? — Let's see, I still have work.

notes.notes: Puyat = sleep-deprived (stayed up late). 'Antok' alone works casually.

examples.tl: Inaantok na ako. — Uwi na tayo, late na rin.
examples.en: I'm sleepy. — Let's head home, it's late anyway.

notes.notes: Uhaw (adj) also works alone, like gutom. 'Uhaw' as slang can mean thirsty for attention, context matters.

examples.tl: Nauuhaw ako. — May tubig sa ref, kuha ka lang.
examples.en: I'm thirsty. — There's water in the fridge, just grab some.

notes.notes: 'Ang + adjective' = exclamation (so X!). Daily conversation starter from March to June. Mainit = hot (plain).

examples.tl: Ang init! — Oo nga, pumasok tayo sa mall, may aircon.
examples.en: It's so hot! — Yeah, let's go in the mall, there's aircon.

examples.tl: Ang init! Parang nasa oven ang Makati ngayon.
examples.en: It's so hot! Makati feels like an oven today.

notes.taglish: Ang init! Aircon please.

notes.en: I need to go home now.
accept_tl: Kailangan ko nang umuwi, late na.
notes.notes: 'Nang' here = 'na' + linker ng. Softer exit: 'Mauna na ako' (I'll go ahead).

examples.tl: Isa pa! — Kailangan ko nang umuwi, may trabaho bukas.
examples.en: One more! — I need to go home now, I have work tomorrow.

notes.notes: Almost everyone in Manila switches without fuss. 'English na lang po' = let's just do English.

examples.tl: Pwede po English? Nag-aaral pa ako. — Sure, no problem!
examples.en: Can we speak English? I'm still learning. — Sure, no problem!

notes.taglish: Wait lang.
notes.notes: Saglit and teka are equally common. 'Teka' also = 'wait, what?' when surprised.

examples.tl: Tara na! — Sandali lang, kukunin ko lang ang wallet ko.
examples.en: Let's go! — Just a moment, I'll just grab my wallet.

examples.tl: Sandali lang po, hinahanap ko ang ID ko.
examples.en: Just a moment, I'm looking for my ID.

notes.notes: Kaya = able to manage. 'Kaya ko' = I can handle it; 'Kaya mo yan!' = you can do it!

examples.tl: Isa pang shot! — Hindi ko na kaya, sobra na.
examples.en: One more shot! — I can't anymore, that's too much.

accept_tl: Miss ko na ang pamilya ko.
notes.taglish: Miss ko na ang pamilya ko.
notes.notes: Miss is fully borrowed: na-miss (did miss), nami-miss (am missing). 'Miss ko na kayo' = I miss you guys.

examples.tl: Uuwi ka ba sa States sa Pasko? — Oo, miss ko na ang pamilya ko.
examples.en: Going home to the States for Christmas? — Yeah, I miss my family.

notes.notes: Gagawin = will do (contemplated). 'May lakad ka bukas?' = you got plans tomorrow?

examples.tl: Anong gagawin mo bukas? — Wala, free ako. Bakit?
examples.en: What are you doing tomorrow? — Nothing, I'm free. Why?

notes.notes: Tara = come on/let's go. 'Kain tayo' is also the polite thing to say when you're eating and someone walks by.

examples.tl: Tara, kain tayo. — Saan? Gutom na rin ako.
examples.en: Come on, let's eat. — Where? I'm hungry too.

notes.notes: Kakain = will eat. The usual non-answer: 'Kahit saan' (anywhere) or 'Ikaw bahala.'

examples.tl: Saan tayo kakain? — Sa Poblacion, may bago doon.
examples.en: Where should we eat? — In Poblacion, there's a new place there.

notes.notes: Magkikita = will see each other. Reply: 'Mga alas-siyete' (around seven) or '7 pm, Filipino time' (meaning late).

examples.tl: Anong oras tayo magkikita? — Mga alas-sais, sa Greenbelt.
examples.en: What time are we meeting? — Around six, at Greenbelt.

notes.notes: 'Sa' + day = on that day. 'Na lang' = let's just... (settling on something).

examples.tl: Busy ako ngayong linggo. — Sige, sa Sabado tayo.
examples.en: I'm busy this week. — Okay, let's do Saturday.

notes.notes: Linggo (capital) = Sunday; linggo = week. 'Pwede ba sa ...?' works for any day or time.

examples.tl: Pwede ba sa Linggo? — Pwede, after mass.
examples.en: Can we do Sunday? — Sure, after mass.

accept: I have plans / something to do.
notes.notes: Lakad literally = walk, but 'may lakad' = have an errand/outing/plans. Polite way to decline without details.

examples.tl: Sama ka mamaya? — Sorry, may lakad ako. Next time.
examples.en: Coming later? — Sorry, I have plans. Next time.

examples.tl: May lakad ako bukas, hindi ako makakasama.
examples.en: I have plans tomorrow, I can't join.
examples.taglish: May lakad ako bukas, eh, next time na lang.

examples.tl: May lakad ba kayo sa weekend?
examples.en: Do you have plans this weekend?

notes.taglish: Sorry, may lakad ako sa Sabado.

notes.notes: 'Abala' is the Tagalog word but 'busy' is what everyone says. 'Eh' at the end softens it as an excuse.

examples.tl: Pwede ka ba ngayon? — Busy ako ngayon, eh. Mamaya na lang?
examples.en: Are you free now? — I'm busy right now. Later instead?

notes.notes: Tapos = finished; also 'then/after that' in storytelling. 'Tapos ka na?' = are you done?

examples.tl: Tapos ka na sa gym? — Tapos na ako, papunta na sa'yo.
examples.en: Done at the gym? — I'm done, heading to you now.

notes.taglish: Otw na ako.
notes.notes: 'Otw' is the standard text. 'Paalis na ako' = just leaving. Everyone knows 'papunta na' often means 'still in the shower'.

examples.tl: Asan ka na? — Papunta na ako, 10 minutes.
examples.en: Where are you? — I'm on my way, 10 minutes.

examples.tl: Papunta na ako, nasa Kalayaan na.
examples.en: I'm heading there, I'm on Kalayaan now.
examples.taglish: Papunta na ako, nasa Kalayaan na, 5 mins.

examples.tl: Papunta pa lang ako sa sakayan.
examples.en: I'm only just heading to the loading area.

notes.notes: Means 'out of the house' or 'right outside the door' depending on context. 'Nasa bahay ako' = I'm home.

examples.tl: Nasa unit ka ba? — Hindi, nasa labas ako, balik ako mamaya.
examples.en: Are you in your unit? — No, I'm out, I'll be back later.

notes.notes: Andito/nandito/narito all = here. Baba = down/below. Text this to a friend or a Grab driver from the lobby.

examples.tl: Andito na ako sa baba. — Sige, bababa na ako.
examples.en: I'm downstairs now. — Okay, I'm coming down.

notes.taglish: Wait mo ako.
notes.notes: Antayin is the spoken variant of hintayin. 'Hintay' alone = wait up.

examples.tl: Hintayin mo ako sa labas. — Sige, dito lang ako sa gate.
examples.en: Wait for me outside. — Okay, I'll be right here by the gate.

notes.taglish: I-pick-up kita.
notes.notes: Kita = I...you. Sundo = pick-up; 'May sundo ka?' = is someone picking you up? 'Hatid-sundo' = drop-off and pick-up.

examples.tl: Paano ako pupunta doon? — Sunduin kita, 6 pm sa lobby.
examples.en: How do I get there? — I'll pick you up, 6 pm at the lobby.

notes.taglish: I-drop kita.
notes.notes: Hatid = escort/bring someone somewhere. Normal courtesy after a night out: 'Hatid na kita' = let me take you home.

examples.tl: Late na, paano ka uuwi? — Okay lang. — Ihahatid kita, malapit lang.
examples.en: It's late, how are you getting home? — I'm fine. — I'll take you home, it's close.

notes.taglish: G ako.
notes.notes: Game = willing/up for it. 'G' is the text version. 'Game ka?' = you in?

examples.tl: Inuman mamaya, game ka? — Game ako, anong oras?
examples.en: Drinks later, you in? — I'm in, what time?

notes.notes: Polite decline. 'Ha?' at the end = okay? Sa susunod = next time (Tagalog).

examples.tl: Sama ka sa Tagaytay? — Next time na lang, may trabaho ako.
examples.en: Coming to Tagaytay? — Maybe next time, I have work.

notes.taglish: Male-late ako ng konti.
notes.notes: Male-late (will be late), na-late (was late). Universal excuse: 'kasi traffic'.

examples.tl: Male-late ako ng konti, traffic sa EDSA. — Okay, order na muna ako.
examples.en: I'll be a little late, traffic on EDSA. — Okay, I'll order first.

notes.notes: 'Asan ka na?' is the text version. Nasaan for location of a person or thing; saan with verbs.

examples.tl: Nasaan ka na? — Nasa Grab na ako, 5 minutes.
examples.en: Where are you now? — I'm in the Grab, 5 minutes.

notes.taglish: See you bukas.
notes.notes: 'Kita-kits' is playful. 'Kita tayo mamaya' = see you later.

examples.tl: Sige, kita tayo bukas. — Sige, ingat!
examples.en: Okay, see you tomorrow. — Okay, take care!

accept_tl: Mag-book na lang tayo ng Grab.
notes.notes: Mag- + brand = use that service: mag-Grab, mag-GCash, mag-jeep, mag-MRT.

examples.tl: Ang hirap mag-taxi dito. — Mag-Grab na lang tayo, ako na mag-book.
examples.en: It's hard to get a taxi here. — Let's just take a Grab, I'll book.

notes.notes: KKB = kanya-kanyang bayad (each pays their own), said as letters 'ka-ka-bi'. 'Hati tayo' = let's split.

examples.tl: Sagot mo ba 'to? — Hindi, KKB tayo ngayon, petsa de peligro.
examples.en: Is this on you? — No, we split today, it's the broke days before payday.

notes.notes: Saklolo is the old emergency word, rarely heard now. Tulong is both the noun 'help' and the shout.

examples.tl: Tulong! May nahulog! — Tawag ka ng guard!
examples.en: Help! Someone fell! — Call the guard!

notes.taglish: Pwede pa-help?
notes.notes: 'Patulong po' is the quick polite version with staff or strangers. Tulungan = help (object focus).

examples.tl: Pwede mo ba akong tulungan? Nawawala ako. — Sige, saan ka pupunta?
examples.en: Can you help me? I'm lost. — Sure, where are you going?

notes.notes: Naliligaw (lost one's way) is the precise word; nawawala (missing) is also used for people. 'Ligaw' also = courting.

examples.tl: Nawawala ako, saan ang MRT? — Doon po, diretso lang, kaliwa.
examples.en: I'm lost, where's the MRT? — Over there, just straight, then left.

notes.notes: Nawala (got lost, done) vs nawawala (is missing right now). Pitaka = wallet, but 'wallet' is more common.

examples.tl: Nawala ang wallet ko sa Grab! — Tawagan mo yung driver sa app.
examples.en: I lost my wallet in the Grab! — Call the driver through the app.

accept_tl: Sira po ang aircon sa unit ko.
notes.notes: Sira = broken. 'Aircon' never 'AC' in speech. 'Hindi lumalamig' = it's not getting cold.

examples.tl: Sira ang aircon sa unit ko. — Pakireport sa admin, tatawag sila ng technician.
examples.en: The aircon in my unit is broken. — Report it to admin, they'll call a technician.

notes.notes: 'Walang ...' = there's no ... Gripo = faucet. Ask 'Hanggang kailan?' (until when?).

examples.tl: Walang tubig sa unit ko. — May water interruption po hanggang alas-tres.
examples.en: There's no water in my unit. — There's a water interruption until three.

notes.taglish: Brownout!
notes.notes: 'Brownout' means any power outage in the Philippines, not a partial one. 'Walang ilaw' is also used.

examples.tl: Walang kuryente sa floor namin. — Brownout sa buong building, may generator naman.
examples.en: There's no electricity on our floor. — Outage in the whole building, but there's a generator.

notes.notes: Signal = mobile data/reception. Mabagal = slow. 'Anong password ng wifi?' = what's the wifi password?

examples.tl: Walang wifi, hindi ako makapag-work. — I-restart mo yung router.
examples.en: There's no wifi, I can't work. — Restart the router.

notes.taglish: Call mo ako.
notes.notes: Tawagan = call (object focus). 'Tatawag ako' = I'll call. 'Missed call mo ako' = give me a missed call.

examples.tl: Tawagan mo ako pag nandito ka na. — Sige, tawag ako pag nasa lobby na.
examples.en: Call me when you're here. — Okay, I'll call when I'm in the lobby.

notes.notes: Phone numbers are read in English. 'Globe ka o Smart?' may follow (network for cheaper calls).

examples.tl: Anong number mo? — 0917... i-save mo, Marco.
examples.en: What's your number? — 0917... save it as Marco.

notes.tl: Pakisabi kay Ana na tatawag ako.
accept: Please tell Ana that I will call.
accept_tl: Sabihin mo kay Ana na tatawag ako.
Pakisabi po kay Ana, tatawag ako.
notes.notes: Pattern: 'Pakisabi kay [name] na [message]'. Kay before a person's name; sa before a place or role.

examples.tl: Pakisabi kay Ana na tatawag ako mamaya. — Sige po, sasabihin ko.
examples.en: Please tell Ana I'll call later. — Okay, I'll tell her.

notes.notes: 'May problema ba?' = is there a problem? 'Anong problema?' = what's wrong?

examples.tl: May problema sa order ko, kulang ng isa. — Ay, sorry po, i-check ko.
examples.en: There's a problem with my order, one is missing. — Oh, sorry, I'll check.

notes.notes: Ayos = in order/fine. 'Ayos na ba?' = is it fixed? Also 'Ayos!' = nice!

examples.tl: Kumusta yung aircon? — Ayos na, naayos ng maintenance kanina.
examples.en: How's the aircon? — Fixed now, maintenance fixed it earlier.

notes.notes: Both the reassurance and the response to thanks. 'Wala yun' = that was nothing.

examples.tl: Sorry, na-late ako. — Walang problema, kakadating ko lang din.
examples.en: Sorry, I was late. — No problem, I just got here too.

notes.notes: Gumagana = functions. 'Ayaw gumana' = it refuses to work (very common phrasing). 'Gumagana na' = it works now.

examples.tl: Hindi gumagana yung card ko sa ATM. — Try mo yung ibang machine.
examples.en: My card isn't working at the ATM. — Try the other machine.

notes.notes: Ospital or hospital, both used. ER is 'emergency' or 'ER'. Botika = pharmacy (Mercury Drug, Watsons).

examples.tl: Kailangan ko ng doktor, masama ang pakiramdam ko. — May clinic sa second floor.
examples.en: I need a doctor, I don't feel well. — There's a clinic on the second floor.

notes.taglish: Na-late ako kasi traffic.
notes.notes: 'Traffic' is a noun, adjective and excuse. 'Na-traffic ako' = I got caught in traffic.

examples.tl: Asan ka na? — Na-stuck ako sa traffic sa EDSA, sorry.
examples.en: Where are you? — I'm stuck in traffic on EDSA, sorry.

accept_tl: Naiwan ko yung phone ko sa Grab.
notes.notes: Naiwan = left behind (accidentally). Cellphone or CP in older usage; 'phone' now.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang phone ko sa unit. — Balik ka muna, hintayin ka namin.
examples.en: I left my phone in the unit. — Go back first, we'll wait for you.

notes.notes: Load = prepaid credit. 'Pa-load' at any sari-sari store. 'Wala akong data' if on wifi only.

examples.tl: Bakit di ka nag-reply? — Wala akong load, nag-wifi lang ako ngayon.
examples.en: Why didn't you reply? — I had no load, I'm just on wifi now.

notes.notes: Lowbat (low battery) is a full-fledged Filipino word; also jokingly 'I'm drained'. Charger = charger, pahiram = lend me.

examples.tl: Lowbat na ako, pahiram ng charger. — Eto, Type-C ba?
examples.en: My phone's dying, lend me a charger. — Here, is it Type-C?

accept_tl: May wifi po ba? Anong password?
notes.notes: Standard café question. Reply usually points to a sign or the receipt.

examples.tl: Anong password ng wifi? — Nasa resibo po, sa baba.
examples.en: What's the wifi password? — It's on the receipt, at the bottom.

notes.notes: Naman adds a mild complaint. Mahal also = love/dear; context makes it clear. Opposite: mura (cheap).

examples.tl: Tatlong libo po. — Ang mahal naman! Pwede bang tumawad?
examples.en: Three thousand. — That's so expensive! Can I haggle?

notes.notes: Sulit = you got your money's worth. 'Sulit na sulit' = totally worth it. 'Hindi sulit' = not worth it.

examples.tl: Unli samgyup, 499 lang. — Sulit! Tara.
examples.en: Unlimited samgyupsal, only 499. — Worth it! Let's go.

notes.notes: For places, views, things, and people. 'Ang ganda ng view' = the view is beautiful. Gwapo for handsome.

examples.tl: Ang ganda ng view dito sa rooftop. — Oo nga, lalo na pag sunset.
examples.en: The view here on the rooftop is beautiful. — Yeah, especially at sunset.

notes.notes: Approval for a plan, a purchase, a result. 'Ayos ba?' = good? Also 'Ayos lang' = it's fine.

examples.tl: Nakakuha ako ng unit malapit sa MRT. — Ayos yan, walang traffic.
examples.en: I got a unit near the MRT. — That's good, no traffic.

notes.notes: Tama = correct. 'Korek ka d'yan' is a jokey old-school version. 'Tama!' alone = right!

examples.tl: Mas mura mag-Grab kung dalawa tayo. — Tama ka, hati tayo.
examples.en: It's cheaper to Grab if there are two of us. — You're right, let's split it.

notes.taglish: Di ako agree.
notes.notes: Sang-ayon is formal/written (news, debates). In conversation people say 'Di ako agree' or just 'Hindi, eh'. Direct disagreement is often softened.

examples.tl: Mas masarap ang Jollibee kaysa McDo. — Hindi ako sang-ayon, pero okay yung Chickenjoy.
examples.en: Jollibee is better than McDo. — I disagree, but the Chickenjoy is okay.

notes.taglish: Same tayo.
notes.notes: Pareho = same/alike. 'Pareho pala tayo' = oh, we're the same (surprise). Friendship starter.

examples.tl: Ayoko ng maanghang. — Pareho tayo, di ko kaya ang Bicol Express.
examples.en: I don't like spicy. — Same here, I can't handle Bicol Express.

notes.notes: Rule: rin after a vowel, din after a consonant, but speakers mix them freely. Negative: 'Ako rin hindi' (me neither).

examples.tl: Gutom na ako. — Ako rin, kain tayo.
examples.en: I'm hungry. — Me too, let's eat.

notes.notes: Bounce any question back. 'Eh ikaw?' is the chatty form. Polite plural: 'Kayo?'

examples.tl: Okay lang ako, pagod lang. Ikaw? — Ayos lang, galing gym.
examples.en: I'm fine, just tired. And you? — Fine, just came from the gym.

notes.notes: Totoo = true/real. 'Totoo ba?' = is it true? 'Hindi totoo yan' = that's not true.

examples.tl: Mas mahal sa BGC kaysa Makati. — Totoo yan, lalo na ang kape.
examples.en: BGC is pricier than Makati. — That's true, especially coffee.

notes.notes: Blunt and dismissive, can sound rude. For 'I'm fine either way' use 'Okay lang sa akin'. 'Pakialamero' = nosy person.

examples.tl: Galit sa'yo si Marco. — Wala akong pakialam, siya ang may kasalanan.
examples.en: Marco is mad at you. — I don't care, he's the one at fault.

notes.notes: The neutral 'I don't mind' (vs. 'Wala akong pakialam' which is rude). 'Kahit ano' = anything, 'kahit saan' = anywhere.

examples.tl: Okay ba sa'yo yung Korean? — Okay lang sa akin, kahit ano.
examples.en: Is Korean okay with you? — It's fine with me, anything.

notes.notes: Tagal = long time. 'Ang tagal mo!' = you took forever! (to a late friend). 'Matagal pa?' = still long?

examples.tl: Eto na yung order niyo. — Ang tagal! Isang oras kami naghintay.
examples.en: Here's your order. — That took so long! We waited an hour.

examples.tl: Ang tagal ng jeep, wala pang dumadaan.
examples.en: The jeep is taking forever, none has passed yet.
examples.taglish: Ang tagal ng jeep, wala pang dumadaan, 20 mins na.

examples.tl: Ang tagal mo! Isang oras na ako dito.
examples.en: You took forever! I've been here an hour.

notes.taglish: Ang tagal ng Grab, 15 minutes na.

notes.notes: Type = to one's liking, for food, music, or people. 'Trip ko' = I feel like / I'm into. 'Type kita' = I like you.

examples.tl: Gusto mo ng balut? — Hindi ko type, pero try ko.
examples.en: Want some balut? — Not my thing, but I'll try.

notes.notes: Ganun/ganon = like that (from gayon). 'Ah, ganun' = ah, I see. 'Ganun?' alone = like that?

examples.tl: Closed ang mall bukas, holiday. — Ganun ba? Di ko alam.
examples.en: The mall is closed tomorrow, holiday. — Is that so? I didn't know.

notes.notes: Nga = agreement/emphasis. 'Oo nga, no?' = right? (seeking agreement). 'Oo nga pala' = oh right, that reminds me.

examples.tl: Ang init talaga ngayon. — Oo nga, eh. Grabe.
examples.en: It's really hot today. — Yeah, I know. Crazy.

notes.notes: Pleading 'maybe you could' when asking for a discount or favor, with a smile. Also a mock-reproach: 'Baka naman!' = seriously?

examples.tl: Fixed price po. — Baka naman, kuya, dalawa bibilhin ko.
examples.en: Fixed price. — Come on, man, I'm buying two.

notes.notes: To housekeeping or a kasambahay. Paki-ayos = please tidy. Kwarto = room (bedroom); unit = whole condo.

examples.tl: Ate, pakilinis ng kwarto mamaya, ha? — Sige po, pagkatapos ng banyo.
examples.en: Ate, please clean the room later, okay? — Yes, after the bathroom.

accept_tl: May delivery po para sa akin.
May dadating na delivery para sa akin.
notes.notes: Tell the guard or reception in advance. 'Dadating' = will arrive. Unit number helps: 'Unit 12B po.'

examples.tl: Kuya, may delivery para sa akin mamaya, Unit 12B. — Sige po, tatawagan ko kayo.
examples.en: Kuya, there's a delivery for me later, Unit 12B. — Okay, I'll call you.

accept: Please accept the package for me.
notes.taglish: Paki-receive po ng package ko.
notes.notes: Tanggap = receive/accept. Most condo lobbies log parcels; 'Pakitanggap na lang po' = just receive it for me.

examples.tl: Pakitanggap po ng package ko, wala ako sa unit. — Sige po, i-log namin.
examples.en: Please receive my package, I'm not in the unit. — Okay, we'll log it.

notes.notes: 'Unit' = your condo. 'Nasa taas' = upstairs. Reply when the guard calls about a visitor or delivery.

examples.tl: Sir, nandito po yung rider. — Nasa unit ako, bababa ako.
examples.en: Sir, the rider is here. — I'm in my unit, I'll come down.

notes.notes: Ilaw = light. 'Patay ang ilaw' = the light is off/dead. 'Bukas ang ilaw' = the light is on. Bumbilya = bulb.

examples.tl: Sira ang ilaw sa banyo ko. — Pakireport sa admin, papalitan ng maintenance.
examples.en: The light in my bathroom is broken. — Report it to admin, maintenance will replace it.

notes.notes: 'Patawag' = have someone call. In condos you usually file at the admin office; the guard can relay after hours.

examples.tl: Pakitawag ng maintenance, tumutulo ang gripo. — Sige po, i-report ko sa admin.
examples.en: Please call maintenance, the faucet is leaking. — Okay, I'll report it to admin.

notes.notes: Kuya (older brother) for male guards, drivers, staff; ate for women; 'boss' is also common for men. Add 'po' if older.

examples.tl: Eto po ang package niyo. — Salamat, kuya. Ingat!
examples.en: Here's your package. — Thanks, kuya. Take care!

notes.notes: The standard goodbye. Kayo = plural or polite singular; ka = casual singular. 'Ingat sa daan' = safe trip.

examples.tl: Sige po, uwi na kami. — Sige, ingat kayo!
examples.en: Okay, we're heading home. — Okay, take care!

notes.notes: Baba = down; bababa = will go down. Many condos don't let riders up, so you go down. 'Aakyat ako' = I'll go up.

examples.tl: Sir, nandito na po yung Grab Food niyo. — Sige, bababa ako.
examples.en: Sir, your Grab Food is here. — Okay, I'll come down.

notes.notes: Tell the guard so they can log the visitor. 'Pwede na po siyang umakyat' = they can come up.

examples.tl: May bisita ako mamaya, si Marco. — Sige po, papa-log in namin siya.
examples.en: I have a visitor later, Marco. — Okay, we'll have him log in.

accept_tl: Papuntahin niyo na po sa unit.
notes.notes: Umakyat = go up. Reply when the lobby calls about a visitor. 'Paakyat' = let (them) up.
