examples.tl: Sir, may bisita po kayo, si Marco. — Pwede na po siyang umakyat, salamat.
examples.en: Sir, you have a visitor, Marco. — He can come up now, thanks.

notes.notes: Bukas = open (and also 'tomorrow', stress differs: bukás open, búkas tomorrow). 'Pakisara' = please close.

examples.tl: Kuya, pakibukas ng gate, may Grab ako. — Sige po.
examples.en: Kuya, please open the gate, I have a Grab. — Okay.

notes.tl: Pa-deliver po ng tubig, isang galon.
notes.en: Please deliver one gallon of water.
accept: One gallon of water delivered, please.
accept_tl: Pa-refill po ng tubig, isang galon.
Pabili ng isang galon ng tubig.
notes.notes: Water refilling stations deliver 5-gallon containers (called 'galon'). Pa- + verb = have it done for you.

examples.tl: Pa-deliver po ng tubig, isang galon, Unit 12B. — Sige po, 30 minutes.
examples.en: Please deliver one gallon of water, Unit 12B. — Okay, 30 minutes.

notes.tl: Dumating na ba ang package ko?
accept_tl: Andito na ba ang delivery ko?
Nandito na ba ang package ko?
May package po ba para sa Unit 12B?
notes.notes: Dumating = arrived. Ask at the lobby desk; give your unit number. 'Wala pa po' = not yet.

examples.tl: Dumating na ba ang package ko? Unit 12B. — Wala pa po, sir.
examples.en: Has my package arrived? Unit 12B. — Not yet, sir.

notes.notes: For deliveries: tell the guard or rider it's paid online. Opposite: 'COD po' (cash on delivery).

examples.tl: Magkano po babayaran? — Bayad na po, GCash.
examples.en: How much to pay? — It's already paid, GCash.

notes.en: Where do I throw the trash?
notes.notes: Basura = trash, basurahan = bin. Condos have a garbage room per floor or a chute; segregation (nabubulok/di-nabubulok) is often required.

examples.tl: Saan ang tapunan ng basura? — May garbage room sa dulo ng hallway.
examples.en: Where do I throw the trash? — There's a garbage room at the end of the hallway.

notes.taglish: Good morning po.
notes.notes: Hapon = afternoon, gabi = evening. In Manila 'Good morning po' is more common than the full Tagalog; both are welcome.

examples.tl: Magandang umaga po, kuya. — Magandang umaga po, sir!
examples.en: Good morning, kuya. — Good morning, sir!

notes.notes: Marami = many/much. Po adds respect for elders, staff, strangers. Casual: 'Salamat!' or 'Thanks!'

examples.tl: Eto po ang sukli. — Maraming salamat po.
examples.en: Here's your change. — Thank you very much.

notes.notes: For squeezing through a crowd, a jeep, or a packed MRT. 'Excuse me po' is also common. 'Daan' = path.

examples.tl: Makikiraan po. — Sige po, dito.
examples.en: Excuse me, coming through. — Sure, here.

examples.tl: Makikiraan po, bababa na ako.
examples.en: Excuse me, I'm getting off.
examples.taglish: Makikiraan po, bababa na ako sa kanto.

examples.tl: Padaan po, salamat.
examples.en: Let me through please, thanks.

notes.taglish: Makikiraan po, bababa ako.

notes.notes: 'Kumusta ka na?' = how have you been (haven't seen you in a while). 'Musta?' is text-casual. Also used for 'how was it?': 'Kumusta ang trip?'

examples.tl: Kumusta ka na? — Okay naman, busy lang. Ikaw?
examples.en: How have you been? — Good, just busy. You?

notes.notes: A greeting as much as a question, like 'how are you'. Standard answer: 'Kumain na' or 'Hindi pa'. Often followed by an offer of food.

examples.tl: Kumain ka na ba? — Hindi pa, gutom na nga ako.
examples.en: Have you eaten? — Not yet, I'm actually hungry.

notes.notes: Hindi pa = not yet. Kumakain (incompleted) is the natural form here, not kumain. If you have: 'Kumain na ako.'

examples.tl: Kain ka na? — Hindi pa ako kumakain, tara sa labas.
examples.en: Have you eaten? — I haven't eaten yet, let's go out.

notes.notes: The polite way to leave a group or the office. Reply: 'Sige, ingat!' Una = first/ahead.

examples.tl: Mauna na ako, may lakad pa ako. — Sige, ingat ka!
examples.en: I'll go ahead, I still have plans. — Okay, take care!

notes.notes: Time is answered in English or Spanish-style: 'Alas-tres na' or 'Three na'. 'Anong oras?' with a verb = at what time?

examples.tl: Anong oras na? — Alas-singko na, uwian na.
examples.en: What time is it? — It's five already, time to go home.

examples.tl: Anong oras na? Baka na-late na tayo.
examples.en: What time is it? We might be late already.
examples.taglish: Anong oras na? Shoot, late na tayo.

notes.taglish: Na-forget ko.
notes.notes: Nakalimutan or nalimutan. 'Nakalimutan ko ang password ko' = I forgot my password. 'Wag mong kalimutan' = don't forget.

examples.tl: Dala mo yung ID? — Ay, nakalimutan ko! Nasa unit.
examples.en: Did you bring the ID? — Oh, I forgot! It's in the unit.

notes.notes: Pupunta = will go. 'San ka punta?' is quick casual. Not nosy; a normal greeting in the hallway or elevator.

examples.tl: Saan ka pupunta? — Sa gym lang, tapos grocery.
examples.en: Where are you going? — Just the gym, then groceries.

accept: I just came from the gym.
notes.taglish: From gym ako.
notes.notes: Galing = came from. Answers 'Saan ka galing?' (where did you come from?). 'Kakagaling ko lang' = I just came from.

examples.tl: Saan ka galing? Pawis ka. — Galing ako sa gym, leg day.
examples.en: Where did you come from? You're sweaty. — I came from the gym, leg day.

notes.notes: Pahiram = let me borrow (pa- + hiram). 'Pahiram ng ballpen/payong/powerbank'. Return: 'Eto na, salamat.'

examples.tl: Pahiram ng charger, lowbat na ako. — Eto, iPhone ba?
examples.en: Can I borrow a charger? My phone's dying. — Here, is it an iPhone?

notes.notes: Called out at a door or gate when there's no doorbell (literally 'a person here!'). Also what a sari-sari store customer shouts.

examples.tl: Tao po! — Sandali lang! Sino yan?
examples.en: Hello, anyone home? — Just a moment! Who is it?

notes.notes: Bawal = forbidden, seen on signs everywhere (Bawal umihi dito). Ask before smoking or taking photos. Opposite: 'Pwede ba dito?'

examples.tl: Bawal ba mag-vape dito? — Bawal po, sa smoking area lang.
examples.en: Is vaping not allowed here? — Not allowed, only in the smoking area.

notes.notes: 'X na lang' = let's just settle on X. Mamaya na lang = later instead. Also used to postpone chores guilt-free.

examples.tl: Gagawin natin ngayon? — Bukas na lang, pagod na ako.
examples.en: Are we doing it now? — Tomorrow instead, I'm tired.

notes.notes: For a crowd, a party, or a traffic jam. 'May meron' (jokey) = there's something going on. 'Anong nangyari?' = what happened?

examples.tl: Anong meron? Ang daming tao. — May sale sa Landmark.
examples.en: What's going on? So many people. — There's a sale at Landmark.

notes.notes: Linker form 'isang' before nouns: isang tao. Tagalog numbers count things; Spanish numbers do time, money, age.

examples.tl: Isa lang ang kailangan ko.
examples.en: I only need one.

examples.tl: Isang order ng sisig, please.
examples.en: One order of sisig, please.

notes.notes: Linker form 'dalawang': dalawang kilo. 'Kaming dalawa' = the two of us.

examples.tl: Dalawang kilo ng manggang hilaw, kuya.
examples.en: Two kilos of green mango, kuya.

examples.tl: Kaming dalawa lang ang pupunta.
examples.en: Only the two of us are going.

notes.notes: Linker form 'tatlong'.

examples.tl: Tatlo kaming magkakapatid.
examples.en: There are three of us siblings.

examples.tl: Tatlong araw na akong walang tulog.
examples.en: I have gone three days without sleep.

notes.notes: Linker form 'apat na' (ends in consonant, so 'na' not '-ng').

examples.tl: Apat na tao, may table pa ba?
examples.en: Four people, is there still a table?

notes.notes: Linker form 'limang'. For five pesos people say 'singko' (Spanish), not 'limang piso'.

examples.tl: Limang piraso ng pandesal, please.
examples.en: Five pieces of pandesal, please.

notes.notes: Linker form 'anim na'.

examples.tl: Anim na buwan na ako sa Makati.
examples.en: I have been in Makati for six months.

notes.notes: Linker form 'pitong'.

examples.tl: Pitong araw sa isang linggo.
examples.en: Seven days in a week.

notes.notes: Linker form 'walong'.

examples.tl: Walong oras ang shift ko.
examples.en: My shift is eight hours.

notes.notes: Linker form 'siyam na'.

examples.tl: Siyam na taon na silang kasal.
examples.en: They have been married nine years.

notes.notes: Linker form 'sampung'. For ten pesos say 'diyes'.

examples.tl: Sampung minuto lang, malapit na ako.
examples.en: Just ten minutes, I am almost there.

notes.notes: labing- + unit = 11 to 19: labindalawa (12), labintatlo (13), labing-apat (14)...

examples.tl: Labing-isang taon na ang anak niya.
examples.en: Her kid is eleven years old now.

notes.notes: Tens: dalawampu, tatlumpu, apatnapu, limampu, animnapu... In money/age people usually say 'bente' instead.

examples.tl: Dalawampung tao ang pumunta sa party.
examples.en: Twenty people came to the party.

notes.notes: Also 'sandaan'. For P100 people just say 'one hundred' or 'isang daan'; 'syento' mostly in dos syentos, tres syentos.

examples.tl: Isang daan lang 'to? Ang mura!
examples.en: This is only a hundred? So cheap!

notes.notes: P1,000 is 'isang libo' or 'one thousand'; 'mil' shows up in 'dos mil', 'singko mil'.

examples.tl: Isang libo ang budget ko sa grocery ngayong linggo.
examples.en: My grocery budget this week is a thousand.

notes.notes: Spanish-derived numbers are used for clock time, prices, and age. 'Uno' alone is rare except 'ala-una' (1 o'clock) and the top grade 1.0 in school.

examples.tl: Nakakuha siya ng uno sa Math.
examples.en: She got a 1.0 (highest grade) in Math.

notes.notes: Used in time (alas-dos), money (dos syentos, dos mil), and lotto/jersey numbers. Counting objects still uses 'dalawa'.

examples.tl: Dos mil ang renta ng parking kada buwan.
examples.en: Parking rent is two thousand a month.

notes.notes: alas-tres = 3 o'clock; tres syentos = 300.

examples.tl: Tres syentos lang ang damit sa ukay.
examples.en: The shirt at the thrift stall is only three hundred.

notes.notes: alas-kwatro = 4 o'clock.

examples.tl: Uwian na namin ng alas-kwatro.
examples.en: Our dismissal is at four.

notes.notes: The everyday word for five pesos and 5 o'clock. 'Singko' also = the P5 coin.

examples.tl: May singko ka? Para exact ang bayad sa jeep.
examples.en: Do you have five pesos? So the jeep fare is exact.

notes.notes: alas-sais = 6 o'clock, the usual uwian/meetup time.

examples.tl: Alas-sais ng gabi tayo magkita sa Ayala.
examples.en: Let's meet at six in the evening at Ayala.

notes.notes: alas-siyete = 7 o'clock.

examples.tl: Alas-siyete pa ang flight, chill lang.
examples.en: The flight is not until seven, relax.

notes.notes: alas-otso = 8 o'clock.

examples.tl: Alas-otso ng umaga ang pasok ko.
examples.en: My work starts at eight in the morning.

notes.notes: alas-nuwebe = 9 o'clock.

examples.tl: Bukas ang mall mula alas-diyes hanggang alas-nuwebe.
examples.en: The mall is open from ten until nine.

notes.notes: Ten pesos = 'diyes'. alas-diyes = 10 o'clock.

examples.tl: Diyes lang ang dagdag kung may extra rice.
examples.en: It is only ten pesos more with extra rice.

notes.notes: alas-dose = noon or midnight. Eleven is 'onse' (alas-onse).

examples.tl: Alas-dose na, lunch tayo.
examples.en: It is twelve already, let's have lunch.

notes.notes: alas-onse = 11 o'clock. Slang: 'ini-onse' = to cheat someone, as in 'na-onse ako'.

examples.tl: Alas-onse pa ang check-in, maaga pa tayo.
examples.en: Check-in is not until eleven, we are early.

notes.notes: Also the 15th (payday: 'kinse'), P15, and quarter past: alas-dos kinse.

examples.tl: Sahod sa kinse, tapos ulit sa katapusan.
examples.en: Payday on the 15th, then again at month end.

notes.notes: Also used for age: 'trenta na ako'.

examples.tl: Trenta na siya pero mukhang bente pa.
examples.en: She is thirty but still looks twenty.

notes.notes: 'Kwarenta y singko' = 45, as in 'alas-dos kwarenta y singko'.

examples.tl: Kwarenta pesos ang bottled water sa loob ng mall.
examples.en: Bottled water inside the mall is forty pesos.

examples.tl: Sisenta na ang tatay ko pero nag-gym pa.
examples.en: My dad is sixty but still goes to the gym.

examples.tl: Setenta ang ulam na may kanin sa karinderya.
examples.en: The meal with rice at the eatery is seventy.

examples.tl: Otsenta pesos ang isang order ng lumpia.
examples.en: One order of lumpia is eighty pesos.

examples.tl: Nobenta na si Lola pero malakas pa.
examples.en: Grandma is ninety but still strong.

notes.notes: Used in dos syentos (200), tres syentos (300), kinyentos (500). P100 alone is 'isang daan' or 'one hundred'.

examples.tl: Dos syentos singkwenta ang Grab papuntang BGC.
examples.en: The Grab to BGC is two hundred fifty.

notes.notes: dos mil = 2,000; singko mil = 5,000; diyes mil = 10,000. 'Isang libo' or 'one thousand' for 1,000.

examples.tl: Singko mil ang deposit sa condo.
examples.en: The condo deposit is five thousand.

notes.notes: 'Una' = first; 'unang beses' = first time; 'nauna' = went first. Ordinals: una, ikalawa, ikatlo...

examples.tl: Unang beses ko sa Palawan!
examples.en: My first time in Palawan!

notes.notes: 'Pangalawa' is the everyday spoken form; 'ikalawa' is more formal/written.

examples.tl: Pangalawang beses na 'to na na-late ka.
examples.en: This is the second time you have been late.

notes.notes: 'Lahat ng' before nouns; 'kayong lahat' = all of you. 'Magkano lahat?' = how much altogether?

examples.tl: Magkano lahat, ate?
examples.en: How much is everything, ate?

examples.tl: Lahat kami na-stuck sa traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: All of us got stuck in traffic on EDSA.

notes.notes: 'Kalahating kilo' = half a kilo; 'kalahating oras' = half an hour. Also just 'half' in Taglish.

examples.tl: Kalahating kilo lang ng baboy, ate.
examples.en: Just half a kilo of pork, ate.

examples.tl: Hati tayo, kalahati sa'yo kalahati sa'kin.
examples.en: Let's split it, half for you, half for me.

notes.notes: 'Isang pares ng sapatos'. Also the beef stew 'pares' at roadside eateries, unrelated meaning.

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng dalawang pares ng medyas sa Divisoria.
examples.en: I bought two pairs of socks in Divisoria.

notes.notes: Eggs are sold by the dozen or by the tray; 'kalahating dosena' = half a dozen.

examples.tl: Isang dosenang itlog, magkano?
examples.en: How much for a dozen eggs?

notes.notes: 'Anong oras?' = what time? 'Isang oras' = one hour. 'Walang oras' = no time. 'May oras ka ba?' = do you have time?

examples.tl: Anong oras ang pasok mo bukas?
examples.en: What time do you start work tomorrow?

examples.tl: Dalawang oras ako sa traffic kanina.
examples.en: I was in traffic for two hours earlier.

notes.notes: Only 1 o'clock uses 'ala-'; all others use 'alas-' (alas-dos, alas-tres...). From Spanish 'a la una'.

examples.tl: Ala-una ng hapon ang meeting natin.
examples.en: Our meeting is at one in the afternoon.

notes.notes: Pattern: alas- + Spanish number. Minutes follow directly: alas-dos diyes = 2:10, alas-dos trenta = 2:30.

examples.tl: Kita tayo sa Glorietta ng alas-dos.
examples.en: Let's meet at Glorietta at two.

notes.notes: 'y medya' = :30. Young people often just say 'three thirty'. Both are fine.

examples.tl: Alas-tres y medya pa ang check-out, may oras pa tayo.
examples.en: Check-out is not until half past three, we still have time.

notes.notes: From Spanish 'y media'. 'Alas-sais y medya' = 6:30. Alternative: 'alas-sais trenta'.

examples.tl: Alas-otso y medya ang call time, wag ma-late.
examples.en: Call time is eight thirty, don't be late.

notes.notes: Older/less common pattern: 'alas-singko menos kinse' = 4:45. Most people now say 'kwarenta y singko' or 'four forty-five'.

examples.tl: Alas-singko menos kinse na, tara na.
examples.en: It is quarter to five, let's go.

notes.notes: Attach after the hour: alas-siyete ng umaga. 'Ng' here is pronounced 'nang'.

examples.tl: Alas-sais ng umaga ang alarm ko pero alas-siyete ako gumigising.
examples.en: My alarm is at six in the morning but I wake up at seven.

notes.notes: Roughly 1 PM to about 6 PM. 'Alas-dos ng hapon' = 2 PM.

examples.tl: Dumating ang Lalamove ng alas-kwatro ng hapon.
examples.en: The Lalamove arrived at four in the afternoon.

notes.notes: From about 6 PM onward. 'Alas-nuwebe ng gabi' = 9 PM.

examples.tl: Umuwi ako ng alas-onse ng gabi galing BGC.
examples.en: I got home from BGC at eleven at night.

notes.notes: 'Tanghalian' = lunch. 'Tanghali na!' = it is late in the morning already (you overslept).

examples.tl: Tanghali na, gising na!
examples.en: It is noon already, wake up!

examples.tl: Sobrang init sa labas pag tanghali.
examples.en: It is so hot outside at midday.

notes.notes: From 'hati' (half) + 'gabi'. Many say 'twelve midnight' or 'alas-dose ng gabi'.

examples.tl: Hatinggabi na nakauwi ang kapatid ko galing sa party.
examples.en: My sibling got home from the party at midnight.

notes.notes: Roughly 1 to 5 AM. 'Alas-tres ng madaling-araw' = 3 AM.

examples.tl: Alas-kwatro ng madaling-araw ang flight ko, kaya Grab na lang.
examples.en: My flight is at four in the morning, so I'll just take a Grab.

notes.notes: 'Alas-dose ng tanghali' = noon; 'alas-dose ng gabi' or 'hatinggabi' = midnight.

examples.tl: Alas-dose ng tanghali ang lunch break namin.
examples.en: Our lunch break is at twelve noon.

notes.notes: 'Mga' before a time or number = approximately: 'mga alas-sais', 'mga bente tao'. Very common when setting meetups.

examples.tl: Mga alas-siyete ako makakarating, traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: I'll arrive around seven, there is traffic on EDSA.
examples.taglish: Mga alas-siyete ako, traffic sa EDSA eh.

notes.notes: 'Bago mag-alas-otso' = before 8 o'clock; 'bago mag-Pasko' = before Christmas; 'bago mag-umaga' = before morning.

examples.tl: Umuwi ka bago mag-alas-diyes, may curfew sa condo.
examples.en: Come home before ten, the condo has a curfew.

notes.notes: Taglish often uses 'minutes': 'five minutes lang'. Tagalog number + 'minuto': limang minuto.

examples.tl: Limang minuto na lang, nasa Buendia na ako.
examples.en: Just five more minutes, I'm on Buendia already.

examples.tl: Ilang segundo lang, mag-lo-load pa ang GCash.
examples.en: Just a few seconds, GCash is still loading.

examples.tl: Kalahating oras ang biyahe pag walang traffic, pero bihira 'yon.
examples.en: The trip is half an hour without traffic, but that's rare.

notes.notes: Short way to ask what time the plan is. Answer: 'Mga alas-sais?' Follow with 'Saan tayo?' (where?).

examples.tl: Anong oras tayo bukas? Saan tayo magkikita?
examples.en: What time are we tomorrow? Where do we meet?
examples.taglish: Anong oras tayo bukas? Sa Greenbelt na lang?

notes.notes: From 'dalawa' (two): two days ago. Compare 'sa makalawa' = the day after tomorrow.

examples.tl: Kamakalawa pa ako nag-order, wala pa rin ang package.
examples.en: I ordered the day before yesterday and the package still isn't here.

notes.notes: 'Sa' marks future time: sa Lunes, sa susunod na linggo, sa makalawa.

examples.tl: Sa makalawa ang kaarawan ni Mama, bili tayo ng cake.
examples.en: Mom's birthday is the day after tomorrow, let's buy a cake.

examples.tl: Paminsan-minsan lang ako umiinom, pag may okasyon.
examples.en: I only drink once in a while, when there's an occasion.

notes.notes: Formal/literary. In speech people say 'hindi... kahit kailan' or just 'never' in Taglish: 'never akong na-late'.

examples.tl: Hindi kailanman ako sumakay sa MRT pag rush hour.
examples.en: I never ride the MRT during rush hour.
examples.taglish: Never akong sumakay ng MRT pag rush hour.

notes.notes: With 'hindi' = never: 'Hindi ako kahit kailan nag-bike sa EDSA.' Alone = whenever you like.

examples.tl: Kahit kailan ka pwedeng dumalaw, open lagi ang bahay.
examples.en: You can visit anytime, the house is always open.

notes.taglish: Wait lang, loading pa.
notes.notes: Pure Taglish and extremely common in texting and speech. 'Wait lang ha' softens it.

examples.tl: Wait lang, pinapa-load ko pa ang GCash ko.
examples.en: Hang on, I'm still topping up my GCash.

notes.notes: 'Maaga pa' = it's still early. 'Nang maaga' = early (adverb). 'Maagang-maaga' = very early.

examples.tl: Maaga pa, alas-singko pa lang.
examples.en: It's still early, it's only five.

examples.tl: Umalis ako nang maaga para iwas traffic.
examples.en: I left early to avoid traffic.

examples.tl: Maaga akong umalis para hindi ma-late.
examples.en: I left early so I wouldn't be late.
examples.taglish: Maaga akong umalis, 6 AM, para hindi ma-late sa flight.

notes.taglish: Maaga tayo umalis, 4 AM, iwas traffic.
Na-late ako kasi traffic.
notes.notes: Everyday Manila speech uses English 'late': 'na-late ako', 'late na'. Tagalog 'nahuli ako' is understood but less common for lateness.

examples.tl: Sorry, na-late ako, sobrang traffic sa Ayala.
examples.en: Sorry I'm late, traffic on Ayala was terrible.

examples.tl: Late na, tulog na tayo.
examples.en: It's late, let's sleep.

notes.notes: 'Huling biyahe' = last trip; 'sa huli' = in the end; 'nahuli' = was late or was caught. 'Last' is also used in Taglish.

examples.tl: Anong oras ang huling biyahe ng MRT?
examples.en: What time is the last MRT trip?

examples.tl: Nahuli ako sa meeting kasi bumaha.
examples.en: I was late to the meeting because it flooded.

examples.tl: Huling biyahe ng MRT ay alas-diyes.
examples.en: The last MRT trip is at ten.
examples.taglish: Last trip ng MRT 10 PM, bilisan natin.

notes.taglish: Huling biyahe na ito, sakay na!
On time ba 'yung flight?
notes.notes: English 'on time' is the normal spoken form. Formal Tagalog 'nasa oras' appears mostly in writing.

examples.tl: Bihirang on time ang bus, kaya maaga ako umaalis.
examples.en: The bus is rarely on time, so I leave early.

notes.notes: 'Linggo' = week AND Sunday (capitalized). 'Isang linggo' = one week; 'ngayong linggo' = this week.

examples.tl: Isang linggo na akong hindi nag-gym.
examples.en: I haven't gone to the gym in a week.

notes.notes: 'Buwanan' = monthly; 'kada buwan' = every month; 'katapusan ng buwan' = end of the month.

examples.tl: Dalawang buwan na akong hindi nakakauwi sa probinsya.
examples.en: I haven't been home to the province in two months.

notes.notes: 'Ilang taon ka na?' = how old are you? Answer with Spanish numbers: 'trenta y dos'. 'Taun-taon' = every year.

examples.tl: Ilang taon ka na? Trenta?
examples.en: How old are you? Thirty?

examples.tl: Dalawang taon na ako dito sa Pilipinas.
examples.en: I've been here in the Philippines for two years.

notes.notes: Same word for day and sun. 'Araw-araw' = every day; 'buong araw' = all day; 'maaraw' = sunny.

examples.tl: Tatlong araw ang holiday, uuwi ako sa probinsya.
examples.en: The holiday is three days, I'll go home to the province.

examples.tl: Ang tirik ng araw, bitbit ka ng payong.
examples.en: The sun is blazing, bring an umbrella.

notes.notes: 'Magandang umaga' = good morning. 'Kaninang umaga' = this morning; 'bukas ng umaga' = tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: Bukas ng umaga ako mag-grocery, mas kaunti ang tao.
examples.en: I'll do groceries tomorrow morning, there are fewer people.

notes.notes: 'Magandang hapon' = good afternoon. Note 'Hapon' with capital H = Japanese.

examples.tl: Umuulan lagi sa hapon pag tag-ulan.
examples.en: It always rains in the afternoon during rainy season.

notes.notes: 'Magandang gabi' = good evening. 'Gabi na' = it's late at night. 'Buong gabi' = all night.

examples.tl: Gabi na, mag-Grab ka na lang pauwi.
examples.en: It's late, just take a Grab home.

notes.taglish: Anong plano mo sa weekend?
notes.notes: English 'weekend' is what people say; 'Sabado at Linggo' is the Tagalog alternative. 'Long weekend' is also used as is.

examples.tl: Sa weekend tayo mag-Tagaytay, long weekend naman.
examples.en: Let's go to Tagaytay on the weekend, it's a long weekend anyway.

notes.notes: 'Sa susunod na' + unit = next: sa susunod na buwan, sa susunod na taon. 'Sa susunod' alone = next time.

examples.tl: Sa susunod na linggo ang move-in ko sa condo.
examples.en: My condo move-in is next week.

notes.notes: Used alone to mean 'next time' or 'in the future'. 'Sa susunod, mag-Grab na lang tayo.'

examples.tl: Sa susunod, mag-book tayo nang maaga para mas mura.
examples.en: Next time, let's book early so it's cheaper.

notes.notes: 'Noong nakaraang' + unit = last: noong nakaraang linggo, noong nakaraang taon. Spoken often shortened to 'last month'.

examples.tl: Noong nakaraang buwan, tumaas ang bill ng Meralco.
examples.en: Last month, the Meralco bill went up.

notes.notes: 'Kada' (from Spanish cada) = per/every: kada buwan, kada oras, kada tao. Common for rates and prices.

examples.tl: Singkwenta kada araw ang parking sa office.
examples.en: Parking at the office is fifty per day.

examples.tl: Linggo-linggo kaming nag-badminton sa BGC.
examples.en: We play badminton in BGC every week.

notes.notes: 'Mula alas-otso hanggang alas-singko' = from 8 to 5. 'Mula noon' = since then. Also 'galing' for 'from (a place)'.

examples.tl: Mula Lunes hanggang Biyernes ang pasok ko.
examples.en: I work from Monday to Friday.

notes.notes: 'Simula bukas' = starting tomorrow; 'sa simula' = at the start; 'magsimula' = to begin.

examples.tl: Simula bukas, diet na ako. Promise.
examples.en: Starting tomorrow, I'm on a diet. Promise.

notes.en: a long time; slow to happen
notes.notes: 'Matagal na' = it's been a long time. 'Ang tagal!' = this is taking forever! 'Matagal pa' = not for a while yet.

examples.tl: Ang tagal ng Grab, bente minutes na akong naghihintay.
examples.en: The Grab is taking forever, I've been waiting twenty minutes.

examples.tl: Matagal na kaming magkaibigan.
examples.en: We've been friends a long time.

examples.tl: Sa ngayon, okay pa ang budget ko.
examples.en: For now, my budget is still okay.

notes.notes: Days are Spanish-derived. 'Sa Lunes' = on (this coming) Monday; 'noong Lunes' = last Monday; 'tuwing Lunes' = every Monday.

examples.tl: Ayoko ng Lunes, sobrang traffic.
examples.en: I hate Mondays, so much traffic.

examples.tl: Sa Martes ang appointment ko sa dentista.
examples.en: My dentist appointment is on Tuesday.

examples.tl: Miyerkules na, kalagitnaan na ng linggo.
examples.en: It's Wednesday already, midweek.

examples.tl: Huwebes ang payday namin ngayong buwan.
examples.en: Our payday is on Thursday this month.

notes.notes: 'Biyernes Santo' = Good Friday, when almost everything closes.

examples.tl: Biyernes na! Inom tayo sa Poblacion mamaya.
examples.en: It's Friday! Let's drink in Poblacion later.

examples.tl: Sabado ng umaga ako nagpapalaba.
examples.en: I have my laundry done Saturday morning.

notes.notes: Capital L = Sunday; lowercase 'linggo' = week. 'Sabado't Linggo' = the weekend.

examples.tl: Linggo ngayon, sarado ang bangko.
examples.en: It's Sunday today, the bank is closed.

notes.notes: Months are Spanish-derived, but in Taglish most people say the English month names. Tagalog months appear on forms and in formal speech.

examples.tl: Malamig sa Baguio pag Enero.
examples.en: It's cold in Baguio in January.

examples.tl: Sa Pebrero ang Valentine's, mahal ang bulaklak.
examples.en: Valentine's is in February, flowers are expensive.

examples.tl: Nagsisimula ang tag-init sa Marso.
examples.en: The hot season starts in March.

examples.tl: Sobrang init sa Manila pag Abril.
examples.en: Manila is extremely hot in April.

notes.notes: Mayo = May (also the brand of mayonnaise, context tells).

examples.tl: Maraming piyesta sa probinsya tuwing Mayo.
examples.en: There are many fiestas in the provinces every May.

examples.tl: Hunyo na, simula na ng tag-ulan.
examples.en: It's June, the rainy season is starting.

examples.tl: Noong Hulyo, tatlong bagyo ang dumaan.
examples.en: Last July, three typhoons passed through.

notes.notes: Agosto = Buwan ng Wika (National Language Month) in schools.

examples.tl: Agosto ang Buwan ng Wika sa mga eskwelahan.
examples.en: August is National Language Month in schools.

notes.notes: The 'ber months' (September to December) are the Christmas season in the Philippines.

examples.tl: Setyembre na, may Christmas songs na sa mall.
examples.en: It's September, there are Christmas songs in the mall already.

examples.tl: Oktubre ang kaarawan ko, sa a-kinse.
examples.en: My birthday is in October, on the 15th.

notes.notes: Nov 1 = Undas (All Saints' Day); traffic out of Manila is heavy.

examples.tl: Sa Nobyembre ang Undas, uuwi kami sa probinsya.
examples.en: Undas is in November, we'll go home to the province.

examples.tl: Disyembre na, Pasko na naman!
examples.en: It's December, it's Christmas again!

notes.notes: Answer: 'A-onse ng Oktubre' or just 'October 11'. Also 'Anong araw ngayon?' = what day is it?

examples.tl: Anong petsa ngayon? Baka due na ang Meralco.
examples.en: What's the date today? The Meralco bill might be due.

notes.notes: 'Kumusta ang panahon?' = how's the weather? 'Sa panahon ngayon' = these days. 'Panahon ko' = my time/era.

examples.tl: Ang gulo ng panahon, mainit tapos biglang uulan.
examples.en: The weather is crazy, hot then suddenly it rains.

notes.notes: March to May. People also say 'summer'. 'Tag-araw' is the dry season in general.

examples.tl: Pag tag-init, sobrang taas ng bill sa aircon.
examples.en: In the hot season, the aircon bill is sky high.

notes.notes: June to about November; typhoons and floods. 'Tag-' prefix = season of.

examples.tl: Tag-ulan na, dala ka lagi ng payong at extra tsinelas.
examples.en: It's rainy season, always bring an umbrella and spare slippers.

notes.notes: December to February, when Manila drops to the low 20s C and people wear jackets. Also used for winter abroad.

examples.tl: Tag-lamig na, 22 degrees sa Manila, jacket weather!
examples.en: It's the cold season, 22 degrees in Manila, jacket weather!

notes.notes: Noun. Verb forms: umulan (rained), umuulan (raining), uulan (will rain). 'Malakas ang ulan' = heavy rain.

examples.tl: Ang lakas ng ulan, walang Grab na tumatanggap.
examples.en: The rain is heavy, no Grab driver is accepting.

examples.tl: Umuulan nang malakas, baha na sa Espana.
examples.en: It's raining hard, Espana is flooded already.
examples.taglish: Malakas ang ulan, baha na sa Espana, wag ka dumaan doon.

examples.tl: Magdala ka ng payong, mukhang uulan.
examples.en: Bring an umbrella, it looks like rain.

notes.taglish: Umuulan sa Makati, delayed ang Grab.

notes.notes: Incompleted aspect of 'umulan'. 'Uulan ba mamaya?' = will it rain later? 'Umulan kanina' = it rained earlier.

examples.tl: Umuulan ba sa inyo? Dito sa Makati malakas.
examples.en: Is it raining where you are? Here in Makati it's heavy.

notes.notes: 'Na' marks that the rain just started. What people shout before grabbing the laundry off the line.

examples.tl: Umuulan na! Dalian mo, kunin mo ang sinampay!
examples.en: It's raining! Hurry, get the laundry!

notes.notes: From 'araw' (sun). 'Matirik ang araw' = the sun is blazing.

examples.tl: Maaraw ngayon, pwede nang magpatuyo ng labada.
examples.en: It's sunny today, the laundry can dry.

notes.notes: Opposite: 'Naiinitan ako' = I feel hot. Common complaint in over-aircon'd offices and buses.

examples.tl: Nilalamig ako sa office, sobrang lakas ng aircon.
examples.en: I'm cold at the office, the aircon is too strong.

notes.notes: 'Malakas ang hangin' = the wind is strong. Also 'hangin' = air, and slang 'hangin' = full of hot air.

examples.tl: Malakas ang hangin, baka may bagyong paparating.
examples.en: The wind is strong, maybe a typhoon is coming.

examples.tl: Mahangin sa Baywalk sa gabi, presko.
examples.en: It's windy at Baywalk at night, refreshing.

notes.notes: Typhoons get local names (Ondoy, Yolanda, Carina). 'May bagyo' = there's a typhoon. 'Signal no. 1-5' are PAGASA warning levels.

examples.tl: May bagyo daw sa Linggo, mag-stock na tayo ng tubig.
examples.en: They say there's a typhoon on Sunday, let's stock up on water.

examples.tl: May paparating na bagyo sa Biyernes.
examples.en: There's a typhoon coming on Friday.
examples.taglish: May paparating na bagyo sa Friday, Signal No. 2 sa Manila.

examples.tl: Na-cancel ang biyahe ng bangka dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: The boat trips were cancelled because of the typhoon.

notes.taglish: May bagyo, cancelled ang flight namin.
Signal no. 2 na sa Metro Manila, walang pasok.
notes.notes: PAGASA wind signals 1 to 5. Signal 2 or 3 in Metro Manila usually means classes and government work are suspended.

examples.tl: Signal no. 2 na sa Maynila, suspended na ang klase.
examples.en: Signal number 2 in Manila now, classes are suspended.

notes.notes: 'Pasok' = going in (to work or school). Announced during typhoons and holidays. 'May pasok ba bukas?' = is there work/school tomorrow?

examples.tl: Walang pasok bukas, signal no. 3!
examples.en: No work or school tomorrow, signal number 3!
examples.taglish: Walang pasok bukas, yes! Netflix all day.

examples.tl: Walang pasok sa Makati bukas dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: No school or work in Makati tomorrow because of the typhoon.
examples.taglish: Walang pasok sa Makati bukas, announced na sa Facebook ng city.

examples.tl: May pasok ba kayo o walang pasok?
examples.en: Do you have work today or is it suspended?

notes.taglish: Walang pasok bukas, suspended dahil sa bagyo.

notes.notes: 'Bumaha' = it flooded; 'binaha' = got flooded; 'baha sa España' = España is flooded. 'Hanggang tuhod' = knee-deep.

examples.tl: Baha na sa Taft, hanggang tuhod daw.
examples.en: Taft is flooded, knee-deep they say.

examples.tl: Baha na sa kalye namin, hanggang tuhod.
examples.en: Our street is flooded, knee-deep.
examples.taglish: Baha na sa street namin, hanggang tuhod, stuck ako sa condo.

examples.tl: Hindi dumaan ang bus dahil sa baha.
examples.en: The bus didn't come through because of the flood.

notes.taglish: Baha sa Taft, hindi dumadaan ang jeep.

notes.notes: From 'ulap' (cloud). 'Makulimlim' = gloomy/overcast, more literary.

examples.tl: Maulap ngayon, mukhang uulan mamaya.
examples.en: It's cloudy today, looks like it'll rain later.

notes.notes: 'Umaambon' = it's drizzling. 'Ambon lang' = just a drizzle, no need for an umbrella.

examples.tl: Ambon lang, kaya pa maglakad hanggang MRT.
examples.en: It's just a drizzle, we can still walk to the MRT.

examples.tl: Umaambon lang, hindi na kailangan ng payong.
examples.en: It's just drizzling, no need for an umbrella.
examples.taglish: Umaambon lang, okay lang, lakad lang tayo.

examples.tl: Nag-ambon kanina, kaya madulas ang daan.
examples.en: It drizzled earlier, so the road is slippery.

notes.taglish: Umaambon lang, kaya pa maglakad.

notes.notes: Stress matters: ba-SA = wet; BA-sa = read. 'Nabasa ako' = I got wet. 'Basang-basa' = soaking wet.

examples.tl: Basang-basa ako, nahuli ako ng ulan sa labas ng MRT.
examples.en: I'm soaking wet, I got caught in the rain outside the MRT.

examples.tl: Basa ang upuan sa jeep, umulan kanina.
examples.en: The jeep seat is wet, it rained earlier.
examples.taglish: Basa yung upuan sa jeep, umulan kanina, lagyan mo ng tissue.

examples.tl: Nabasa ang sapatos ko sa baha.
examples.en: My shoes got wet in the flood.

notes.taglish: Basang-basa ako, naabutan ng ulan.

notes.notes: Stress matters: tu-YO = dry; TU-yo = dried fish (breakfast staple). 'Tuyo na ang labada' = the laundry is dry.

examples.tl: Tuyo na ba ang damit? Isusuot ko mamaya.
examples.en: Are the clothes dry yet? I'll wear them later.

notes.taglish: Sobrang humid ngayon, nakakapagod.
notes.notes: The sticky heat before a storm. Many just say 'humid' or 'sobrang init'. 'Alinsangan' = humidity.

examples.tl: Maalinsangan ngayon, parang uulan mamaya.
examples.en: It's muggy today, feels like it'll rain later.

notes.notes: 'Kidlat' = lightning. 'Kumukulog' = it's thundering. 'Kulog at kidlat' = thunder and lightning.

examples.tl: Ang lakas ng kulog, natakot ang aso.
examples.en: The thunder is so loud, the dog got scared.

notes.notes: 'Kumikidlat' = there's lightning. Also slang for someone very fast.

examples.tl: May kidlat, wag ka munang mag-swimming.
examples.en: There's lightning, don't go swimming yet.

notes.notes: 'Lumindol' = there was an earthquake. 'Nilindol ba kayo?' = did you feel the quake? Phivolcs reports intensity.

examples.tl: Lumindol kanina! Naramdaman mo ba sa condo?
examples.en: There was an earthquake earlier! Did you feel it in the condo?

notes.notes: Useful shopping and Grab-spotting question. Answer with the color word alone: 'Itim.'

examples.tl: Anong kulay ang gusto mo, itim o puti?
examples.en: What color do you want, black or white?

notes.notes: 'Mapula' = reddish. Red taxis and red jeeps are common sights.

examples.tl: Pulang jeep ang sakyan mo, 'yung may sign na Guadalupe.
examples.en: Take the red jeep, the one with the Guadalupe sign.

notes.notes: 'Maputi' = fair-skinned, often used as a compliment. 'Puting damit' = white clothes.

examples.tl: Puting Vios ang Grab, plate na nagtatapos sa 88.
examples.en: The Grab is a white Vios, plate ending in 88.

notes.notes: 'Maitim' = dark-skinned. 'Itim na kape' = black coffee.

examples.tl: Itim na lang ang bibilhin ko, hindi madumi.
examples.en: I'll just buy black, it doesn't look dirty.

notes.notes: 'Blue' is said just as often. 'Bughaw' is the purist word, rarely spoken.

examples.tl: Asul ang uniform ng guard sa condo namin.
examples.en: The guards' uniform at our condo is blue.

notes.notes: 'Green' is equally common. 'Berdeng biro' = a dirty joke. 'Luntian' is literary.

examples.tl: Pag berde na ang ilaw, tumawid ka na.
examples.en: When the light is green, cross.

notes.notes: Yellow taxis in Manila are the airport taxis (more expensive). 'Dilaw' also has political connotations (Aquino party).

examples.tl: Wag ka sumakay sa dilaw na taxi, mas mahal 'yon.
examples.en: Don't take the yellow taxi, that one is more expensive.

notes.notes: Almost everyone says 'orange'. 'Kahel' is the textbook word; you'll see it on forms and in school.

examples.tl: Orange ang shirt ng rider, 'yung Shopee delivery.
examples.en: The rider's shirt is orange, the Shopee delivery one.

notes.notes: 'Violet' is the common spoken word. 'Ube' (purple yam) is used to describe that shade too.

examples.tl: Violet ang paborito niyang kulay, kaya ube lahat ng gamit niya.
examples.en: Violet is her favorite color, so all her stuff is ube-colored.

notes.notes: 'Rosas' = pink and also the rose flower. 'Pink' is more common in speech. 'Kulay rosas' = pink-colored.

examples.tl: Pink ang helmet ng Angkas rider ko kanina.
examples.en: My Angkas rider's helmet earlier was pink.

notes.notes: Mostly used for skin tone with pride ('kayumangging Pilipino'). For objects people say 'brown'.

examples.tl: Kayumanggi ang kutis ng Pilipino, ipagmalaki mo.
examples.en: Filipinos have brown skin, be proud of it.

notes.notes: English 'gray' is what people say; 'abo' means ash, so 'kulay-abo' = ash-colored.

examples.tl: Gray ang building namin, 'yung katabi ng 7-Eleven.
examples.en: Our building is gray, the one next to 7-Eleven.

notes.notes: For lighting and shades: 'madilim na kulay' = dark color; 'madilim na' = it's dark already (evening).

examples.tl: Madilim na, umuwi na tayo.
examples.en: It's dark already, let's go home.

examples.tl: Madilim ang daan, walang ilaw sa kalye.
examples.en: The road is dark, there are no streetlights.
examples.taglish: Madilim ang daan, walang streetlight, mag-Grab ka na lang.

examples.tl: Umuwi ka na, madilim na.
examples.en: Go home now, it's getting dark.

notes.taglish: Madilim ang eskinita, dumaan ka sa main road.

notes.notes: Lighting, and also 'clear' as in 'maliwanag ba?' = is that clear/understood?

examples.tl: Maliwanag pa, pwede pa tayong mag-jogging sa Ayala Triangle.
examples.en: It's still bright, we can still jog at Ayala Triangle.

notes.notes: 'Sapat na' = that's enough. In speech 'enough na' or 'okay na' is also common. Opposite: 'kulang'.

examples.tl: Sapat na ang isang libo para sa grocery ng isang linggo? Hindi na, mahal na lahat.
examples.en: Is a thousand enough for a week's groceries? Not anymore, everything's expensive.

notes.notes: Literally 'has no contents'. 'Walang laman ang ref' = the fridge is empty. 'Walang laman ang GCash ko' = my GCash is empty.

examples.tl: Walang laman ang GCash ko, pa-load muna ako sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: My GCash is empty, I'll top up at 7-Eleven first.

notes.notes: Model for number + linker + unit: tatlong kilo, limang kilo, kalahating kilo.

examples.tl: Dalawang kilo ng bigas, tapos isang supot ng sibuyas.
examples.en: Two kilos of rice, then one bag of onions.

notes.notes: 'Dalawang daang gramo' = 200 grams; in practice people say 'two hundred grams' or 'quarter kilo' (kapat).

examples.tl: Dalawang daang gramo lang ng keso, para sa isang tao lang.
examples.en: Just 200 grams of cheese, it's just for one person.

notes.notes: Gas and water: 'isang litro', 'limang litro ng tubig' (the refill jug). Taglish 'liter' also fine.

examples.tl: Tumaas ulit ang gasolina, singkwenta y singko kada litro.
examples.en: Gas went up again, fifty-five per liter.

notes.notes: Also 'metro' = taxi meter ('metro lang, kuya' = use the meter). 'Limang metro' = five meters.

examples.tl: Metro lang, kuya, wag fixed price.
examples.en: Just use the meter, kuya, no fixed price.

examples.tl: Mga sampung metro lang ang layo ng 7-Eleven sa gate.
examples.en: The 7-Eleven is only about ten meters from the gate.

notes.notes: Taglish often 'kilometers' or 'km'. 'Ilang kilometro?' = how many kilometers?

examples.tl: Limang kilometro lang pero isang oras ang biyahe dahil sa traffic.
examples.en: Only five kilometers but the trip takes an hour because of traffic.

notes.notes: Counter for items sold individually: 'limang piraso ng pandesal'. Also 'pira-piraso' = in pieces. Taglish 'pieces' is common too.

examples.tl: Tatlong piraso ng siopao, ate, asado.
examples.en: Three pieces of siopao, ate, asado.

notes.notes: 'Isa lang' also works. 'Tig-isang piraso' = one piece each.

examples.tl: Isang piraso lang ng mangga, pang-isahan lang.
examples.en: Just one piece of mango, it's just for one person.

notes.taglish: Isang pack ng Marlboro at isang Coke.
notes.notes: English 'pack' is the everyday word at sari-sari stores and groceries; 'pakete' is the Tagalog form, less used.

examples.tl: Dalawang pack ng pancit canton, 'yung extra hot.
examples.en: Two packs of pancit canton, the extra hot one.

notes.notes: 'Isang bote ng tubig'. 'Bote-bote' = bottle after bottle. Bottle deposits are a thing: 'ibalik ang bote'.

examples.tl: Isang bote ng malamig na tubig, please.
examples.en: One bottle of cold water, please.

examples.tl: Ilang bote ng Red Horse ang inubos niyo kagabi?
examples.en: How many bottles of Red Horse did you finish last night?

notes.notes: 'De-lata' = canned goods (corned beef, sardines). 'Isang lata ng Coke'.

examples.tl: Mag-stock tayo ng de-lata, baka bumaha ulit.
examples.en: Let's stock up on canned goods, it might flood again.

notes.notes: 'Supot' = the small plastic or paper bag from a store or palengke. 'Pa-supot' = please bag it. 'Bag' for handbags.

examples.tl: Pa-supot po, ate, wala akong eco bag.
examples.en: Please bag it, ate, I don't have an eco bag.

examples.tl: Isang supot ng sibuyas at isang supot ng bawang.
examples.en: One bag of onions and one bag of garlic.

notes.notes: Palengke vendors sell tomatoes, chilies, kalamansi by the 'tumpok' at a fixed price: 'bente isang tumpok'.

examples.tl: Magkano isang tumpok ng kamatis? Bente? Sige, dalawang tumpok.
examples.en: How much for a pile of tomatoes? Twenty? Okay, two piles.

notes.notes: Prefix for 'each/apiece': tig-bente = twenty each, tig-isa = one each, tig-dalawa = two each. 'Tig-isa tayo' = one each.

examples.tl: Tig-bente ang siomai, tatlo para singkwenta.
examples.en: Siomai are twenty each, three for fifty.

examples.tl: Tig-isa na lang tayo ng beer, may pasok bukas.
examples.en: Let's just have one beer each, there's work tomorrow.

notes.notes: 'Bawat isa' = each one; 'bawat tao' = every person. 'Kada' is the casual equivalent for rates.

examples.tl: Bawat isa may dalang ulam, potluck tayo.
examples.en: Each one brings a dish, let's potluck.

notes.notes: 'Buong araw' = all day; 'buong linggo' = the whole week; 'buong manok' = a whole chicken. 'Buo pa' = still intact.

examples.tl: Buong araw akong nasa bahay dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: I was home all day because of the typhoon.

examples.tl: Isang buong manok, 'yung inihaw.
examples.en: One whole chicken, the roasted one.

notes.notes: Root of 'marami'. 'Ang dami!' = so many! 'Gaano kadami?' = how many/how much? 'Dami mo namang satsat' = you talk so much.

examples.tl: Ang dami ng tao sa Divisoria, Pasko na nga.
examples.en: There are so many people in Divisoria, it's Christmas season after all.

notes.notes: The everyday intensifier: sobrang init, sobrang mahal, sobrang late. Also 'super' in Taglish: 'super traffic'.

examples.tl: Sobrang init ngayon, 38 degrees daw.
examples.en: It's extremely hot today, 38 degrees they say.

examples.tl: Sobrang mahal ng renta sa BGC.
examples.en: Rent in BGC is super expensive.

notes.notes: Prefix intensifier: napakainit, napakamahal, napakatagal. Slightly more emphatic/formal than 'sobrang'; both are common.

examples.tl: Napakatagal ng pila sa NAIA immigration kanina.
examples.en: The line at NAIA immigration earlier was extremely long.

notes.notes: From Spanish 'veces'. 'Ilang beses?' = how many times? 'Dalawang beses' = twice; 'unang beses' = first time; 'minsan' = once.

examples.tl: Tatlong beses na akong nag-Palawan, hindi pa ako nagsasawa.
examples.en: I've been to Palawan three times and I'm not tired of it yet.

examples.tl: Ilang beses ka kumakain sa labas kada linggo?
examples.en: How many times do you eat out per week?

notes.notes: Short follow-up question, typically about traffic, rain, or prices. Answer: 'Oo, lagi' or 'Minsan lang'.

examples.tl: Ganito ba lagi ang traffic sa EDSA? Oo, lalo na pag Biyernes.
examples.en: Is EDSA traffic always like this? Yes, especially on Fridays.

notes.taglish: Mag-jeep lang tayo.
notes.notes: Spelled 'jeep' in texts. Verb: mag-jeep / sumakay ng jeep. Modern e-jeeps are still 'jeep'.

examples.tl: Sumakay ako ng dyip papuntang Guadalupe.
examples.en: I took a jeep to Guadalupe.
examples.taglish: Nag-jeep lang ako papuntang Guadalupe, mura lang.

examples.tl: Dadaan ba ang dyip na ito sa Ayala?
examples.en: Does this jeep pass by Ayala?

notes.taglish: Mag-trike na lang tayo.
notes.notes: Motorcycle with sidecar; short hops inside barangays. 'Trike' is the common text form.

examples.tl: Walang traysikel sa Ayala, bawal daw.
examples.en: There are no tricycles on Ayala, they're banned.
examples.taglish: Walang trike sa Ayala, bawal daw doon.

examples.tl: Magkano ang traysikel papunta sa palengke?
examples.en: How much is the tricycle to the market?

notes.taglish: Mag-bus ako sa EDSA.
notes.notes: Verb: mag-bus. EDSA Carousel = the busway along EDSA. Provincial buses leave from terminals in Cubao/Pasay/PITX.

examples.tl: Nag-bus ako mula Cubao hanggang Ayala.
examples.en: I took a bus from Cubao to Ayala.
examples.taglish: Nag-bus lang ako, EDSA Carousel, mabilis naman.

examples.tl: Saan ang sakayan ng bus papuntang Baguio?
examples.en: Where do you catch the bus to Baguio?

notes.taglish: Mag-MRT ka, mas mabilis kesa EDSA.
notes.notes: MRT-3 runs along EDSA; LRT-1 and LRT-2 are the other lines. Verb: mag-MRT / mag-LRT. Formal word 'tren' is rare in Manila.

examples.tl: Mag-MRT na lang tayo, traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: Let's just take the MRT, EDSA is jammed.
examples.taglish: Mag-MRT na lang tayo, grabe ang traffic sa EDSA.

examples.tl: Bumaba ka sa Ayala station tapos maglakad ka.
examples.en: Get off at Ayala station then walk.

notes.taglish: Mag-taxi na lang ako.
notes.notes: Usually spelled 'taxi' in texts. Ask 'Metro po ba?' to make sure the meter is on.

examples.tl: Mag-taksi na lang tayo, gabi na.
examples.en: Let's just take a taxi, it's late.
examples.taglish: Mag-taxi na lang tayo, gabi na, wala nang jeep.

examples.tl: Kuya, metro po ba?
examples.en: Sir, is the meter on?

notes.taglish: Mag-Grab na lang ako.
notes.notes: Verb: mag-Grab. Also GrabFood for delivery. People say 'Grab' for the car and the app.

examples.tl: Nag-Grab ako kasi umuulan.
examples.en: I took a Grab because it was raining.
examples.taglish: Nag-Grab na lang ako kasi umuulan, ang hirap mag-jeep.

examples.tl: Ang mahal ng Grab ngayon, surge.
examples.en: Grab is expensive right now, surge pricing.

notes.taglish: Mag-Angkas ako, mas mabilis sa traffic.
notes.notes: Brand name from 'angkas' = to ride pillion / hitch a ride. 'Pa-angkas' = can I ride with you. JoyRide and Move It are similar.

examples.tl: Nag-Angkas ako para hindi ma-late.
examples.en: I took an Angkas so I wouldn't be late.
examples.taglish: Nag-Angkas na lang ako, mas mabilis sa traffic.

examples.tl: Pa-angkas naman hanggang kanto.
examples.en: Can I hitch a ride to the corner?

notes.notes: Informal unregistered motorcycle taxi, more common in provinces; in Manila people mostly say Angkas or 'motor'.

examples.tl: Sa probinsya, habal-habal ang sakay namin papunta sa falls.
examples.en: In the province we rode a habal-habal to the falls.
examples.taglish: Sa Siargao, habal-habal lang ang sakay papunta sa beach.

notes.taglish: Para po, sa tabi lang!
notes.notes: From Spanish 'parar'. Shout it when you want the jeep to pull over. Add 'po' to be polite.

examples.tl: Para po! Sa kanto lang.
examples.en: Stop please! Just at the corner.
examples.taglish: Para po, sa kanto lang, salamat!

examples.tl: Hindi narinig ni manong ang para ko.
examples.en: The driver didn't hear me say stop.

notes.taglish: Kuya, sa tabi lang po, dito na ako.
notes.notes: 'Tabi' = side. Standard way to tell a Grab or taxi driver where to let you off.

examples.tl: Sa tabi lang po, pagkatapos ng 7-Eleven.
examples.en: Just pull over, right after the 7-Eleven.
examples.taglish: Kuya, sa tabi lang po after ng 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: Sa tabi lang po, bababa na ako.
examples.en: Just on the side please, I'm getting off.

notes.taglish: Sa kanto lang po, Kuya.
notes.notes: 'Kanto' = street corner / intersection. Common drop-off point for jeeps and trikes.

examples.tl: Para po, sa kanto lang.
examples.en: Stop please, just at the corner.
examples.taglish: Para po, sa kanto lang, doon sa may Mercury Drug.

examples.tl: Hintayin mo ako sa kanto, bababa na ako.
examples.en: Wait for me at the corner, I'm getting off.

notes.taglish: Diretso lang po, tapos kanan.
notes.notes: Also spelled 'deretso'. Verb: dumiretso = go straight. 'Diretso lang' = just keep going.

examples.tl: Diretso lang po, tapos kaliwa sa ikalawang kanto.
examples.en: Go straight, then left at the second corner.
examples.taglish: Diretso lang po, tapos kaliwa sa second corner.

examples.tl: Diretso ka lang hanggang makita mo ang Shell.
examples.en: Just go straight until you see the Shell station.

notes.taglish: Kanan po sa may Jollibee.
notes.notes: 'Kumanan' = turn right. 'Sa kanan' = on the right.

examples.tl: Kanan po sa susunod na kanto.
examples.en: Right at the next corner please.
examples.taglish: Kanan po sa next corner, tapos diretso lang.

examples.tl: Nasa kanan ang entrance ng building.
examples.en: The building entrance is on the right.

notes.taglish: Kaliwa po pagkatapos ng flyover.
notes.notes: 'Kumaliwa' = turn left. 'Sa kaliwa' = on the left.

examples.tl: Kaliwa po sa may gasolinahan.
examples.en: Left at the gas station please.
examples.taglish: Kaliwa po sa may Petron, tapos sa tabi lang.

examples.tl: Nasa kaliwa ang Starbucks, hindi mo mamimiss.
examples.en: Starbucks is on the left, you can't miss it.

notes.taglish: Liko ka sa may Ministop.
notes.notes: Root liko. 'Liko sa kanan/kaliwa' = turn right/left. 'Likuan' = a turn or bend in the road.

examples.tl: Lumiko ka sa kanan pagkatapos ng tulay.
examples.en: Turn right after the bridge.
examples.taglish: Liko ka sa kanan after ng tulay, tapos diretso.

examples.tl: Huwag kang lumiko dito, one-way yan.
examples.en: Don't turn here, that's one-way.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Takes ng/sa + vehicle. 'Sakay!' = hop in. Opposite: bumaba.

examples.tl: Sumakay kami ng jeep papuntang Guadalupe.
examples.en: We rode a jeep to Guadalupe.

examples.tl: Sumakay kami ng bus sa Cubao.
examples.en: We got on a bus in Cubao.
examples.taglish: Sumakay kami ng bus sa Cubao tapos nag-MRT.

examples.tl: Saan ako sasakay papuntang BGC?
examples.en: Where do I catch a ride to BGC?

notes.taglish: Sakay na, aalis na ang jeep!

notes.en: to go down; to get off
accept: to get off, to go down
notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). On a jeep: 'Bababa ako sa kanto' or just 'Para!' to stop.

examples.tl: Bababa ako sa kanto, ha.
examples.en: I'll get off at the corner, okay?

examples.tl: Bumaba ako sa maling station.
examples.en: I got off at the wrong station.
examples.taglish: Bumaba ako sa maling station, nakakahiya.

examples.tl: Bababa po ako sa kanto.
examples.en: I'll get off at the corner.

notes.taglish: Baba na ako dito.

notes.notes: From Spanish. 'Mga pasahero' = passengers.

examples.tl: Puno na ang jeep, walang nang pwesto para sa pasahero.
examples.en: The jeep is full, no more room for passengers.
examples.taglish: Punuan na, wala nang space para sa pasahero.

examples.tl: Naghihintay ng pasahero ang mga drayber sa terminal.
examples.en: The drivers are waiting for passengers at the terminal.

notes.taglish: Nag-cancel ang driver ko sa Grab.
notes.notes: Spelled 'driver' in texts. Address a driver as 'Manong' or 'Kuya', older ones 'Tatay'.

examples.tl: Mabait ang drayber, hindi nag-overcharge.
examples.en: The driver was nice, he didn't overcharge.
examples.taglish: Mabait ang driver, 5 stars, hindi nag-overcharge.

examples.tl: Tinawagan ako ng drayber, nasa labas na siya.
examples.en: The driver called me, he's already outside.

notes.taglish: Otw, traffic sa EDSA.
notes.notes: Used as noun and adjective: 'traffic sa EDSA', 'ma-traffic'. Default excuse for being late in Manila.

examples.tl: Na-late ako kasi traffic.
examples.en: I was late because of traffic.
examples.taglish: Sorry, na-late ako, grabe ang traffic sa EDSA.

examples.tl: Ma-traffic ba ngayon sa Buendia?
examples.en: Is Buendia jammed right now?

notes.taglish: Siksikan sa MRT pag rush hour.
notes.notes: Root siksik = to cram. Describes a jammed train, jeep, or mall. 'Nakikipagsiksikan' = squeezing in with the crowd.

examples.tl: Siksikan sa MRT tuwing umaga.
examples.en: The MRT is packed every morning.
examples.taglish: Siksikan sa MRT pag umaga, kaya nag-Grab ako.

examples.tl: Ayoko sumakay, siksikan na yan.
examples.en: I don't want to get on, it's already packed.

notes.taglish: Traffic sa EDSA as usual.
notes.notes: Epifanio de los Santos Avenue, the main north-south artery; MRT-3 runs above it. Shorthand for Manila traffic itself.

examples.tl: Dumaan kami sa EDSA, dalawang oras kami sa daan.
examples.en: We went via EDSA, we were on the road two hours.
examples.taglish: Dumaan kami sa EDSA, two hours kami sa daan.

examples.tl: Iwasan mo ang EDSA pag Friday ng gabi.
examples.en: Avoid EDSA on Friday nights.

notes.taglish: Dumaan ka sa flyover para iwas traffic.
notes.notes: Road bridge over an intersection (e.g. Buendia flyover, Magallanes). Not the same as a pedestrian overpass.

examples.tl: Dumaan ka sa flyover, mas mabilis.
examples.en: Take the flyover, it's faster.
examples.taglish: Kuya, dumaan po tayo sa flyover, mas mabilis.

examples.tl: Bumaba ako ng jeep pagkatapos ng flyover.
examples.en: I got off the jeep after the flyover.

notes.taglish: Mag-U-turn ka sa susunod na slot.
notes.notes: 'U-turn slot' = the designated turnaround gap in the median. Verb: mag-U-turn.

examples.tl: Mag-U-turn po tayo sa susunod na slot.
examples.en: Let's U-turn at the next slot.
examples.taglish: Kuya, mag-U-turn po tayo sa next slot, nalampasan natin.

examples.tl: Bawal mag-U-turn dito.
examples.en: No U-turns allowed here.

notes.taglish: Dumaan ka sa overpass, bawal tumawid sa baba.
notes.notes: In Manila 'overpass' usually means the pedestrian footbridge; 'flyover' is for cars. Also 'underpass'.

examples.tl: Dumaan ka sa overpass, delikado tumawid sa EDSA.
examples.en: Use the footbridge, crossing EDSA is dangerous.
examples.taglish: Dumaan ka sa overpass, delikado tumawid sa EDSA.

examples.tl: Magkita tayo sa baba ng overpass.
examples.en: Let's meet at the bottom of the footbridge.

notes.taglish: Tumawid ka sa pedestrian, may pulis diyan.
notes.notes: Often shortened to just 'pedestrian'. The Tagalog 'tawiran' (crossing) is also used.

examples.tl: Tumawid ka sa pedestrian lane, baka mahuli ka.
examples.en: Cross at the crosswalk, you might get caught.
examples.taglish: Tumawid ka sa pedestrian, may MMDA diyan.

examples.tl: Walang pedestrian lane dito, dumaan ka sa overpass.
examples.en: There's no crosswalk here, use the footbridge.

notes.taglish: Tawid ka lang sa kabila, nandoon ang 7-Eleven.
notes.notes: Root tawid. 'Tawiran' = crossing. 'Sa kabila' = across the street.

examples.tl: Tumawid ka sa kabila, nandoon ang bangko.
examples.en: Cross to the other side, the bank is there.
examples.taglish: Tawid ka lang sa kabila, nandoon ang BPI.

examples.tl: Mahirap tumawid dito, walang stoplight.
examples.en: It's hard to cross here, there's no traffic light.

notes.notes: Collects fares and shouts the route on provincial and city buses. Also 'kundoktor'.

examples.tl: Tanungin mo ang konduktor kung dadaan sa Ortigas.
examples.en: Ask the conductor if it passes Ortigas.
examples.taglish: Tanungin mo yung conductor kung dadaan sa Ortigas.

notes.taglish: Nasa terminal na ako, saan ka?
notes.notes: Where jeeps, UV Express vans, and provincial buses load. PITX in Paranaque is the big one for the south.

examples.tl: Saan ang terminal ng van papuntang Antipolo?
examples.en: Where's the van terminal to Antipolo?
examples.taglish: Saan yung terminal ng van papuntang Antipolo?

examples.tl: Puno ang terminal pag Semana Santa.
examples.en: The terminal is packed during Holy Week.

notes.taglish: Bumaba ka sa Buendia station.
notes.notes: People mostly say 'station' in English for MRT/LRT. 'Istasyon ng pulis' = police station.

examples.tl: Aling istasyon ang pinakamalapit sa Greenbelt?
examples.en: Which station is closest to Greenbelt?
examples.taglish: Anong station ang pinakamalapit sa Greenbelt? Ayala?

examples.tl: Mahaba ang pila sa istasyon ngayon.
examples.en: The line at the station is long right now.

notes.taglish: Anong ruta ng jeep na ito?
notes.notes: Jeep routes are painted on the side. 'Byahe' on a jeep sign also means its route.

examples.tl: Anong ruta ng jeep na ito?
examples.en: What route does this jeep take?
examples.taglish: Anong ruta nito? Dadaan ba sa Makati Med?

examples.tl: Nagbago ang ruta dahil sa road closure.
examples.en: The route changed because of a road closure.

notes.taglish: Nag-aabang ako ng jeep, wala pa.
notes.notes: Root abang = to lie in wait / look out for. Used for waiting for a jeep, taxi, or a person to pass by.

examples.tl: Nag-aabang ako ng taxi sa kanto, wala pa.
examples.en: I'm waiting for a taxi at the corner, none yet.
examples.taglish: Nag-aabang ako ng taxi sa kanto, wala pa, 20 minutes na.

examples.tl: Abangan mo ako sa labas ng mall.
examples.en: Watch for me outside the mall.

accept: to drop off, to take someone
notes.notes: Object focus (i-). Roots starting with h take ini- in the completed: inihatid. Hatid-sundo = drop-off and pick-up.

examples.tl: Inihatid niya ako sa NAIA Terminal 3.
examples.en: He dropped me off at NAIA Terminal 3.

examples.tl: Ihahatid kita sa airport bukas.
examples.en: I'll take you to the airport tomorrow.
examples.taglish: Ihahatid kita sa airport bukas, anong oras ang flight mo?

examples.tl: Hinatid ako ng kaibigan ko hanggang bahay.
examples.en: My friend dropped me off at home.

notes.taglish: Ihatid na kita, gabi na.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in); o becomes u: sunduin. For picking up a person (sundo); for things use kunin.

examples.tl: Susunduin kita sa airport bukas.
examples.en: I'll pick you up at the airport tomorrow.

examples.tl: Susunduin kita sa airport mamaya.
examples.en: I'll pick you up at the airport later.
examples.taglish: Susunduin kita sa NAIA mamaya, text mo lang pag landed.

examples.tl: May sundo ka ba, o mag-Grab ka?
examples.en: Is someone picking you up, or will you Grab?

notes.taglish: Susunduin kita sa lobby.
Kuya, dahan-dahan lang po, hindi tayo nagmamadali.
notes.notes: 'Dahan-dahan' = slowly / carefully. Useful with aggressive drivers. Opposite: 'Bilisan po' = hurry.

examples.tl: Kuya, dahan-dahan lang po, madulas ang daan.
examples.en: Sir, slow down please, the road is slippery.
examples.taglish: Kuya, dahan-dahan lang po, madulas, umuulan.

examples.tl: Dahan-dahan ka sa paghila ng maleta, mabigat.
examples.en: Pull the suitcase slowly, it's heavy.

notes.taglish: Dito na lang po, Kuya, lalakad na ako.
notes.notes: Tells a driver to stop where you are, often when traffic makes the last stretch not worth it.

examples.tl: Dito na lang po, maglalakad na lang ako.
examples.en: Here is fine, I'll just walk.
examples.taglish: Dito na lang po, Kuya, traffic, maglalakad na lang ako.

examples.tl: Dito na lang po, sa tapat ng Mercury.
examples.en: Just here please, in front of Mercury Drug.

notes.taglish: Sa unahan pa po, after ng stoplight.
notes.notes: Root una = first/front. 'Sa unahan pa' = a little further ahead. Opposite: 'sa likuran' / 'sa hulihan' (at the back).

examples.tl: Sa unahan pa po, pagkatapos ng stoplight.
examples.en: A bit further ahead, after the traffic light.
examples.taglish: Sa unahan pa po, after ng stoplight, tapos sa tabi lang.

examples.tl: Nasa unahan ang babaan, hindi dito.
examples.en: The unloading spot is up ahead, not here.

notes.taglish: May sasakyan ka ba, o commute?
notes.notes: Root sakay. General word for any vehicle; 'kotse' = car specifically. 'May sasakyan ka?' = do you have a car / a ride?

examples.tl: Wala akong sasakyan, nag-commute lang ako.
examples.en: I don't have a car, I just commute.
examples.taglish: Wala akong sasakyan, commute lang ako araw-araw.

examples.tl: Anong sasakyan mo? Para makita kita sa labas.
examples.en: What's your vehicle? So I can spot you outside.

notes.taglish: Iparada mo ang kotse sa basement.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'coche'. 'Mag-kotse' is not used; say 'magdala ng kotse' = bring the car.

examples.tl: Nasa shop ang kotse ko, kaya nag-Grab ako.
examples.en: My car's in the shop, so I took a Grab.
examples.taglish: Nasa casa ang kotse ko, kaya Grab muna ako this week.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng kotse mo, kasya ba sa parking?
examples.en: Your car's huge, will it fit in the parking?

notes.taglish: Nag-motor lang siya papuntang work.
notes.notes: 'Motorsiklo' is formal; everyone says 'motor'. 'Rider' = delivery or motorcycle driver. Verb: mag-motor.

examples.tl: Mabilis ang motor sa traffic.
examples.en: A motorcycle is fast in traffic.
examples.taglish: Mabilis ang motor sa traffic, kaya sikat ang Angkas.

examples.tl: Nabangga ang motor sa kanto kanina.
examples.en: A motorcycle got hit at the corner earlier.

notes.taglish: Mag-bike lang ako sa BGC.
notes.notes: 'Bike' in casual speech. 'Bike lane' along Ayala and in BGC. Verb: mag-bike / mag-bisikleta.

examples.tl: May bike lane na sa Ayala Avenue.
examples.en: There's a bike lane on Ayala Avenue now.
examples.taglish: May bike lane na sa Ayala, mas safe mag-bike.

examples.tl: Nag-bisikleta siya papuntang opisina para iwas traffic.
examples.en: He biked to the office to avoid traffic.

notes.taglish: Magpa-gas muna tayo bago umalis.
notes.notes: 'Mag-gas' / 'magpa-gas' = fill up. 'Krudo' = diesel in older speech, now mostly 'diesel'.

examples.tl: Tumaas ulit ang presyo ng gasolina.
examples.en: Gas prices went up again.
examples.taglish: Tumaas ulit ang gasolina, kaya mahal din ang Grab.

examples.tl: Magpa-gas muna tayo, malapit nang maubos.
examples.en: Let's fill up first, it's almost empty.

notes.taglish: Check mo ang plate number bago sumakay.
notes.notes: Check the plaka against the Grab app. Also the basis of 'number coding'.

examples.tl: Tingnan mo ang plaka, tama ba sa app?
examples.en: Check the plate, does it match the app?
examples.taglish: Check mo ang plaka, tama ba sa Grab app?

examples.tl: Hindi ko nakuha ang plaka ng taxi.
examples.en: I didn't get the taxi's plate number.

notes.taglish: Coding ako ngayon, commute ako.
notes.notes: MMDA scheme banning cars by plate ending digit on set weekdays, rush hours. 'Coding ako' = my car is banned today.

examples.tl: Coding ako ngayon, kaya mag-Grab ako.
examples.en: My car is banned today, so I'll take a Grab.
examples.taglish: Coding ako today, kaya Grab muna ako.

examples.tl: Wala nang coding pag 7 PM.
examples.en: Number coding is over after 7 PM.

notes.taglish: Dumaan tayo sa Skyway, mas mabilis pero may toll.
notes.notes: SLEX (south), NLEX (north), Skyway (elevated, Makati to airport). You pay toll via RFID (Autosweep / Easytrip).

examples.tl: Dumaan kami sa SLEX papuntang Tagaytay.
examples.en: We took SLEX to Tagaytay.
examples.taglish: Dumaan kami sa SLEX papuntang Tagaytay, two hours lang.

examples.tl: May toll sa Skyway, pero iwas EDSA.
examples.en: Skyway has a toll, but you avoid EDSA.

notes.taglish: Nasa labas na ako, white Vios.
notes.notes: Standard text to a Grab driver or to someone you're picking up. Driver version: 'Nasa labas na po ako.'

examples.tl: Nasa labas na ako, nasa may guard house.
examples.en: I'm outside, by the guard house.
examples.taglish: Nasa labas na ako, sa may guard house, grey na shirt.

examples.tl: Nasa labas na po ako, Ma'am.
examples.en: I'm already outside, Ma'am.

notes.taglish: Otw na ako, traffic lang sa EDSA.
notes.notes: 'Otw' (on the way) is the standard text; spoken: 'papunta na ako'. Often followed by an excuse.

examples.tl: Otw na ako, 10 minutes.
examples.en: I'm on the way, 10 minutes.
examples.taglish: Otw na ako, 10 mins, traffic lang sa Buendia.

examples.tl: Otw na ba kayo o kakaalis lang?
examples.en: Are you on the way or did you just leave?

notes.taglish: Ilang minuto pa, Kuya? May meeting ako.
notes.notes: 'Ilang' = how many. 'Gaano katagal?' = how long? Answer: 'Mga sampung minuto' = about 10 minutes.

examples.tl: Ilang minuto pa bago tayo makarating?
examples.en: How many more minutes until we arrive?
examples.taglish: Ilang minutes pa bago tayo makarating sa BGC?

examples.tl: Ilang minuto lang ang lakad mula station.
examples.en: It's just a few minutes' walk from the station.

notes.taglish: Malayo pa ba? Napapagod na ako maglakad.
notes.notes: Answer: 'Malapit na' (almost there) or 'Malayo pa' (still far). Classic passenger question.

examples.tl: Malayo pa ba ang terminal?
examples.en: Is the terminal still far?
examples.taglish: Malayo pa ba yung terminal? Ang init.

examples.tl: Malayo pa ba? Malapit na, isang kanto lang.
examples.en: Still far? Almost there, just one block.

notes.taglish: Kuya, dadaan po ba ito sa Makati Med?
notes.notes: Root daan. Ask the driver or a fellow passenger before boarding. Answer: 'Dadaan' / 'Hindi dadaan'.

examples.tl: Manong, dadaan po ba ito sa Buendia?
examples.en: Sir, does this pass by Buendia?
examples.taglish: Manong, dadaan po ba ito sa Buendia? Sakay po.

examples.tl: Hindi dadaan sa Ayala ito, sa kabila ka sumakay.
examples.en: This doesn't pass Ayala, board on the other side.

notes.taglish: Saan ang sakayan ng jeep papuntang Guadalupe?
notes.notes: Root sakay. Opposite: 'babaan' = unloading area. Signs often say 'Loading / Unloading'.

examples.tl: Saan ang sakayan ng jeep papuntang Taft?
examples.en: Where's the jeep stop going to Taft?
examples.taglish: Saan yung sakayan ng jeep papuntang Taft? Dito ba?

examples.tl: Doon ang sakayan ng Grab, sa may Gate 2.
examples.en: The Grab pickup is over there, by Gate 2.

notes.taglish: Bawal bumaba dito, sa babaan lang.
notes.notes: Root baba. Drivers say 'sa babaan lang po' when they can't stop where you asked.

examples.tl: Sa babaan lang po tayo bababa, bawal dito.
examples.en: We'll get off at the drop-off point, not here.
examples.taglish: Sa babaan lang po, bawal dito, may MMDA.

examples.tl: Nasa unahan ang babaan, lampas ng overpass.
examples.en: The unloading area is ahead, past the footbridge.

notes.taglish: Magkano po ang pamasahe hanggang Cubao?
notes.notes: For trikes always ask before riding: 'Magkano hanggang...?' For jeeps the fare is fixed.

examples.tl: Magkano po ang pamasahe hanggang Market! Market!?
examples.en: How much is the fare to Market! Market!?
examples.taglish: Kuya, magkano po hanggang Market Market?

examples.tl: Magkano ang trike papuntang Rockwell? Special?
examples.en: How much is the trike to Rockwell? Special trip?

notes.taglish: May aberya ang MRT ulit, naka-stuck kami.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'avería'. Used for a train glitch, car breakdown, or any snag in plans.

examples.tl: May aberya ang MRT, kaya na-late ang lahat.
examples.en: The MRT had a glitch, so everyone was late.
examples.taglish: May aberya ulit ang MRT, kaya late lahat sa office.

examples.tl: Walang aberya ang biyahe, smooth lang.
examples.en: The trip had no hitches, just smooth.

notes.en: to inch forward, to move along
notes.taglish: Hindi umuusad ang traffic sa Guadalupe.
notes.notes: Root usad. Classic traffic word: 'hindi umuusad' = not moving at all. Also 'usad-pagong' = snail's pace.

examples.tl: Hindi umuusad ang mga sasakyan sa EDSA.
examples.en: The cars on EDSA aren't moving.
examples.taglish: Hindi umuusad ang EDSA, 30 minutes na kami dito.

examples.tl: Umusad ka nang kaunti, may space pa sa harap.
examples.en: Move forward a bit, there's space in front.

notes.taglish: Kasya pa isa! Sakay na.
notes.notes: Jeep barkers shout 'Kasya pa!' (there's still room). Also for clothes: 'Hindi kasya' = doesn't fit.

examples.tl: Kasya pa ba ang isa diyan?
examples.en: Is there room for one more there?
examples.taglish: Kasya pa ba isa diyan? Sakay na ako.

examples.tl: Hindi kasya ang maleta sa trunk ng Grab.
examples.en: The suitcase doesn't fit in the Grab's trunk.

notes.taglish: Pakiabot po ng bayad, dalawa, Ayala.
notes.notes: Jeep etiquette: passengers relay coins to the driver. 'Abot' = reach/hand over. Reply with 'Salamat po.'

examples.tl: Pakiabot po ng bayad, isa lang, Guadalupe.
examples.en: Please pass my fare, one person, Guadalupe.
examples.taglish: Pakiabot po ng bayad, isa lang, Guadalupe. Thank you po.

examples.tl: Pakiabot po ng sukli ko.
examples.en: Please pass my change back.

notes.taglish: Anong lugar yan? First time ko dito.
notes.notes: From Spanish. 'Taga-saan ka?' = where are you from. 'Magandang lugar' = nice place.

examples.tl: Magandang lugar ang Intramuros para mag-lakad.
examples.en: Intramuros is a nice place to walk around.
examples.taglish: Magandang lugar ang Intramuros for a walk, may mga kalesa pa.

examples.tl: Hindi ko alam ang lugar na ito, naligaw ako.
examples.en: I don't know this place, I got lost.

notes.taglish: Anong kalye yan? Hindi ko makita sa Waze.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'calle'. 'Kalsada' = paved road. People often just say 'street' in Taglish.

examples.tl: Anong kalye ang bahay mo?
examples.en: What street is your house on?
examples.taglish: Anong kalye ang condo mo? Para ma-pin ko sa Grab.

examples.tl: Baha sa kalye namin tuwing umuulan.
examples.en: Our street floods every time it rains.

notes.taglish: Alam mo ba ang daan papuntang BGC?
notes.notes: Also the root of dumaan (to pass by). 'Nasa daan na ako' = I'm on the road. 'Saan ang daan papunta sa...?' = which way to...?

examples.tl: Masikip ang daan papunta sa palengke.
examples.en: The road to the market is narrow.
examples.taglish: Masikip ang daan papunta sa palengke, trike lang kasya.

examples.tl: Nasa daan na kami, malapit na.
examples.en: We're on the road, almost there.

notes.taglish: Nasa kanto ako, malapit sa 7-Eleven.
notes.notes: Also 'kanto boy' = guy who hangs out on the street. 'Sa kanto' is the default jeep drop-off.

examples.tl: Magkita tayo sa kanto ng Jupiter at Makati Ave.
examples.en: Let's meet at the corner of Jupiter and Makati Ave.
examples.taglish: Meet tayo sa kanto ng Jupiter at Makati Ave, sa may 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: May tindahan sa kanto, bumili ka ng tubig.
examples.en: There's a store at the corner, buy some water.

notes.taglish: Dumaan tayo sa eskinita, shortcut.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'esquinita'. Narrow lanes between houses; shortcuts but can be sketchy at night.

examples.tl: Dumaan kami sa eskinita para umiwas sa traffic.
examples.en: We went through an alley to avoid traffic.
examples.taglish: Dumaan kami sa eskinita, shortcut papuntang Poblacion.

examples.tl: Huwag kang dumaan sa eskinita pag gabi.
examples.en: Don't go through the alley at night.

notes.taglish: Anong building yan? Ang taas.
notes.notes: Formal-ish; in speech people say 'building'. Useful for reading signs and news.

examples.tl: Nasa ikatlong palapag ng gusali ang opisina.
examples.en: The office is on the third floor of the building.
examples.taglish: Nasa 3rd floor ng building yung office, may elevator.

examples.tl: Ang taas ng mga gusali sa BGC.
examples.en: The buildings in BGC are so tall.

notes.taglish: Magsisimba kami sa Greenbelt chapel.
notes.notes: Root simba (to attend Mass). Churches are common landmarks: 'sa tapat ng simbahan'.

examples.tl: Nasa tapat ng simbahan ang sakayan ng jeep.
examples.en: The jeep stop is in front of the church.
examples.taglish: Nasa tapat ng simbahan yung sakayan, sa may Sta. Cruz.

examples.tl: Puno ang simbahan tuwing Linggo ng umaga.
examples.en: The church is full every Sunday morning.

notes.taglish: Traffic sa may school pag dismissal.
notes.notes: Root aral. 'Eskwelahan' is the more common spoken word; 'school' in Taglish. Traffic spikes at school dismissal.

examples.tl: Traffic sa tapat ng paaralan tuwing hapon.
examples.en: It's jammed in front of the school every afternoon.
examples.taglish: Traffic sa tapat ng school pag 4 PM, dismissal.

examples.tl: Malapit sa paaralan ang bahay nila.
examples.en: Their house is near the school.

notes.taglish: Tumambay kami sa park sa Legazpi.
notes.notes: 'Park' in casual speech. Ayala Triangle, Legazpi Active Park, Rizal Park (Luneta).

examples.tl: Nag-jogging kami sa parke sa Ayala Triangle.
examples.en: We jogged at the park in Ayala Triangle.
examples.taglish: Nag-jogging kami sa Ayala Triangle, maaga, hindi pa mainit.

examples.tl: May libreng concert sa parke sa Sabado.
examples.en: There's a free concert at the park on Saturday.

notes.taglish: Beach trip tayo sa long weekend!
notes.notes: Literally 'beside the sea'. Everyone says 'beach'. 'Dalampasigan' is literary. 'Dagat' = sea.

examples.tl: Pumunta kami sa tabing-dagat sa Batangas.
examples.en: We went to the beach in Batangas.
examples.taglish: Nag-beach kami sa Batangas, Laiya, three hours lang.

examples.tl: Gusto kong tumira malapit sa tabing-dagat.
examples.en: I want to live near the sea.

notes.taglish: Mag-hike tayo sa bundok sa Rizal.
notes.notes: 'Umakyat ng bundok' = climb a mountain. 'Taga-bundok' can be an insult (hillbilly), so be careful.

examples.tl: Umakyat kami ng bundok sa Rizal noong Sabado.
examples.en: We climbed a mountain in Rizal last Saturday.
examples.taglish: Umakyat kami ng bundok sa Rizal, Mt. Batolusong, sobrang ganda.

examples.tl: Malamig sa bundok, magdala ka ng jacket.
examples.en: It's cold in the mountains, bring a jacket.

notes.taglish: Uuwi ako sa probinsya sa Undas.
notes.notes: Anything outside Metro Manila. 'Umuwi sa probinsya' = go home to the province, especially at Christmas and Undas.

examples.tl: Uuwi ako sa probinsya sa Pasko.
examples.en: I'm going home to the province for Christmas.
examples.taglish: Uuwi ako sa probinsya sa Pasko, sa Bicol, 10 hours na bus.

examples.tl: Mas tahimik sa probinsya kesa sa Manila.
examples.en: It's quieter in the province than in Manila.

notes.taglish: Pumunta tayo sa bayan, bibili ako ng load.
notes.notes: 'Sa bayan' = downtown / town proper, where the church, plaza, and market are. Also = nation ('Bayan ko').

examples.tl: Pupunta ako sa bayan para bumili ng gamot.
examples.en: I'm going to town to buy medicine.
examples.taglish: Pupunta ako sa bayan, may botika doon, bibili ng gamot.

examples.tl: May pista sa bayan nila sa Mayo.
examples.en: Their town has a fiesta in May.

notes.taglish: Makati City ang pinakamayaman na lungsod daw.
notes.notes: Formal; on signs ('Lungsod ng Makati'). In speech people say 'city' or 'siyudad'.

examples.tl: Makati ang pinakamayamang lungsod sa Pilipinas.
examples.en: Makati is the richest city in the Philippines.
examples.taglish: Makati daw ang pinakamayamang city sa Pilipinas.

examples.tl: Labing-anim na lungsod ang nasa Metro Manila.
examples.en: There are sixteen cities in Metro Manila.

notes.taglish: Hatid mo ako sa airport, Terminal 3.
notes.notes: Root lipad (fly). Everyone says 'airport' or 'NAIA' (nay-ah). Specify the terminal: T1, T2, T3, T4.

examples.tl: Papunta na ako sa paliparan, Terminal 3.
examples.en: I'm heading to the airport, Terminal 3.
examples.taglish: Papunta na ako sa airport, NAIA T3, 2 hours before flight.

examples.tl: Ang layo ng Terminal 4 sa Terminal 3.
examples.en: Terminal 4 is far from Terminal 3.

notes.taglish: Sa pier kami sasakay ng ferry papuntang Coron.
notes.notes: Manila North/South Harbor; Batangas Pier for Mindoro/Romblon. Tagalog 'pantalan' / 'daungan' are rare in Manila speech.

examples.tl: Sumakay kami ng barko sa pier sa Batangas.
examples.en: We boarded a ship at the Batangas pier.
examples.taglish: Sumakay kami ng ferry sa Batangas pier papuntang Puerto Galera.

examples.tl: Anong oras ang huling biyahe sa pier?
examples.en: What time is the last trip from the pier?

notes.taglish: Sa may gas station ka bumaba.
notes.notes: Common landmark in directions: 'sa may Shell / Petron / Caltex'. Good spot to wait for a Grab.

examples.tl: Lumiko ka sa may gasolinahan, tapos diretso.
examples.en: Turn at the gas station, then go straight.
examples.taglish: Liko ka sa may gasolinahan, Petron yun, tapos diretso.

examples.tl: Hintayin mo ako sa gasolinahan, mag-gas lang ako.
examples.en: Wait for me at the gas station, I'll just fill up.

notes.taglish: Saan ang parking? Puno na ang basement.
notes.notes: Verb: mag-park / ipark. 'Paradahan' is the Tagalog word, seen on signs. 'Bawal pumarada' = no parking.

examples.tl: Puno na ang parking sa mall, umikot pa kami.
examples.en: The mall parking was full, we had to circle.
examples.taglish: Puno na yung parking sa mall, umikot pa kami ng 20 minutes.

examples.tl: Magkano ang parking per hour dito?
examples.en: How much is parking per hour here?

notes.taglish: Pagkatapos ng tulay, kanan ka.
notes.notes: Guadalupe Bridge, Estrella-Pantaleon Bridge (Makati to Mandaluyong). Also 'tulay' = go-between in dating slang.

examples.tl: Traffic sa tulay ng Guadalupe tuwing umaga.
examples.en: Guadalupe Bridge is jammed every morning.
examples.taglish: Traffic sa Guadalupe bridge every morning, iwas ka.

examples.tl: Tumawid kami sa tulay papuntang Rockwell.
examples.en: We crossed the bridge to Rockwell.

notes.taglish: Nasa tabi ng Pasig River ang condo.
notes.notes: Pasig River (ilog Pasig) splits Makati from Mandaluyong. 'Ilog' also used for creeks (estero).

examples.tl: May ferry sa ilog Pasig, mula Guadalupe hanggang Escolta.
examples.en: There's a ferry on the Pasig River, from Guadalupe to Escolta.
examples.taglish: May Pasig River ferry, Guadalupe to Escolta, iwas traffic.

examples.tl: Umapaw ang ilog dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: The river overflowed because of the typhoon.

notes.taglish: Anong barangay yan? Para sa address.
