notes.notes: Smallest government unit; every address has one. 'Barangay hall' is where you get clearances. Pronounced ba-rang-GUY.

examples.tl: Nasa Barangay Poblacion ang condo ko.
examples.en: My condo is in Barangay Poblacion.
examples.taglish: Nasa Barangay Poblacion ang condo ko, malapit sa Rockwell.

examples.tl: Pumunta ka sa barangay hall para sa clearance.
examples.en: Go to the barangay hall for the clearance.

notes.taglish: Nasa loob ng village ang bahay, may guard sa gate.
notes.notes: 'Village' in Makati means a gated subdivision (Dasmarinas Village, Bel-Air). Guards may ask for ID at the gate.

examples.tl: Nasa loob ng subdivision ang bahay nila, kailangan ng ID sa gate.
examples.en: Their house is inside the subdivision, you need an ID at the gate.
examples.taglish: Nasa loob ng village yung bahay nila, kailangan ng ID sa gate.

examples.tl: Bawal ang trike sa loob ng subdivision.
examples.en: Tricycles aren't allowed inside the subdivision.

notes.taglish: Nasa Poblacion banda ako.
notes.notes: Follows the place: 'sa Makati banda' = around Makati. 'Saang banda?' = which part / whereabouts?

examples.tl: Saang banda ka sa Makati?
examples.en: Whereabouts in Makati are you?
examples.taglish: Saang banda ka sa Makati? Poblacion or Salcedo?

examples.tl: Nasa Kalayaan banda ang bahay niya.
examples.en: His house is around the Kalayaan area.

notes.en: directly in front of, across from
notes.taglish: Nasa tapat ng 7-Eleven ang jeep stop.
notes.notes: 'Sa tapat ng X' = right in front of / facing X. Most common landmark phrase in Manila directions.

examples.tl: Bumaba ka sa tapat ng Jollibee.
examples.en: Get off in front of the Jollibee.
examples.taglish: Baba ka sa tapat ng Jollibee, tapos tawag ka sa akin.

examples.tl: Nasa tapat ng condo ko ang laundry shop.
examples.en: The laundry shop is right across from my condo.

notes.taglish: Sa harap ng building ang pickup.
notes.notes: 'Sa harap ng X' = in front of X. 'Harapan' = the front area. 'Sa harap' in a jeep = seat beside the driver.

examples.tl: Hintayin mo ako sa harap ng gate.
examples.en: Wait for me in front of the gate.
examples.taglish: Wait mo ako sa harap ng gate, sa may guard.

examples.tl: Umupo ako sa harap, sa tabi ng drayber.
examples.en: I sat in front, next to the driver.

notes.taglish: Sa gilid ng building may entrance.
notes.notes: 'Sa gilid ng X' = at the side of X. 'Gilid ng daan' = roadside. 'Tabi' is also 'side' but more for 'beside / next to'.

examples.tl: May entrance sa gilid ng gusali.
examples.en: There's an entrance at the side of the building.
examples.taglish: May entrance sa gilid ng building, sa may parking exit.

examples.tl: Tumabi tayo sa gilid, may dumadaan.
examples.en: Let's step to the side, someone's passing.

notes.taglish: Sa kabila ka sumakay, pabalik yan.
notes.notes: 'Sa kabila' = across the street. 'Kabilang kalye' = the next street over. Key when told you're on the wrong side.

examples.tl: Sa kabila ang sakayan papuntang Cubao.
examples.en: The stop for Cubao is on the other side.
examples.taglish: Sa kabila yung sakayan papuntang Cubao, tawid ka sa overpass.

examples.tl: Nasa kabilang kalye ang bahay nila.
examples.en: Their house is on the next street over.

notes.taglish: Nandito ako sa may 7-Eleven.
notes.notes: 'Sa may X' = around / by X, less exact than 'sa tapat'. Extremely common in Manila directions.

examples.tl: Nasa may Jollibee ako, sa kanto.
examples.en: I'm by the Jollibee, at the corner.
examples.taglish: Nasa may Jollibee ako, sa kanto, wait mo ako.

examples.tl: Lumiko ka sa may Shell, tapos diretso.
examples.en: Turn by the Shell station, then go straight.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Takes sa + place. Casual invite: 'Punta tayo sa mall.'

examples.tl: Pupunta kami sa BGC mamaya.
examples.en: We're going to BGC later.
examples.taglish: Pupunta kami sa BGC mamaya, sama ka?

examples.tl: Pumunta kami sa Tagaytay noong weekend.
examples.en: We went to Tagaytay last weekend.
examples.taglish: Pumunta kami sa Tagaytay last weekend, ang lamig.

examples.tl: Saan ka pupunta mamaya?
examples.en: Where are you going later?

notes.taglish: Punta tayo sa BGC mamaya.

notes.en: to pass by, to stop by
notes.taglish: Dumaan muna tayo sa 7-Eleven.
notes.notes: Root daan. Both 'pass through a route' and 'drop by briefly'. 'Dadaan ako' = I'll stop by.

examples.tl: Dumaan muna tayo sa ATM bago sumakay.
examples.en: Let's stop by the ATM before boarding.
examples.taglish: Dumaan muna tayo sa ATM, wala akong cash pang-jeep.

examples.tl: Dadaan ba ito sa Taft?
examples.en: Does this pass through Taft?

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). 'Hinahanap ka ni boss' = the boss is looking for you.

examples.tl: Hinahanap ka ni Ma'am kanina.
examples.en: Ma'am was looking for you earlier.

examples.tl: Hinahanap ko po ang One Ayala, saan po iyon?
examples.en: I'm looking for One Ayala, where is it?
examples.taglish: Hinahanap ko po yung One Ayala, saan po yun?

examples.tl: Hanapin mo ang exit sa may Landmark.
examples.en: Look for the exit by Landmark.

notes.taglish: Hinahanap ko ang Tower 2, saan po?
Naligaw ako sa Megamall, ang laki.
notes.notes: Root ligaw. 'Naligaw ako' = I got lost. Note 'manligaw' (same root) = to court someone.

examples.tl: Naligaw ako sa loob ng mall.
examples.en: I got lost inside the mall.
examples.taglish: Naligaw ako sa loob ng Megamall, sobrang laki.

examples.tl: Baka maligaw ka, mag-Waze ka na lang.
examples.en: You might get lost, just use Waze.

notes.taglish: Nawala ang wallet ko sa jeep.
notes.notes: Root wala. For things that went missing. For a person who lost their way, use 'naligaw'.

examples.tl: Nawala ang phone ko sa bus.
examples.en: I lost my phone on the bus.
examples.taglish: Nawala ang phone ko sa bus, baka nadukot.

examples.tl: Huwag mong iwan ang bag, baka mawala.
examples.en: Don't leave your bag, it might go missing.

notes.taglish: Paano po pumunta sa Greenbelt mula dito?
notes.notes: 'Paano' = how. 'Mula dito' = from here. Add 'po' for guards and strangers.

examples.tl: Paano po pumunta sa Greenbelt mula dito?
examples.en: How do I get to Greenbelt from here?
examples.taglish: Paano po pumunta sa Greenbelt from here? Lakad lang ba?

examples.tl: Paano pumunta sa BGC nang hindi dadaan sa EDSA?
examples.en: How do you get to BGC without going via EDSA?

notes.taglish: Gaano kalayo ang BGC from here?
notes.notes: 'Gaano ka-' + adjective root = how + adjective. 'Gaano katagal?' = how long. Answer in minutes: 'Mga 15 minutes lang.'

examples.tl: Gaano kalayo ang airport mula sa Makati?
examples.en: How far is the airport from Makati?
examples.taglish: Gaano kalayo ang airport from Makati? 30 mins kung walang traffic?

examples.tl: Gaano kalayo ang lakad? Kaya ba?
examples.en: How far is the walk? Is it doable?

notes.notes: Root turo = to point / teach. Handy when you can't follow the verbal directions.

examples.tl: Pakituro po kung saan ang elevator.
examples.en: Please show me where the elevator is.
examples.taglish: Pakituro po kung saan yung elevator, first time ko dito.

examples.tl: Ituro mo sa map kung saan tayo.
examples.en: Point on the map where we are.

notes.taglish: Nasa loob ako ng mall, sa food court.
notes.notes: 'Sa loob ng X' = inside X. 'Pumasok sa loob' = go inside. Also 'kalooban' = inner self.

examples.tl: Nasa loob ng mall ang terminal ng jeep.
examples.en: The jeep terminal is inside the mall.
examples.taglish: Nasa loob ng mall yung jeep terminal, sa basement.

examples.tl: Pumasok ka sa loob, mainit sa labas.
examples.en: Come inside, it's hot outside.

notes.taglish: Nasa labas na ang Grab mo.
notes.notes: 'Sa labas' = outside. 'Lumabas' = to go out. 'Labasan' = exit. 'Mag-labas' is not used; say 'lumabas tayo'.

examples.tl: Hintayin mo ako sa labas ng 7-Eleven.
examples.en: Wait for me outside the 7-Eleven.
examples.taglish: Wait mo ako sa labas ng 7-Eleven, bibili lang ako ng tubig.

examples.tl: Lumabas ka sa Gate 3, doon ang Grab pickup.
examples.en: Exit at Gate 3, the Grab pickup is there.

notes.taglish: Sa itaas ang CR, second floor.
notes.notes: 'Sa itaas' = upstairs / on top. 'Umakyat' = go up. 'Taas' root. 'Sa baba / ibaba' = downstairs.

examples.tl: Nasa itaas ang food court, sa ikaapat na palapag.
examples.en: The food court is upstairs, on the fourth floor.
examples.taglish: Nasa itaas yung food court, 4th floor, escalator sa kanan.

examples.tl: Umakyat ka sa itaas, doon ang MRT platform.
examples.en: Go upstairs, the MRT platform is there.

notes.taglish: Sa baba na lang tayo magkita, sa lobby.
notes.notes: 'Sa ibaba' / 'sa baba' = downstairs / below. 'Bumaba' = go down / get off.

examples.tl: Nasa ibaba ang parking, basement 2.
examples.en: The parking is below, basement 2.
examples.taglish: Nasa baba yung parking, B2, elevator sa kaliwa.

examples.tl: Magkita tayo sa ibaba ng overpass.
examples.en: Let's meet at the bottom of the footbridge.

notes.taglish: Sa dulo ng street ang condo, dead end.
notes.notes: 'Sa dulo ng kalye' = at the end of the street. 'Hanggang dulo' = all the way to the end.

examples.tl: Nasa dulo ng kalye ang bahay nila.
examples.en: Their house is at the end of the street.
examples.taglish: Nasa dulo ng street yung bahay nila, yung may puting gate.

examples.tl: Diretso hanggang dulo, tapos kanan.
examples.en: Straight to the end, then right.

notes.taglish: Saan ang entrance ng Tower 1?
notes.notes: Root pasok. Also 'pasukan' = start of the school year or work hours ('may pasok' = there's work/school). People say 'entrance' for buildings.

examples.tl: Saan ang pasukan ng parking?
examples.en: Where's the parking entrance?
examples.taglish: Saan ang entrance ng parking? Sa Makati Ave side?

examples.tl: Sarado ang pangunahing pasukan, dumaan ka sa gilid.
examples.en: The main entrance is closed, go through the side.

notes.taglish: Anong exit ang malapit sa Ayala station?
notes.notes: Root labas. People say 'exit' in buildings and on expressways ('Magallanes exit'). 'Labasan' seen on signs.

examples.tl: Saan ang labasan papunta sa MRT?
examples.en: Where's the exit to the MRT?
examples.taglish: Saan yung exit papuntang MRT? Sa may Landmark?

examples.tl: Bumaba ka sa Alabang exit, tapos kanan.
examples.en: Take the Alabang exit, then right.

notes.taglish: Safe biyahe! Text mo ako pag nakarating ka.
notes.notes: From Spanish 'viaje'. 'Ingat sa biyahe' = safe travels. On a jeep, 'byahe' also means it's departing. Texted as 'byahe'.

examples.tl: Ang tagal ng biyahe, apat na oras.
examples.en: The trip was so long, four hours.
examples.taglish: Ang tagal ng byahe, 4 hours, traffic sa SLEX.

examples.tl: Ingat sa biyahe, text ka pag nakarating.
examples.en: Safe trip, text when you arrive.

notes.en: to travel, to take a trip
notes.taglish: Mag-travel kami sa Japan sa March.
notes.notes: Root biyahe. 'Mag-travel' is more common in Taglish for leisure trips. 'Bumiyahe' also used for a jeep leaving: 'Bumiyahe na ang jeep.'

examples.tl: Bumiyahe kami nang maaga para iwas traffic.
examples.en: We traveled early to avoid traffic.
examples.taglish: Bumiyahe kami ng 5 AM para iwas traffic sa SLEX.

examples.tl: Gusto kong bumiyahe sa Palawan next year.
examples.en: I want to travel to Palawan next year.

notes.taglish: Bakasyon ko sa May, Palawan tayo?
notes.notes: Verb: magbakasyon = go on vacation. 'Nagbabakasyon' = on vacation. 'Summer' in PH = April-May.

examples.tl: Saan kayo magbabakasyon sa summer?
examples.en: Where are you vacationing this summer?
examples.taglish: Saan kayo magbabakasyon this summer? Beach or abroad?

examples.tl: Nagbakasyon kami sa Boracay nang isang linggo.
examples.en: We vacationed in Boracay for a week.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Also 'to set off/leave'. Maglakad = to walk around as an activity.

examples.tl: Lumakad lang kami papuntang Greenbelt.
examples.en: We just walked to Greenbelt.

examples.tl: Naglakad lang kami mula Greenbelt hanggang Glorietta.
examples.en: We just walked from Greenbelt to Glorietta.
examples.taglish: Lakad lang kami from Greenbelt to Glorietta, may aircon walkway.

examples.tl: Lumakad na ba sila? Wala na sila sa lobby.
examples.en: Have they left already? They're not in the lobby anymore.

notes.taglish: Lakad lang tayo, malapit lang.
Nabili ko na ang ticket, Cebu Pac, promo.
notes.notes: Spelled 'ticket' in texts. 'Bumili ng tiket' = buy a ticket. Also MRT 'beep card' or single journey ticket.

examples.tl: Bumili ka na ba ng tiket papuntang Cebu?
examples.en: Did you buy your ticket to Cebu yet?
examples.taglish: Nabili mo na ba ang ticket papuntang Cebu? May piso sale.

examples.tl: Nawala ang tiket ko sa MRT.
examples.en: I lost my MRT ticket.

notes.taglish: Anong oras ang flight mo? Hatid kita.
notes.notes: Everyone says 'flight'. 'Eroplano' = airplane. 'Lumipad' = to fly. 'Na-delay ang flight' = flight delayed.

examples.tl: Anong oras ang flight mo bukas?
examples.en: What time is your flight tomorrow?
examples.taglish: Anong oras flight mo bukas? Ihahatid kita sa T3.

examples.tl: Maaga ang flight ko, alas-sais ng umaga.
examples.en: My flight is early, six in the morning.

notes.taglish: Na-delay ang flight ko ng 2 hours.
notes.notes: Taglish verb from 'delay'. 'Naantala' is the formal Tagalog, used in announcements. Also 'na-cancel'.

examples.tl: Na-delay ang flight namin dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: Our flight was delayed because of the typhoon.
examples.taglish: Na-delay ang flight namin ng 3 hours dahil sa bagyo.

examples.tl: Na-delay ang MRT, kaya late ako.
examples.en: The MRT got delayed, so I was late.

notes.taglish: Nag-check-in na ako online, no bags.
notes.notes: Taglish verb. 'Check-in' noun also = a hotel stay ('nag-check-in kami sa Tagaytay'). 'Check-out' likewise.

examples.tl: Mag-check-in tayo ng dalawang oras bago ang flight.
examples.en: Let's check in two hours before the flight.
examples.taglish: Mag-check-in tayo 2 hours before, mahaba ang pila sa T3.

examples.tl: Alas-dos pa ang check-in sa hotel.
examples.en: Hotel check-in isn't until two.

notes.taglish: May check-in baggage ka ba o hand carry lang?
notes.notes: From Spanish. 'Hand carry' = carry-on. 'Maleta' = suitcase specifically.

examples.tl: Sobra sa timbang ang bagahe ko, nagbayad pa ako.
examples.en: My luggage was overweight, I had to pay extra.
examples.taglish: Overweight ang bagahe ko, nagbayad pa ako ng 1,500.

examples.tl: Saan ang claim ng bagahe?
examples.en: Where's the baggage claim?

notes.taglish: Ang bigat ng maleta mo, ano laman?
notes.notes: From Spanish. 'Mag-impake' = to pack. 'Hilahin ang maleta' = pull the suitcase.

examples.tl: Hindi kasya ang maleta sa trunk ng taxi.
examples.en: The suitcase doesn't fit in the taxi trunk.
examples.taglish: Hindi kasya yung maleta sa trunk, sa likod na lang.

examples.tl: Nasira ang gulong ng maleta ko sa airport.
examples.en: My suitcase wheel broke at the airport.

notes.taglish: Saan kayo nag-stay? Hotel o Airbnb?
notes.notes: 'Mag-hotel' = stay at a hotel. 'Staycation' = local hotel stay without traveling.

examples.tl: Malapit ang hotel namin sa beach.
examples.en: Our hotel is near the beach.
examples.taglish: Malapit lang ang hotel namin sa beach, 5 minutes walk.

examples.tl: Mag-staycation tayo sa hotel sa BGC.
examples.en: Let's do a staycation at a hotel in BGC.

notes.taglish: May pool ang resort, pang-bata.
notes.notes: Beach resorts in Batangas/Zambales; 'private resort' = rented house with a pool, popular for family outings.

examples.tl: Nag-rent kami ng private resort sa Laguna.
examples.en: We rented a private resort in Laguna.
examples.taglish: Nag-rent kami ng private resort sa Laguna, overnight, may videoke.

examples.tl: Puno ang mga resort sa Semana Santa.
examples.en: The resorts are full during Holy Week.

notes.taglish: Mag-book ka na ng Grab, matagal pag rush hour.
notes.notes: Taglish verb. 'I-book mo' = book it. 'Na-book ko na' = I've booked it. Also 'booking' as noun.

examples.tl: Nag-book na ako ng Grab, 5 minutes daw.
examples.en: I already booked a Grab, 5 minutes they said.
examples.taglish: Nag-book na ako ng Grab, 5 mins daw, white Innova.

examples.tl: I-book mo na ang hotel, baka maubos.
examples.en: Book the hotel now, it might sell out.

notes.taglish: Island hopping tayo sa El Nido!
notes.notes: From Spanish. 'Island hopping' is the standard tour term. 'Pulo' is the pure Tagalog word, rare in speech.

examples.tl: Maraming magagandang isla sa Palawan.
examples.en: There are many beautiful islands in Palawan.
examples.taglish: Maraming magagandang isla sa Palawan, El Nido best.

examples.tl: Bangka ang sakay papunta sa isla.
examples.en: You take a boat to get to the island.

notes.taglish: Mag-tour tayo sa Intramuros, may kalesa.
notes.notes: 'Mag-tour' = go on a tour / show someone around. 'I-tour kita' = I'll show you around.

examples.tl: Kumuha kami ng island tour sa Coron.
examples.en: We got an island tour in Coron.
examples.taglish: Kumuha kami ng island tour sa Coron, 1,500 per head.

examples.tl: I-tour kita sa Makati pag dumalaw ka.
examples.en: I'll show you around Makati when you visit.

notes.en: gift brought back from a trip
notes.taglish: Pasalubong ko sa office, dried mangoes.
notes.notes: Core Filipino custom: bring treats back for family/coworkers. 'May pasalubong ka?' is the expected question.

examples.tl: May pasalubong ako mula Cebu, dried mangoes.
examples.en: I brought back a gift from Cebu, dried mangoes.
examples.taglish: May pasalubong ako from Cebu, dried mangoes at otap.

examples.tl: Huwag kalimutan ang pasalubong ha!
examples.en: Don't forget the pasalubong, okay!

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Irregular: d becomes r in the reduplicated forms (dumarating, darating).

examples.tl: Darating ang Grab sa loob ng limang minuto.
examples.en: The Grab will arrive within five minutes.
examples.taglish: Darating na yung Grab, five minutes.

examples.tl: Dumating ang flight nang alas-dose ng hatinggabi.
examples.en: The flight arrived at midnight.
examples.taglish: Dumating ang flight ng 12 midnight, wala nang MRT.

examples.tl: Kakadating lang namin, pahinga muna.
examples.en: We just arrived, let's rest first.

notes.taglish: Dumating na ang Grab, baba na tayo.

notes.en: to make it (in time), to reach
notes.taglish: Hindi ako aabot sa flight, traffic!
notes.notes: Root abot. 'Aabot ba ako?' = will I make it? 'Hindi umabot' = didn't make it. 'Maabutan' = to catch (a jeep, a person).

examples.tl: Umabot kami sa huling biyahe ng MRT.
examples.en: We made the last MRT trip.
examples.taglish: Umabot kami sa last trip ng MRT, buti na lang.

examples.tl: Hindi ako umabot sa meeting kasi traffic.
examples.en: I didn't make it to the meeting because of traffic.

notes.taglish: Dala mo ba ang passport mo? Need sa check-in.
notes.notes: Everyone says 'passport'. Renewal at DFA; 'DFA appointment' is a known hassle.

examples.tl: Nakalimutan ko ang pasaporte ko sa condo!
examples.en: I forgot my passport at the condo!
examples.taglish: Nakalimutan ko ang passport ko sa condo, balik tayo!

examples.tl: Expired na ang pasaporte ko, kailangan mag-renew.
examples.en: My passport is expired, I need to renew.

notes.taglish: Maraming tourist sa Intramuros pag weekend.
notes.notes: From Spanish. 'Mukhang turista' = looks like a tourist (may get charged more). 'Foreigner' / 'kano' for Americans.

examples.tl: Maraming turista sa Boracay tuwing Disyembre.
examples.en: There are lots of tourists in Boracay every December.
examples.taglish: Maraming turista sa Boracay pag December, peak season.

examples.tl: Huwag kang magmukhang turista, baka ma-overcharge ka.
examples.en: Don't look like a tourist, you might get overcharged.

notes.taglish: May balikbayan box na padala ang tita ko.
notes.notes: Balik (return) + bayan (country). 'Balikbayan box' = big box of goods shipped home. Balikbayan lane at NAIA immigration.

examples.tl: Balikbayan ang pinsan ko, galing Dubai.
examples.en: My cousin is a balikbayan, from Dubai.
examples.taglish: Balikbayan ang pinsan ko from Dubai, may pasalubong.

examples.tl: Dumating ang balikbayan box pagkatapos ng dalawang buwan.
examples.en: The balikbayan box arrived after two months.

notes.en: to roam around, go out and about
notes.taglish: Gala tayo sa BGC mamaya.
notes.notes: Root gala. 'Gala tayo' = let's go out somewhere. 'Palagi kang gumagala' = you're always out. Casual, friendly.

examples.tl: Gumala kami sa Binondo buong araw.
examples.en: We roamed around Binondo all day.
examples.taglish: Gumala kami sa Binondo buong araw, food trip.

examples.tl: Gala tayo sa weekend, wala akong plano.
examples.en: Let's go out this weekend, I have no plans.

notes.en: to go out for leisure, stroll
notes.taglish: Pasyal tayo sa Luneta, libre.
notes.notes: Root pasyal (from Spanish 'pasear'). 'Pasyalan' = a place to visit / tourist spot. 'Mamasyal' is a bit gentler than 'gumala'.

examples.tl: Namasyal kami sa Intramuros noong Linggo.
examples.en: We strolled around Intramuros last Sunday.
examples.taglish: Namasyal kami sa Intramuros last Sunday, nag-kalesa pa.

examples.tl: Anong magandang pasyalan malapit sa Manila?
examples.en: What's a good place to visit near Manila?

notes.taglish: Lakwatsa muna tayo bago umuwi.
notes.notes: Verb: maglakwatsa. Slightly teasing: 'lakwatsera/lakwatsero' = someone always out and about.

examples.tl: Naglakwatsa kami sa Tagaytay pagkatapos ng exam.
examples.en: We went gallivanting in Tagaytay after the exam.
examples.taglish: Naglakwatsa kami sa Tagaytay after exams, bulalo trip.

examples.tl: Puro lakwatsa ka, kailan ka mag-aaral?
examples.en: You're always out, when will you study?

notes.taglish: Long weekend next week, beach tayo?
notes.notes: Used as-is in Tagalog. 'Holiday' for public holidays; 'bakasyon' for a vacation. Triggers 'out of town' trips.

examples.tl: May long weekend sa susunod na linggo, out of town tayo.
examples.en: There's a long weekend next week, let's go out of town.
examples.taglish: Long weekend next week, out of town tayo, Baler?

examples.tl: Traffic sa SLEX tuwing long weekend.
examples.en: SLEX is jammed every long weekend.

notes.taglish: Bangka ang sakay papuntang isla, 30 minutes.
notes.notes: Outrigger boats for island hopping. 'Barko' = large ship. 'Ferry' for Batangas-Mindoro. 'Sumakay ng bangka'.

examples.tl: Sumakay kami ng bangka papunta sa isla.
examples.en: We took a boat to the island.
examples.taglish: Sumakay kami ng bangka papuntang isla, maalon, nabasa kami.

examples.tl: Walang bangka pag may bagyo.
examples.en: There are no boats when there's a typhoon.

notes.taglish: Mag-van tayo sa Alabang, mas mabilis sa bus.
notes.notes: UV Express vans run fixed routes from terminals (older people still say 'FX'). Also provincial vans to Tagaytay, Antipolo.

examples.tl: Sumakay kami ng van sa Ayala papuntang Alabang.
examples.en: We took a van from Ayala to Alabang.
examples.taglish: Nag-van kami from Ayala to Alabang, 60 pesos lang.

examples.tl: Puno na ang van, hintayin natin ang susunod.
examples.en: The van's full, let's wait for the next one.

notes.taglish: Hindi pa ako nag-impake, flight ko bukas!
notes.notes: Root impake (from Spanish 'empacar'). 'Mag-pack' is also common in Taglish.

examples.tl: Nag-impake ako kagabi para sa biyahe.
examples.en: I packed last night for the trip.
examples.taglish: Nag-impake ako kagabi, carry-on lang, 3 days lang naman.

examples.tl: Mag-impake ka na, aalis tayo nang alas-kuwatro.
examples.en: Pack now, we're leaving at four.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: hintayin. 'Hintay lang' / 'Wait lang' = hold on.

examples.tl: Naghintay kami ng isang oras ng Grab.
examples.en: We waited an hour for a Grab.

examples.tl: Hintayin mo ako sa labas, bababa na ako.
examples.en: Wait for me outside, I'm coming down.
examples.taglish: Antayin mo ako sa labas, bababa na ako, 2 mins.

examples.tl: Naghintay kami ng isang oras sa terminal.
examples.en: We waited an hour at the terminal.

notes.taglish: Wait lang, hinihintay ko pa ang Grab.

notes.en: to go along with, ride together
notes.taglish: Sabay na tayo sa Grab, split tayo.
notes.notes: Root sabay = simultaneous / together. 'Sabay tayo' = let's go together. 'Makisabay' = ask to tag along. 'Pasabay' = can I ride with you?

examples.tl: Sumabay ako sa kotse ng officemate ko pauwi.
examples.en: I rode home with my officemate in his car.
examples.taglish: Sumabay ako sa officemate ko pauwi, same village kami.

examples.tl: Pasabay naman hanggang Makati.
examples.en: Can I ride with you as far as Makati?

notes.taglish: Grabe ang init, mag-mall na lang tayo.
notes.notes: 'Mainit' = hot. 'Ang init!' = it's so hot! 'Tag-init' = hot/dry season (Mar-May). 'Alinsangan' = humid.

examples.tl: Ang init sa labas, 38 degrees daw.
examples.en: It's so hot outside, 38 degrees they say.
examples.taglish: Grabe ang init sa labas, 38 degrees, heat index 45.

examples.tl: Huwag kang maglakad sa tanghali, sobrang init.
examples.en: Don't walk at noon, it's extremely hot.

notes.taglish: Suspended ang classes sa NCR, Signal No. 3.
notes.notes: Used as-is for classes/work during storms. 'Suspendido' in news Tagalog. Also 'suspended ang MRT operations'.

examples.tl: Suspended ang klase sa lahat ng antas sa Metro Manila.
examples.en: Classes at all levels are suspended in Metro Manila.
examples.taglish: Suspended ang classes all levels sa Metro Manila, pati work sa gov't.

examples.tl: Suspended ang biyahe ng ferry hanggang bukas.
examples.en: Ferry trips are suspended until tomorrow.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). 'Ingat!' or 'Ingat ka' is the everyday 'take care' farewell.

examples.tl: Nag-iingat kami pag-uwi ng gabi.
examples.en: We're careful when going home at night.

examples.tl: Mag-ingat ka sa bag mo sa MRT, may mandurukot.
examples.en: Watch your bag on the MRT, there are pickpockets.
examples.taglish: Mag-ingat ka sa bag mo sa MRT, maraming mandurukot pag siksikan.

examples.tl: Mag-ingat kayo sa daan, madulas.
examples.en: Be careful on the road, it's slippery.

notes.taglish: Mag-ingat ka sa phone mo sa jeep.
Delikado maglakad diyan pag gabi.
notes.notes: From Spanish. 'Mapanganib' is formal. 'Delikado yan' = that's risky. Also for a precarious situation.

examples.tl: Delikado tumawid sa EDSA, dumaan ka sa overpass.
examples.en: Crossing EDSA is dangerous, use the footbridge.
examples.taglish: Delikado tumawid sa EDSA, dumaan ka sa overpass please.

examples.tl: Delikado ang lugar na yan pag gabi, mag-Grab ka.
examples.en: That area is dangerous at night, take a Grab.

notes.taglish: Safe ba dito maglakad pag gabi?
notes.notes: 'Ligtas' also = rescued. 'Safe' is more common in Taglish speech. 'Kaligtasan' = safety.

examples.tl: Ligtas ba maglakad dito sa gabi?
examples.en: Is it safe to walk here at night?
examples.taglish: Safe ba maglakad dito pag gabi? May mga guard ba?

examples.tl: Ligtas kami, nakarating na sa hotel.
examples.en: We're safe, we've reached the hotel.

notes.taglish: May na-holdap sa jeep sa Pasay kagabi.
notes.notes: From English 'hold-up'. 'Na-holdap' = got robbed. 'Holdaper' = robber. Common news word about jeeps and buses.

examples.tl: Na-holdap ang kaibigan ko sa jeep sa Quiapo.
examples.en: My friend got robbed on a jeep in Quiapo.
examples.taglish: Na-holdap ang friend ko sa jeep sa Quiapo, kinuha ang phone.

examples.tl: May holdap sa bangko kanina, maraming pulis.
examples.en: There was a robbery at the bank earlier, lots of police.

notes.taglish: Tumawag ka ng pulis, 911.
notes.notes: 'Pulis' = police / policeman. 'Istasyon ng pulis' = police station. Emergency number 911. MMDA = traffic enforcers, not police.

examples.tl: May pulis sa kanto, huwag kang tumawid doon.
examples.en: There's a cop at the corner, don't cross there.
examples.taglish: May pulis sa kanto, wag ka tumawid doon, ticket ka.

examples.tl: Tumawag kami ng pulis dahil sa aksidente.
examples.en: We called the police because of the accident.

notes.taglish: Wag dito, Kuya, sa unahan, bawal dito.
notes.notes: 'Huwag' (texted 'wag') = don't. 'Huwag dito, sa unahan' = not here, up ahead. Guards say 'bawal dito' = not allowed here.

examples.tl: Huwag dito, bawal bumaba, sa babaan po.
examples.en: Not here, you can't get off here, at the unloading point.
examples.taglish: Wag dito, bawal, may MMDA, sa babaan po.

examples.tl: Huwag dito kayo pumarada, towing zone.
examples.en: Don't park here, it's a towing zone.

notes.taglish: Bawal mag-U-turn dito, may camera.
notes.notes: On signs everywhere: 'Bawal tumawid' (no crossing), 'Bawal umihi dito'. 'Bawal yan' = that's not allowed.

examples.tl: Bawal tumawid dito, dumaan ka sa overpass.
examples.en: No crossing here, use the footbridge.
examples.taglish: Bawal tumawid dito, may MMDA, overpass ka.

examples.tl: Bawal ang jeep sa Ayala Avenue.
examples.en: Jeeps aren't allowed on Ayala Avenue.

notes.taglish: Ingat sa snatcher, wag mo ilabas phone mo sa jeep.
notes.notes: English loan used as-is. 'Na-snatch' = got snatched. 'Mandurukot' = pickpocket. 'Riding in tandem' = two on a motorbike who snatch.

examples.tl: Maraming snatcher sa may Baclaran.
examples.en: There are lots of snatchers around Baclaran.
examples.taglish: Maraming snatcher sa Baclaran, itago mo phone mo.

examples.tl: Na-snatch ang phone niya habang nasa jeep.
examples.en: Her phone got snatched while she was on a jeep.

notes.taglish: May magnanakaw sa building, nawalan ng laptop.
notes.notes: Root nakaw = steal. 'Ninakaw' = was stolen. 'Mandurukot' = pickpocket specifically. 'Magnanakaw!' is shouted to raise alarm.

examples.tl: Ninakaw ang bisikleta ko sa labas ng condo.
examples.en: My bike was stolen outside the condo.
examples.taglish: Ninakaw yung bike ko sa labas ng condo, kahit may guard.

examples.tl: Nahuli ng pulis ang magnanakaw sa palengke.
examples.en: The police caught the thief at the market.

notes.taglish: May aksidente sa EDSA, kaya traffic.
notes.notes: From Spanish. 'Nabangga' = got hit / crashed. 'Banggaan' = collision. Accidents are the usual reason EDSA stops moving.

examples.tl: May aksidente sa Guadalupe, hindi umuusad ang traffic.
examples.en: There's an accident at Guadalupe, traffic isn't moving.
examples.taglish: May aksidente sa Guadalupe, hindi umuusad, 1 hour na kami.

examples.tl: Naaksidente ang kaibigan ko sa motor.
examples.en: My friend had a motorcycle accident.

notes.taglish: Mag-isa ka lang? Ingat ka pauwi.
notes.notes: 'Mag-isa lang ako' = I'm alone. 'Solo' also used. 'Huwag kang mag-isa doon' = don't go there alone.

examples.tl: Huwag kang maglakad mag-isa doon pag gabi.
examples.en: Don't walk there alone at night.
examples.taglish: Wag kang maglakad mag-isa doon pag gabi, delikado.

examples.tl: Mag-isa akong nag-travel sa Siargao.
examples.en: I traveled solo to Siargao.

notes.taglish: Gabi na, mag-Grab ka na lang, wag jeep.
notes.notes: 'Gabi' = night. Said to urge someone home or to take a safer ride. 'Gabing-gabi na' = it's very late.

examples.tl: Gabi na, uwi na tayo.
examples.en: It's late, let's go home.
examples.taglish: Gabi na, uwi na tayo, may pasok pa bukas.

examples.tl: Gabi na, wala nang jeep, mag-taxi na lang tayo.
examples.en: It's late, no more jeeps, let's just take a taxi.

notes.taglish: May hatid-sundo ang hotel papuntang airport.
notes.notes: Compound of hatid (drop off) + sundo (pick up). Used for school service vans, hotel transfers, and a partner doing the driving.

examples.tl: May hatid-sundo ang school ng anak nila.
examples.en: Their kid's school has a shuttle service.
examples.taglish: May hatid-sundo service yung school ng anak nila, 3,000 a month.

examples.tl: Ako ang hatid-sundo ng asawa ko ngayong linggo.
examples.en: I'm my wife's driver this week.

notes.taglish: Nakarating na ako sa hotel, safe.
notes.notes: Root dating with maka- (managed to). 'Nakauwi' = made it home. The standard 'I'm here safe' text.

examples.tl: Nakarating na kami sa Baguio, malamig.
examples.en: We've arrived in Baguio, it's cold.
examples.taglish: Nakarating na kami sa Baguio, 6 hours, ang lamig.

examples.tl: Text mo ako pag nakarating ka na ha.
examples.en: Text me when you've arrived, okay.

notes.taglish: Nag-kalesa kami sa Intramuros, 500 for 30 mins.
notes.notes: Tourist ride in Intramuros and Binondo. From Spanish. Agree on the price first.

examples.tl: Sumakay kami ng kalesa sa Intramuros.
examples.en: We rode a kalesa in Intramuros.
examples.taglish: Nag-kalesa kami sa Intramuros, tour na rin.

notes.taglish: Mag-pedicab lang tayo hanggang palengke.
notes.notes: Pedal-powered trike for short hops inside barangays. Also called 'padyak'. Cheaper and slower than a trike.

examples.tl: Sumakay kami ng pedicab mula palengke hanggang bahay.
examples.en: We took a pedicab from the market to the house.
examples.taglish: Nag-pedicab lang kami from palengke to bahay, 20 pesos.

examples.tl: Walang pedicab sa Makati CBD, bawal.
examples.en: There are no pedicabs in Makati CBD, they're banned.

notes.taglish: Mag-load ka ng beep card, mahaba ang pila sa ticket.
notes.notes: Stored-value card for MRT/LRT, EDSA Carousel, some buses. 'Mag-load' = top up. Also 'Tap!' at the gate.

examples.tl: Wala nang load ang beep card ko.
examples.en: My beep card is out of credit.
examples.taglish: Wala nang load yung beep card ko, mag-load muna ako sa station.

examples.tl: Mag-tap ka ng beep card sa gate.
examples.en: Tap your beep card at the gate.

notes.taglish: Special na lang tayo, 150 hanggang Rockwell.
notes.notes: Hiring a trike or jeep just for yourself instead of waiting to fill it. Costs more; negotiate first: 'Magkano special?'

examples.tl: Special na lang, Kuya, magkano hanggang Guadalupe?
examples.en: Private trip please, how much to Guadalupe?
examples.taglish: Special na lang, Kuya, magkano hanggang Guadalupe? 100?

examples.tl: Nag-special kami ng trike kasi gabi na.
examples.en: We hired a trike privately because it was late.

notes.taglish: Lampas na tayo, Kuya! Mag-U-turn po.
notes.notes: 'Lampas ng X' = past X. 'Nalampasan' = we passed it / missed the turn. 'Lumampas' = to go past.

examples.tl: Lampas ng Jollibee, kanan ka.
examples.en: Past the Jollibee, turn right.
examples.taglish: Lampas ng Jollibee, kanan ka, tapos sa tabi lang.

examples.tl: Nalampasan natin ang kanto, balik tayo.
examples.en: We passed the corner, let's go back.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). 'Babalik ako' = I'll be back. Object focus ibalik = return something.

examples.tl: Babalik ako bukas ng umaga.
examples.en: I'll come back tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: Bumalik kami sa hotel kasi umulan.
examples.en: We went back to the hotel because it rained.
examples.taglish: Bumalik kami sa hotel kasi umulan, ang lakas.

examples.tl: Babalik ako sa Manila sa Lunes.
examples.en: I'll be back in Manila on Monday.

notes.taglish: Balik tayo, nakalimutan ko ang passport.
Umikot pa kami kasi one-way, ang hassle.
notes.notes: Root ikot. 'Umikot' = go around / detour / circle for parking. 'Mag-ikot' = look around a place. 'Ikot' jeep = a loop route.

examples.tl: Umikot kami nang tatlong beses para makahanap ng parking.
examples.en: We circled three times to find parking.
examples.taglish: Umikot kami 3 times para makahanap ng parking sa Greenbelt.

examples.tl: Mag-ikot muna tayo sa mall bago kumain.
examples.en: Let's look around the mall first before eating.

notes.taglish: May shortcut sa Kalayaan, iwas Makati Ave.
notes.notes: Used as-is. 'Mag-shortcut' = take a shortcut. Waze shortcuts through eskinitas are a Manila thing.

examples.tl: May alam akong shortcut papuntang BGC.
examples.en: I know a shortcut to BGC.
examples.taglish: May alam akong shortcut papuntang BGC, via Kalayaan flyover.

examples.tl: Nag-shortcut ang Grab driver sa eskinita.
examples.en: The Grab driver took a shortcut through an alley.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Object focus: tawagan (call someone). Also 'to call out/shout for'.

examples.tl: Tumawag ang landlord kanina.
examples.en: The landlord called earlier.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Also 'come out/appear' (lumabas ang resulta). 'Labas tayo' = let's go out.

examples.tl: Lalabas kami ngayong gabi.
examples.en: We're going out tonight.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Object focus: tulungan (help someone). 'Tulong!' = help!

examples.tl: Tumulong siya sa akin kahapon.
examples.en: He helped me yesterday.

notes.notes: Actor focus (um-). 'Maupo po kayo' is the polite invitation to sit; 'Upo ka' is casual.

examples.tl: Umupo siya sa tabi ko sa jeep.
examples.en: She sat beside me on the jeep.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Root tayo (stress on last syllable), not the pronoun tayo (we).

examples.tl: Tumayo ang lahat nang tumugtog ang Lupang Hinirang.
examples.en: Everyone stood when the national anthem played.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Also 'to run for office'. Taglish: mag-jogging.

examples.tl: Tumatakbo siya tuwing umaga sa Ayala Triangle.
examples.en: She runs every morning at Ayala Triangle.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Takes ng + the thing requested. Humingi ng tawad = apologize.

examples.tl: Humingi siya ng tulong sa guard.
examples.en: He asked the guard for help.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Object focus: gawin. Gumawa ng paraan = find a way.

examples.tl: Gumawa siya ng paraan para makarating.
examples.en: He found a way to get there.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Object focus: sagutin. Also 'to shoulder the cost' (ako ang sasagot).

examples.tl: Hindi siya sumagot sa text ko.
examples.en: He didn't reply to my text.
examples.taglish: Hindi siya sumagot sa text ko, seen lang.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Object focus: tingnan. In a store 'Tumitingin lang po' = just browsing.

examples.tl: Tumitingin lang po kami.
examples.en: We're just looking, thanks.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Tawanan = to laugh at someone. Nakakatawa = funny.

examples.tl: Tumawa lang siya nang sabihin ko.
examples.en: She just laughed when I said it.

notes.notes: Actor focus (um-). Iyakin = crybaby. Umiiyak = is crying.

examples.tl: Umiyak ang baby buong gabi.
examples.en: The baby cried all night.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). Magkanta also common. Root from Spanish cantar. Kantahin = sing a song.

examples.tl: Kumanta siya sa videoke hanggang alas-dos.
examples.en: He sang videoke until 2 a.m.

notes.notes: Actor focus (um-). Umuulan = it's raining; uulan daw = they say it will rain.

examples.tl: Umuulan na naman sa Makati.
examples.en: It's raining again in Makati.
examples.taglish: Umuulan na naman, baha na siguro sa Taft.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). 'Lumapit ka' = come closer. Malapit = near.

examples.tl: Lumapit ang bata at humingi ng barya.
examples.en: The kid came up and asked for coins.

notes.en: to go along; to come with
notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). 'Sama ka?' = coming along? Isama = bring someone along; samahan = accompany.

examples.tl: Sasama ako sa inyo sa Tagaytay.
examples.en: I'll go with you guys to Tagaytay.

notes.notes: Actor focus (-um-). 'Susunod' also means 'next' (susunod na linggo). Sundin = follow a rule.

examples.tl: Sumunod lang kami sa Waze.
examples.en: We just followed Waze.

notes.notes: Ability actor focus (maka-). Nakakain = managed to eat. The 'ka' reduplicates: nakakakain.

examples.tl: Hindi ako nakakain ng lunch kasi back-to-back ang meetings.
examples.en: I didn't get to eat lunch because meetings were back-to-back.

notes.notes: Ability actor focus (maka-). 'Nakapunta ka na ba sa...?' = have you ever been to...?

examples.tl: Nakapunta ka na ba sa Siargao?
examples.en: Have you ever been to Siargao?

notes.en: to fall asleep; to manage to sleep
notes.notes: Ability actor focus (maka-). Nakatulog = fell asleep (vs natulog = went to bed).

examples.tl: Nakatulog ako sa bus pauwi.
examples.en: I fell asleep on the bus going home.

notes.notes: Ability actor focus (maka-). 'Nakauwi ka na?' is the standard check-in text after a night out.

examples.tl: Nakauwi ka na ba? Ingat.
examples.en: Did you make it home yet? Take care.

notes.notes: Potentive object focus (ma- + kausap): the person spoken to is the subject. 'Nakausap ko na siya' = I got to talk to him.

examples.tl: Nakausap ko na ang admin tungkol sa parking.
examples.en: I already got to talk to the admin about parking.

notes.notes: Ability actor focus (maka-). Hindi ako nakabili = I wasn't able to buy.

examples.tl: Hindi ako nakabili ng load kanina.
examples.en: I wasn't able to buy load earlier.

notes.en: to tag along; to go along with
notes.notes: Social actor focus (maki-): join someone already doing it. Nakisabay sa kotse = rode along.

examples.tl: Nakisabay ako sa kotse ni Jen pauwi.
examples.en: I rode along in Jen's car going home.

notes.en: to plead; to ask a favor
notes.notes: Request actor focus (maki-). 'Nakikiusap ako' = I'm begging you / please, I'm asking.

examples.tl: Nakikiusap ako, pakibaba naman ng volume.
examples.en: I'm asking nicely, please turn the volume down.

notes.notes: Request actor focus (maki-). Root daan, d becomes r. 'Makikiraan po' is the standard excuse-me when squeezing past.

examples.tl: Makikiraan po.
examples.en: Excuse me, coming through.

notes.notes: Request actor focus (maki-): ride in someone else's vehicle.

examples.tl: Nakisakay lang ako sa kanila hanggang Ayala.
examples.en: I just hitched a ride with them up to Ayala.

notes.notes: Request actor focus (maki-). 'Makikigamit po ng CR' = may I use the restroom.

examples.tl: Makikigamit po ng CR.
examples.en: May I use the restroom, please?

notes.notes: Causative actor focus (magpa-): have someone cut your hair. The 'pa' reduplicates: nagpapagupit.

examples.tl: Nagpagupit ako sa barbero sa kanto.
examples.en: I got a haircut at the corner barber.

notes.notes: Causative actor focus (magpa-): have something fixed or arranged. Also 'get your hair/makeup done'.

examples.tl: Nagpaayos kami ng aircon noong Sabado.
examples.en: We had the aircon fixed on Saturday.

notes.en: to say goodbye; to ask permission
notes.notes: Actor focus (magpa- + alam): let someone know you're leaving. 'Magpapaalam na ako' = I'll say goodbye now.

examples.tl: Nagpaalam na siya sa boss niya kasi may lakad.
examples.en: She told her boss she was leaving because she had plans.

notes.en: to get checked by a doctor
notes.notes: Causative actor focus (magpa-): have yourself looked at. Magpatingin sa doktor / sa dentista.

examples.tl: Nagpatingin ako sa doktor kasi tatlong araw na akong may lagnat.
examples.en: I saw a doctor because I had had a fever for three days.

notes.notes: Causative actor focus (magpa-): commission work from someone. Object focus: ipagawa.

examples.tl: Magpapagawa kami ng cabinet sa kwarto.
examples.en: We're having a cabinet made for the bedroom.

notes.notes: Taglish causative (magpa- + picture). 'Magpa-picture tayo!' = let's take a photo of us.

examples.tl: Nagpa-picture kami sa harap ng Rizal Monument.
examples.en: We had our picture taken in front of the Rizal Monument.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Hyphen before a vowel root; the vowel reduplicates: nag-aaral. Also 'to attend school'.

examples.tl: Nag-aaral siya sa Mapua.
examples.en: She studies at Mapua.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Magsalita ng Tagalog = speak Tagalog. Mag-usap = converse with someone.

examples.tl: Nagsasalita ba siya ng Tagalog?
examples.en: Does he speak Tagalog?

notes.en: to walk around; to take a walk
notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-): walking as an activity. Lumakad = walk or set off toward somewhere.

examples.tl: Naglalakad kami sa Ayala Triangle tuwing gabi.
examples.en: We walk around Ayala Triangle every evening.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: hanapin. Humanap also used.

examples.tl: Naghahanap siya ng bagong trabaho.
examples.en: He's looking for a new job.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: basahin. Bumasa also used. Root basa (read) stresses the 1st syllable.

examples.tl: Nagbabasa siya ng libro sa MRT.
examples.en: She reads a book on the MRT.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: isulat. Sumulat also used. Sulat = letter.

examples.tl: Nagsusulat siya ng blog tungkol sa pagkain.
examples.en: He writes a blog about food.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: dalhin (irregular). 'May dala ka ba?' = did you bring anything?

examples.tl: Nagdala ako ng payong kasi baka umulan.
examples.en: I brought an umbrella in case it rains.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: ibigay (the thing); recipient focus: bigyan (the person).

examples.tl: Nagbigay siya ng tip sa rider.
examples.en: He gave the rider a tip.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: simulan. 'Nagsimula na' = it has started. Taglish: mag-start.

examples.tl: Nagsimula na ang meeting nang dumating ako.
examples.en: The meeting had already started when I arrived.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Tanungin = ask someone; itanong = ask the question itself.

examples.tl: Nagtanong ako sa guard kung saan ang exit.
examples.en: I asked the guard where the exit was.

notes.en: to talk; to have a conversation
notes.notes: Reciprocal actor focus (mag-). Kausapin = to talk to someone. 'Usap tayo' = let's talk.

examples.tl: Nag-usap kami nang matagal sa phone.
examples.en: We talked on the phone for a long time.

notes.notes: Actor focus (magka- + mali 'wrong'); the 'ka' reduplicates: nagkakamali. 'Nagkamali ako' = my bad.

examples.tl: Nagkamali ako ng baba, sa Buendia pa pala.
examples.en: I got off at the wrong stop; it was Buendia, it turns out.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Taglish mag-drive is just as common. Root from Spanish manejar.

examples.tl: Hindi ako nagmamaneho sa Manila, nakaka-stress.
examples.en: I don't drive in Manila, it's stressful.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus buksan is more common. Bukas (stress on 2nd syllable) also = tomorrow.

examples.tl: Nagbukas ang bagong coffee shop sa Poblacion.
examples.en: A new coffee shop opened in Poblacion.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: isara. 'Nagsara na' = closed for the day or for good. Sarado = closed.

examples.tl: Nagsasara ang mall ng alas-diyes.
examples.en: The mall closes at ten.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). With a consonant cluster, reduplicate only pa: nagpaplano. Planuhin = plan something.

examples.tl: Nagpaplano kami ng trip sa Palawan.
examples.en: We're planning a trip to Palawan.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Maglaro ng basketball / ng ML (Mobile Legends). Laruan = toy.

examples.tl: Naglalaro ng basketball ang mga bata sa court.
examples.en: The kids are playing basketball at the court.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: mahalin. Mahal also = expensive. Letters end 'Nagmamahal, ...'.

examples.tl: Nagmahal siya ng taong hindi siya mahal.
examples.en: He loved someone who didn't love him back.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-). Object focus: ituro (also 'to point out'). Guro/teacher.

examples.tl: Nagtuturo siya ng English online.
examples.en: She teaches English online.

notes.notes: Taglish actor focus (mag- + text). Reduplication 'nagte-text' is also written nagtetext. Object: i-text (mo ako).

examples.tl: Nag-text siya na late siya.
examples.en: He texted that he's running late.

notes.notes: Actor focus (mag-): change by itself or change one's ways. Bago = new. Baguhin = change something.

examples.tl: Nagbago na ang schedule ng MRT.
examples.en: The MRT schedule has changed.

notes.notes: Object focus (ma-, perception). 'Nakita ko' = I saw it. 'Nakikita mo ba?' = can you see it?

examples.tl: Nakita ko si Paolo sa Landmark kanina.
examples.en: I saw Paolo at Landmark earlier.

notes.notes: Object focus (ma-, perception). Root dinig: d becomes r after the prefix (ma-rinig, na-ririnig).

examples.tl: Narinig ko yung sinabi mo.
examples.en: I heard what you said.

notes.notes: Object focus (ma-...-an). 'Hindi ko maintindihan' = I don't understand. Taglish: na-gets ko.

examples.tl: Naintindihan mo ba yung sinabi ng driver?
examples.en: Did you understand what the driver said?
examples.taglish: Na-gets mo ba yung sinabi ng driver?

notes.notes: Actor focus (ma-). Matuto ng Tagalog / matutong magluto. Reduplicate tu: natututo.

examples.tl: Natututo na akong mag-Tagalog.
examples.en: I'm learning to speak Tagalog.

notes.notes: Object focus (ma-). Root alaala; ma- + alaala contracts to maalala. 'Naalala ko!' = oh, I remember now.

examples.tl: Naalala ko na kung saan ko nilagay ang susi.
examples.en: I remember now where I put the key.

notes.en: to find out; to come to know
notes.notes: Object focus (ma-...-an) of alam. 'Nalaman ko' = I found out. For plain 'I know' just say 'alam ko'.

examples.tl: Nalaman ko lang kahapon na lilipat na siya.
examples.en: I only found out yesterday that she's moving.

notes.notes: Object focus (ma- + ka-...-an) of limot. 'Nakalimutan ko' = I forgot. Shorter kalimutan is also used.

examples.tl: Nakalimutan ko ang wallet ko sa condo.
examples.en: I forgot my wallet at the condo.

notes.notes: State focus (ma-, not mag-). 'Nagugutom na ako' = I'm getting hungry. 'Gutom na ako' = I'm hungry.

examples.tl: Nagugutom na ako, kain na tayo.
examples.en: I'm getting hungry, let's eat.

notes.notes: State focus (ma-). 'Napagod ako' = I got tired. 'Pagod ako' = I'm tired. Nakakapagod = tiring.

examples.tl: Napagod ako sa commute, dalawang oras one way.
examples.en: I got tired from the commute, two hours one way.

notes.en: to be late; to get caught
notes.notes: Actor focus (ma-). 'Nahuli ako' = I was late or I got caught, by context. Taglish: na-late.

examples.tl: Nahuli ako sa meeting kasi traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: I was late to the meeting because of traffic on EDSA.

notes.notes: State/object focus (ma-). 'Natapos na' = it's done. Tapusin = finish something. Tapos = done; also 'then'.

examples.tl: Natapos na ang shift ko ng alas-sais.
examples.en: My shift ended at six.

notes.notes: Actor focus (ma-). Root patay: the p becomes m (ma-matay). Also for batteries, phones, lights going dead.

examples.tl: Namatay ang phone ko sa kalagitnaan ng call.
examples.en: My phone died in the middle of the call.

notes.en: to run out; to be used up
notes.notes: State focus (ma-). Naubos na ang load / kanin / pera. Ubusin = finish it all off.

examples.tl: Naubos na ang load ko.
examples.en: My phone load is all used up.

notes.notes: State focus (ma-). 'Nawala ang wallet ko' = my wallet got lost. 'Nawawala' = is missing.

examples.tl: Nawala ang signal sa loob ng elevator.
examples.en: The signal dropped inside the elevator.

notes.notes: Actor focus (ma-). 'Nahulog ang phone ko' = my phone fell. Also 'fall in love' (nahulog ang loob).

examples.tl: Nahulog ang phone ko sa sahig ng jeep.
examples.en: My phone fell on the jeep floor.

notes.notes: State focus (ma-). 'Nasira ang aircon' = the aircon broke. Sira = broken. Sirain = break something.

examples.tl: Nasira ang aircon namin, init na init.
examples.en: Our aircon broke, it's so hot.

notes.notes: State focus (ma-). Root basa 'wet' (stress on 2nd syllable). Same spelling as basa 'read', so mabasa can also mean 'manage to read'.

examples.tl: Nabasa ako sa ulan pauwi.
examples.en: I got soaked in the rain going home.

notes.notes: Emotion focus (ma-). 'Natatakot ako' = I'm scared. 'Takot ako sa ipis' = I'm scared of cockroaches.

examples.tl: Natakot ako nang lumindol kagabi.
examples.en: I got scared when the earthquake hit last night.

notes.notes: Emotion focus (ma-, not mag-). 'Nagalit siya' = he got mad. 'Galit ka?' = are you mad?

examples.tl: Nagalit si Mama kasi late ako umuwi.
examples.en: Mom got mad because I came home late.

notes.notes: Irregular linking verb (ma- + -ging, no separate root). Naging = became/was; nagiging = is becoming; magiging = will be.

examples.tl: Naging mahirap ang commute noong bumaha.
examples.en: The commute became hard when it flooded.

notes.en: to meet; to get to know
notes.notes: Object focus (ma-): the person met is the subject. 'Nakilala ko siya' = I met him. Kilala = known / acquainted.

examples.tl: Nakilala ko siya sa isang party sa Poblacion.
examples.en: I met her at a party in Poblacion.

notes.notes: Taglish state verb (ma- + late). 'Na-late ako' = I was late. The reduplicated 'le' spelling varies in texts (nalelate).

examples.tl: Na-late ako kasi traffic sa Buendia.
examples.en: I was late because of traffic on Buendia.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). Gawa + -in = gawin (a drops out). 'Anong ginagawa mo?' = what are you doing?

examples.tl: Anong ginagawa mo ngayon?
examples.en: What are you doing right now?

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). Root sabi + -hin. 'Sabi ko' = I said. Sabihan = tell someone.

examples.tl: Sinabi ko na sa kanya kahapon.
examples.en: I already told him yesterday.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). Completed infixes -in- after h: hinintay. 'Hintayin mo ako' = wait for me.

examples.tl: Hinihintay ko pa yung rider.
examples.en: I'm still waiting for the rider.
examples.taglish: Hinihintay ko pa yung Grab rider, 10 mins pa daw.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in); o becomes u: lutuin. Roots starting with l use ni- for completed: niluto (older: linuto).

examples.tl: Niluto ni Lola ang sinigang para sa lahat.
examples.en: Grandma cooked sinigang for everyone.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). Roots starting with l take ni- instead of the -in- infix: nilinis, nililinis.

examples.tl: Nilinis ko na ang CR.
examples.en: I already cleaned the bathroom.

notes.notes: Object focus (-an). 'Hugasan mo ang plato' = wash the dishes. Hugasan as a noun = the sink.

examples.tl: Hinugasan ko na ang mga plato.
examples.en: I already washed the dishes.

notes.notes: Object focus (i-): the thing given is the subject. Completed: i- + b-in-igay = ibinigay. Bigyan = give to someone.

examples.tl: Ibinigay ko ang sukli sa driver.
examples.en: I gave the change to the driver.

notes.notes: Object focus (i-). Isinulat = wrote it. Sulatan = write to someone. Taglish: i-type.

examples.tl: Isinulat ko ang address sa resibo.
examples.en: I wrote the address on the receipt.

notes.notes: Beneficiary focus (i-): the person you buy for is the subject. 'Ibili mo ako ng tubig' = buy me water.

examples.tl: Ibinili niya ako ng kape sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: She bought me coffee at 7-Eleven.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). Irregular: dala + -in drops a vowel: dalhin. Completed dinala. 'Dalhin mo' = bring it.

examples.tl: Dinala ko ang laptop sa office.
examples.en: I brought the laptop to the office.

notes.notes: Object focus (i-). Vowel root: completed is ini- + uwi = iniuwi. 'Iuuwi ko' = I'll take it home.

examples.tl: Iniuwi niya yung tirang pizza.
examples.en: He took the leftover pizza home.

notes.notes: Object focus (i-). 'Ibabalik ko' = I'll return it. Bumalik = to come back (actor focus).

examples.tl: Ibinalik ko na ang susi sa guard.
examples.en: I already returned the key to the guard.

notes.notes: Object focus (i-). Roots starting with l take ini- in the completed: inilagay. 'Ilagay mo dito' = put it here.

examples.tl: Saan mo inilagay ang remote?
examples.en: Where did you put the remote?

notes.notes: Object focus (i-). Completed: i- + t-in-apon = itinapon. Basurahan = trash can.

examples.tl: Itinapon ko na yung expired na gatas.
examples.en: I already threw out the expired milk.

notes.notes: Object focus (i- + pa- + dala) of magpadala. Completed ipinadala; ipinadadala also heard. 'Ipapadala ko' = I'll send it.

examples.tl: Ipinadala ko na yung documents via LBC.
examples.en: I already sent the documents via LBC.

notes.notes: Object focus (i-). 'Ituro mo sa akin' = teach/show me. Also 'to point at'.

examples.tl: Itinuro niya sa akin kung paano mag-GCash.
examples.en: He taught me how to use GCash.

notes.notes: Object focus (i- + pa- + kita). Completed ipinakita; ipinakikita also heard. Casual short form: 'Pakita mo'.

examples.tl: Ipinakita ko ang QR code sa cashier.
examples.en: I showed the QR code to the cashier.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in): the person asked is the subject; o becomes u. Itanong = ask the question itself.

examples.tl: Tinanong ko ang guard kung saan ang CR.
examples.en: I asked the guard where the restroom was.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in); o becomes u: sagutin. Also 'to pay for' (sasagutin ko ang bill).

examples.tl: Hindi niya sinagot ang tawag ko.
examples.en: He didn't answer my call.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). Root bisita + -hin. Native synonym: dalawin. Bumisita = actor focus.

examples.tl: Binisita namin si Lolo sa Bulacan.
examples.en: We visited Grandpa in Bulacan.

notes.en: to go to (a place or person)
notes.notes: Directional focus (-an): the place or person gone to is the subject. 'Pupuntahan kita' = I'll come to you.

examples.tl: Pupuntahan kita sa office mo mamaya.
examples.en: I'll come by your office later.

notes.notes: Object focus (-an): the person helped is the subject; o becomes u. 'Tulungan mo ako' = help me.

examples.tl: Tinulungan ako ng kapitbahay magbuhat ng ref.
examples.en: The neighbor helped me carry the fridge.

notes.notes: Object focus (-an). Vowel root: completed is in- + alaga = inalagaan. Alaga as a noun = pet / ward.

examples.tl: Inaalagaan niya ang lola niya sa bahay.
examples.en: She takes care of her grandmother at home.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). More deliberate than maintindihan; also 'to mind'. 'Wag mo nang intindihin' = don't mind it.

examples.tl: Hindi ko inintindi ang sinabi niya.
examples.en: I didn't pay attention to what he said.

notes.notes: Object focus (-an); o becomes u: subukan. 'Subukan mo' = try it. Taglish: i-try mo.

examples.tl: Sinubukan ko ang bagong ramen place sa Salcedo.
examples.en: I tried the new ramen place in Salcedo.

notes.notes: Object focus (-an). Irregular: tingin + -an drops a vowel: tingnan. Completed tiningnan. 'Tingnan mo' = look.

examples.tl: Tiningnan ko ang Waze, red lahat.
examples.en: I checked Waze, everything was red.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in). Root basa + -hin. 'Binasa ko' = I read it. Babasahin as a noun = reading material.

examples.tl: Binasa mo ba yung message ko?
examples.en: Did you read my message?

notes.notes: Object focus (ka-...-an) of limot; o becomes u. Mostly a command: 'Kalimutan mo na' = forget it. Everyday past: nakalimutan.

examples.tl: Kinalimutan na niya ang nangyari.
examples.en: She has let go of what happened.

notes.en: to remember; to keep in mind
notes.notes: Object focus (-in) of alaala. 'Alalahanin mo' = keep in mind. Also 'to worry about' (inaalala kita).

examples.tl: Aalalahanin ko ang sinabi mo.
examples.en: I'll keep in mind what you said.

notes.notes: Object focus (-in) of gusto; o becomes u. Everyday 'I want' is just 'gusto ko'. Mostly in 'kung gugustuhin mo' = if you want to.

examples.tl: Kung gugustuhin mo, pwede kang mag-stay dito.
examples.en: If you want, you can stay here.

notes.notes: Recipient focus (-an). Irregular: bigay + -an drops a vowel: bigyan. 'Bigyan mo ako ng...' = give me...

examples.tl: Binigyan niya ako ng discount.
examples.en: She gave me a discount.

notes.notes: Object focus (-an): the person accompanied is the subject. 'Samahan mo ako' = come with me.

examples.tl: Sinamahan ko siya sa ospital.
examples.en: I went with her to the hospital.
